people.bio: Born in Malaysia, lived most of my life in the UK, been in New Zealand the last 4 years. I have many obsessions, including tech, military history, comics as well as, of course, science fiction and fantasy.
people.name: A Ming Has No Name

people.bio: A. L. Kaplan's love of books started as a child and sparked a creative imagination. Born on a cold winter morning in scenic northern New Jersey, USA, her stories and poems have been included in several anthologies and magazines. Her most recent publication is Mark of the Goddess. She is a member of the Science Fiction & Fantasy Writers Association, is the Maryland Writers' Association President and holds an MFA in sculpture from the Maryland Institute College of Art. When not writing or indulging in her fascination with wolves, this proud mother of two lives in Maryland, USA, with her husband and dog. ALKaplanauthor.com
people.name: A. L. Kaplan

people.bio:
Associate Professor, History of Religion, Umea University
Series Editor, Bloomsbury Studies in Popular Fiction and Religious Dynamics

I write about how fiction shapes religion and vice-versa.
people.name: A. M. Vincent

people.bio: A.T. Greenblatt is a Nebula Award winning writer and mechanical engineer. She lives in New York City where she's known to frequently subject her friends to various cooking and home brewing experiments. Her work has been nominated for a Hugo, Locus, and Sturgeon Award, has been in multiple Year's Best anthologies, and has appeared in Tor.com, Beneath Ceaseless Skies, Lightspeed, and Clarkesworld, as well as other fine publications. You can find her online at http://atgreenblatt.com and on Bluesky at @AtGreenblatt
people.name: A. T. Greenblatt

people.bio:
Alice is the #1 Sunday Times bestselling author of Shanghai Immortal, the first in a trilogy following the shenanigans of charmingly profane, irreverent, sometimes petulant but always entertaining half hulijing fox spirit Lady Jing.

She’s lived in Calgary, Taipei, Paris, Stockholm, Beijing, London, and Hong Kong, giving her the unique experience of being a minority in Canada and the UK, one kind of foreigner in Taiwan, China and Hong Kong SAR, and another kind in France and Sweden, as well as an expat in England. Belonging nowhere and everywhere, depending on her mood and mindset, she’s fascinated by the interplay between self-perceived versus imposed identity and how this intersects with belonging and enjoys exploring these spaces in her stories.

A recovering lawyer and xiaolongbao enthusiast, she knits to soothe anxiety and has a deep abiding love for Hobonichi planners and kawaii planner stickers. Between summer or winter, she’ll take the mountains capped in champagne powder and bluebird skies every time, including the frozen nostril hairs! 

Alice lives in London with her geo-historian hubby, chatterbox daughter, and sweet rescue pup. She’s grateful for the support of the Canada Council for the Arts. Find her online at aychao.com and @ay_chao on Twitter and Instagram.
people.name: A. Y. Chao

people.bio: Abigail Nussbaum is a Hugo-winning blogger and critic. She is the former reviews editor of Strange Horizons, and blogs at Asking the Wrong Questions and Lawyers, Guns & Money. Her review collection, Track Changes, is published by Briardene Books.
people.name: Abigail Nussbaum

people.bio: Author of the award-winning hopepunk Terra Ignota series, Ada Palmer teaches history at the University of Chicago, focusing on the Renaissance, heresy, and censorship. Current projects: “Hearthfire” first of a Norse myth duology (Tor, 2026), two nonfiction books “Inventing the Renaissance” (HeadOfZeus 2025) and “Why We Censor, from the Inquisition to the Internet”, and two projects co-authored with Jo Walton, the essay collection “Trace Elements: Conversations on the Craft of Science Fiction and Fantasy” (Tor, 2025), and a novel about exoplanet terraforming.  She writes essays for Strange Horizons, composes & performs music with Sassafrass, studies anime/manga, and blogs/podcasts at ExUrbe.com.
people.name: Ada Palmer

people.bio:
Having spent three and a half decades playing games and the best part of a decade writing about them, Adam hopes to spend whatever remains of his life making games. He joined Larian Studios during the early phase of Baldur’s Gate 3 production. More than a million words and six years later, he is now Larian’s Writing Director.

In his spare time he reads, plays, watches and listens… to just about anything that seems interesting. His dream is to write a book so frightening that it causes you to lose sleep.
people.name: Adam Smith

people.bio: Adri is a critic and senior co-editor at the Hugo and Ignyte-winning online fanzine nerds of a feather, flock together, which publishes daily reviews, interviews, roundtables and analysis of all things nerd culture. She also writes for Strange Horizons and has been published in the British Fantasy Society journal. She is a regular jurist for the Subjective Chaos Kind of Awards, a blogger-led award recognising excellent books without taking itself too seriously. She also finds time for her day job supporting democracy and rule of law worldwide, scuba diving with interesting wildlife, and providing emotional support to her elderly whippet.
people.name: Adri Joy

people.bio: I have been attending conventions since 1994 and been interested in all aspects of Science-Fiction and Fantasy all my life in all formats.
people.name: Adrian Emery

people.bio: Adrian Hon is a game designer, author, and former CEO and founder of Six to Start, co-creator of the world's bestselling smartphone fitness game "Zombies, Run!" with ten million players. He wrote a critique of gamification called, "You've Been Played: How Corporations, Governments, and Schools Use Games to Control Us All" and the sci-fi novel "A History of the Future in 100 Objects". Adrian has spoken at the flagship TED conference, the Long Now Foundation, GoogleX, and Disney Imagineering. Before becoming a game designer, Adrian was a neuroscientist and experimental psychologist at Cambridge, UCSD, and Oxford.
people.name: Adrian Hon

people.bio: ADRIAN M. GIBSON is a Canadian sci-fi author, podcaster and illustrator (as well as occasional tattoo artist). He studied English Literature and has worked in music journalism, restaurants, tattoo studios, clothing stores and a bevy of odd jobs. In 2021, he created the SFF Addicts podcast, which he co-hosts with fellow author M. J. Kuhn. The two host in-depth interviews with an array of science fiction and fantasy authors, as well as writing masterclasses. He lives in Quito, Ecuador with his wife and sons. His debut novel is MUSHROOM BLUES, which released in March 2024.
people.name: Adrian M. Gibson

people.bio: Adrian Tchaikovsky is an award-winning SFF novellist. His works include the Children of Time, Final Architecture and Shadows of the Apt series, Dogs of War, City of Last Chances, Doors of Eden and many more.
people.name: Adrian Tchaikovsky

people.bio: Adrienne Law is a Senior Writer at Larian Studios, an independent developer dedicated to pushing the boundaries of storytelling and player freedom. As a writer on Larian's award-winning D&D-based fantasy epic Baldur's Gate 3, she helped to craft heroes and villains, gods and monsters, and even the occasional pigeon. Prior to joining Larian, Adrienne was a writer and narrative designer on Interior/Night's interactive drama As Dusk Falls, and at ustwo Games she was the producer of Monument Valley 2, and the producer and writer of Assemble with Care.
people.name: Adrienne Law

people.bio:
Ahmed Mourad, born in Cairo in 1978, is an Egyptian writer who first launched his career in the realm of cinema, studying Cinematography at the Higher Institute of Cinema, from which he graduated in 2001 with honors. His graduation projects "The Wanderers – The Three Cards – and On the Seventh Day" garnered awards for short films in festivals in England, France, and Ukraine.
Ahmed began writing his first novel "Vertigo" in the winter of 2007, which was published in the same year by Merit Publishing House. It was later translated into English by Bloomsbury Publishing, then into Italian by Marsilio Editori, and was adapted into a TV series starring actress Hend Sabry, airing in 2012.
In February 2010, Mourad released his second novel "Diamond Dust", which was also translated into Italian by Marsilio Editori, and into German by Lenos Verlag, Switzerland. The novel was turned into a feature film in 2018, starring Asser Yassin, Menna Shalaby, and Maged El Kidwani, with Mourad penning the screenplay and dialogue, and directed by Marwan Hamed.
In October 2012, Mourad released his third novel "The Blue Elephant", achieving first place in book sales at the Cairo International Book Fair 2013, and sales estimated at one and a half million paperback copies within two years of its release, and also translated to German by Lenos Verlag, Switzerland.
It was later adapted into a film featuring actor Karim Abdel Aziz, with screenplay and dialogue by Mourad, and directed by Marwan Hamed. The novel earned Mourad a spot on the shortlist for the Arabic Booker Prize in 2014 and was translated into German by Lenos Verlag, Switzerland.
Mourad wrote a second part for 'The Blue Elephant' as a direct screenplay for cinema, the film being released in 2019.
In 2014, Mourad released his fourth novel "1919", a historical piece set in the 1920s, which was adapted into a film starring Karim Abdel Aziz, Ahmed Ezz, and Hend Sabry, and directed by Marwan Hamed in 2022.
In 2016, Mourad published his fifth novel "The Land of God", a story set in Ancient Egypt between the era of the 18th dynasty and the time of Ptolemy II Philadelphus, King of the Greeks in Alexandria. The novel was translated into English by Dar Al Shorouk.
In 2017, Mourad released his sixth novel "Deer Hunting Season", a novel set in the year 2061, addressing the concept of returning to past lives, reincarnation, and it is a romantic fantasy novel.
In 2020, Mourad published his seventh novel "Locanda Ber El Wataweet" Bat well Motel, a crime novel set in Cairo year 1865, The novel talks about a hero detective suffering from paranoid delusions.
In 2022, Mourad released a book titled "Killing for Beginners", a guide to writing cinematic screenplays.
In the fall of 2023, he released his eighth novel, "Abo El-Hol” Sphinx, the novel utilizes the same protagonist from the novel 'Locanda Bir Al-Watawit', the detective afflicted with paranoia, but in a new thrilling adventure set in the year 1869.
Novels:
1. Vertigo (2007)
2. Diamond Dust (2010)
3. The Blue Elephant (2012)
4. 1919 (2014)
5. The Land of God (2016)
6. Deer Hunting Season (2017)
7. Locanda Ber El Wataweet (2020)
8. Killing for Beginners (2021)
9. Sphinx (2023)
Films and TV Series:
1. Vertigo (TV Series, 2012)
2. The Blue Elephant (Film, Part I, 2014)
3. The Originals (Film, 2017)
4. Diamond Dust (Film, 2018)
5. The Blue Elephant (Film, Part II, 2019)
6. "Kira and the Gin" adapted from the novel 1919 (Film, 2021)
Awards:
1. "Mediterranean Culture Award" in 2013 for his debut novel "Vertigo" from Italy.
2. Shortlisted for the Arabic Booker Prize in 2014 for "The Blue Elephant" from UAE.
3. The “State Excellence” Award for his overall works in 2018.
Ahmed Mourad began teaching screenwriting in Cairo in 2016. More than 300 students graduated under his tutelage before he began teaching writing in the United Arab Emirates, the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, and Jordan. Currently, Mourad hosts the program “Al-Tawleefa” on “Nogoum FM” radio in Cairo since 2019.
people.name: Ahmed Mourad

people.bio: Ai Jiang is a Chinese-Canadian writer, Ignyte Award winner, Hugo, Astounding, Nebula, Bram Stoker, BSFA, and Locus Award finalist, and an immigrant from Fujian currently residing in Toronto, Ontario. She is a member of HWA and SFWA. Her work can be found in F&SF, The Dark, Uncanny, among others. She is the recipient of Odyssey Workshop's 2022 Fresh Voices Scholarship and the author of Linghun and I AM AI. Find her on Twitter (@AiJiang_) and online (http://aijiang.ca).
people.name: Ai Jiang

people.bio: Ailsa has worked in book marketing for over eight years, predominantly at traditional publishers before making the switch to freelance work, where she mainly works directly with independent authors. She has covered a variety of genres but SFF has always been her passion.
people.name: Ailsa Stuart

people.bio: Aimee Ogden is an American werewolf in the Netherlands. Her debut novella SUN-DAUGHTERS, SEA-DAUGHTERS was a Nebula Award finalist, and her most recent novella, EMERGENT PROPERTIES, arrived in July 2023. Her short fiction has appeared in publications such as Lightspeed, Clarkesworld, Analog, and Beneath Ceaseless Skies, and she co-edits Translunar Travelers Lounge, a magazine of fun and optimistic speculative fiction.
people.name: Aimee Ogden

people.bio: Alan Bailey is the co-creator, cohost, ad editor of the If This Goes On (Don’t Panic) podcast. In the past he also created, edited, and cohosted, the Alan & Jeremy VS Science Fiction podcast. He has been an educator for most of his life, starting in the Pittsburgh Public Schools and moving on to write curriculum for tech and insurance companies, post-secondary schools, and grocery chains. He has also been the bassist for numerous Pittsburgh bands.
people.name: Alan Bailey

people.bio: Alan Bond has been a convention planner from the Pacific Northwest for a number of years.  They have run Special Events, Tech and Convention Services for Norwescon, and  been the Tech Director for Chicon, and the Online Convention Lead for the 2020 NASFiC and Glasgow 2024 and the Member Services DH for Seattle 2025.  In 2020-2021 they co-produced and occasionally hosted Essence of Wonder a Videocast on YouTube and Twitch that discussed current topics in Data Science, Philosophy and Science Fiction.  They enjoy assisting their kids building costumes and props and building sculptures and items from wire.
people.name: Alan Bond

people.bio: Longtime SF fan: my first convention was in Glasgow in the mid-1980s, and I volunteered at my second. Took a long time away until 2016 but have rapidly got back in to the swing of things. Area Head for the Info Desk  here in Glasgow, stop by and find things out!
people.name: Alan Fleming

people.bio: I X-ray crystals for a living. I promise that there are good scientific reasons for doing this. I spend most of my time researching structural properties of materials, but I much prefer trying to teach the world about important scientific concepts. To date the world doesn't seem too care too much which I do.
people.name: Alan Kennedy

people.bio: Alan Smale writes alternate history and hard SF. His novella of a Roman invasion of ancient America, “A Clash of Eagles”, won the Sidewise Award, and related novels Clash of Eagles, Eagle in Exile, and Eagle and Empire (2015-2017) are available from Del Rey. His Roman-baseball collaboration with Rick Wilber, The Wandering Warriors, came out from WordFire Press (2020), and Hot Moon, his alternate-Apollo “technothriller with heart” from CAEZIK in 2022, with a sequel scheduled for 2024. Alan has sold 40+ stories to Asimov’s and other magazines and anthologies, and non-fiction essays to Lightspeed, Journey Planet, and Galaxy’s Edge.
people.name: Alan Smale

people.bio: Alasdair Stuart is a professional enthusiast, pop culture analyst, writer and voice actor. He co-owns the Escape Artists podcasts and hosts their weekly horror fiction show, PseudoPod. He is an Audioverse Award winner, a multiple Hugo Award and BFA finalist, writes the multiple-award nominated weekly pop culture newsletter, The Full Lid, blogs at www.alasdairstuart.com , streams on Twitch, and tweets @AlasdairStuart.
people.name: Alasdair Stuart

people.bio: Alastair Reynolds is a former space scientist turned full-time science fiction writer. He is the author of more than twenty novels and around eighty short stories. He has been shortlisted for the Hugo, Clarke, & Philip K Dick awards, and has won the BSFA, Locus, Seiun, Sidewise and European Science Fiction society awards. He and his wife live in Wales.
people.name: Alastair Reynolds

people.bio: The most relevant of my activities is that I am an aerospace engineer who has been the Head of Secretariat for the UK Magnetics Society for 12 years. The Society is a leading international society bringing together magnetics experts in industry and academia worldwide. As a result I have a wide but shallow knowledge of most magnetic and electromagnetic technologies underpinning the modern world. I share these with the wider public through talks like this, or through a STEM club I run with my wife for primary school children.
people.name: Alastair Stewart

people.bio: Aleksandra Hill is a Polish-Canadian writer of speculative fiction and the founder and publisher of khōréō, a magazine of speculative fiction by immigrant and diaspora writers. Her stories have appeared or are forthcoming in Analog, LeVar Burton Reads, Uncharted, Writer's Digest, and others. Learn more at www.aleksandrahill.com
people.name: Aleksandra Hill

people.bio: Alex Acks is an award-winning writer, geologist, contributing editor at Book Riot, and dapper AF. Angry Robot Books has published their novels HUNGER MAKES THE WOLF (winner of the Kitschies Golden Tentacle award) and BLOOD BINDS THE PACK under the pen name Alex Wells, while Queen of Swords has published their steampunk novella series starting with the Colorado Book Award-nominated MURDER ON THE TITANIA AND OTHER STEAM-POWERED ADVENTURES. They’ve written Thor and Loki for Six to Start's Marvel Move, stories for StarCraft and World of Warcraft for Activision-Blizzard, and they've had their short fiction published by Strange Horizons, Lightspeed, Daily Science Fiction, Shimmer, and more. Alex lives in Denver, where they twirl their mustache, watch movies, and bike. For more information, see http://www.alexacks.com.
people.name: Alex Alex

people.bio: Alex Kingsley (they/them) is a writer, comedian, and game designer. They are a co-founder of Strong Branch Productions and creator of sci-fi comedy podcast The Stench of Adventure. Their short fiction has appeared in Translunar Travelers Lounge, Radon Journal, and The Storage Papers. Their short story collection The Strange Garden and Other Weird Tales was released in 2023, and their debut novel Empress of Dust will be released in Fall 2024.
people.name: Alex Kingsley

people.bio:
Alex Penland is a former museum kid. He spent his childhood running rampant through the Smithsonian museums, which kicked off an early career as a child adventurer. Alex has worked in the field with NASA scientists, linguists, and acclaimed photographers.

Now twice a Pushcart-nominated author with a recent spot on the BFSA longlist, Alex lives in Scotland while studying for a PhD in Creative Writing at the University of Edinburgh. Prior adventures include founding a writing organization in Iowa, collaborating on micro-operas, diving with sharks, and volunteering with the Smithsonian for nearly a decade. His work has been internationally published, appearing in Interzone and Olney Magazine; Andrion is his first novella.

Catch him on most social media as @AlexPenname.
people.name: Alex Penland

people.bio: Alexander is an Arabic-to-English translator. He completed a Master's degree in Middle Eastern studies at SOAS, University of London. His first translation of Diaa Jubaili's short story, 'The Darwinist', was published in Strange Horizons magazine. He is also interested in teaching Arabic as a foreign language and in Arabic dialectology.
people.name: Alexander Hong

people.bio:
Alexandra is a fantasy-folklore author and an adventurous spirit who wanders in misty woodlands who takes part in Live Action Fantasy Role Play.

She writes fantasy entwined with folklore and is influenced by her background in gothic fiction. Her books, DISSONANCE OF BIRD SONG and TESTAMENT OF THE STARS, are praised as being haunting, epic folkloric tales of courage, love and loss.
people.name: Alexandra Beaumont

people.bio: Ali Baker is a lecturer at University of East London in initial teacher education MA in Education. She recently submitted a PhD thesis on White Working-Class Children in Children’s Fantasy Fiction. She has published on girls’ horror comics, stepfamilies in Diana Wynne Jones’ novels and social class in Harry Potter, and hosts the podcast Fantasy Book Swap.
people.name: Ali Baker

people.bio: Alicia Hilton is an author, editor, arbitrator, professor, actor, and former FBI Special Agent. Her work has appeared or is forthcoming in Back 2 OmniPark, Creepy Podcast, Daily Science Fiction, Eastern Iowa Review, Gamut, Litro, Mslexia, Neon, NonBinary Review, Space and Time, Strange Horizons, Unnerving, Vastarien, Year’s Best Hardcore Horror Volumes 4, 5 & 6, and elsewhere. She is a member of the Horror Writers Association, the Science Fiction and Fantasy Poetry Association, and the Science Fiction and Fantasy Writers Association. Her website is https://aliciahilton.com. Follow her on Twitter @aliciahilton01 and Bluesky @aliciahilton.bsky.social.
people.name: Alicia Hilton

people.bio:
Aliette de Bodard lives and works in Paris. She has won three Nebula Awards, an Ignyte Award, a Locus Award, a British Fantasy Award and six British Science Fiction Association Awards.

She is the author of A Fire Born of Exile, a sapphic Count of Monte Cristo in space (Gollancz/JABberwocky Literary Agency, Inc., 2023), and of Of Charms, Ghosts and Grievances (JABberwocky Literary Agency, Inc, 2022 BSFA Award winner), a fantasy of manners and murders set in an alternate 19th Century Vietnamese court.

She also wrote Fireheart Tiger (Tor.com, 2021 BSFA Award winner), a sapphic romantic fantasy inspired by pre colonial Vietnam, where a diplomat princess must decide the fate of her country, and her own. She lives in Paris.
people.name: Aliette de Bodard

people.bio:
I am a Librarian with Glasgow Libraries. I've worked in the South of the city for 8 years and was a School Librarian for 5 years before this. 
I am the buyer for Young Adult books including YA comics for the city.
people.name: Alison Nicol

people.bio: Alison Sampson is an artist, author, architect and sometime writer based in London, UK, but working with a variety of US-based publishers, including Marvel, DC, Dark Horse, IDW, Boom Studios, Vault, Z2, AWA and many more. Her publications include Hellboy and the BPRD (with Mike Mignola), Department of Truth (with James Tynion IV), Winnebago Graveyard (with Steve Niles) and the graphic novel adaptation of Sleeping Beauties, with Stephen and Owen King. She is a prolific book cover artist and is currently working on a creator owned series, The Blue Tarantula, with JH Williams III and Image Comics.
people.name: Alison Sampson

people.bio: Alison Scott is a UK based SF fan. She has won many awards, including Hugos and Novas for the fanzine Plokta. She has worked on too many conventions to count, most recently the 2023 Eastercon. She won the Rotsler Award for lifetime fan art achievement and, unexpectedly, the Doc Weir Award for being an unsung hero. In 2023 she visited Australia and New Zealand as the GUFF (Going Under Fan Fund) delegate, representing European fandom. She can be heard pontificating about SF and fandom every fortnight on the podcast Octothorpe.
people.name: Alison Scott

people.bio: Aliya Whiteley has written novels and novellas that have been shortlisted for multiple awards, including a Shirley Jackson award and the Arthur C. Clarke award. Her latest novel, Three Eight One, was published by Solaris in January 2024. Her short fiction has appeared in many anthologies and magazines, and her latest collection, Drive or be Driven, was recently published by NewCon Press. She writes a regular non-fiction column for Interzone magazine.
people.name: Aliya Whiteley

people.bio: Dr. Allen Stroud is a lecturer and researcher at Coventry University. He is the Chair of the British Science Fiction Association. His award-winning research is in the development of macrotext documents for commercial media properties in science fiction, fantasy and horror. He is also an award-winning science fiction writer who has published internationally successful commercial novels, with his principle focus on fiction set in 2118 AD. Stroud has spoken at international conventions, giving a presentation in Helsinki in 2017 at the World Convention of Science Fiction on modern media mythologies. He is an experienced event organiser, panel moderator and contributor.
people.name: Allen Stroud

people.bio:
Writer, editor, teacher, mom
2024 Hugo Finalist, Best Fanzine category
Graduate of Stonecoast (MFA through the University of Maine)
people.name: Allison Hartman Adams

people.bio: Alma Alexander is an internationally published novelist, short story writer, and anthologist/editor with more than 20 published books to her credit. She lives in the Pacific Northwest of the USA with two obligatory writers' cats.
people.name: Alma Alexander

people.bio: Alyx Dellamonica is the award-winning author of 7 SF and Fantasy novels and over 50 short stories. Their most recent books, Gamechanger and Dealbreaker, are solarpunk thrillers written under the pseudonym L.X. Beckett.
people.name: Alyx Dellamonica

people.bio: Amal El-Mohtar writes fiction, poetry, and criticism. She won the Hugo, Nebula, and Locus Awards for her 2016 short story "Seasons of Glass and Iron" and again for her 2019 novella This Is How You Lose the Time War, written with Max Gladstone, which became a New York Times Best Seller and has been translated into over ten languages. Her reviews and articles have appeared in the New York Times and on NPR Books, and her debut novella, The River Has Roots, is forthcoming from Tordotcom. She lives in Ottawa. Find her online at amalelmohtar.com
people.name: Amal El-Mohtar

people.bio: Aman was born in Mysore, India. He grew up in Vizag, studied in Bangalore, lived in Bangkok, completed a PhD in experimental psychology at the University of Canterbury, and has settled (for now) in Melbourne, Australia. His writing draws from modern Indian history and is influenced by writers and artists like David Gemmell, Brandon Sanderson, Takehiko Inoue, and Kentaro Miura. KAVITHRI, his debut novel, is published by Gollancz.
people.name: Aman J. Bedi

people.bio: Amanda Cherry is a queer, disabled author of contemporary and historical urban fantasy, TTRPGs, and an award-winning screenwriter.
people.name: Amanda Cherry

people.bio: Amanda Wakaruk co-edits the Unofficial Hugo Bookclub Blog along with Olav Rokne. They are repeat Hugo nominees and frequent volunteers at science fiction conventions. Outside of fandom, Amanda is an academic librarian with a current research interest in copyright anxiety and chill.
people.name: Amanda Wakaruk

people.bio: Amber Morrell is an author and librarian hailing from Southern California. She writes whimsical fantasy and science fiction for children and adults. Her work explores the liminal spaces between science and magic. In her free time, she plays D&D, watches Star Trek, and makes TikTok videos about esoteric knowledge. The Alchemy of Letting Go is her first novel.
people.name: Amber Morrell

people.bio: Andrea Stewart is the Sunday Times bestselling author of The Drowning Empire trilogy and a writing coach at The Novelry. Her short fiction can be found in Daily Science Fiction, Beneath Ceaseless Skies, Galaxy’s Edge, and other venues. When she’s not writing, she can be found herding cats, looking at birds, and falling down research rabbit holes.
people.name: Andrea Stewart

people.bio: Andrew has been an indie board game designer since 2018, and fan-vidder since 2022.
people.name: Andrew January

people.bio: Andrew M. Butler (he/him) is the author of Solar Flares: Science Fiction in the 1970s (Liverpool University Press, 2011), Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind (BFI, 2014), as well as books on Philip K. Dick, Cyberpunk, Terry Pratchett, Postmodernism and Film Studies and articles on Folk Horror, District 9 and special effects. He is coeditor of Rendezvous with Arthur C. Clarke (2022), The New Routledge Companion to Science Fiction (2024) and the journal Extrapolation. He is the non-voting chair of judges for the Arthur C. Clarke Award. In his spare time, he collects shiny trousers.
people.name: Andrew M Butler

people.bio: Andrew Penn Romine teaches animation and VFX, following a career working on films such as How to Train Your Dragon, Big Hero Six, and Avengers: Infinity War. His stories have appeared in Lightspeed, FUNGI, and HELP FUND MY ROBOT ARMY and have made honorable mentions on year’s best horror lists. He enjoys mixing cocktails and watching terrible movies.
people.name: Andrew Penn Romine

people.bio: Andrija Popovic is a native of the Washington DC metropolitan area who indulges in photography, spends entirely too much on books, and occasionally adds to the #NoirAlley Twitter discourse as @andrian6. By day he works with non-profits to leverage technology as an advocacy tool. His stories have previously been published in Daily Science Fiction and the anthologies ALIEN ARTIFACTS, THE DEATH OF ALL THINGS, PORTALS, DERELICT and NOIR. For more, check Biomechanoid Blues (biomechanoidblues.wordpress.com)
people.name: Andrija "Andy" Popovic

people.bio: András Fodor is a weird author and an independent scholar. He obtained his PhD at University of Szeged, Faculty of Arts, Doctoral School of Literature in 2021. He has been publishing reviews and short stories since 2010 mainly in his native tongue, Hungarian. In 2016 he won the JAKKendő Award for his manuscript collection of short stories, The Smiling Juggler, which was published later in the same year. His research interests are spatiality, cities, the New Weird, and hope.
people.name: András Fodor

people.bio:
Andy Dudak has translated 41 stories by 26 science fiction luminaries, including Liu Cixin, Chen Qiufan, and Bao Shu. He's had original stories in Interzone, Asimov’s Science Fiction, Analog Science Fiction & Fact, Clarkesworld, The Magazine of Fantasy & Science Fiction, Forever Magazine, Apex, Science Fiction World (科幻世界), and more.
He has paneled at three Worldcons. 
His story ‘Love in the Time of Immuno-Sharing’ was a finalist for the Eugie Foster Award.
His fiction has been anthologized in Neil Clarke’s Best Science Fiction of the Year, Jonathan Strahan’s Year’s Best Science Fiction, and three volumes of Rich Horton’s Year’s Best Science Fiction and Fantasy.  
He has done narrative design in the game industry. He's also an optioned and produced screenwriter.
people.name: Andy Dudak

people.bio: Andy is a Professor of Chemistry at the University of Manchester.
people.name: Andy Pitt

people.bio:
Angela Slatter is the author of the gothic fantasy novels All the Murmuring Bones, The Path of Thorns, and The Briar Book of the Dead (Titan Books), and the supernatural crime novels Vigil, Corpselight and Restoration (Jo Fletcher Books). She’s also written twelve short story collections, including The Girl with No Hands and Other Tales, Sourdough and Other Stories, The Bitterwood Bible and Other Recountings, and A Feast of Sorrows: Stories, and the novellas, Of Sorrow and Such, Ripper and The Bone Lantern. Her Hellboy Universe collaboration with Mike Mignola, Castle Full of Blackbirds, was released in 2022.

Vigil was longlisted for the Dublin Literary Award in 2018, and Angela has won a World Fantasy Award, a British Fantasy Award, a Shirley Jackson Award, a Ditmar, three Australian Shadows Award and eight Aurealis Awards. All the Murmuring Bones was shortlisted for the Queensland Premier’s Literary Awards’ Book of the Year and the Shirley Jackson Award. Angela’s short stories have appeared in Australian, UK and US Best Of anthologies. Her work has been translated into Bulgarian, Dutch, Chinese, Russian, Italian, Spanish, Japanese, Polish, Hungarian, Turkish, French and Romanian. Film rights have been optioned for her novelette “Finnegan’s Field”.

She has an MA and a PhD in Creative Writing, is a graduate of Clarion South 2009 and the Tin House Summer Writers Workshop 2006, and in 2013 she was awarded one of the inaugural Queensland Writers Fellowships. In 2016 Angela was the Established Writer-in-
Residence at the Katharine Susannah Prichard Writers Centre in Perth. She has been awarded career development funding by Arts Queensland, the Copyright Agency and the Australia Council for the Arts.
people.name: Angela (A.G.) Slatter

people.bio:
Ann Gry / also known as Ann Grá (Graigh)
is a poet and writer and three-time finalist for the Hugo Awards as a co-editor of Journey Planet fanzine. Ann writes speculative fiction, prose, poetry and scripts, wandering within and without.

Ann also manages and programmes Irish film festivals and is a passionate promoter of Irish culture. As an educator, she lectures in law, ethics, and cinema at a university.

In SF&F, Ann loves space, vampires, kaiju, and many other things. 

Find her at anngry.com and @anngraigh on X.
people.name: Ann Gry

people.bio: Growing up in East Germany on a steady diet of Grimms and Russian Fairy Tales until falling under the thrall of Tolkien and Pratchett in her teens, it is little surprising that Ann Landmann is now the founder and director of Cymera: Scotland's Festival of Science Fiction, Fantasy and Horror Writing. Some might say it's a cunning ploy to feed her addiction to those genres and to book events.  As the former Events Manager at Blackwell's, Edinburgh's oldest bookshop, and with degrees in Bookselling, Publishing and Events Management under her belt, books and literary events have been Ann's passion since she was 19, culminating in the creation of Cymera in 2018. In her day job, she travels around Scotland as a sales representative for Birlinn Ltd, one of Scotland's biggest publishers.
people.name: Ann Landmann

people.bio: Anna Cheung is a poet based in Glasgow. Her debut poetry collection entitled Where Decay Sleeps was published by Haunt Publishing. Amongst other writings, her previous works were published in the anthologies Golden Hours, Haunted Voices, Forward Book of Poetry and literary magazines such as The Dark Horse, Myth & Lore, Banshee Journal, Dreich and Zarf. She was highly commended by the Forward Prize in 2022. She has performed at various spoken word events including Cymera Festival, Granite Noir, Edinburgh Literary Salon and Edinburgh Book Festival
people.name: Anna Cheung

people.bio: Anna McFarlane is a Lecturer in Medical Humanities at the University of Leeds and author of the monograph Cyberpunk Culture and Psychology: Seeing Through the Mirrorshades (2021). Her research on traumatic pregnancy and its expression in fantastika was awarded a British Academy Postdoctoral Fellowship, and she is a Visiting Collaborator on the Wellcome-Trust funded Future of Human Reproduction project at the University of Lancaster. She is the co-editor of The Routledge Companion to Cyberpunk Culture, Fifty Key Figures in Cyberpunk Culture, and the forthcoming Edinburgh Companion to Science Fiction and the Medical Humanities.
people.name: Anna McFarlane

people.bio: Anna Oleszczuk is a research assistant at the Catholic University of Lublin in Lublin, Poland. Their research seeks to examine how the potential of speculative comics to conceptualize the deviations from the heteronormative cultural standard has been realized in modern texts and how it can be utilized to explore queer gender and sexualities.
people.name: Anna Oleszczuk

people.bio: Anna Raftery has been coming to conventions since the early 2000’s and not stopped since. She has work on conventions, including 2014 London Worldcon, and was the 2016 TAFF delegate.
people.name: Anna Raftery

people.bio: Anna Smith Spark is the author of the Empires of Dust grimdark epic fantasy series The Court of Broken Knives, The Tower of Living and Dying and The House of Sacrifice; the standalone A Woman of the Sword; and A Sword of Bronze and Ashes, book one of her folk horror high fantasy series The Remaking of This World Ruined. Her work has been described as ‘a masterwork’ and ‘awe-inspiring’. She’s dyslexic, dyspraxic, ASD, PhD; previous jobs include English teacher, fetish model and petty bureaucrat. You may know her by the heels of her shoes
people.name: Anna Smith Spark

people.bio:
Anna Stephens is the author of the Godblind and Songs of the Drowned trilogies through HarperVoyager, and also writes for Black Library in their Age of Sigmar and Warhammer Horror imprints, as well as for Marvel Comics through their tie-in publisher, Aconyte Books. 
These literary feats have been accomplished despite the nefarious intentions of Bailey the miniature poodle, who deploys his weapons-grade cuteness with irresponsible abandon. 
As a black belt in Shotokan Karate and a once upon a time historical fencer, Anna’s no stranger to the feeling of being hit in the face, which is more help than you would expect when writing fight scenes.
people.name: Anna Stephens

people.bio:
Annabel writes fantasy with fierce female characters, disaster wizards and all the fun tropes. Her debut novel, THE OUTCAST MAGE, the first part in a fantasy trilogy, will be published in early 2025.

She lives near Lanark, Scotland, in a village where most of her neighbours are sheep. She has a PhD in cardiovascular science, and when not making things up for a living, she works from home as a Medical Writer.
people.name: Annabel Campbell

people.bio: Annalee Newitz is a science journalist who also writes science fiction. They are the author of The Terraformers, Autonomous, and Four Lost Cities: A Secret History of the Urban Age, among others, and co-host the podcast Our Opinions Are Correct. They were the founder of io9, and are a columnist for New Scientist magazine.
people.name: Annalee Newitz

people.bio: Anne Perry is the award-winning Publishing Director of Arcadia, the SFF imprint of Quercus, a division of Hachette UK. She co-founded the Kitschies literary award and serves on the board, and is the co-founder of the award-winning geek culture website Pornokitsch. She has experince in all aspects of the publishing world, including as an agent and as a querying author, and is a proud Hugo loser.
people.name: Anne C. Perry

people.bio: Anne Charnock’s Dreams Before the Start of Time won the 2018 Arthur C. Clarke Award. Her writing career began in journalism, and her reports appeared in New Scientist, The Guardian, International Herald Tribune and others. She has written four novels in the field of near-future science fiction. Anne's novella, The Enclave won the 2017 BSFA Short Fiction Award. A Calculated Life (2013), her debut, was shortlisted for the Philip K. Dick Award and The Kitschies. Her latest novel is Bridge 108 (2020). She studied environmental sciences at the University of East Anglia and fine art at The Manchester School of Art. Her short fiction and essays have appeared in a range of publications and anthologies including The Utopia of Us (2024) and Writing the Future (2023).
people.name: Anne Charnock

people.bio: After 16 years as a criminal defence lawyer, Anne decided to abandon the world of legal aid for a - worryingly - more stable and viable career as a writer. Her first novel, The Space Between the Stars was published by Pan Macmillan in the UK and Random House in the US, and her second novel, The Theatre of Glass and Shadows came out in May with Bonnier. Her short fiction has been published in various magazines and anthologies and has won several awards.
people.name: Anne Corlett

people.bio: Anne-Louise Fortune is an expert in theatre and popular culture, holding an MA in World Theatres from Goldsmiths, University of London, and another in Popular Culture from Edge Hill University. She also has over twenty years experience in the performing and creative arts, and on the fringes of the publishing industry. She is interested in cultural texts which present the stories and histories of women. She is a writer of fiction and non-fiction, including for Starburst Magazine, the UK's longest running magazine for genre entertainment.
people.name: Anne-Louise Fortune

people.bio:
From the moment young Anton Marks crafted an adventure story for his third-grade class - complete with illustrations that had his classmates in a stir, it was clear that his imagination was boundless. Awarded a gold star by his headmaster, albeit with advice to tone down the edginess, Anton's creative spark was ignited against the backdrop of his family's longing for their Jamaican roots.

Upon returning to Jamaica, Anton, feeling like an outsider, embraced the island fully - its culture, language, and people. This immersion fueled his unique narrative style, heavily influenced by the island's customs and folklore, particularly the tales of Anancy by Miss Lou (Louise Bennett), a pioneering Jamaican author who brought the dialect and myths of the island to life in her writings.

Anton's passion for reading and storytelling was nurtured by a wide array of influences, from children's encyclopedias, Marvel comics, DC comics, and Miss Lou's works to Hollywood blockbusters and Hong Kong Shaw Brother epics popular in Jamaican cinemas. This eclectic mix of influences is evident in his genre-spanning body of work, which seamlessly blends elements of science fiction, adventure, horror, and crime.

His debut novel, Dancehall, published by X-Press Publishers in London, broke new ground with its unique combination of crime thriller elements set against the vivid backdrop of Jamaica's dancehall culture. Following Dancehall, Anton navigated the complexities of the publishing world, eventually releasing a succession of thrilling novels including In the Days of Dread, Bushman, and 69, each exploring different facets of speculative fiction with a distinctly Caribbean flair.

Anton didn't stop there. He ventured into the realm of supernatural thrillers with his series Bad II the Bone, Good II be Bad, and Good Girls Gone Bad, and embraced young adult sci-fi/fantasy under his birth name with titles like Joshua N'Gon: Last Prince of Alkebulahn, Joshua N'Gon and the Battle for St. Augustine and the third in the series Joshua N'Gon and the Trial on Gorilla Mountain to be published 2025, delving into rich, fantastical worlds with deep cultural roots.

His latest endeavours include the Urban Fantastic Shorts is a collection showcasing stories like Messiah, Chauffeur, Omega Point, and Pest Control and the upcoming AfroTech Supernatural thriller Headhunters, which promises to add exciting new dimensions to his oeuvre.

Anton Marks continues to craft stories that captivate and thrill, drawing readers into worlds where the fantastical meets the familiar, and the past intertwines with the future. For those yet to discover his work, there's no better time than now to explore the imaginative realms of this master storyteller.

For a complete journey through Anton Marks imaginative universe, visit www.antonmarks.com, where the adventure never ends and every story is a gateway to new, uncharted territories.

Bibliography Highlights

  • Dancehall - A groundbreaking crime thriller with a dancehall backdrop.
  • In the Days of Dread - A futuristic thriller exploring themes of dystopia and resilience.
  • Bushman & 69 - Engaging narratives that blend crime, thriller, and speculative elements.
  • Bad II the Bone Trilogy - A supernatural thriller series with a dynamic female lead.
  • Joshua N'Gon Series - A young adult sci-fi/fantasy saga filled with adventure and discovery.
  • Urban Fantastic Shorts - A collection of novellas that fuse urban life with fantastical elements.
  • Headhunters (Upcoming) - An AfroTech Supernatural thriller that promises to be a genre-bending masterpiece.

Whether you're a fan of speculative fiction, thrilling adventures, or stories that beautifully blend African and Caribbean culture with imaginative storytelling, Anton Marks's work is an essential addition to your reading list.
people.name: Anton Marks

people.bio: Antonija Mežnarić is a Croatian writer and editor who lives and breathes speculative fiction. She writes queer horror and fantasy, mostly inspired by South Slavic folklore, which is evident in her queer folk horror collection The Lost Treasure Hunters and Other Tales of Folk Terrors, several published horror novellas, various short stories in anthologies and magazines, and the dark urban fantasy novel From the Cradle to the Grave (English ed. coming in Fall 2024). You can follow her book ramblings on hauntednarratives.com or on Instagram and TikTok @antonijamezni.
people.name: Antonija Mežnarić

people.bio: Aparna Verma was born in Rajasthan, India, and grew up in the United States. She graduated from Stanford University with Honors in the Arts and a B.A. in English. In 2021, she self-published The Boy with Fire, which quickly gained attention on TikTok and social media, and was later republished by Orbit Books as The Phoenix King in 2023. When she is not writing, Aparna likes to lift heavy (arm days are her favorite), dance to Bollywood music, and find cozy cafes to read myths from ancient worlds. You can connect with Aparna on TikTok at @aparnawrites, and Twitter and Instagram at @spirited_gal.
people.name: Aparna Verma

people.bio: Aramo Olaya (PhD) is a second PhD candidate in Performance Studies with a focus on Science and Technology studies at UC Davis. A queer science fiction writer and fictional theory advocate, they practice somatic communication with the ISSC (Institute for the Study of Somatic Communication) towards wider understandings of language in SETI (Search for Extraterrestrial Intelligence.) Their interests include queer practices of touch and language, science fiction performative writing, cross-cultural understandings of energy and embodiment in somatics and postmodern dance, and fictional and non-fictional theories of bioelectricity in somatic communication between humans and with the non-human.
people.name: Aramo Olaya

people.bio: Arkady Martine is the author of the Teixcalaan series, the novella ROSE/HOUSE, a multitude of short stories, and various other science fiction, fantasy, & horror. She is also Dr. AnnaLinden Weller, who is a Byzantinist, a climate & energy policy analyst, and a city planner. She is not bored, but she is often tired.
people.name: Arkady Martine

people.bio: Artist & fanwriter,  youtuber,  haver of opinions
people.name: Arwen (TwoPeople'sOpinion)

people.bio: Ash Charlton is a longtime queer F/SF writer and fan. He is director of a training company specialising in people skills and personal development, and is a qualified psychologist and therapist. He has had the privilege of giving, moderating and contributing to many sessions at various Worldcons over the years, usually on Queer or social justice issues.
people.name: Ash Charlton

people.bio: Asher Rose Fox is the director of education for the Editorial Freelancers Association. They have been a professional book reviewer since 2002, and for over ten years, they edited the science fiction, fantasy, horror, romance, and erotica reviews sections for Publishers Weekly. They are the co-editor of Long Hidden: Speculative Stories from the Margins of History, and a longtime freelance editor specializing in genre fiction. For several years, they chaired or co-chaired the program for Readercon. They live in New York City with two partners, one child, one cat, and several thousand books.
people.name: Asher Rose Fox

people.bio: Ava Kelly is a nonbinary speculative writer, dedicated to tales of compassion and trope subversion, stories that give the void a voice. Among their latest works is the illustrated dual-language book of nonbinary fairy tales Alia Terra - Stories from the Dragon Realm. In the daily life, Ava (as Monica Patrascu) is a researcher at the University of Bergen, Norway, working with complex psycho-social and biosystems, artificial intelligence, symptom tracking for neurological diseases. They are currently working with artificial intelligence ethics and decoding death and dying for people with dementia.
people.name: Ava Kelly

people.bio: Dr. Avani Gadani is a computer scientist with delusions of neuroscience at Emory University, where she works on brains, security, and insecurities.  She's a graduate of Viable Paradise 2023, and she has worked as an engineer, systems administrator, lab animal wrangler, and spent a year getting paid to play Barbie Horse Adventures.
people.name: Avani

people.bio: Avery Delany is a small science fictional creature, and a lover of soft futures and obnoxious fictional men. They are a renegade PhD student where they were once doing research on video games, human/non-human relations and futurity. Avery is a member of the Beyond Gender collective, podcaster with Lore Party media, and an ex co-director of the London Science Fiction Research Community
people.name: Avery Delany

people.bio: Avner Shahar Kashtan is a long-time reader, watcher, writer and talker, talking in fan conventions about everything from fantasy epistemology to cyberpunk techno-determinism to Star Wars.
people.name: Avner Shahar Kashtan

people.bio: BE is an independent scholar, a short indie filmmaker, an author, and a freelance editor and proofreader who regularly contracts with Atmosphere Press. They have an MA in Literature with a concentration in science fiction from Texas State University in San Marcos, Texas, USA. BE received an award from The Heinlein Society for their presentation "Questioning Mononormativity: Heinleinian Non-Monogamies" at WorldCon76 in San Jose. They have been published in Queer SciFi: Migrations, The Heinlein Journal, and Exploring the Fantastic:: Genre, Ideology, and Popular Culture (eds. Batzke et al.).
people.name: BE Allatt

people.bio: Dr Barbara Postema is Lecturer in English at the University of Groningen. Her book Narrative Structure in Comics (2013) was published in translation in Brazil in 2018. She has contributed work on narrative theory, wordless comics, and abstract comics to various journals and edited collections. Barbara regularly teaches courses related to science fiction and fantasy.
people.name: Barbara Postema

people.bio: Beatrice manages Foresight Institute's Existential Hope program, encouraging thoughtful discussions on technology’s role in society. She also co-hosts the Existential Hope podcast and oversees its platform, fostering a space for collaborative exploration and ideas. Her work is centred around connecting people and ideas to shape a positive technological future.
people.name: Beatrice Erkers

links.othersocialmedia: @HopeExistential is our smaller Twitter for Xhope stuff only

people.bio: Ben Galley is a British author of dark, epic fantasy who currently lurks in Vancouver, Canada. Since publishing his Emaneska Series in 2010, Ben has released the award-winning Scarlet Star Trilogy and The Heart of Stone, the critically-acclaimed Chasing Graves Trilogy and Scalussen Chronicles, and the new Bloodwood Saga. His goal is to escort you into deep, vibrant worlds that live rent free in your head, alongside plots that cause emotional damage when you get too close to the wrong characters.
people.name: Ben Galley

people.bio: Benjamin C. Kinney is a neuroscientist, SFF writer, and the Assistant Editor of Escape Pod from 2017-2023. His short stories have appeared in Lightspeed, Strange Horizons, Analog, and elsewhere. You can learn more about him and his stories at benjaminckinney.com.
people.name: Benjamin C. Kinney

people.bio: Benjamin Liar is a writer, musician, filmmaker and game designer. He has been writing for most of his life, but The Failures is his first published novel. He has performed his music under many names and in many places and recently published a virtual reality game. His name is clearly a pseudonym, but you still shouldn’t trust anything he says.
people.name: Benjamin Liar

people.bio: Beth Tabler, editor of the quarterly issues of Grimdark Magazine and resident cat-herder/jello-nailer for the Before We Go Blog, lives in Las Vegas, Nevada where she takes long-bubble baths while planning her next move to conquer the fantasy and sci-fi review world. She enjoys whiskey and sticking up for the marginalized with deadly precision. She is on her third SPFBO, and can't wait for more. You will find her with a coffee in one hand and her iPad in the other.
people.name: Beth Tabler

people.bio: Bethany Jacobs is a former college instructor of writing and science fiction. In 2019, she made the leap to the tech industry so that she would have more time to write. When not working on her novels, she is an introvert of predictable habits. She likes reading, cooking, writing fanfiction, and snuggling in bed. She lives in Buffalo, New York, with her wife and her dog. Her debut novel, These Burning Stars, won the 2024 Philip K. Dick Award, and was a finalist for the Locus Award for Best First Novel, the Compton Crook Award for Best First Novel, and the Dragon Award for Best Science Fiction Novel. Her second novel, On Vicious Worlds, releases in October, 2024!
people.name: Bethany Jacobs

people.bio:
I am a freelance dance artist and practitioner based in the UK. I found my love for performance, a deep curiosity and passion for movement and the body’s possibility for expression during my upbringing and dance training in Bern, Switzerland. Dance brought me to London to study contemporary dance and choreography at London Contemporary Dance School. After graduating I worked as a dancer for various dance companies and choreographers in London, most notably with CandoCo Dance Company (from 2004 to 2011), touring, performing and teaching internationally. Other highlights have been co-creating and performing the award winning dance theatre pieces Metamorphosis (2011 & 2013) and The World’s Greatest Show (2014) by choreographer Arthur Pita  and working closely with choreographers Annie Pui Ling Lok and Marc Brew over many years.

 

In 2015 I completed an MA in Dance at the University of Chester and in 2017 co-founded Company Carpi with my beautiful husband, the composer Gary Lloyd. As a company we have created several ACE funded dance and live music pieces, always based on text or pieces of writing. Our latest work - When You Light A Candle You Also Cast A Shadow -  which included a specially commissioned poetry cycle by WorldCon known and loved author Mary Talbot, was nominated for a One Dance UK award in 2022 and toured to 7 different venues around the NW in 2023.

As Company Carpi, Gary and I shared three extracts from our upcoming opera Dotter of Her Father’s Eyes (based on Mary & Brian Talbot’s award winning graphic novel by the same title and with a libretto written by Mary herself).

I am absolutely thrilled to be working with Gary and the brilliant Ken McLeod to bring dance and opera to the stage for this year’s WorldCon, sharing my passion for dance and live performance with such a fantastic, generous and open audience!

For more information please visit https://www.companycarpi.com/

And for more information about the opera please see: https://glasgow2024.org/whats-on/events/opera/
people.name: Bettina Carpi

people.bio: Bill Higgins writes and speaks about spaceflight, astronomy, and the crossroads between science, history, and science fiction. He has been part of Chicago fandom for more than four decades.  As a radiation safety physicist at Fermilab, he is involved with the transport of high-energy particle beams. He's a volunteer speaker in NASA’s Solar System Ambassadors outreach program. Bill also plays the baritone ukulele, not skillfully, but with enthusiasm.
people.name: Bill Higgins

people.bio: My professional career spans 6 years of USAF computer programming plus 33 years as an intelligence analyst, systems engineer, and program analyst. I’m a vocal Space Exploitation Advocate, read hard-SF whenever I have time, give blood six times a year (222 pints & counting!), run & drink (simultaneously!) with Hash House Harrier groups, and judge at several Science Fairs every year. At a Convention, you can spot me relaxing in my Space-kilt or on science-oriented panels. I’m also an avid life-long Wargamer and the US Army published my entry in their “Mad Scientist Science Fiction Writing Contest 2019.” https://smallwarsjournal.com/jrnl/art/angry-engineer https://madsciblog.tradoc.army.mil/141-the-otso-incident-with-donovia-in-2030/?doing_wp_cron=1599056351.4567658901214599609375
people.name: Bob Hranek

people.bio:
Bon started reading and watching science fiction and fantasy when she was very young with her dad (an old school Star Trek fan), and never stopped. When she went to university, it opened her eyes and being a sci-fi nerd wasn't something that you had to hide. She found her people! Bon has been involved in many of Ireland's RPG gaming conventions and can often be found running or playing games of Cyberpunk. 

Now, Bon works in the field of clinical trials and can no longer watch zombie movies without shouting at the screen.
people.name: Bon

people.bio: Bradford Lyau is a historian by training and once taught at several universities in California and Europe.  He is an entrepreneur and also a political activist/consultant.  He has published academic articles on American, British, European, and Chinese science fiction.  He was an invited participant for the George Orwell Conference held in London (1984), the Utopian Conference held in Yverdon-les-Bain, Switzerland (1991), and other conferences.  His book, The Anticipation Novelists of 1950s French Science Fiction:  Stepchildren of Voltaire, received very positive reviews from leading academic SF journals and is a listed reference under the FRANCE entry in the Science Fiction Encyclopedia.
people.name: Bradford Lyau

people.bio: Breaking Light Productions is a local theater and film company based in Boston, MA.
people.name: Breaking Light Productions

people.bio: Brenda Noiseux is community builder, artist, gamer, convention organizer, and all around geek. Former co-host of the New Books in Science Fiction podcast and writer for Women Write about Comics. Current Product Maven at the indie tabletop game studio, Almost a Game.
people.name: Brenda Noiseux

people.bio: Brenda W. Clough is the first female Asian-American SF writer, first appearing in print in 1984. Her latest work is a novelette, ‘Clio’s Scroll’, which appeared in Clarkesworld in July 2023. A historical novel A Door In His Head won the 2023 Diverse Voices Award. Her novella ‘May Be Some Time’ was a finalist for both the Hugo and the Nebula awards and became the novel Revise the World. Marian Halcombe, a series of eleven neo-Victorian thrillers appeared in 2021.  Her complete bibliography is up on her web page, brendaclough.net
people.name: Brenda W. Clough

people.bio: Brian is a writer of short fiction and a member of the Glasgow Science Fiction Writer's Circle. He is also a massive Who nerd who lives in a field and will gladly show you his cow pictures.
people.name: Brian M. Milton

people.bio: Bryce Moore is the author of YA thrillers and fantasy. His latest book, A Family of Killers, was just released in the United States. When he's not writing, he's a library director in western Maine.
people.name: Bryce Moore

people.bio:
C. L. Polk (they/them) wrote the Hugo-nominated Kingston Cycle, including the World Fantasy Award winning Witchmark, The Midnight Bargain, and the Nebula-winning Even Though I Knew The End. 
Before writing fantasy novels, they worked as a film extra, a costermonger, and also identified lepidoptera by eye. Mx. Polk lives in Calgary, on the territories of the Blackfoot Confederacy, the Tsuut’ina, the Îyâxe Nakoda Nations, and the Métis Nation (Region 3).
Mx. Polk is represented by Caitlin McDonald of the Donald Maass Literary Agency.
people.name: C. L. Polk

people.bio:
Chris Winspear is an Australian author and narrative designer. Winner of the Grand Prize in the Writers of the Future Contest 2020, he is currently developing Frostpunk 2 at 11-bit Studios, in Warsaw, Poland. He is avid traveller, having lived on five of the world’s continents and visited more countries than he can count.  
His saucy 1001-nights-inspired fantasy, Nights Under The Sun, was published in 2023. His spec-fic stories have also appeared in Teleport Magazine and the anthologies Short and Twisted and Empty Sky. He has a Master’s of Creative Writing from UTS, Sydney. His literary short stories “The Market” and “No More Piano Lessons” earned awards from the Peter Cowan Writer Centre and Rhonda Jankovic Literary Awards, and his novel manuscript The Lightreaders won the Writing NSW Varuna Fellowship.
cwinspear.com
people.name: C. Winspear

people.bio: C.L. is a London-based writer and editor. His fantasy and horror fiction can be found in the queer flash collections "Innovation" and "Ink", and in the anthology “The Crawling Moon” (Neon Hemlock, 2024). He is also Editor of the LGBTQIA+ anthology “I Want That Twink Obliterated!” (Bona Books, 2024). When not writing, he can be found walking the corridors of Whitehall as a professional nerd. The rest of the time he spends being agonisingly homosexual.
people.name: C.L. McCartney

people.bio:
CE Murphy began writing around age six, when she submitted three poems to a school publication. The teacher producing the magazine selected (inevitably) the one she thought was by far the worst, but also told her–a six year old kid–to keep writing, which she has. She has also held the usual grab-bag of jobs usually seen in an authorial biography, including public library volunteer (at ages 9 and 10; it’s clear she was doomed to a career involving books), archival assistant, cannery worker, and web designer. Writing books is better.

She was born and raised in Alaska, and now lives with her family in her ancestral homeland of Ireland.
people.name: CE (Catie) Murphy

people.bio: CL Hellisen is a South African writer living in Scotland. Their stories and poems have appeared in The Magazine of Science Fiction and Fantasy, Tor.com, Apex, Shimmer, Daily Science Fiction, Shoreline of Infinity and others. Their novel Cast Long Shadows was shortlisted for the British Fantasy Award in 2023.
people.name: CL Hellisen

people.bio:
I am a sci-fi writer, publisher at Beyond Cataclysm, host of the What Is Roleplay & This Book I Read... podcasts, and also work for Tabletop Gaming Magazine.

I also enjoy eating trifle, rather too much.

Find me on socials as @cmlowryauthor, or my personal site at allaboutchris.org
people.name: CM Lowry

people.bio: Caitlin Rozakis has had too many careers, including mechanical engineering (left after the murderous robot incident), finance (amortizing tequila receivables is not as fun as drinking tequila), and the American Museum of Natural History (who knew emus had birth certificates?). Now she specializes in tech marketing and lives in Jersey City with her husband and son. Her short fiction has been featured in multiple anthologies and publications including Cast of Wonders, Aurealis, Daily Science Fiction, Weirdbook, and Andromeda Spaceways Inflight Magazine. She was nominated for a Pushcart Prize and won LUMINA’s 2018 Speculative Fiction contest. The New York Times bestselling Dreadful is her first novel.
people.name: Caitlin Rozakis

people.bio: Cameron Bolinger is a trans woman writer represented by the Bond Literary Agency. Professionally, she works as a Unity game developer with a focus on educational games and apps. Her projects include work for major clients such as NASA and IBM, as well as original IPs developed by the studio she co-founded. Her most recent work has focused on game based-learning for autistic individuals. Cameron writes both long and short-form science fiction with her co-writer, Erica, and currently resides in Budapest with her freakishly muscular cat.
people.name: Cameron Bolinger

people.bio: Cameron Johnston is a Scottish writer of fantasy and lives in the city of Glasgow. He is a student of Historical European Martial Arts, a member of the Glasgow Science Fiction Writers' Circle, and enjoys exploring ancient sites and camping out under the stars.
people.name: Cameron Johnston

people.bio: Maybe not "all" trades, but Carl Fink is a Jack of several. (My middle name is "Jack".) I've been a retail clerk and store manager, museum guide, science teacher, business trainer, software developer, and freelance tech journalist. That's in addition to working at various conventions, including being the Chair of two LI-CONs on Long Island, where I reside. I was briefly DDH Program at Worldcon 76--no, the other DDH, not Gary. I was on the Winnipeg Worldcon Bid Committee as well. I read a lot, mostly novels.
people.name: Carl Fink

people.bio:
Caroline Hardaker is a novelist, poet, and librettist who mainly writes dark tales exploring everything speculative, from folklore to future worlds. 

Her novels have featured in The Washington Post (which listed her debut novel - Composite Creatures - as one of the top science fiction reads of 2021), The Guardian, and New Scientist. Last year, her work was also shortlisted for a Golden Tentacle Award (The Kitschies).

Her second novel – Mothtown – features original illustrations by Chris Riddell and was published by Angry Robot in November 2023.

Her poetry has been published worldwide, most recently in Macmillan anthologies 'Gods and Monsters' and 'We Will Soar', and her two collections are available from Valley Press.
people.name: Caroline Hardaker

people.bio: Caroline Mersey cosplays as a grown-up. When not attending or running book events, or talking about books, she binges on the latest box set while making beautiful things.
people.name: Caroline Mersey

people.bio: Caroline found SF fandom via a bookshop and a Worldcon in 1979 and never stopped. Took up running cons with BECCON '83. Most recently Chair of the 2023 Eastercon, Conversation, and on the staff of this Worldcon. Trustee and officer of the Science Fiction Foundation for over 20 years. Guest of Honour at Dysprosium, the 2015 Eastercon, and Swecon in 2016. Writes for APAs and fanzines, hangs out at Porcupine Books, and is interested in gardens, history and the happening world.
people.name: Caroline Mullan

people.bio: Carrie Cooper, Assistant Director of the Ray Bradbury Center, is an editor, writer, podcast producer, artist, and musician. From these creative spaces she weaves intricate narratives that push the boundaries of imagination. With a bachelor's degree in Fine Art and a current pursuit of her PhD in American Studies, she explores the intersections of arts and social justice. Carrie's presentations at conventions like Chicon8 and Indy Comic Con showcase her expertise in how creative expression can catalyze transformative change. Her curiosity, passion for storytelling, and commitment to advocacy shine through her diverse skill set, making her a vital voice.
people.name: Carrie Cooper

people.bio: Carrie Vaughn's work includes the Philip K. Dick Award winning novel Bannerless, the New York Times Bestselling Kitty Norville urban fantasy series, over twenty novels and upwards of 100 short stories, two of which have been finalists for the Hugo Award. Her next novel, The Naturalist Society, is about 19th century ornithologists, awkward love triangles, and the magic of binomial nomenclature. An Air Force brat, she survived her nomadic childhood and managed to put down roots in Boulder, Colorado.
people.name: Carrie Vaughn

people.bio: Cass Morris lives her life at the intersection of storytelling, performance, and education as a writer and editor of novels, short fiction, and immersive experiences. Her novels, The Aven Cycle, are Roman-flavored historical fantasy. She is also one-third of the team behind the four-time Hugo Award Finalist podcast Worldbuilding for Masochists. Cass works as Story Editor at Mythik Camps, providing writing and developmental editing for mythology-themed interactive theatrical experiences, as well as other programming and media projects. Previously, she worked in the education department at the American Shakespeare Center in Staunton, VA. She holds a Master of Letters in Shakespeare studies from Mary Baldwin University and a BA in English and History from the College of William and Mary.
people.name: Cass Morris

people.bio: Cassidy Cobbs is a molecular biologist working on genomics technologies and a contributor of biological considerations to interstellar research groups such as I4IS in the UK and StellarCorp in the US. They live New York City with an exceedingly dumb pit bull named Mando.
people.name: Cassidy Cobbs

people.bio: A multidisciplinary artist and multimedia storyteller, Cat is Mother Brain of Omniverse and award-winning showrunner of The Call of Cthulhu Mystery Program, a historical fiction horror-comedy audio drama and the sci-fi adventure series, “MOTHER,” She Wrote. Her career in podcasting and journalism spans over a decade. She’s founder and host of the formative games and hobbies podcast, Nerdy Show, a pioneer in improvisational audio drama podcasts, and a voice actor on projects such as Moonbase Theta, Out and Midnight Burger. Her work is devoted to uplifting and transformative stories that go to strange places and ask big questions.
people.name: Cat Blackard

people.bio: Catherine Asaro has authored thirty+ books in sf and fantasy. A two-time winner of the Nebula®, she also has multiple Hugo nominations. Her most recent book, The Down Deep, comes out in summer 2024. Her doctorate is in chemical physics from Harvard, and she directed the Chesapeake Math Program for decades. She has appeared as a speaker at numerous institutions, including Harvard and the US Naval Academy, and as the GoH at cons across the US and abroad, most recently COSine in Colorado. She served two terms as president of SFWA and is also a vocalist and dancer.
people.name: Catherine Asaro

people.bio:
Professor Catherine Heymans (she/her), the Astronomer Royal for Scotland, will be appearing online as a Special Guest at this year’s Worldcon. As Professor of Observational Cosmology at the University of Edinburgh and Director of the GCCL Institute at the Ruhr University Bochum, Germany, Catherine specialises in observing the dark side of our Universe using deep sky observations to test whether we need to go beyond Einstein with our current theory of gravity. 

Catherine is currently part of a large international team preparing for first light at the Vera Rubin Observatory in Chile. As one of the largest telescopes in the world, Rubin will  create the first movie of our Universe, looking for anything that moves in order to locate potential killer asteroids that could one day obliterate planet Earth!  Catherine is certainly hoping that we won’t find any evidence for that future doomsday scenario, with her true passion lying in the by-product of this search: the deepest widest view of the cosmos, the ultimate data set to unveil the origin of the mysterious dark energy that permeates our Universe.
people.name: Catherine Heymans

people.bio: Catherine Lundoff is a Minneapolis-based award-winning writer, editor and publisher. Her books include the dark fantasy novels Silver Moon and Blood Moon and the single author collections Out of This World: Queer Speculative Fiction Stories and Unfinished Business: Tales of the Dark Fantastic. She is also the editor of the fantastical pirate anthology Scourge of the Seas of Time (and Space). In addition, she is the publisher at Queen of Swords Press, a small press specializing in tales from out of this world. www.CatherineLundoff.net
people.name: Catherine Lundoff

people.bio: Catherine (Cie) Sangster is a sociolinguist and phonetician who works as Head of Pronunciations for Oxford Languages, including the Oxford English Dictionary. Before moving into lexicography, she worked in the BBC Pronunciation Unit. Her research interests include language and gender/sexuality, accents and dialects, Latin, Germanic languages, the phonology of conlangs, and the use and reception of linguistic difference in popular culture. Her doctoral study was about phonetic variation among speakers of Liverpool English. She ran Geek Dictionary Corner at Nine Worlds 2014 - 2018 (see https://www.oed.com/discover/looking-back-at-geek-dictionary-corner).
people.name: Catherine Sangster

people.bio:
(mutters something about not planning to be on any programme items, but not wanting to let her fellow Pokémon Go players down...)

Catherine is a conrunner and technical writer from Wales, who spent many years living in Northern Ireland and working on Irish conventions. She's currently Programme Deputy Division Head so if you are a programme participant for Glasgow 2024, you've probably had an email from her at least once. In her limited free time, she enjoys cold water swimming, cat wrangling, and more conrunning.
people.name: Catherine Sharp

people.bio: Catriona Silvey was born in Glasgow and grew up in Scotland and England. After collecting an unreasonable number of degrees from various universities in the UK and the US, she moved to Edinburgh where she lives with her husband and children. She is the author of Meet Me in Another Life (2021) and the upcoming time-travel romantic comedy Love and Other Paradoxes.
people.name: Catriona Silvey

people.bio: Celeste Tyler is an author of the weird, wild, and wonderful. Her stories have (literally) taken her across the Sahara on the back of a camel, sky high on aerial silks, and aboard a replica 18th-century tall ship. She is a graduate of the 2019 Odyssey Writing Workshop, and you can find her fiction in Fantasy Magazine, Beneath Ceaseless Skies, and Podcastle. She currently resides in Colorado with her 10/10 husband, three marvelous children, a warrior-goddess cat named Athena, and a bearded dragon that goes by Divine Beast Vah Rudania.
people.name: Celeste C. Tyler

people.bio:
I am a retired Science Fiction/Fantasy & Marvel Comics fan based in London, United Kingdom and loved those genres since I was old enough to read. Have attended a good selection of conventions since the 1987 Worldcon in Brighton. I've also loved the Art that comes alongside and have found these conventions great places to meet the genre Artists. 🎨

These days I'm consuming my genre content mostly via films 🎬 & tv 🖥and love talking about. Whether on entertaining panels or at the Fan Bar. 🍻 

I also keep up with Spaceflight and Astronomy news so have liked that there is a strong Science & Technology stream at major conventions.🚀

I'm am a photography fan and am interested in most subject matters. These days I'm doing most of my shots on a smartphone. I've run a Smartphone photography workshop programme item at previous conventions and as the mobile tech improves year on year, its definitely worth revisiting and helps fans get the best out of capturing their own personal convention memories.📱
people.name: Chad Dixon

people.bio: Charlie Jane Anders is the author of The Prodigal Mother, due in 2025. She also wrote Never Say You Can't Survive, a book about using creative writing to get through hard times, and a short story collection, Even Greater Mistakes. Her young adult Unstoppable trilogy won two Locus Awards. She co-hosts the podcast Our Opinions Are Correct.
people.name: Charlie Jane Anders

people.bio:
Charles Stross, 59, is a full-time science fiction writer and resident of Edinburgh, Scotland. The author of seven Hugo-nominated novels and winner of three Hugo awards for best novella, Stross's works have been translated into over twelve languages. His next novel, "A Conventional Boy" is due out from Tor.com and Orbit in January 2025; His next novel, "The Regicide Report", is due out in June 2025.

Both novels are part of the Laundry Files series, which is shortlisted for the Hugo award for best series in 2024.

Like many writers, Stross has had a variety of careers, occupations, and job-shaped-catastrophes in the past, from pharmacist (he quit after the second police stake-out) to first code monkey on the team of a successful dot-com startup (with brilliant timing he tried to change employer just as the bubble burst). Along the way he collected degrees in Pharmacy and Computer Science, making him the world's first officially qualified cyberpunk writer (just as cyberpunk died).
people.name: Charlie Stross

people.bio: Chelsea Mueller is a fantasy and horror author. Her YA slasher Prom House was a 2022 YALSA Pick for Reluctant Readers. Her short fiction was most recently published in The Sunday Morning Transport. She also writes speculative thrillers as Chelsea Conradt. Find her online at ChelseaMueller.com
people.name: Chelsea Mueller

people.bio: Cheryl Morgan is a writer, editor, and publisher. She is the winner of four Hugo Awards and is the owner of Wizard's Tower Press. Her non-fiction has appeared in a variety of venues including Locus, the SFWA Bulletin, the Science Fiction Encyclopaedia, Vector and Strange Horizons. Her fiction has appeared in a number of small press magazines and anthologies. Cheryl was a Guest of Honour at the 2012 Eurocon in Zagreb and the 2019 Finncon in Jyväskylä. She was a keynote speaker at the Worlding SF academic conference at the University of Graz in 2018, and at When It Changed, an online conference on feminist science fiction organised by the University of Glasgow in December 2022.
people.name: Cheryl Morgan

people.bio: Chloe Smith writes science fiction and fantasy stories. Her short fiction has appeared in Three-Lobed Burning Eye, Daily Science Fiction, Bourbon Penn, and elsewhere, and her debut novella, Virgin Land, came out from Luna Press Publishing in 2023. When not writing, she works with middle-school students, which is never boring. She taught English and history for over a decade, and recently completed a masters' degree in library science, before transitioning to work as her school's teacher librarian. She has also worked as a proofreader, including stints for Fantasy and Locus Magazines. She was born and raised in the San Francisco Bay Area, and lived in Texas and Washington states, New York City, and rural France before coming back to California.
people.name: Chloe Smith

people.bio: Artist and designer.
people.name: Chris Baker (Fangorn)

people.bio: Chris Balliet is a speculative fiction writer who lives in Philadelphia with his wife and daughter, traversing the city in search of playgrounds and good coffee. He is a graduate of Taos Toolbox in 2023 and has been published in StarShipSofa. You can find him on Threads/Instagram @chrisballietwrites, Twitter @chrisballiet or his website chrisballiet.com.
people.name: Chris Balliet

people.bio: Chris Garcia is a fanzine editor, curator, historian, true crime writer, film festival programmer, and archivist from Boulder Creek, California. He's won a couple of Hugos for his fanzine work on The Drink Tank and Journey Planet. He lives in the mountains with his darling wife, and two miniature fans-in-training.
people.name: Chris Garcia

people.bio: Chris Sugden is one of the authors of High Vaultage (Gollancz 2024) and the audio drama podcast Victoriocity.
people.name: Chris Sugden

people.bio: Chris Wooding is the author of 26 books for both adults and children, including the Tales of the Ketty Jay and Darkwater Legacy series. He also writes for videogames, and has worked on the Assassin's Creed, Avatar and Star Wars franchises.
people.name: Chris Wooding

people.bio: Mainly because she doesn’t know what she wants to do when she grows up, Christianne has followed an interdisciplinary route through science during her career.
