She is a self-confessed space geek but has a wide range of interests including building resilience to the effects of climate change and loss of biodiversity; how life originally developed on Earth and what that tells us about the potential for life in the wider cosmos. Oh, and quantum biology. A big fan of science fiction, Christianne's favourites include everything Star Trek, The Expanse (books), Expeditionary Force and The Lost Fleet.
people.name: Christianne Wakeham

people.bio: Christina Orlando is the Senior Books Editor for Tor.com, where they get to be a book nerd all day. As a freelance writer, their work has appeared Electric Literature, Catapult, gal-dem, THEM, Adroit Journal, and Book Riot. Christina currently resides in Brooklyn, NY with their queer found family.  Twitter: @cxorlando
people.name: Christina Orlando

people.bio: Dr. Christine Doyle is a physician trained in anesthesiology and critical care, who practices in Silicon Valley.  She has been active in fandom for over 2 decades, mostly working on program and costuming for local and regional conventions as well as multiple Worldcons. She is a lifelong computer geek and is currently completing her coursework for a Masters in Biomedical Informatics.
people.name: Christine A Doyle

people.bio: Christine Amsden is the author of nine award-winning fantasy and science fiction novels, including the Cassie Scot Series. In addition to writing, she is a freelance editor and political activist. In her free time, she enjoys role playing, board games, and a good cup of tea. She lives in the Kansas City area with her husband and two kids.
people.name: Christine Amsden

people.bio:
Dr Christine Davidson CChem FRSC FHEA is an academic at the University of Strathclyde with more than 30 years' research experience in analytical chemistry and environmental chemistry. She has published over 120 papers in peer-reviewed scientific literature; supervised over 40 (mainly international) PhD students to succesful completion of studies; and worked extensively with industry on Knowledge Transfer Partnerships.

In 2007 she was one of the co-founders of Satellite, Scotland's (roughly) biennial fan-run SF convention, the by-line of which is Science Fiction, Science Fact, Science Fun. Christine has organised the programme for all Satellite conventions to date, including Satellite 4, Eastercon 2014. She is currently co-Area Head for the Science & Technology Programme track at Glasgow 2024.
people.name: Christine Davidson

people.bio: Christine Taylor-Butler has published close to one hundred books for children, including her speculative series The Lost Tribes series (Move Books) and three titles in Chelsea Clinton’s Save The …(Animals) series (Penguin Random House). In addition, she’s written a number of articles including, "When Failure Is Not An Option" an essay on the need for diversity in STEM literature (The Horn Book November/December 2021). Christine currently serves as an MLK Visiting Scholar at MIT.
people.name: Christine Taylor-Butler

people.bio: Christopher Buehlman is a native Floridian male of partial Mediterranean descent, easily identifiable by his sun-damaged skin and a short dorsal mane which stands up when he is agitated. He is the author of The Blacktongue Thief, The Daughters’ War, and Between Two Fires. If you encounter him away from his habitat, give him good bourbon and he will talk about medieval history, cats, or horror films until you walk away.
people.name: Christopher Buehlman

people.bio: Christopher Kastensmidt is an American-born author living in Brazil since 2001. One of the most diverse media authors of his generation, his productions have reached tens of millions and include books, comics, video games, short stories, tabletop RPGs, animated series and a full-length feature movie. Christopher's work has earned him recognition for a dozen different awards, including a Nebula nomination in 2010 and an ENnie win in 2019. Some of his better known works include The Elephant and Macaw Banner and Starlit Adventures. He currently works with games in education at Synthesis Inc. and is the owner of Time Galleon Visual Novels.
people.name: Christopher Kastensmidt

people.bio: Claire Brialey has been enjoying science fiction since she was a child and publishing fanzines and running conventions since she was a teenager, all of which started in a previous century; this might be why she's interested in fan history. She has been a judge for the Arthur C Clarke Award and the Rotsler Award, administered the BSFA awards and the FAAn awards, and won a plethora of awards too, mostly for fanzines. She undertakes determined admin for a range of other fannish projects, including fan funds, and is unable to function without coffee, books, and Mark Plummer.
people.name: Claire Brialey

people.bio: Claire E. Jones (she/her) is a queer fantasy romance author and small publisher who is committed to changing the world for the better through inclusive stories and practices. As an established small business and entrepreneurship expert of 20 years, she has founded and launched four of her own businesses and now mentors other creatives, visionaries, and innovators in achieving their goals in less time with less stress. She shares a range of diverse novels, planners, and journals with the world from Seattle WA, where she lives with her precious pup, Karma.
people.name: Claire E. Jones

people.bio:
I am an author of speculative fiction for children, young adults and adults. My work is feminist in focus and interested in exploring what women do when faced with impossible choices. I began a career in history and archaeology, but realized I like learning things better than I like knowing them, so now I take inspiration from various historical events and weave them into my work. I live in Denmark with one husband, one child and one cat.

I am represented by Kurestin Armada of Root Literary.
people.name: Claire Eliza Bartlett

people.bio: I am an editor with Gollancz, the oldest dedicated SFF publisher in the UK. I work with SF, Fantasy and Horror, looking for diverse voices across the front and backlist. I enjoy a wide range of media, and seek stories that hit the dopamine centres of my brain just right. In general I prefer the happier and the hopeful over the dark and grim - even horror can have a happy ending!
people.name: Claire Ormsby-Potter

people.bio: Clara lives in Scotland in a creaky old building with pipes for gas lighting still lurking under her floorboards. She is an experimental linguist by profession, and calligrapher and Islamic geometric artist by vocation. She reads All The Books and reviews them for Nerds of a Feather. During figure skating season she does blather on a bit about figure skating.
people.name: Clara Cohen

people.bio: Clara Ward lives in Silicon Valley, California on the border between reality and speculative fiction. Their latest novel, Be the Sea, features a near-future ocean voyage, chosen family, and sea creature perspectives, while delving into our oceans, our selves, and how all futures intertwine. Their short fiction has appeared in Strange Horizons, Decoded Pride, and is upcoming in The Neurodiversiverse. When not using words to teach or tell stories, Clara uses wood, fiber, and glass to make practical or completely impractical objects. More of their words along with crafted creations can be found at: https://clarawardauthor.wordpress.com
people.name: Clara Ward

people.bio: Born and raised in Cameroon, Clementine E Burnley now lives and works between Scotland and Germany. The themes of her work are (re)migration, diasporic kinship, intergenrational trauma, and collective resilience.  Her art practice has evolved through poetry, audio-visual pieces, stage performance, fiction and essay forms. She loves to curate community spaces and relationships.
people.name: Clementine E Burnley

people.bio: Colin is James Watt Chair, Professor Engineering Science at the University of Glasgow. He leads a busy research group developing a range of emerging space technologies; these range from centimetre-scale femto-spacecraft to in-space manufacturing of large space structures, with research on asteroid resources and energy from space. The group’s programme of research is currently supported by the Royal Academy of Engineering and the European Research Council. Aside from his research activities, Colin has served on the Scottish Science Advisory Council and served as Chair of the UK Space Agency’s Space Technology Advisory Committee.
people.name: Colin McInnes

people.bio: Constance Fay is the author of the Uncharted Hearts series which includes CALAMITY and FIASCO. She has a background in medical device R&D and lives in Colorado with a cat who edits all her work first.
people.name: Constance Fay

people.bio:
Cora Buhlert was born and bred in Bremen, North Germany, where she still lives today – after time spent in London, Singapore, Rotterdam and Mississippi. Cora holds an MA degree in English from the University of Bremen.

Cora has been a science fiction fan for as long as she can remember and blogs about SFF both at her own site and Galactic Journey. Cora has a special interest in the past of our genre and likes to review and discuss SFF dating from the 1920s to 1960s. Cora Cora is the winner of the 2022 Hugo Award for Best Fan Writer and the 2021 Space Cowboy Award.

Cora has been writing, since she was a teenager, and has published stories, articles and poetry in various international magazines. Though she writes in various genres, science fiction and fantasy will always be her first love. When Cora is not writing, she works as a translator and teacher.
people.name: Cora Buhlert

people.bio: Courtney Floyd grew up in New Mexico, where she learned to write between tarantula turf wars and apocalyptic dust storms. She currently lives at the bottom of a haunted mountain in the woods of Vermont with her partner and pets. Her debut fantasy novel, Higher Magic, will be published by Mira in Fall 2025. Courtney's short fiction can be found in publications including Small Wonders, Fireside Magazine,  and Wizards in Space. Her audio drama, The Way We Haunt Now, is available on all major podcast platforms. Find her online at courtney-floyd.com.
people.name: Courtney Floyd

people.bio: Science fiction writer, producer, researcher, and professor. Doctor in Communication. Editor and director of the Hispano-American digital science fiction magazine "Teoría Ómicron" and editor of the science fiction imprint "Omicron Books". He has published the books "Between Science Fiction and Fantasy"; "Dark Nights, Big Mouths"; "Mission Antares"; "Twelve Hours"; "The Return of the Light"; "Underbreak"; "Dead Time"; "The Unproductive Ones"; and "The Instinct of Light". He has won several literary awards. He has written, directed, and produced various documentaries and documentary series. His papers on science fiction have been published in scientific journals.
people.name: Cristián Londoño Proaño

people.bio: Cy Villyard (she/her) is a member of the SCBWI and has studied eastern and western martial arts. As a two-time national bronze medalist in women's saber for the United States Fencing Association, she has trained a stunt double for the Netflix series The Originals. Her poetry has appeared in print in The Weekly Alibi in her hometown of Albuquerque, New Mexico, and The Bad Bitch Adult Coloring Book is available on Amazon.
people.name: Cynthia Villyard

people.bio: D is a Glasgow-based bookseller with a major bookselling chain, responsible for their shop's events programme. They are also an avid reader, a lapsed Classicist, and have been involved in Glasgow 2024 in various capacities and areas for some years now, so are very excited to see it come to fruition!
people.name: D Franklin

people.bio: D.A Lascelles is a clinical scientist turned teacher of healthcare who dabbles in photography and occasionally even finds time to write something.
people.name: D,A Lascelles

people.bio: D. H. Timpko is the author of the Firma Twins adventures, a series of science fantasy novels for kids. As Alexis Dupree, she wrote "Knee Replacement Advice, Checklists, and Journal" and "Managing Major Chronic Diseases: Advice from a Patient."
people.name: D. H. Timpko

people.bio: D. Wes Rist is an international human rights lawyer with a specializtion in prevening genocide and mass atrocities.  He has worked with non-profit and non-governmental organizations around the world, conducted trainings for international lawyers and atrocity prevention experts, and advised governments and international organizations. He also works on the intersection of space law and policy and human rights and ethics, serving as a cofounding member of Project Lodestar. Wes previously worked at the American Society of International Law and the Prevention and Protection Working Group, and was a law professor at the University of Pittsburgh School of Law. He is currently an Atrocities Prevention Policy Advisor in the Bureau of Conflict & Stabilization Operations at the U.S. Department of State. Wes holds a JD and an LL.M. (with distinction) in International Human Rights Law.
people.name: D. Wes Rist

people.bio:
D.K. McCUTCHEN’s Speculative Fiction trilogy includes: JELLYFISH DREAMING, a Leapfrog Press Global Fiction Prize winner; ELECTRIC ICE forthcoming (2024) winner of a Speculative Literature Foundation grant; & PLASTIC EATERS forthcoming (2025). WHALE ROAD, creative nonfiction about sailing with whale researchers through the South Pacific was a Kiriyama Prize Notable Book and Pushcart Nominee, published in NZ & the UK with an update by JackLeg Press, US (2023). D.K. teaches writing for College of Natural Sciences, University of Massachusetts Amherst, and is an Associate Director of the Junior Year Writing Program.   
A streamlined website is at: https://dkmccutchen.ag-sites.net/index.htm
people.name: D.K. McCutchen

people.bio: Dan Coxon is an award-winning editor and writer. His non-fiction anthology Writing the Uncanny (co-edited with Richard V. Hirst) won the British Fantasy Award for Best Non-Fiction 2022, while his short story collection Only the Broken Remain (Black Shuck Books) was shortlisted for two British Fantasy Awards in 2021 (Best Collection, Best Newcomer). In 2018 his anthology This Dreaming Isle was a finalist for the Shirley Jackson Awards and the British Fantasy Awards. His latest non-fiction book, Writing the Future, was published by Dead Ink Books in September 2023.
people.name: Dan Coxon

people.bio: Dan Ritter is the managing editor for First Fandom Experience, a collaborative publishing project whose aim is to honor, preserve, and bring to life the history and impact of science fiction fandom.
people.name: Dan Ritter

people.bio:
Dr. Dana Little is an Assistant Professor of Writing and Rhetoric at the University of Virginia, where she teaches undergraduate courses in digital writing, cultural criticism, and critical media studies. 

Her research focuses on approaching artificial intelligence as a human behavioral barometer. She originated the social media genre of “factions,” which her forthcoming book for Kendall Hunt Publishing, Factional Futures: Understanding the Social Media Genre of Factions, examines in detail. 

The-Channel-Show podcast features her digital twin persona, Dr. Wu—an AI mystic who can channel any person, place, or thing. T-C-S was recently added to the WTJU podcast collective, and they will air her mini-series Buchanan: An American Sequel later this year.
people.name: Dana L. Little

people.bio:
Hungarian author Daniel Makk (writing as Daniel McDaniel) achieved his dream of becoming a writer after years of working in finance. Daniel always had a love for fantasy and sci-fi but was often unable to obtain the works of his favorite authors in his mother tongue.

​

Twelve years ago, Daniel began to improve his English on his own in order to consume more works from his favorite authors, first of all Brandon Sanderson.

​

The language opened new doors, and Daniel saw an opportunity to follow his true passion: writing. With the growth of self-published authors, Daniel realized that there were new ways of achieving success.

​

Despite the steep climb he faced as a self-taught English learner, Daniel is now a published author with his debut Luminocity - Grieving Gold, the first in his Luminocity series.

​

Daniel lives with his fantastic wife—and dedicated beta reader—who shares his passion for fantasy. Their young son also shows a great love for books and stories, and Daniel proudly hopes that one day he can share his own work with him
people.name: Daniel McDaniel

people.bio: I am an academic/researcher at the Department of Physics, University of Stratclyde, Glasgow, Scotland. My main areas of interest are the development of Space Quantum Technologies (particularly satellite quantum communication and the space quantum internet), quantum information theory, and fundamental physics.
people.name: Daniel Oi

people.bio: Darcie Little Badger is a Lipan Apache writer with a PhD in oceanography. Her critically acclaimed debut novel, Elatsoe, was featured in Time Magazine as one of the best 100 fantasy books of all time. Elatsoe also won the Locus award for Best First Novel and is a Nebula, Ignyte, and Lodestar finalist. Her second fantasy novel, A Snake Falls to Earth, received a Nebula Award, an Ignyte Award, and a Newbery Honor and is on the National Book Awards longlist. Her third book, Sheine Lende, is coming April 2024.
people.name: Darcie Little Badger

people.bio:
Darlene Marshall is an award-winning author of historical romance featuring pirates, privateers, smugglers, and the occasional possum. She loves working at a job where business attire is shorts and a shirt festooned with pink flamingos and palm trees.

Marshall has worked as a broadcast and print journalist, news anchor, radio station owner, obituary writer, and a few other odd jobs. She became a novelist because there were fake people in her head having adventures, so it was either write it down or check into therapy. She’s never been a pirate, but the day is not yet over.

Her books have been published in English, German, French, and Estonian. She’s Section Leader of Erotic Writing at the LitForum.com and Membership Director of Regency Fiction Writers, for writers of all fiction Regency related: Time-travel, fantasy, historical, romance, horror, mystery.

While writing romance is her dayjob, her hobby is attending science fiction conventions and Marshall can usually be found on panels at Boskone (North East Regional US convention in February) and the World Science Fiction Convention discussing writing romance and researching history. 

Represented by Barbara Collins Rosenberg of The Rosenberg Group.
people.name: Darlene Marshall

people.bio: Daryl Gregory’s novels and short stories have been translated into a dozen languages and have won multiple awards, including the World Fantasy and Shirley Jackson awards, and have been nominated for the Hugo, Nebula, Edgar, Locus, Lambda, and Sturgeon awards. His latest books are the novel Revelator and the novella The Album of Dr. Moreau. His eight other books include Spoonbenders, We Are All Completely Fine, Afterparty, the Crawford-Award-winning novel Pandemonium, and the collection Unpossible and Other Stories. He's written for TV and and is a regular instructor at the Viable Paradise Writing Workshop.
people.name: Daryl Gregory

people.bio: Dave Klecha is, among other things, a science fiction and fantasy writer from Detroit, Michigan.
people.name: Dave Klecha

people.bio: David Baillie is a Scottish writer and artist. As well as various strips for 2000 AD and Judge Dredd Megazine, he also created and wrote the Glasgow-set series Red Thorn for Vertigo/DC. He lives in London with his darling wife, mischievous daughter and a multitude of unforgiving deadlines.
people.name: David Baillie

people.bio:
David Cartwright was born in 1981, and raised in a Golden Age of Saturday morning cartoons. From that time and forever more he has been an avid watcher and reader of Science-Fiction and Fantasy, encompassing the likes of The Hitchhikers Guide to the Galaxy, The Walking Dead and the works of J.R.R. Tolkien and Neil Gaiman.
David has been a Jack of many trades, but so far, a master of none, working mostly in manufacturing whilst studying in Media and Counselling.
He lives in Hampshire, England with his family, cat and growing collection of flannel shirts.
people.name: David Cartwright

people.bio: David Craig grew up on the west coast of Scotland.  He studied Software Engineering at university, but lost interest in the subject after (and admittedly prior to) graduation. He currently works as a resourcing administrator for a public service contact centre, and lives near Glasgow with his wife, daughter and dog
people.name: David Craig

people.bio: David D. Levine is the author of space-opera caper novel The Kuiper Belt Job. His previous works include Andre Norton Nebula Award winning novel Arabella of Mars, sequels Arabella and the Battle of Venus and Arabella the Traitor of Mars, and over sixty SF and fantasy stories. His story “Tk’Tk’Tk” won the Hugo, and he has been shortlisted for awards including the Hugo, Nebula, Campbell, and Sturgeon. Stories have appeared in Asimov’s, Analog, Clarkesworld, F&SF, Tor.com, numerous Year’s Best anthologies, and his award-winning collection Space Magic.
people.name: David D. Levine

people.bio: David DeGraff is Emeritus Professor of Physics & Astronomy at Alfred University in Alfred NY where, along with the usual Physics and Astronomy classes, he has also taught classes on The Science in Science Fiction; Life in the Universe;The Theory and Practice of Time Travel; Aliens and Alienation; Tricorder, Transporters and Tribbles; Muggles, Magic and Mayhem; A Beginner’s Guide to World Domination; and The Doctor in the Police Box. His short fiction has appeared in a Carbide Tipped Pens, Lightspeed and The Magazine of Fantasy and Science Fiction. He can be found online at DavidDeGraff.com
people.name: David DeGraff

people.bio: I am a long time speculative fiction fan, especially of SF. I love older SF while also enjoying the diversity of current SF. I have come to active fandom fairly late in life, and love attending worldcons. I have enjoying writing a mostly SF oriented blog for about two years. My focus the last few years has been more on short SF.
people.name: David E. Hook

people.bio: I am a Lecturer in Philosophy, Ethics and Religion at Leeds Trinity University who researches the overlap of religious language and belief from a Wittgensteinian perspective. I have a publication forthcoming on the philosophy of language and speaking with aliens.
people.name: David Ellis

people.bio: David Fenne is an author, actor, and improv comedian in Pinch Punch, the improv theatre company he co-runs. Originally from a small village in coastal Dorset, he went to London in 2012 for drama school and trained abroad at Syracuse University, NY. From improvised musical pantos to a sell-out Agatha Christie-style improvised whodunnit, he's entertained audiences the length and breadth of the UK (in many a wig and outrageous accent). OVEREMOTIONAL, the first in his YA urban fantasy trilogy, was Sunday Times Children's Book of the Week, and it's sequel, OVERTHINKING, was Scottish Book Trust's Book of the Month. The final book in the trilogy, SO OVER THIS, is set to be released November 2024.
people.name: David Fenne

people.bio: David Goodman is a novelist and short story writer based in East Lothian, Scotland. He has been previously published in Clarkesworld and Analog Magazines, but also writes in a range of other genres, from spy novels to space operas. He’s an enthusiastic member of Edinburgh SFF and the Codex Writers group. Like everyone else he’s on most of the socials, but you can always find him at www.davidgoodman.net. He is represented by Harry Illingworth of DHH Literary.
people.name: David Goodman

people.bio: Editor of The Banksoniain, an Iain (M) Banks fanzine. Ex-President of ZZ9 Plural Z Alpha, the Official Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy Appreciation Society. Book collector (and reader).
people.name: David Haddock

people.bio: David Keener is an author, editor, and speaker who lives in Virginia, USA with his wife and two, oops, three, inordinately large dogs. He writes SF, Fantasy, and Mystery but loves mashing up his favorite genres in new and unexpected ways. He is the grand instigator behind the Worlds Enough anthology series, and co-editor of the first two volumes, Fantastic Defenders and Fantastic Detectives. His next anthology will be The Forever Inn, about a mysterious inn that travels randomly throughout the multiverse. He is a founding member of the Hourlings Podcast Project, covering writing-related topics.
people.name: David Keener

people.bio:
David runs the small press, Guardbridge Books, located in Scotland where he lives with his wife, daughter, and cats. He publishes a variety of science fiction and fantasy, as well as history/non-fiction. For a while in the early 2000s, he ran a small webzine, Parageography, focusing on stories with interesting worldbuilding.
He has a PhD in History from the University of St Andrews - that's what brought this American to Scotland. Before that he had a long a twisted academic path, studying Astronomy, Physics, Philosophy, Music, and a little bit a nearly everything else. A real renaissance man, unfortunately living several hundred years after the renaissance.
people.name: David Stokes

people.bio:
David Wake has published 13 novels including 'I, Phone', the 'Derring-Do Club' adventures and the near-future SF ‘Thinkersphere’ series. While taking an MA in Creative Writing at Birmingham City University, he was introduced to independent publishing. He co-founded and co-runs New Street Authors, an indie-publishing collective and co-wrote 'Punk Publishing' on why and how to self-publish.
He has previously written for theatre, winning awards and taking shows to the Edinburgh Fringe, London and on UK tours. He wrote, directed and starred in the Captain Tartan plays performed at Eastercons.
He’s been a Guest of Honour at the SF conventions ArmadaCon and Redemption.
And he invented the Drabble.
people.name: David Wake

people.bio: I enjoy costuming and cosplay! I have been lucky enough to win a few local (California) masquerades. Talking about costuming is great fun and hope to see you at panels.
people.name: Debbie Bretschneider

people.bio: Debbie Iancu-Haddad is a Science Fiction and Fantasy author. Her books include the Children of the Stars series and the Achten Tan series. She has also been featured in over a dozen anthologies.
people.name: Debbie Iancu-Haddad

people.bio: Debora Godfrey co-edited the best-selling Alternative Apocalypse and Alternative War, was published in several Alternative anthologies. She was one of the editors and authors of Post Roe Alternatives: Fighting Back and Holiday Leftovers, as well as Madam President and Alternative Leadership. She is a member of SFWA. She recently exchanged life in a cohousing community for an existence with a cheerful husband, several grumpy hummingbirds, and a usually even-tempered lawyer, not to mention a multitude of tiny frogs, a long-haired Chihuahua Jasper, and a googly-eyed vacuum cleaner named Vinny.
people.name: Debora Godfrey

people.bio: DEENA MOHAMED is an Egyptian designer, illustrator and writer. She first began making comics at eighteen when she created the viral webcomic Qahera, a satirical superhero strip starring a visibly Muslim superheroine. She then began working on Shubeik Lubeik, an original Arabic graphic novel trilogy published by Dar el-Mahrousa in Egypt, Pantheon in the US and Granta in the UK. Shubeik Lubeik was awarded Best Graphic Novel and the Grand Prize of the Cairo Comix Festival. She lives, works and is usually asleep in Cairo, Egypt.
people.name: Deena Mohamed

people.bio: Delia Sherman is the author of numerous short stories and novels for both adults and younger readers, somewhere in the historical-fantastical-comical-romantic-feminist vein. Her most recent novel is The Evil Wizard Smallbone. She is or has been a teacher, an editor, a judge of literary awards, a clerk in a bookstore, a secretary, a gardener, a knitter, a cook, a traveler, and a flaming liberal. She lives with fellow-author Ellen Kushner in New York City in an apartment with no pets, a lot of books, and too many pieces of paper.
people.name: Delia Sherman

people.bio: Dell Christy is an avid reader and filker and data geek.  She was part of the crew who started the GAFilk filk convention in Atlanta, Georgia, USA and was a member of the Charlotte 2002 Worldcon bid.  In her (not so-) copious spare time, she is a fiber artist who spins yarn, knits, weaves, quilts, embroiders, and makes lace.
people.name: Dell Christy

people.bio: Dena Bain Taylor has spent most of her life in Toronto, Canada, pursuing her joint passions for music and books. She is a classically-trained singer and enjoyed a long career as a professor at the University of Toronto. She is also a writer, critic, tv script advisor, literary award juror, and erstwhile owner of Ben Abraham Books (specializing in the occult). The author of numerous books and articles, her most recent publication is Bones and Keeps, a historical fantasy about the great hero Beowulf.
people.name: Dena Bain Taylor

people.bio:
Denis Taillandier is professor at Ritsumeikan University’s College of International Relations, where he teaches courses on Japanese culture. He obtained his Ph.D. from Lyon 3 Jean-Moulin University (France) with a dissertation on the imagination of nanotechnology in Japanese SF. His research focuses on Japanese science fiction from the perspective of cultural studies.
He won the Special Prize for the 8th Japanese Science Fiction Criticism Award. He has translated several Japanese SF short stories from authors such as Ueda Sayuri, Fujii Taiyō, Miyauchi Yūsuke, Enjoe Toh, and Tobi Hirotaka.
He currently serves as a member of the SFWJ board of directors.
people.name: Denis Taillandier

people.bio: Denise Dumars writes poetry and short fiction in the genres of science fiction, fantasy, and horror. She is best known for her cosmic horror work. She is a former literary agent, librarian, and college English professor.
people.name: Denise Dumars

people.bio: Derek Tyler Attico is a science fiction author, essayist, and photographer. He won the Excellence in Playwriting Award from the Dramatist Guild of America. Derek is also a two-time winner of the Star Trek Strange New Worlds short story contest, published by Simon and Schuster. He is the author of the bestselling, critically acclaimed Star Trek Autobiography of Benjamin Sisko from Titan Books. With a degree in English and History, Derek is an advocate of the arts, human rights, and inclusion. He can be found at DerekAttico.com and on social media platforms under the handle @Dattico.
people.name: Derek Tyler Attico

people.bio: Desola Coker is an avid reader of Sci-Fi, Fantasy and Horror, with eclectic tastes and a penchant for a good story. She works at Angry Robot Books and can be found sharing a good meme on bookstagram.
people.name: Desola Coker

people.bio: Akintoba Kalejaye hails from Nigeria. He is a lawyer, comic writer, and graphic artist. Akintoba has brought to life over 20 comics under the umbrella of the award-winning publisher Comic Republic, including the critically acclaimed VISIONARY and METALLA both inspired by Yoruba mythology and the Nigerian way of life. He’s also the mastermind behind other thrilling comics like BEATZ, ITAN, VANGUARDS AFTERMATH, and ERU #8 to name a few. Akintoba’s contributions to the comic world have garnered him numerous accolades, including winning “Best Traditional Comic” at the 2017 Comic Connect Award and earning a nomination for “Best Writer” at the 2023 Glyph Awards. Akintoba’s work has caught the attention of Universal Studios, who are currently adapting some of his comic creations into live-action TV series and movies. He is also part of the Saauti Collective, a collection of African writers who released the Anthology "Mothersound" in 2023, under Android Press publishing.
people.name: DestructCode(As an artist)

people.bio: Translator, former purchasing editor, and once and future publisher of translated science fiction and fantasy.
people.name: Didi Chanoch

people.bio: Donald Eastlake has been helping on science fiction conventions for over 50 years and a fan for longer than that. He first worked on Registration at the Noreascon I Worldcon in 1971. He Co-Chaired Boskone 11 and Chaired Boskone 16 in Boston. He has been Convention Center Liaison for two Worldcons and Facilities Division Head for one. There have been dozens of years in which he was Presiding Officer or on the staff for WSFS Business Meetings. He was instrumental in the formation of the WSFS Mark Protection Committee and served as its Chair for many years. He is a Master Costumer in the International Costumers Guild and a member of the New England Costumers Guild.
people.name: Donald Eastlake

people.bio:
Donna Scott is a writer, editor, podcaster and stand-up comedian. 

She is a former chair and current Director of BSFA. She is the editor of the Newcon Press anthology series Best of British Science Fiction, now in it's 8th iteration.

In 2023, Donna launched a new publication venture: The Slab Press.
people.name: Donna Scott

people.bio: Doug Banks is a writer and narrative designer who creates podcasts, audio dramas, and screenplays for film and television. A founding member of Omniverse Media’s Storytelling Team, Doug is a published author and an award-winning independent filmmaker. In 2012, he updated the out-of-print Ghostbusters TTRPG for a new generation of players, and used it to create the actual play podcast Ghostbusters: Resurrection. He co-stars in the award-winning actual play The Call of Cthulhu Mystery Program and more recently he pioneered the “Surprise RPG” genre as the creator and lead writer of K8 Was Here and The Extermination at Omniverse.
people.name: Doug Banks

people.bio: In days gone by, people would ask Doug to muck around with their computers and he would invoice them appropriately. These days he only mucks around with his own computers, and he doesn't see much sense in invoicing himself. He also writes and delivers inclusive & affirming ceremonies for funerals and other occasions.
people.name: Doug S

people.bio: Douglas Reay studied Physics and Philosophy at Cambridge University, and has worked as a school teacher and software developer.   He is the author of a science fiction novel,  published by Royal Road, about the impact upon society of robots and computer programs becoming capable of matching human performance in an increasing number of employment categories.
people.name: Douglas Reay

people.bio: Annie is an ex-professional singer, singing teacher, and academic working at the University of Leeds as a lecturer in Music Psychology and Performance. Her key current interest is exploring the effects of music listening on science fiction and fantasy authors, but she is also interested in the effects of teaching mindfulness to musicians (mindfulnessforsingers.co.uk). Annie likes to read science fiction and fantasy as well as do crochet and build Lego.
people.name: Dr Anne-Marie Czajkowski

people.bio:
Emma is a neurodivergent science communicator and space enthusiast with a background in physics and a passion for wildlife and conservation.  Since completing her PhD in Cosmology she has worked in a wide variety of fields from science communication to project management, forestry and construction, and was one of the top 2% of candidates in the 2021 ESA astronaut selection process.

Passionate about sustainability on the planet and beyond, Emma has volunteered on wildlife conservation projects around the world and is now working for the UK Space Agency's Space Sustainability Team. She believes that space exploration is a powerful force for driving technological advancements with which to address the ecological crisis facing our planet, and is enthusiastic about tackling off-world design challenges with a view to improving how we live on Earth.
people.name: Dr Emma J King

people.bio: Chair of the Kirkmichael Trust which managed the award-winning restoration of medieval Kirkmichael in the Black Isle; and a great fan of f&sf from the 1960s.
people.name: Dr Jim Mackay

people.bio: Dr Patricia Kennon is an Associate Professor in children's and young-adult literature and culture at Maynooth University, Ireland.
people.name: Dr Patricia Kennon

people.bio: Dr Sarita Robinson is the Associate Dean at the University of Central Lancashire in the School of Psychology and Humanities. She is also one of the world’s leading academic researcher in area of survival psychology and so is often referred to as Doctor Survival! Survival psychology focuses on how people respond in disaster situations – everything from a terrorist attack to a ship sinking. Sarita is keen not to rely on dusty books to inform her academic research and so has undertaken some hands-on survival training. This means Sarita has had some hair-raising adventures, including completing training in Helicopter Underwater Escape, Fire-Fighting and Coastal Survival. In Sarita's spare time she enjoys Science Fiction and especially loves Dr Who. Sarita frequently combines her love of science with her love of Science Fiction and has written book chapters on the Psychology of Dr Who and Westworld as well as contributing to a science text book - The Science of Superheroes.
people.name: Dr Sarita Robinson

people.bio:
Dr. Jason Aukerman is a dedicated educator and researcher with a wealth of experience in American Studies and English. He currently serves as a Clinical Assistant Professor at Indiana University, Indianapolis, where he also holds the role of Director of the Ray Bradbury Center. Dr. Aukerman's academic journey has led him to explore diverse topics such as the war fiction of United States veteran authors, 20th Century American genre fiction, and adult literacy advancement.

At IUI, Dr. Aukerman passionately teaches courses on American Supernatural, Conspiracy Theories, Banned Books, Science Fiction, and introductory literature. His leadership at the Ray Bradbury Center involves overseeing one of the largest single-author archives in the United States, preserving the legacy of Ray Bradbury's literary works for future generations.

Through his work at the Bradbury Center, Dr. Aukerman aims to promote equity and inclusion through literacy advancement. He believes strongly in the power of literacy to spark critical and creative thinking, and he works tirelessly to position the center as a valuable resource for addressing the literacy challenges facing the United States.

Outside of academia, Dr. Aukerman enjoys exploring new ideas and engaging with communities to promote a deeper appreciation for literature and literacy.
people.name: Dr. Jason Aukerman

people.bio: The editor-in-chief of Margaret Atwood Studies, Karma Waltonen teaches professional writing and literature at the University of California, Davis, including courses on Doctor Who, Margaret Atwood, and Writing & Performing Stand-Up Comedy.
people.name: Dr. Karma

people.bio: Kevin B. Hewett, Ph.D.  spends his days working for the Air Force Research Laboratory developing high energy lasers for military applications. As a senior research scientist, he oversees a team of 10-15 scientists, technicians, and contractors. In his spare time he helps runs SF conventions (notably Bubonicon – the oldest SF convention in New Mexico) and participates in convention masquerades as a master costumer with his wife Rebecca.  Together they have participated in numerous masquerades.  Some of the more notable costumes include: 2013 WC - "Public Service Announcement" (Most humorous in Master Class); 2016 WC - "A Paid Poitical Announcement" (Honorable mention for beadwork); 2019 CC - "Senatus Populusque Romanus" (multiple awards including best in show for documentation); 2019 NASFiC - "Coyote Dream" (multiple awards including "Book Come to Life" in master class); and most recently 2021 WC - "A Ka'a Christmas Carol" (best in show workmanship).
people.name: Dr. Kevin

people.bio:
Pianist, clarinetist, and singer, Dr. Mary C Crowell writes jazzy songs about gaming and mythology. She is a music teacher, composer, arranger, and accompanist. Mary's most recent album is "I Have Missed You at My Table" (2022). She also makes silly music videos and songs on Patreon.

 

Dr. Crowell performs with Play It With Moxie, Dead Sexy, and Three Weird Sisters. These bands mostly formed in Atlanta, Georgia through the GAFIA filk community. Mary is currently collaborating with CSE Cooney and Tina Connolly on a fiendish musical to be released as six podcast episodes.
people.name: Dr. Mary C Crowell

people.bio:
Dr. Nadav Almog is a lecturer, editor and translator. He teaches at Haifa University. His research centers on fantasy literature, and in particular children's literature, middle-grade, and YA.
Nadav's research has focused on elements of the uncanny in children's literature, as well as on the home as a concept and a theme. His literary research is rooted in nearly two decades of experience in the publishing industry, in Israel and abroad. He also writes, himself, and his writing has been published in Hebrew, English, and Japanease.
people.name: Dr. Nadav Almog

people.bio: Yen Ooi is a 2023 & 2024 Hugo Awards finalist writer-researcher-editor whose works explore culture, identity and values. She is currently completing her PhD at Royal Holloway, University of London looking at Sino science fiction and developments in zoefuturism. Yen is narrative director and writer on Road to Guangdong (puzzle game), and author of The Ancient Chinese Art of Finding Peace and Fulfilment (non-fiction), Sun: Queens of Earth (fiction) and A Suspicious Collection of Short Stories and Poetry (collection). She is also co-editor of Ab Terra, Brain Mill Press's science fiction imprint.
people.name: Dr. Yen Ooi

people.bio: Drake Andersen (he/him) is a visiting professor in the department of music at Vassar College in Poughkeepsie, NY, USA, where he teaches music composition and electronic music. He is a composer, sound designer, and writer on music and sound. His research explores the role of technology in the creative process in diverse contexts including experimental music, improvisation, and open-source audio software development communities. This is his first Worldcon.
people.name: Drake Andersen

people.bio: Duncan Lawie was introduced to the Fantastic as a child with copies of The Hobbit and The Invisible Man and has rarely stopped reading since. He has been reviewing since 1996 and was an Arthur C Clarke Award judge for 2013 and 2014 books.
people.name: Duncan Lawie

people.bio:
Dylan Phelan is a final year PhD candidate in the department of English and Digital
Humanities at University College Cork. His current research focuses on science fiction and
critical theory and examines the influences and processes of literary Othering. Specifically,
his PhD thesis examines the portrayal of the posthuman subject in contemporary science
fiction, as well as the effects of capitalist co-option on said portrayal. Dylan's research on
science fiction and posthumanism has recently featured in both the Movable Type Journal
and Fantastika.
people.name: Dylan Phelan

people.bio: Author of the urban fantasy/mythic fiction The Paternus Trilogy, and the first in a new dragon rider/progression fantasy, Kraken Rider Z. PhD in Film Studies, dissertation subject the The Lord of the Rings films and the “cinema books” of Gilles Deleuze. Professor of Screenwriting and Cinema Studies. Former SAG/AFTRA actor. Published scholar of film and television. Specialties include mythology & folklore, cultural criticism, philosophy, film, and self-publishing. Former panelist at ConFusion, ConCoction, BristolCon, WorldCon Dublin, and TitanCon/EuroCon Belfast.
people.name: Dyrk Ashton

people.bio:
E. C. Ambrose writes knowledge inspired adventure fiction including The Dark Apostle series about medieval surgery, The Singer's Legacy fantasy series as by Elaine Isaak, and the Bone Guard international thrillers as by E. Chris Ambrose. Recent releases include The Roman Candle (Bone Guard 6), Drakemaster (Guardbridge 2022), and YA SF novel A Wreck of Dragons (WaterDragon Publishing, 2023). In the process of researching her books, Elaine learned how to hunt with a falcon, clear a building of possible assailants, and pull traction on a broken limb.  

Her short stories have appeared in Fireside, Warrior Women and Fantasy for the Throne, among many others, and she has edited several volumes of New Hampshire Pulp Fiction. A graduate of the Odyssey Writing Workshop, Elaine has returned there to teach, as well as at conventions and writer's groups across the country. She has judged writing competitions from New Hampshire Literary Idol to the World Fantasy Award.  

Elaine dropped out of art school to found her own business.   A former professional costumer and soft sculpture creator, Elaine now works as a part-time adventure guide.  In addition to writing, Elaine creates wearable art employing weaving, dyeing and felting into her unique garments.  To learn about all of her writing, check out RocinanteBooks.com
people.name: E. C. Ambrose

people.bio: E.D.E. Bell (she/her or e/em) is a fantasy writer and small press editor. A passionate vegan and earnest progressive, she feels strongly about issues related to equality and compassion. Her works are quiet and queer and often explore conceptions of identity and community, including themes of friendship, family, and connection. She lives in Ferndale, Michigan, where she writes stories, revels in garlic, and manages the creative side of her indie press, Atthis Arts. You can follow eir adventures at edebell.com.
people.name: E.D.E. Bell

people.bio: E.G. Condé (he/him/Él) is a queer Boricua writer of speculative fiction and fantasy. Condé is one of the creators of “Taínofuturism”, an emerging artistic genre that imagines a future of indigenous renewal and decolonial liberation for Borikén (Puerto Rico) and the Caribbean.
people.name: E.G. Condé

people.bio: SFF writer from Scotland. Her short story collection, Under the Moon, won a British Fantasy Award in 2023.
people.name: E.M. Faulds

people.bio: E.Saxey is a queer Londoner who works in universities and loiters in libraries. Their collection of short weird fiction queer fiction, Lost in the Archives, is available from Lethe Press. Their first novel, Unquiet, is a gothic tale, set in Victorian London but wandering into the countryside for a spot of folk horror.
people.name: E.Saxey

people.bio:
Eboni J. Dunbar (She/her) lives in Northern California with her wife.  She received her BA from Macalester College in English and her MFA in Creative Writing from Mills College. She is a VONA Alum, and the former managing editor for the Hugo Award-Winning FIYAH Literary Magazine. She is also the winner of the Lambda Literary 2023 Randall Kenan Prize for Black LGBTQ Fiction.

Her work can be found in Stellium Literary Magazine, FIYAH Magazine of Black Speculative Fiction, Drabblecast, Anathema: Spec from the margins, Nightlight Podcast and Beneath Ceaseless Skies. She also has a novella, Stone and Steel, out from Neon Hemlock, order here.

Eboni has also been nominated for an Ignyte Award in the Novella Category for Stone and Steel.

She can be found on Twitter: @ebonidunbar, BlueSky: @ebonidunbar.bsky.social IG: ej_beezington
people.name: Eboni Dunbar

people.bio: Ed Fortune is the Literary Editor for the world's oldest genre entertainment periodical, Starburst Magazine. He writes the TTRPG and Book columns. He has interviewed 100's of people from across the media. He's based in Edinburgh these days.
people.name: Ed Fortune

people.bio: Eddie Robson is a novelist, scriptwriter and journalist, based in Lancaster, UK. His novels include Drunk On All Your Strange New Words, Hearts of Oak and Tomorrow Never Knows, and his short fiction has been published by Uncanny. He wrote the BBC Radio sitcom Welcome To Our Village, Please Invade Carefully and three episodes of the Chinese adaptation of the SF drama Humans. His other work includes children’s animation such as Sarah & Duck and The Amazing World Of Gumball, comic strips for 2000AD and many Doctor Who audio plays. His work outside SF&F includes the Audible rom-com Car Crash.
people.name: Eddie Robson

people.bio: Edgar Governo is a freelance writer living in Winnipeg, Canada. In fandom circles, he is best known for The History of Things That Never Were, a longstanding website offering an annotated bibliography of fictional timelines from television shows, movies, books, games, and comics.
people.name: Edgar Governo

people.bio: Edgard Wentz is an alien in Dublin (of the Brazilian, not the extraterrestrial kind). He is a GigaNotoSaurus associate editor and made a kaiju attack Rio de Janeiro in a Brazilian anthology. He translated into Portuguese stories by Lawrence M. Schoen and Chantal Beaulne.
people.name: Edgard Wentz

people.bio: A computer science academic by day who has taken to writing nerdy folk songs with and ever growing collection of ukuleles by night.
people.name: Edwin Brady

people.bio: Eero Suoranta is a doctoral researcher at the University of Helsinki where his work focuses on alienation and estrangement in contemporary Chinese science fiction. He has also translated Chinese SF into Finnish, worked as a freelance journalist and literary critic, and been featured as an expert on Chinese literature and philosophy by the Finnish public broadcasting company YLE.
people.name: Eero Suoranta

people.bio: Ehigbor Okosun, or just Ehi, is the #1 Sunday Times Bestselling author of FORGED BY BLOOD, the first in a Nigerian mythology epic fantasy duology. Raised across four continents, she now resides in the US, where she writes speculative fiction, mystery thrillers, and contemporary novels for adult and YA audiences. She writes in hopes of doing justice to the myths and traditions she grew up steeped in, and to honor her large, multiracial and multiethnic family. She is a graduate of the University of Texas with degrees in Plan II Honors, Neurolinguistics, and English, as well as Chemistry and Pre-Medical studies and is a Cynthia Leitich Smith Mentorship Award finalist. When she’s not reading, you can catch her bullet journalling, gaming, baking, singing, doing yoga and spending time with her loved ones. At the moment, she is hard at work at Forged By Blood’s sequel, EXILED BY IRON, which is available where books are sold in October 2024.
people.name: Ehigbor Okosun

people.bio: I'm the editor of Once Upon a Future, a yearly anthology of Israeli speculative fiction, I write essays and reviews, speaking in cons in Israel and abroad since 2003 and an MA student in English literature at the university of Haifa.
people.name: Ehud Maimon

people.bio: Elaine is a writer, screenwriter, poet, city councillor and trans person. She has been an environmental manager, a metrology engineer, a forensic scientist, and is a qualified rocket scientist. Her debut novella is Unexploded Remnants, published by Tor.com
people.name: Elaine Gallagher

people.bio: Eleanor Pender is a writer and senior lecturer at the University of the West of England (UWE). Working in the arts and creative sector for over ten years, Eleanor combines teaching with freelance arts project work with festivals, independent creatives and collaborative partner projects. Her creative practice research explores independence within collaborative storytelling, drawing on genre fiction, publishing models and role-playing games. As a writer, Eleanor is a member of The Society of Authors, the British Fantasy Society, the British Science Fiction Association, and the working group for Cymera Festival. She is a professional event moderator, chairing events since 2015 at the Edinburgh International Book Festival, the Young Adult Literature Convention (YALC), Bath Children’s Literature Festival, Bristol Women’s Literature Festival, Forbidden Planet and Waterstones bookshop events and more. Highlights include chairing V.E. Schwab at Cymera Festival in 2019 and interviewing V. V. James over Instagram Live from her back garden.
people.name: Eleanor Pender

people.bio: Eleanor is the Publisher of Angry Robot Books - publishing a small and focused list of the weirdest and best SFF
people.name: Eleanor Teasdale

people.bio:
Elena Pavlova lives in Montana, Bulgaria, and since early age is madly in love with SF. Her short stories have appeared in various Bulgarian anthologies and magazines, winning awards from national competitions. In 2021, her novel Christmas Carolers vs Hallus Beasts won the ESFS Best Work for Children award. Also in 2021 she was awarded the SLF's Diverse Worlds grant. 2024 her story A Pilgrimage to Memories Tattooed was shortlisted for BSFA award for translation. Some of her short stories had been published in English, most recently - Renting to Killers in May/June 2024 issue of Azimov's Magazine.
Curtently Elena Pavlova is the resident writer for Scars of Honor, an MMORPG.
people.name: Elena Pavlova

people.bio: Eli K.P. William is a British-Canadian novelist and translator who has spent most of his adult life in Japan. The only member of the Science Fiction and Fantasy Writers of Japan who writes novels in English, he is the author of The Jubilee Cycle trilogy (Skyhorse Publishing), set in a dystopian future Tokyo. He also translates Japanese literature, including the bestselling novel A Man by Keiichiro Hirano, and is now a writing consultant for a well-known Japanese video game company. His translations, essays, and short stories have appeared in such publications as Granta, The Southern Review, Monkey, and The Malahat Review. His essay on xenolinguistics for Aeon is forthcoming.
people.name: Eli K.P. William

people.bio: Elijah Kinch Spector is a writer, dandy, and rootless cosmopolitan from the Bay Area who now lives in Brooklyn. His first novel, Kalyna the Soothsayer, was a British Fantasy Award finalist and received acclaim from NPR, Nerds of a Feather, Tor.com, Foreword, and Paste Magazine, among others. A sequel, Kalyna the Cutthroat, is expected in November 2024.
people.name: Elijah Kinch Spector

people.bio: Elisa A. Bonnin was born and raised in the Philippines, after which she moved to the United States to study chemistry and later oceanography. After completing her doctorate, she moved to Germany, where she now works as a scientific writer. A lifelong learner, Elisa is always convinced that she should “maybe take a class in something” and as a result, has amassed an eclectic collection of hobbies. But writing will always be her true love. Publishing a book has been her dream since she was eight years old, and she is thrilled to finally be able to share her stories. She is the author of Dauntless and Stolen City.
people.name: Elisa A. Bonnin

people.bio: Eliza Chan is a Scottish-born speculative fiction author who writes about East Asian mythology, British folklore and reclaiming the dragon lady. Her debut novel FATHOMFOLK — inspired by mythology, East and Southeast Asian cities and diaspora feels — was a Sunday Times Number One Bestseller. Her short fiction has been published in The Dark, Podcastle, Fantasy Magazine and The Best of British Fantasy. She has been a medical school drop-out, a kilt shop assistant, an English teacher and a speech and language therapist, but currently spends her time tabletop gaming, cosplaying, crafting and toddler wrangling. Find out more on her website www.elizachan.co.uk.
people.name: Eliza Chan

people.bio: Elizabeth Bear is the Hugo, Sturgeon, and Astounding Award winning author of over thirty novels and more than a hundred short stories. Her next novel, FOLDED SKY, is a space opera to be published in 2025.
people.name: Elizabeth Bear

people.bio: Elizabeth Stell is a Junior Research Fellow at the University of Oxford working in Hebrew Bible. She recently completed her doctorate which explored the ambiguities inherent in reading fragmentary texts and especially dream texts in ancient Jewish literature, focussing on the tragedy, the Exagoge of Ezekiel. Her research interests include conceptions of the prophetic and prophetic literature, the role of the fragmentary, performance theory, and dream and dream interpretation in ancient Jewish literature and beyond. She is also a lifelong reader across the spectrum of speculative literature and eager to fold this into her scholarship.
people.name: Elizabeth Stell

people.bio: Ellen Datlow is an award-winning editor who has been editing sf/f/h short fiction for more than four decades, currently acquiring short stories and novellas for Tor.com and its horror imprint Nightfire. Her most recent original anthology is Christmas and Other Horrors. She has edited a Best Horror of the Year anthology for more than thirty-five years. Datlow is recipient of the Karl Edward Wagner Award for "outstanding contribution to the genre," the Life Achievement Award given by the HWA, and Life Achievement Award given by the World Fantasy Convention.
people.name: Ellen Datlow

people.bio: Ellen Kushner’s cult novel Swordspoint introduced readers to the “fantasy of manners” genre, and to the city to which she has returned in two more novels and the collaborative prequel Tremontaine. A longtime performer and public radio host, she narrated all three as audiobooks for Neil Gaiman Presents. Her award-winning Thomas the Rhymer is a Gollancz “Fantasy Masterwork.” With Holly Black, she co-edited Welcome to Bordertown. She has taught writing at Clarion, Odyssey, and Hollins University. She lives in New York City with her wife, author and educator Delia Sherman, and a growing pile of theater and airplane ticket stubs.
people.name: Ellen Kushner

people.bio: Elliot works in Birmingham as a geo-environmental engineer and writes minimally published sci-fi.
people.name: Elliot Craggs

people.bio: Em X. Liu is a writer and biochemistry graduate who is fascinated by stories of artificial intelligence and Shakespeare in equal measure. Chronically cold-blooded, Em nevertheless resides in Canada.
people.name: Em X. Liu

people.bio: Emil Hjörvar Petersen is an award-winning Icelandic author of fantasy, post-apocalyptic and horror. The TV and publishing rights to his trilogy Survivors of Ragnarök were recently sold to Skybound Entertainment in LA. His praised quadrilogy of novels, Handan Hulunnar, is a combination of fantasy, folklore and Nordic Noir. The audiobook giant Storytel has published five popular horror novels by him, one is now available in English: Oh, Karitas. A short story in English by Petersen, The Cryptid, was included in the Locus nominated anthology The Best of World SF vol. 1. He was the Icelandic GoH at Icecon in 2024.
people.name: Emil Hjörvar Petersen

people.bio:
Emilie Morscheck is the Australian author of several published short stories including "Astraea's Wish" and "Firestorm". In 2019 Emilie received an artsACT grant to edit her YA fantasy novel These Cursed Waters. She was a 2020 Anne Edgeworth Fellow, receiving support to develop her second novel The Selkie Curse. Emilie was shortlisted for the 2021 Text Prize and an inaugural recipient of the Steph Bowe Mentorship for her novel These Cursed Waters. She is a fan of kelpies, selkies and watery graves.
Emilie is a PhD candidate at the University of Canberra researching autistic representation in young adult fantasy.
people.name: Emilie Morscheck

people.bio: Emily C. Skaftun’s tales of flying tigers, space squids, and evil garden gnomes have appeared in Clarkesworld, Beneath Ceaseless Skies, Asimov’s, and more and are collected as Living Forever & Other Terrible Ideas, available from Fairwood Press. Emily is a beginner taxidermist and plays roller derby as V. Lucy Raptor.
people.name: Emily C. Skaftun

people.bio:
Emily Carding is an experienced Shakespearean actor, having appeared in versions of over twenty of Shakespeare’s plays, both on stage and screen. They hold a BA (hons) in Theatre Arts from Bretton Hall and an MFA in Staging Shakespeare from the University of Exeter.  Emily has, together with independent theatre company Brite Theater, created a number of challenging and innovative shows including Hamlet (an experience) and Richard III (A One Woman Show) both of which have won multiple awards and rave reviews internationally. Both adaptations use the audience as characters within the play and create a truly immersive experience with very little other than actor, text, space and audience.

This focus on the intimate connection between actor and audience has led to further immersive and interactive work, with Emily playing key characters in both The Locksmith’s Dream and Key of Dreams which have both received great praise from critics and guests, including actor Neil Patrick Harris.

Emily is also an accomplished screen actor, and played opposite Martin Freeman in the British horror movie hit, Ghost Stories. They will appear in a supporting role in the forthcoming Return to Silent Hill which is due in cinemas in 2024.

In 2018 Emily was commissioned by London Science Museum to create a solo theatre piece inspired by Mary Shelley’s Frankenstein. Quintessence imagines a future where humanity has become extinct and must be recreated by an AI, using Shakespeare as a guide to the human spirit. This won the outstanding theatre award at Brighton Fringe in 2019.

Emily is also a published creator of a number of highly popular Tarot decks including The Transparent Tarot and Tarot of the Sidhe, and author of esoteric works, including Faery Craft,(Llewellyn 2012), So Potent Art: The Magic of Shakespeare (Llewellyn 2021) and Seeking Faery (Llewellyn 2022)
people.name: Emily Carding

people.bio: Emily researches intersections between science fiction, science, and space policy. Her research has focused on multilingualism and translation between Russian, Polish and English, and the early Soviet theorists who aimed to make literary analysis more scientific. She is Co-Director of the St Andrews Centre for Exoplanet Science.
people.name: Emily Finer

people.bio: Author of Inanna (August 2023) and Gilgamesh (August 2024), the first two novels of the Sumerians trilogy, an epic series set in Ancient Mesopotamia. Also, science fiction reviewer for New Scientist magazine.
people.name: Emily H Wilson

people.bio: Emily's been attending and running conventions for over 20 years and loves to be able to discuss Science Fiction and Fantasy with people. She's also an amateur potter, whose work can be found in the Art Show.
people.name: Emily January

people.bio: Emily Tesh is the author of the Greenhollow Duology, which begins with Silver in the Wood and concludes with Drowned Country. Tesh is a winner of the Astounding Award and of the World Fantasy Award for Best Novella. Some Desperate Glory, her first novel, was released in 2023.
people.name: Emily Tesh

people.bio: Emily Xueni Jin (she/her) is a researcher and literary translator, translating both from Chinese to English and the other way around. She is currently a Ph.D. candidate in East Asian Languages and Literature at Yale University. Her most recent Chinese to English translations can be found in The Way Spring Arrives and Other Stories, the first Chinese speculative fiction anthology in translation produced by female and non-binary creators, AI2041: Ten Visions for Our Future, a collection of science fiction and essays cowritten by Dr. Kaifu Lee and Chen Qiufan, and A View from the Stars by Cixin Liu. Her essays can be found in her column for Sixth Tone, as well as Paper Republic’s Field Guide to Contemporary Chinese Literature, Vector, Wenhsun Magazine, and more.
people.name: Emily Xueni Jin

people.bio: Emma Sterner-Radley is an ex-librarian turned fantasy author. Originally Swedish, she now lives with her wife and two grumpy old cats in the U.K. She spends her time writing, reading, daydreaming, lifting weights, and watching whatever is the most gay on TV.
people.name: Emma (Em) Sterner-Radley

people.bio: Emma French is a PhD student at the Centre for Fantasy and the Fantastic at the University of Glasgow. Her recently-submitted thesis focuses on D&D and D&D actual play as a transformative response to fantasy literature. In her spare time she is also a player and DM, a recreational romancer of videogame NPCs, and the owner of two very pretty cats, Jester and Vex.
people.name: Emma French

people.bio: Emma Johanna Puranen is an interdisciplinary researcher studying the portrayal of science in science fiction, with an eye towards how science fiction can be used for science communication. She is also an award-winning science fiction writer and audio drama creator. Her anthology "Around Distant Suns" was reviewed in Nature Astronomy, and her show ROGUEMAKER won 9 Audio Verse Awards. Emma is also a huge polar history buff, and works part time on the historic Antarctic research ship RRS Discovery, in Dundee.
people.name: Emma Johanna Puranen

people.bio: Emma Newman writes short stories, novels and novellas in multiple speculative fiction genres. She is a professional audiobook narrator, and a Hugo Award winning podcaster. Her current podcasts are ‘Imagining Tomorrow’ and ‘Tea and Sanctuary’. www.enewman.co.uk
people.name: Emma Newman

people.bio:
Emma loves telling stories with pictures and believes that comics should be "For everyone, About anything, By anyone" (F.A.B).
Since starting her freelance career in 2006 with Selfmadehero's manga Shakespeare: Hamlet, she has worked as an artist and writer across multiple publishers, genres and formats; winning the writers' Scribe award for best graphic novel with her Life in Strange comic series in 2022. 
Whether spies, vampires, superheroes or teenaged troublemakers, her work often focuses on human connection and matters of the heart.
2024 sees her BREAKS series (co-created with Malin Ryden) released as a three book series from Orbit books.
Past titles include: the award winning six-book series, Life is Strange (titan comics); the New York Times best selling Vampire Academy: the graphic novel series (Penguin random house); ), The Modern Frankenstein (Magma comix), Olivia Twist (Dark Horse), Back to the Future (IDW)  and a plethora of comics and graphic novels besides, for publishers including: Marvel, DC, Image, Walker books, Harper Collins, Simon & Schuster and Oni press.
people.name: Emma Vieceli

people.bio: Eric Choi is an award-winning writer, editor, and aerospace engineer in Toronto, Canada. He was the first recipient of the Asimov Award (now the Dell Award) for his novelette “Dedication”, has twice won the Aurora Award for his short story “Crimson Sky” and the anthology The Dragon and the Stars (DAW), and received a 2023 Sidewise Award for Best Short Form Alternate History for his novelette “A Sky and a Heaven”. With the late Ben Bova, he co-edited the hard SF anthology Carbide Tipped Pens (Tor). His first collection of short fiction is Just Like Being There (Springer).
people.name: Eric Choi

people.bio: By day, Erica is an indie game developer at Explorasaurus Studios, with whom she has published over a dozen games, apps, and virtual experiences. By night, she’s a speculative fiction writer represented by Becky LeJeune of the Bond Agency. Her first novel, a comedic SF,  is currently on submission. She has a B.A. in music from Edinburgh Napier University, and an M.S. in game design from Full Sail University. Erica is also a folk harpist, research consultant, and trivia magpie with an exhaustive collection of science facts. She lives in Budapest.
people.name: Erica Holcomb

people.bio:
Erik is a short story author and has been creating stories since he could read and write. Encouraged by high-school writing and literature teachers, he decided to become a professional author one day. That day, as it turns out, just happened to be over thirty five years later. He is now threatening to write a novel. He enjoys public speaking on panels because he can carry on and on and people are less likely to run away.

Erik has been published in Analog Science Fiction and Fact (a fact that is still mindboggling to Erik) and graduated Taos Toolbox.

Erik currently lives in the Boston area, but has not yet been to Arkham, Massachusetts. 

Erik thinks referring to himself in the third person is strange and is getting tired of starting sentences with 'Erik.'
people.name: Erik M Johnson

people.bio: Cherith Baldry was born in Lancaster, UK, and studied at Manchester and Oxford. She was a teacher for some years, including a spell at Fourah Bay College, Freetown, Sierra Leone. She is now a full-time writer, mostly of science fiction and fantasy. In 2003 she became a member of the Erin Hunter team, writing the Warriors and Seekers series. We recently celebrated the 21st birthday of Warrior cats. Cherith is a widow with two grown up children and two cats.
people.name: Erin Hunter

people.bio: Erin Roberts tells stories across formats. Her short stories and interactive fiction have appeared in publications including Asimov’s, Clarkesworld, Strange Horizons, and The Dark, and her tabletop role-playing game writing credits include Journeys through the Radiant Citadel, which was a finalist for the Nebula Award for Best Game Writing. Erin earned her MFA from the Stonecoast program at the University of Southern Maine and is currently a Provost’s Early Career Fellow at the University of Texas at Austin. She is also one of the hosts of Writing Excuses, an award-winning podcast about the business and craft of writing.
people.name: Erin Roberts

people.bio: Eris Young is a queer, trans writer of speculative fiction. Their fiction has appeared in publications such as Pseudopod, Fusion Fragment, Metastellar, and the Immigrant Sci-fi Short Stories anthology from Flame Tree Press, and their novel-in-progress, Idomeneja, was longlisted for the Cheshire Novel Prize in 2023. They are the fiction editor at Shoreline of Infinity, Scotland's foremost science fiction magazine.
people.name: Eris Young

people.bio: Errick Nunnally was raised in Boston, served in the USMC, and graduated from art school. He has three published novels, BLOOD FOR THE SUN, ALL THE DEAD MEN, and LIGHTNING WEARS A RED CAPE, a short novel, THE QUEEN OF SATURN AND THE PRINCE IN WAITING, and several stories in anthologies and magazines. Visit erricknunnally.us to learn more about his work.
people.name: Errick Nunnally

people.bio: Esko Suoranta, PhD, is a post-doctoral researcher with the Kone Foundation funded research project Imagine, Democracy! Narrative Fiction as a Tool for Imagining Democracy in Finland at Tampere University and Narrare: Centre for Interdisciplinary Narrative Studies. His 2023 dissertation analyzes, through the theory of literary affordance, contemporary anglophone technonaturalist SF and its ways of approaching complex phenomena like digital capitalism. Suoranta co-edits Avain – Finnish Review of Literary Studies and is a former co-editor-in-chief for Fafnir – Nordic Journal of Science Fiction and Fantasy Research in which capacity he won the 2020 World Fantasy Award.
people.name: Esko Suoranta

people.bio: Esme Addison is the Amazon & BN.com bestselling author and Agatha nominee for Best First Book. She is a member of Sisters In Crime National, International Thriller Writers and Crime Writers of Color, and resides in coastal North Carolina with her family. Learn more about Esme at https://esmeaddison.com and follow her on Goodreads, Facebook, Twitter, Youtube and Instagram @EsmeAddison. Subscribe to her newsletter at https://esmeaddison.com/newsletter/.
people.name: Esme Addison

people.bio: Californian fan living in the North East of England.
people.name: España Sheriff

people.bio: Esther is the Chair of Glasgow 2024, A Worldcon for our Futures. She is also a Professor of Game Studies, and has published widely on players, games, and the stories they tell when they play. She is currently writing about TRPGs and how they have developed in recent years.
people.name: Esther MacCallum-Stewart

people.bio: Dr. Ethan Mills is associate professor of philosophy at the University of Tennessee at Chattanooga (USA) and President of the Science Fiction and Philosophy Society. His writing on popular culture and philosophy has appeared in Dune and Philosophy, Philip K. Dick and Philosophy, and The Journal of Science Fiction and Philosophy. He has taught courses on popular culture and philosophy focusing on science fiction and horror. He writes about science fiction, philosophy, and other stuff on his blog, Examined Worlds.
people.name: Ethan Mills

people.bio: Eugen Bacon, MA, MSc, PhD, is an African Australian author and editor. She’s a British Fantasy and Foreword Indies Award winner, a twice World Fantasy Award finalist, and a finalist in other awards, including the Shirley Jackson, Philip K. Dick Award, as well as the Nommo Awards for speculative fiction by Africans. Eugen was announced in the honor list of the Otherwise Fellowships for ‘doing exciting work in gender and speculative fiction’. Danged Black Thing made the Otherwise Award Honor List as a ‘sharp collection of Afro-Surrealist work’.
people.name: Eugen Bacon

people.bio: Eugenia Triantafyllou is a Greek author and artist with a flair for dark things. Her work has won the Shirley Jackson Award and has been nominated for the Ignyte, Locus, Nebula, and World Fantasy Awards. She is a graduate of Clarion West Writers Workshop. You can find her stories in Tor.com, Uncanny, Strange Horizons, Apex, and other venues. She currently lives in Athens with a boy and a dog. Find her on Twitter and Bsky @foxesandroses and on her IG @eugeniatriantafyllou
people.name: Eugenia Triantafyllou

people.bio: Eva L. Elasigue is an eclectic science fiction fantasy author and poet, with published works ranging through various subgenres and forms, notably the novel trilogy Bones of Starlight. She works varied modes of creative expression into her life, while dedicated to the written word.
people.name: Eva L. Elasigue

people.bio: F D. Lee is the author of the internationally bestselling fantasy series, The Pathways Tree, and the award-winning SF novel, In the Slip. A lifelong SFF fan, Faith has been featured in The Independent, appeared on BBC Radio 4, and has given a mini-TED talk on why stories matter. Faith is online and always happy to chat! Facebook, Instagram, Threads: @fdleeauthor (Facebook is the best place to catch her!). Visit www.fdlee.co.uk to read her work, including free short stories and sample chapters.
people.name: F. D. Lee

people.bio: Farah Mendlesohn is a con-runner, an Emerita History Professor, a charity manager, co-editor of the Hugo Award Winning Cambridge Companion to Science Fiction, author of the Hugo nominated The Pleasant Profession of Robert A. Heinlein and is currently working on a short book about Joanna Russ’s The Female Man. Farah chaired three Eastercons and served in various capacities in Worldcons and Eastercons. Farah is part of the World Fantasy 2025 team. (Farah/they/she). Farah's pre-con volunteer time at Glasgow2024 has been donated in part by her employer, The Association of Charity Independent Examiners.
people.name: Farah Mendlesohn

people.bio: Fatima Taqvi is a Pakistani writer of fantasy and horror. She is a graduate of Clarion West 2023 and has words in the Magazine of Fantasy and Science Fiction, Lightspeed Magazine, Nightmare Magazine, and Strange Horizons. She was shortlisted for the Future Worlds Prize in 2021 and was a finalist for the Salam Award for Imaginative Fiction in 2019. She has forthcoming work in OwlCrate anthology "Monsters in Masquerade" and Apex Book Company's "Map of Lost Places."
people.name: Fatima Taqvi

people.bio: Faye is a librarian from the Chicago area who delights in pets, reading, travel, and writing.
people.name: Faye Levin-O'Leary

people.bio:
I am Felix Meyer zu Venne the editor in chief/translator of Kapsel - Fantastische Geschichte aus China (https://www.instagram.com/kapselmagazin/). 
Kapsel is a SF magazine that exclusively focuses on publishing Chinese SF in Germany. So far we have released five issues and are currently finalizing our next magazine. Each issue has one short story at its centre and is accompanied by a variety of texts that are more or less connected to the story itself. Until now we have published short stories by Chen Qiufan, Xia Jia, Regian Kanyu Wang, Baoshu, Liu Yang, Anna Wu, Chi Hui; reviews by e.g. Ken Liu, A Que and Peter Watts; essays by Jiang Zhenyu … to name a few.
Every issue is illustrated by numerous artists. Recently, we have started to create audiobooks on tape. The story is read by an actor and interpreted by musicians. Here is a link to the first one we did:  (https://econore.bandcamp.com/track/kadavar-die-wahrheit-der-utopischen-liebe-snippet)
Over the past few years we have extended our output and have started to publish anthologies as well. So far we have releases one short story collection (Science-Fiction aus China) and one anthology with texts by Chi Hui (Das Erbe der Menschheit). We did in a workshop collaborate closely with German writers and have encouraged them to write science fiction as well. All those texts were relased in anther anthology (Kollaps und Hope Porn).
You can find images of all collections and magazines here: https://www.maroverlag.de/41-kapsel
people.name: Felix Meyer zu Venne

people.bio: Edinburgh-based pyromaniac and typemonger with an obsessive interest in things that look like steampunk but actually existed. Describer of Curious Contraptions on Wordpress and YouTube.
people.name: Feòrag

people.bio:
Finn McLellan (they/he) is an autistic disabled transmasc butch fantasy writer, hailing from the wilds of the northern UK.

When they’re not writing they’re busy immersing themselves in a variety of ridiculous hobbies, most of which also involve disappearing into fantasy worlds and/or waving swords at people.
people.name: Finn McLellan

people.bio: Fiona Moore is a BSFA Award winning writer and academic whose work has appeared in Clarkesworld, Asimov, Interzone, and six consecutive editions of The Best of British SF. Her most recent non-fiction is the book Management Lessons from Game of Thrones. Her publications include one novel; numerous articles in journals such as Foundation; guidebooks to Blake’s Seven, The Prisoner, Battlestar Galactica and Doctor Who; three stage plays and four audio plays. When not writing, she is a Professor of Business Anthropology at Royal Holloway, University of London. She lives in Southwest England with a tortoiseshell cat which is bent on world domination. More details, and free content, can be found at www.fiona-moore.com, and she is @drfionamoore on all social media. She is represented by the John Jarrold Literary Agency.
people.name: Fiona Moore

people.bio: I'm Flamma, a fan of science fiction games. I work for an institution that is conducting the Top World Science Fiction Games Charts in China. I would like to share this year's results with all the science fiction fans during the Worldcon, and to share the latest information in this field with the whole community, and even more important, I would like to build the connection between the fans in China and abroad.
people.name: Flamma
