people.bio: Flis Brown is an avid crocheted with an interest in costuming, sewing, space exploration and speculative fiction. Her favourite authors include Mary Robinette Kowal, Andy Weir, Robin Hobb and Diana Wynne Jones.
people.name: Flis Brown

people.bio: Flis Brown is an avid crocheter with an interest in costuming, sewing, space exploration and  speculative fiction. Her favourite authors include Mary Robinette Kowal, Andy Weir, Robin Hobb and Diana Wynne Jones.
people.name: Flis Brown

people.bio: Foz Meadows is a queer Australian SFF author and essayist based in California. In 2019, they won the Hugo Award for Best Fan Writer.
people.name: Foz Meadows

people.bio: Retired conrunner (Eastercons mainly), co-ordinator of Sheffield SFF Group on Facebook and Discord, foodie, Cult of Zoe, lives with John Dowd and some cats. Fan of good books and bad movies.
people.name: Fran Dowd

people.bio:
Frances Hardinge writes dark, bizarre genre fiction for children and young adults. She has won a number of awards including the Costa Book of the Year, the LA Times Book Award (YA category), the Branford Boase Award, the Children of the Night award for Gothic fiction, the Robert Holdstock Award at the British Fantasy Awards, and the British Science Fiction Association's Award for Best Book for Younger Readers. Her most recent book, Island of Whispers, is a gothic-YA-fairytale-ghost-story-sea-adventure created in collaboration with award-winning illustrator Emily Gravett.

She is physically inseparable from her Fedora, and is addicted to volcanoes.
people.name: Frances Hardinge

people.bio: Frances White is the author of Voyage of the Damned, a fantasy murder mystery at sea. A Nottingham resident, Frances is a creative writing graduate from Royal Holloway University of London. She has a soft spot for writing unlikely, flawed, messy heroes and loves mixing humour and heartbreak. Frances is also passionate about bringing more LGBTQIA+ representation and fat positivity into fantasy. When not writing, she can be found sewing nerdy costumes for comic conventions or researching obscure historical facts.
people.name: Frances White

people.bio: Francesca Kuehlers is a Coloradan at heart and a Berlinerin by choice. When she's not reading, cooking or writing, you'll find her working as a translator and parent. Francesca considers herself a wug counter par excellence.
people.name: Francesca Kuehlers

people.bio: Francesca T Barbini is the founder of Award Winning Luna Press Publishing. Established in 2015 in Edinburgh, Luna is home to SFF in fiction and academia.
people.name: Francesca T Barbini - Luna Press Publishing

people.bio:
Francesco Verso (Bologna, 1973) is one of the most relevant voices of European Science Fiction and editor of Future Fiction. Over the last 15 years he has won many SF awards, including 2 Urania Awards, 3 Europa Awards, 1 Italy Award, 1 Galaxy Award and 1 Golden Dragon Award for the promotion of International Science Fiction. His books include: Antidoti umani, e-Doll, Nexhuman, Bloodbusters, The Roamers, Zendroide (with Duan Ziqi) and Futurespotting. His novels Nexhuman and Bloodbusters – translated in English by Sally McCorry – have been published in the US, UK and China with the translation of Zhang Fan and Shaoyan Hu for Bofeng. The Roamers – translated by Jennifer Delare, was published in the USA and UK by Flame Tree Press in May 2023. His short stories appeared in magazines like Robot, MAMUT, International Speculative Fiction #5, Chicago Quarterly Review #20, Words Without Borders, Future Affairs Administration and international anthologies such as Sunspot Jungle (Rosarium Publishing), A Dying Earth (Flame Tree Press) and The Best of World SF (Head of Zeus), Llaqtamasi (Pandemonium) and What’s the Future Like? (Guangzhou Blue Ocean Press). 
He’s a public speaker and panelist at many SF Cons across the world, including WorldCons, EuroCons, and Chinese SF Conventions. In 2020 and 2021 he co-organized the FutureCon an online SF convention with 67 panellists coming from more than 25 countries and in 2022 he co-organized the SolariseCon, one of the first international conventions on Solarpunk.   
Since 2014 he has worked as editor of Future Fiction, a multicultural project, scouting and publishing the best SF in translation from 14 languages and more than 40 countries with authors like James P. Kelly, Ian McDonald, Ken Liu, Xia Jia, Liu Cixin, Chen Qiufan, Pat Cadigan, Olivier Paquet, Vandana Singh, Lavie Tidhar and many others. Lately, Future Fiction started an imprint called Futuresque, dedicated to Science Fiction comics from many countries. He lives in Rome and may be found online at www.futurefiction.org.
people.name: Francesco Verso

people.bio:
Anna Ziegelhof is a science fiction and horror writer originally from Germany, now based in the San Francisco Bay Area. 
Her background is in social science and humanities research, linguistics, and recently tech (Research and Development in voice AI). 
Her short fiction can be found in numerous anthologies and magazines, among others The Horror Library, Flametree Press, Luna Station, and Shoreline of Infinity. She particularly enjoys quiet stories exploring darker aspects of the creaturely experience.
people.name: Frauke Uhlenbruch (Anna Ziegelhof)

people.bio: I am a concept artist, illustrator and writer. Initially I worked as a book cover artist, working traditionally in acrylics and oils, mainly for science fiction paperbacks but also other genres. I have created covers for writers like Arthur C Clarke, Issac Asimov and Larry Niven. I was an early adopter of digital art and in 2001 I began working as a concept artist for film and games. Movies include Guardians of the Galaxy and Thor Ragnarock and games like Epic Mickey. In 2024 my first novel Dark Shepherd is to be published by Newcon Press May 14th
people.name: Fred Gambino

people.bio: Fulvio Gatti is an Italian speculative fiction writer who’s been writing in English since 2018. His stories can be found in pro magazines, magazines and anthologies published in US, UK, Canada, and Australia. He’s been a student of Kevin J. Anderson and Rebecca Moesta’s Superstars Writing Seminars and part of Dave Wolverton’s Apex Writing Group. He’s also been a panelist at Worlcon/Discon III, among other international events. Since 2022 he’s a SFWA associate member. He lives with his wife and daughter on the wine hills of the Northwestern Italy, where he works as a local reporter and event organizer.
people.name: Fulvio Gatti

people.bio: Passionate about anime/manga, science fiction and theater, especially if all three are combined. Having worked as head of events and marketing for the premier Swedish science fiction bookstore, run anime conventions, headed a podcast for three years and arranged multiple Pride-events, have insight in both publishing trends and the broader fandom world in northern Europe. Active reader, theater goer, bookseller as well as engaged in transformative fandom and non-profit fan activities. Fascinated by the intersection of different ways of enjoying and engaging with culture in all its shapes.
people.name: Gabi GL

people.bio: Gabe is a PhD researcher at the University of Glasgow theorising the Digital Fantastic. They are published in First Person Scholar, Games and Culture, Springer and Poetic Sexploration the Anthology. Their branching interactive narrative I just want to remember, and more information is available on their website: digital-fantastic.com
people.name: Gabriel Elvery

people.bio: Gabrielle worked closely with Harlan Ellison in producing and directing the audiobook version of his CITY ON THE EDGE OF FOREVER teleplay with a full cast, and funded by a successful Kickstarter. Gabrielle de Cuir is an audiobook publisher, narrator and a succesful blogger and crowd-funder. She has narrated over two hundred audiobook titles specializing in fantasy, humor and titles requiring extensive foreign language and accent skills. She’s narrated Cory Doctorow, Ursula LeGuin, Gregory Benson, Ben Bova and Orson Scott Card. She is the director mastermind behind the full-cast dramatization of ENDER”S GAME ALIVE! She has narrated and produced most of Jonathan Howard’s The Brothers Cabal Series and Goon Squad. She produced Jonathan Maberry’s V-WARS on audio. She has directed the bulk of John Scalzi’s work on audio (including The Interdependency Series) with Wil Wheaton as narrator. She created unded Kickstarters to produce the audiobook version Harlan Ellison's original THE CITY ON THE EDGE OF FOREVER script and of both WOMEN DESTROY SCIENCE FICTION and QUEERS DESTROY SCIENCE FICTION with Christie Yant and Mur Lafferty. She is the daughter of four time Oscar wiinner production deisgner John De Cuir and grew up in the UK and Rome.
people.name: Gabrielle de Cuir

people.bio: Gail (she/they) is a software engineer, nerd, singer, fiber crafter, Red Sox fan, avid tabletop gamer, "hardcore causal video gamer" (very into phone games), and organizational management buff. They spend way too much of their time writing convention software for fun. They are aslo queer, Jewish, neurosparkly, and disabled. They would like to be your friend!
people.name: Gail "RGB" Terman

people.bio: Gao weiming is a current student in the Science Fiction Studies MA programme in University of Liverpool, he is also a member of British Science Fiction Association. His main research interest is science fiction and fantasy in the era of globalisation, especially in ACG. His reviews for the American and Japanese Science Fiction ACG have been published as chapters in the books Introduction to Science Fiction and World Science Fiction Frontiers Annual 2021. He recently participated as a member of the research group in completing a science fiction board game research project funded by the China Science Fiction Research Center in 2023.
people.name: Gao Weiming

people.bio: Gareth's works include The Embers of War trilogy, The Continuance Series, The Ack-Ack Macaque trilogy, Light Chaser (written with Peter F. Hamilton), and About Writing, his guide for aspiring authors. He has twice won the BSFA Award for Best Novel and has become one of the most shortlisted authors in the award’s 50-year history. He has also been a finalist for the Locus Award, the British Fantasy Award, the Seiun Award, and the Canopus Award.
people.name: Gareth L. Powell

people.bio: Gary Couzens has had fiction in F & SF, Interzone and other magazines and anthologies, with two collections published. Gary has had reviews and articles in print and online at Black Static, Cine Outsider and others.
people.name: Gary Couzens

people.bio:
Gary Ehrlich stalks the hallways of Northeast conventions and assorted filk conventions. In mundania he is a mild-mannered structural engineer for a major trade association, representing them on material design standards committees and at building code hearings. At cons he can be found on a stage or in the filk room, offering songs of space flight, lunar colonies and hyperspace hotels. Gary has worked on various incarnations of NEFilk, the Floating Northeast Filk Con and is currently Balticon's Director of Filk and Other Musical Mayhem. In April 2012 Gary was inducted into the Filk Hall of Fame for his contributions to the filk community.

Gary appears on five collections of convention recordings: "How Many of them Can We Make Die?"; "The Filk Was Great..."; "Millennium Pandemonium, Volume 1"; "Triskaidekafilkia" and "Filk Heroes". He has a few songs available at gorgeousgary.bandcamp.com
people.name: Gary Ehrlich

people.bio:
Gary K. Wolfe is Emeritus Professor of Humanities at Roosevelt University.  Books include Evaporating Genres:  Essays on Fantastic Literature, (Locus Award, 2012). For the Library of America, he edited American Science Fiction: Nine Classic Novels of the 1950s and American Science Fiction: Eight Classic Novels of the 1960s. His 24-lecture series How Great Science Fiction Works appeared in 2016.
He received distinguished achievement awards from the Science Fiction Research Association and the International Association for the Fantastic in the Arts, a World Fantasy Award for criticism, and ten Hugo nominations, winning for The Coode Street Podcast, co-hosted with Jonathan Strahan.
people.name: Gary K Wolfe

people.bio:
Needs a little update but this is ok:
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gary_Lloyd
people.name: Gary Lloyd

people.bio: Gavia Baker-Whitelaw is a geek culture journalist, film/TV critic, co-host of the Overinvested film podcast, and co-editor of the Rec Center fandom newsletter. You can read her work at the Daily Dot, TV Guide, Inverse, Reactor and more.
people.name: Gavia Baker-Whitelaw

people.bio: Author of the Invisible Library series and the Scarlet Revolution series. Enjoys knitting, patchwork, rpgs and reading. Sleeps in at weekends. Lives in the north of England.
people.name: Genevieve Cogman

people.bio: Genoveva Dimova is a Bulgarian fantasy author and archaeologist based in Scotland. Her debut novel inspired by Slavic folklore, Foul Days, is coming out in June 2024, with the sequel, Monstrous Nights to follow in October 2024. When she’s not writing, she likes to explore old ruins, climb even older hills, and listen to practically ancient rock music.
people.name: Genoveva Dimova

people.bio: GEOFF RYMAN’s work has won numerous awards including the John W. Campbell Memorial Award first place, the Arthur C. Clarke Award (twice for The Child Garden and for Air), the James W Tiptree Memorial Award (for Air), the Philip K. Dick Memorial Award (for 253), the British Science Fiction Association Award (three times, once for the series of interviews with African writers and the Canadian Sunburst Award (twice for Air a volume of short stories, Paradise Tales.  In 2012 he won a Nebula Award for his Nigeria-set novelette 'What We Found'.  In December of 2023 his novel HIM was published and made both the Financial Times and The Guardian's lists of the five best SFF novels of the year.  HIH was shortlisted for a BSFA Award for Best Novel.  Geoff was originally from Canada and has lived since 1973 in the UK.
people.name: Geoff Ryman

people.bio: Dr. Geoffrey A. Landis is a science-fiction writer and a scientist. He has won the Hugo and Nebula awards for science fiction, and is the author of the novel Mars Crossing and collection Impact Parameter (& Other Quantum Realities). He works for NASA on developing advanced technologies for spaceflight. He was a member of the Pathfinder and Mars Exploration Rovers Science teams, and most recently working on a mission to return a sample from the surface of Venus as part of the NASA Innovative Advanced Concepts project. He is also known for work on concepts for interstellar flight. In his spare time, he goes to fencing tournaments to stab strangers with a sword.  More information about him can be found at his somewhat-outdated web page: http://www.geoffreylandis.com/, or on Wikipedia.
people.name: Geoffrey A. Landis

people.bio:
George Jreije ("jer-age") is an Arab American author and creative writing teacher. He has published the Shad Hadid fantasy series with HarperCollins, and currently has graphic novels and a new fantasy series on the way. He has also published short stories with UNICEF. 

Currently, George is a creative writing instructor with Gotham Writers Workshop. He has been a featured speaker for WriteHive, WorldCon, SCBWI, and the Highlights Foundation. In his free time, he loves connecting with other writers and readers to geek out about books and comics.
people.name: George Jreije

people.bio:
Georgina Kamsika is a speculative fiction writer born in Yorkshire, England, to Anglo-Indian immigrant parents and has spent most of her life explaining her English first name, Polish surname and South Asian features.  
As a second-generation immigrant, her work often utilises the speculative element to examine power structures that are mirrored in the real world, touching on issues of race, class, and gender.
You can find her at www.kamsika.com or @GKamsika on socials
people.name: George Kamsika

people.bio: George Sandison is an editor, independent publisher and writer. By day he heads up the fiction team at Titan Books, acquiring, editing and publishing originated and licensed genre fiction, working with authors such as V. E. Schwab, H. M. Long, Paul Tremblay, Kritika H. Rao, Caitlin Rozakis and many more. Before/alongside that he ran the multiple-award-winning Unsung Stories, which closed in 2023. His short collection, Hinterlands, is published by Black Shuck Books, and his work has appeared in Nightmare, and more, and has received honourable mentions in Ellen Datlow's Best of the Year lists.
people.name: George Sandison

people.bio: Minneapolis fan living in Wales (the one in Massachusetts, USA) for the last 20 years. Fanzine fan; Idea editor (2024 Best Fanzine Hugo Finalist); 2019 TAFF Delegate; mostly-retired convention runner; dilettante fan historian; and susceptible to special projects. Also on the Board of Governors for the Ig Nobel Prizes.
people.name: Geri Sullivan

people.bio:
Gillian Clinton started out as an aerospace engineer and graduated to running her own information research company which has provided her with the opportunity to work on a wide variety of projects for some very strange clients.  As an interdisciplinary engineer, information researcher, reference librarian and amateur astronomer, she is able to assimilate information and share it effectively with others.  Resistance is futile!  Gillian loves talking about the solar system and citizen science.  

She has been attending cons since her high school science fiction club dragged her to the first Toronto Star Trek convention held many, many years ago - Thanks Rob Sawyer!  One day she hopes to have time to actually read all the books she has collected and maybe, just maybe, she'll get a chance to look through her telescope on a clear night.
people.name: Gillian Clinton

people.bio:
Dr Gillian POLACK is an award-winning Australian speculative fiction writer and historian. She received the 2020 A. Bertram Chandler (lifetime achievement in science fiction) award. She is also an ethnohistorian with a special interest in how story transmits culture, mainly Medieval and modern. Her most recent non-fiction book is Story Matrices: Cultural Encoding and Cultural Baggage in the Worlds of Science Fiction and Fantasy. Her most recent novel is The Green Children Help Out and her most recent short story (short-listed for the Sidewise Award)is in Other Covenants, “Why the Bridgemasters of York Pay No Taxes.”
https://gillianpolack.com/
https://www.patreon.com/GillianPolack
people.name: Gillian Polack

people.bio: Gina Saucier is a life long science fiction and fantasy enthusiast. Historian by education with a focus on Empires, Colonialism, and Globalization. She has worked in Regional Government - Court Administration for a decade and is heavily involved in Equity Social Justice and Diversity efforts in her field. She very much enjoys writing and is a consummate theatre kid at heart.
people.name: Gina Saucier

people.bio: Dr. Ginger Lee Thomason recently completed her PhD in Creative Writing at Anglia Ruskin University. Her creative writing thesis was a high fantasy novel titled How to Cook a Dragon, with an accompanying critical commentary on food in speculative fiction. She has a BA in Creative Writing and English and an MFA in Writing. She also has a passion for pub quizzes and in 2020 she and her team beat the Chaser Jenny Ryan on the ITV game show The Chase. She currently lives in Northern Colorado and works for the US Department of Energy.
people.name: Ginger Lee

people.bio: I've been mad about jewellery and beads all of my life and really, really want to spread the love!
people.name: Giulia De Cesare

people.bio: Giulia Iannuzzi’s research interests lie in the history of publishing and translation processes, and in speculative imagination in a comparative perspective. She holds a PhD in Italian Studies from the University of Trieste, and a PhD in Early Modern History from the University of Florence. She has published in journals such as SFRA Review, International Journal of Translation, History: The Journal of The Historical Association, Journal for Eighteenth-Century Studies, Perspectives: Studies in Translation Theory and Practice, and History Workshop Journal. Her books include Futuristic Fiction, Utopia, and Satire in the Age of the Enlightenment. Samuel Madden’s 'Memoirs of the Twentieth Century' (1733) (Turnhout, Brepols, 2024).
people.name: Giulia Iannuzzi

people.bio: Glen Engel-Cox has lived and worked in Texas, California, Malaysia, Ohio, Saudi Arabia, and Washington (both state and District of Columbia) providing communication management to energy research and international development companies. He earned an MFA with honors from American University. Glen has published a novel, Darwin’s Daughter; a non-fiction compilation, First Impressions; and short fiction in LatineLit, Utopia, Nature, Triangulation, Factor Four Magazine, SFS Stories, and others.
people.name: Glen Engel-Cox

people.bio:
GOURAV MOHANTY. Author. Lawyer. Comic. Recovering Burgers Addict. As evident, his life has many tabs open. 
Though he was doing well as a lawyer in Mumbai, he is now pursuing the infinitely more unattainable dream of being the first 'epic-grimdark fantasy novelist' from India. A connoisseur of mythologies and momos, a scholarship took him to the castles of Europe. Ever since, he has wanted to play medieval matchmaker by marrying Ancient Indian Lore to a Renaissance inspired World. 
Sons of Darkness is his first novel. Give it a shot for the poor author owes considerable gold to goblins.
people.name: Gourav Mohanty

people.bio: Grace Ann Thomas Worm (she/they) is a *mumbled* year PhD researcher on Female Fantasy in Tamora Pierce's fantasy world of Tortall at the University of Glasgow where she serves as the deputy chair for GIFCon, is Vice Editor for the student journal Mapping the Impossible, and the Headquarters Officer for the Centre for Fantasy and the Fantastic and moderator of its Discord server. Grace is an English Literature International Bachelorette accredited secondary teacher who has taught across the U.S. Her teaching experience, research interests, and publications cover fantasy, gender, race, class, ecology, YA, comics, video games, TTRPGs, worldbuilding, neo-medievalism, poetry, theatre, post-humanism, ecocriticism and speculative fiction.
people.name: Grace A.T. Worm

people.bio: Grace Borland Sinclair is a PhD researcher at the University of Glasgow, supported by the Scottish Graduate School for Arts & Humanities. She works between the Scottish Literature Department and the Centre for Fantasy and the Fantastic. Her research explores the speculative fiction of Scottish women writers across the 20th century, centring imagination as an outgrowth of lived experience and an element of activist praxis. She has recently published on Naomi Mitchison’s Memoirs of a Spacewoman in Fafnir – The Nordic Journal of Science Fiction and Fantasy and is a current committee member of the Postgraduate Gender Research Network of Scotland.
people.name: Grace Borland Sinclair

people.bio: Graham is a lifelong fan of Science Fiction and Fantasy. He lives in Cardiff with his wife, kidsand  dog. As a Master Digital Physical Design Engineer, Graham does chip design for a living
people.name: Graham Scott

people.bio: Graham Sleight has been writing about sf and fantasy since 2000. He's been an editor of _Foundation_, Managing Editor of _The Encyclopedia of Science Fiction_ (Hugo & BSFA winner), and Contributing Editor for _Locus_. He's published books on Doctor Who, and is currently working on a history of sf through its cover art (with Adam Roberts).
people.name: Graham Sleight

people.bio:
Gray has been learning about Scottish history since they moved to Glasgow. However, when they joined an ArtWalk in 2016 which detailed the women's history of Govan, this became a special interest and they joined the volunteers of the Protests and Suffragettes team - https://protestsandsuffragettes.com/ - in order to be more involved in learning and sharing these hidden histories.

Gray is also an avid and active SFF fan.
people.name: Gray Mitchell

people.bio: Greer Gilman’s mythic fantasies are Cloud & Ashes: Three Winter's Tales and Moonwise. Her Ben Jonson mysteries, set in 1600s London, are Cry Murder! In a Small Voice and Exit, Pursued by a Bear. She has written on the languages of the fantastic, on archetypes of girls in fantasy, and on Sylvia Townsend Warner. Her works have won the Otherwise (Tiptree), World Fantasy, Shirley Jackson, and Crawford awards, and have been cited in the OED. She likes to say she does everything James Joyce ever did, only backward and in high heels.
people.name: Greer Gilman

people.bio: Gregory A. Wilson is Professor of English at St. John's University in New York, where he teaches creative writing and speculative fiction. He is the author of the epic fantasy The Third Sign, the award-winning graphic novel Icarus and dark fantasies Grayshade and Renegade, and the D&D adventure/sourcebook Tales and Tomes from the Forbidden Library, plus many short stories. He co-hosts the actual play podcast Speculate! and is program consultant for the Gen Con Writers' Symposium. Under the moniker Arvan Eleron, he runs a Twitch channel focused on narrative, with sponsored TTRPG campaigns. He lives with his family in Connecticut.
people.name: Gregory A. Wilson

people.bio: Greta Kelly is the author of the critically acclaimed adult fantasy novels THE FROZEN CROWN, THE SEVENTH QUEEN and THE QUEEN OF DAYS (Voyager). Her writing has also appeared in Nerdist, i09 and Writer’s Digest. She currently lives in the U.S. with her husband EJ, and daughters Lorelei and Nadia who are doing their level-best to take over the world. You can follow her on Instagram, Twitter and TikTok @gretakkelly.
people.name: Greta Kelly

people.bio: Gretchen McCulloch is an internet linguist, the author of Because Internet, and cohost of Lingthusiasm, a podcast that's enthusiastic about linguistics.
people.name: Gretchen McCulloch

people.bio:
Gu Shi is a speculative fiction writer and a senior urban planner. She is the author of two SF story collections, Möbius Continuum(2020) and 2181 Overture (2024). Her story Introduction to 2181 Overture, Second Edition was nominated for the best novelette of 2024 Hugo Awards. Her short fiction works have also won several Galaxy Awards and Chinese Nebula (Xingyun) Awards.
Her stories have appeared in English translation in the collections Sinophagia(2024), Climate Action Almanac(2024), Book of Beijing (2023), Sinopticon (2021), Broken Stars (2019) and Clarkesworld magazine. Her stories have also been translated into German, Italian, Japanese, Romanian, and other languages.
people.name: Gu Shi 顾适

people.bio: H. G. Parry is the author of The Unlikely Escape of Uriah Heep, the Shadow Histories duology, The Magician's Daughter, and the forthcoming The Scholar and the Last Faerie Door. She holds a PhD in English Literature from Victoria University of Wellington, New Zealand, and currently lives in Wellington with her sister and an increasing menagerie of small animals.
people.name: H.G. Parry

people.bio:
Hannah is a Northumbrian writer living in Scotland. She is inspired by world mythologies, angry women, speculative fiction, and the stories we tell ourselves about being human.

Her debut fantasy novel Godkiller was an instant #1 Sunday Times Bestseller upon release in January 2023, and her second novel Sunbringer was #1 Sunday Times Bestseller in February 2024. Her Fallen Gods trilogy will be translated into 14 languages.
people.name: Hannah Kaner

people.bio: Hannah Mimiec is a part-time PhD student and part-time lecturer in law at the University of Dundee, currently researching narratives of policing in weird fiction. They hold an LLB and an MLitt from the University of Glasgow, where they were part of the 2022/23 Fantasy MLitt cohort. Specialising in cultural legal studies; their research interests include the intersection of law with weird and horror fiction, children’s literature, and tabletop games. When not thinking about tentacles, they are usually thinking about their next knitting project.
people.name: Hannah Mimiec

people.bio: Heather Rose Jones is the author of the Alpennia historic fantasy series and the fairy-tale novella The Language of Roses. She has short fiction in the anthology series Sword and Sorceress and Lace and Blade, as well as the audio magazine Podcastle. She has non-fiction publications on topics ranging from biotech to historic costume to naming practices and has a PhD in Linguistics. Heather creates the Lesbian Historic Motif Project blog and its associated podcast, presenting research on gender and sexuality in history as a resource for authors writing historic-based fiction, as well as promoting lesbian historical fiction in general.
people.name: Heather Rose Jones

people.bio: Heather Valentine (literary horror and fantasy)/Hex Valentine (love stories and online ephemera) is a queer Scottish writer. Her short fiction has been published in anthologies and magazines including We Were Always Here, Unspeakable: A Queer Gothic Anthology and Shoreline of Infinity.
people.name: Heather Valentine

people.bio:
Helen Gould (she/he/they) is an experienced moderator and speaker, as well as a writer, sensitivity consultant, and DEI trainer. 

They have previously spoken at conventions like Dragonmeet, Flights of Foundry (where they were also a guest of honour), Eastercon, and Nine Worlds on a variety of topics related to media and sociopolitical issues. 

They have contributed to TTRPG projects from Rowan, Rook and Decard; MacGuffin & Co.; Black Armada Games; Leyline Press; Golden Goblin Press; and many more. She also works with Rusty Quill (creators of The Magnus Archives) as Head of Inclusion and as a performer.
people.name: Helen Gould

people.bio: Helen McCarthy has been attending SFF and Star Trek conventions since 1974. She has been involved in costuming, art creation, art show management, panels and presentations for all of that time. She helped to create and run the first ever anime stream on a UK convention programme at Eastcon 90, and has written over a dozen books translated from English into seven languages, with another due this year, and academic papers.
people.name: Helen McCarthy

people.bio: Plant Pathologist with a background in molecular biology, genetics and statistics, working at Defra. I paint plant disease paintings as a hobby!
people.name: Helen Pennington

people.bio: Helen was read The Hobbit too young and has been having nightmares about giant spiders since. After accidentally turning a love of fantasy into a career by becoming an academic, Helen teaches and does research at Deakin University, Australia, currently as an Australian Research Council Future Fellow leading the project “The Politics of Medievalism.” In collaboration with Kavita Mudan Finn, Helen smuggled an entire chapter on fantasy into their book Global Medievalism: An Introduction (Cambridge University Press, 2022). Helen’s best-known book is Race and Popular Fantasy Literature: Habits of Whiteness (Routledge, 2016).
people.name: Helen Young

people.bio:
Helena writes role-playing games like Rivers of London, Dune and Conan, choose-your-own adventures like You Are Rorschach, and cult TV miniatures game 7TV.
They have written for the Scarred For Life books, and regularly contribute to fanzine Journey Planet.
people.name: Helena Nash

people.bio: Henry Spencer is a systems programmer and spacecraft engineer, with sidelines in spaceflight history and open-source software.  As a consultant to University of Toronto's Space Flight Laboratory, he was software architect for the MOST astronomy satellite, and is the creator and maintainer of much of SFL's most critical on-board software, now running in orbit on 50+ satellites.  Earlier, he was one of the founders of the open-source software movement -- there is probably some of his code in your computer.  He was a co-founder of the Canadian Space Society.  He is a Fellow of the British Interplanetary Society, and a member of the Senior Advisory Board of the Space Studies Institute. Asteroid 117329 Spencer is named after him.
people.name: Henry Spencer

people.bio: Born and raised in Southampton, Hesper Leveret studied Ancient History at Oxford and now lives in Liverpool with her family and chronic pain. She writes speculative fiction about beauty and heartbreak, magic and imagined mythology. Her stories appear in venues including Fireside, Interzone, Cosmic Roots and Eldritch Shores, and Luna Station Quarterly. Her interests include reading books and escaping rooms.
people.name: Hesper Leveret

people.bio:
Hildur Knútsdóttir is an SFFH writer from Iceland. She writes fiction for both adults and teenagers, as well as plays, screenplays and short fiction. Hildur is known for her evocative fantastical fiction and spine-chilling horror. Her horror novella The Night Guest will be published by Tor Nightfire in 2024 in English translation by Mary Robinette Kowal.

Her work has received various nominations and awards, including The Icelandic Women’s Literary Prize, The Icelandic Literature Prize, The Reykjavík Children’s Literature Prize for best original work and The Icelandic Bookseller’s Prize. Hildur is a feminist and a climate activist and she chaired the Icelandic Climate Fund from 2019-2024. She lives in Reykjavík.
people.name: Hildur Knútsdóttir

people.bio: Associate Professor, Department of Management Engineering, Faculty of Science and Technology, Keio University/Visiting Associate Professor, Department of Systems and Information Sciences, University of Tsukuba; President of HAI Laboratory; Director of Keio Science Fiction Center. He has been extensively engaged in research on human-agent interaction and artificial intelligence. Co-author of “Werewolf Intelligence: Artificial Intelligence to Deceive, See Through, and Persuade,” “SF Prototyping: A New Strategy to Create Innovation from Science Fiction,” “100 Science Fiction that Gave Birth to AI,” etc. etc. He is a chief editor of the Japanese Society for Artificial Intelligence, and 21st president of Science Fiction and Fantasy Writers of Japan.
people.name: Hirotaka OSAWA

people.bio: Holly Black is the #1 New York Times bestselling author of fantasy books, including the Novels of Elfhame, The Coldest Girl in Coldtown, the Spiderwick Chronicles, and her adult debut, Book of Night. She has been a finalist for an Eisner Award and the Lodestar Award, and the recipient of the Mythopoeic Award, a Nebula, and a Newbery Honor. Her books have been translated into 32 languages worldwide and adapted for film. She currently lives in New England with her husband and son in a house with a secret library.
people.name: Holly Black

people.bio: Holly Swinyard is a pop culture author, games writer and journalist. They have written for Steamforged and Cubicle 7, as well as PLAY magazine, the BBC and the Guardian. Their third book "A History of Fans and Fandom" was published this year by Pen and Sword. Holly is a bit of a cosplay addict and loves to explore realms of imagination through play.
people.name: Holly Rose Swinyard

people.bio:
Howard Davidson was captured by a Heinlein book in second grade, and hasn't been seen much since. Inspired to do science fiction by reading it, he went off and got a Ph.D. in physics, the best training available for becoming a crackpot inventor. 

He is currently a senior physicist in the computer industry.  He gets to write science fiction for the annual budget cycle.
people.name: Howard Davidson

people.bio: Ian Hunter is a Scottish children's author, short story writer, editor and poet. He is a member of the British Fantasy Society and has been their poetry editor for the past 15 years. He is also a member of the Glasgow SF Writers Circle, the Science Fiction Poetry Association, the BSFA, and the Horror Writers Association. He is the former editor and publisher of three magazines - "Footsteps"(quiet horror), "Urges"(erotic horror and fantasy) and "Unspoken Water" (weird stories and poems),
people.name: IAN HUNTER

people.bio:
Iain is a medical doctor of nearly 20 years experience, specialising in the field of public health , with particular interests in emerging pathogens and outbreak management.

His love of SF and Fantasy comes from 80s TV and reading Terry Pratchett.
people.name: Iain Kennedy

people.bio:
Ian Green is a science-fiction and fantasy writer from Aberdeen, Scotland. He is the author of The Sunday Times bestselling epic fantasy series THE ROTSTORM published by the Ad Astra imprint of Head of Zeus: THE GAUNTLET AND THE FIST BENEATH; THE GAUNTLET AND THE BURNING BLADE; THE GAUNTLET AND THE BROKEN CHAIN.

Ian has a PhD in clinical epigenetics, and his fiction has been widely published including winning the BBC Radio 4 Opening Lines competition and winning the Futurebook Future Fiction prize. He was shortlisted for Best Newcomer at the British Fantasy Awards.

His debut science fiction novel EXTREMOPHILE launches August 2024.
people.name: Ian Green

people.bio: I am a (mostly) SF writer living just outside Belfast, N Ireland. I'm a Hugo, Locus, BSFA and PHilip K Dick award winner, and mty most recent novel in Hopeland (Gollanczl, Tor). Next: The Wilding! (Sept 24)
people.name: Ian McDonald

people.bio: Ian Nichols, PhD, MA, BA (Hons), BA, Dip Teach, Dip Design, Dip Arts, and there's other stuff. Most of it has revolved around F&SF, as is evidenced by my attendance at around 100 cons, programming 12 and being on the program for most of them. My MA was on Conan and LOTR, my Doctorate on Historical Fiction, and I wrote novels for both of them. Ex-president West Australian Science Fiction Association, founder member West Australian Science Fiction Foundation. I like good food, good drink, good company, most animals, most people and going to conventions. Oh, and I study and practice  art and teach writing to Seniors. And sing. And play guitar. Oh, and I write, and some of it's been published.
people.name: Ian Nichols

people.bio: Ian R MacLeod is the author of many critically acclaimed and award-winning novels and short stories, which have widely anthologised and translated into more than a dozen languages, and span the entire spectrum of fantastic fiction. His novel Song of Time won the Arthur C Clarke award for the Year’s Best Novel, and he has twice won both the World Fantasy Award and the Sidewise Award for Alternative-World Fiction.
people.name: Ian R MacLeod

people.bio: I am a fan of sf and fantasy, reader of books and comics, watcher of films and TV. In my personal life, I have previously run a small-press comics convention, and professionally I am a science communicator, focused mainly at primary-school aged children.
people.name: Ian Snell

people.bio: A fan since the 80's, performer of (in)famous musicals and plays. Nominated for a Hugo for best short form dramatic presentation in 2006, winner of best fanzine Nova Award and GoH at 2006 Eastercon. Ran many Glasgow conventions and served on the 1987 Worldcon steering committee. Still working hard at being modest.
people.name: Ian Sorensen

people.bio:
First Sf novel, The Embedding, appeared 50 years ago. Invented Warhammer 40K fiction. Screen Credit for Spielberg's A.I. Artificial Intelligence movii 2001. Co-
won BSFA short fiction award 2009. Lives Spain.
people.name: Ian Watson

people.bio: Author of the Arabian best selling novel HWJN that has been adapted to a movie, creative director as Focus agency.
people.name: Ibraheem Abbas

people.bio: Igor Rendić is a multiple award winning speculative fiction writer and translator from Croatia. Author of A Town Called River urban fantasy series. Editor and podcaster at Morina kutija online magazine and Mora FM podcast.
people.name: Igor Rendić

people.bio: Boston, Massachusetts (US) area-based convention runner, software product manager, mom to college student, and spouse to a great guy who also loves SFF and helping cons go.
people.name: Ilene Tatroe

people.bio:
Professor of English at Sookmyung Women’s University, Seoul, Korea. Director of Sookmyung Research Institute of Humanities. Currently a vice president of Posthuman Research Network of Korea.
Recent articles include “Is the World Flat?: a Study on the Posthuman Materialisms in the Pandemic Era,” “Philip Dick’s Kitsch World: Man, Machine, and Science Fiction in Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep?,” and “’The Uncanny Valley’ Revisited: the Posthuman Apocalypse in Simon Stålenhag’s The Electric State.”
Major books and translations are After the Death of the Novel, William Burroughs’ Cities of the Red Nights and Thomas Pynchon’s Slow Learner, Vineland, and Bleeding Edge.
people.name: Inchan Pak

people.bio: Inge Heyer was born and raised in Berlin, Germany. Her first two years of university were spent studying Judo and Japanese language at Tenri University, Japan. Schooling continued with BAs in physics and astronomy at Smith College in Massachusetts, an MS degree in astronomy at the University of Hawaii, and a doctoral degree in science education at the University of Wyoming. Inge worked as a senior data analyst at the Space Telescope Science Institute and as an astronomy educator at the Joint Astronomy Centre in Hawaii. Now she is a professor at Loyola University Maryland. She co-authored seven books, including "Investigating Astronomy."
people.name: Inge Heyer

people.bio: Isaac Sage is a writer and researcher currently living in Glasgow, Scotland. Born in Los Angeles, he studied English, Creative Writing and History at Kenyon College, before flying halfway across the world for a master’s degree in Fantasy Literature at the University of Glasgow. He manages to eke out time for writing in-between trips to the indie cinema, games of D&D, and a long-running effort to visit every art gallery in Europe.
people.name: Isaac Sage

people.bio:
Isabel has a BSc in Foreign Languages from University of Alaska Fairbanks. Currently she is a Manager at UK Parliament Vistitor Services.
She has a special interest Disability and diversity in Fandom, and how the interests and needs of diverse people are accomodated. Isabel also is interested in languages and cultures of aboriginal people.
She enjoys boardgames and TTRPGs.
people.name: Isabel Nunez

people.bio: I am the lead marketer for Del Rey UK, the home of Science-Fiction and Fantasy at Penguin Random House UK.
people.name: Isabella Levin

people.bio: I am a Polish science-fiction writer. I published a dozen short stories in Polish magazines and anthologies and two novels. In my writing I focus on transhumanism, posthumanism and threats to humanity such as climate catastrophe or pandemics. I work as a software engineer.
people.name: Istvan Vizvary

people.bio: J A Mortimore has been active in science fiction and fantasy circles for longer than she cares to think about. She has published fanfic and run fan clubs.  In recent years, she has self-published a series of light space adventures, and has also co-authored two fantasy novels with Penelope Hill which are published by Elsewhen Press.  Now retired, she lives in Gloucestershire, UK with two friends, a number of cats, and far too many books and half-written manuscripts.  Prior to retirement, she worked with several UK police forces.
people.name: J A Mortimore

people.bio: Jim is a full-time SF&F writer, scientist (Ph.D. Electrical Engineering, specialty laser physics), and former running-dog-lackey for the bourgeois capitalist establishment. With 19 published books, he writes hard science fiction, epic fantasy and urban fantasy, frequently with strong YA themes. He's been successful in self-publishing and with traditional publishers like Open Road Media and Harper Collins. Jim has an abiding interest in all things scientific, like orbital mechanics, space travel, laser weapons, and other geekie stuff. He lives in Tucson, AZ with his wife Karen, and two little cats, Simone and Paris.
people.name: J. L. Doty

people.bio:
J.J. Green is a British-Australian science fiction author who writes about ordinary people living with the challenges of existence in future societies, and kickass sci-fi heroines.
Her series include Star Legend, Space Colony One, Star Mage Saga, Shadows of the Void, Interstellar Fleet and Carrie Hatchett, Space Adventurer.
J.J. was born in London’s East End within the sound of the church bells of St. Mary Le Bow, Cheapside, which makes her a bona fide Cockney. She has lived in Australia, Laos and Taiwan and currently lives aboard her starship in Cambridge, UK, with her ship’s cat, called Black Cat.
people.name: J.J. Green

people.bio: J.S. Breukelaar is an American-Australian author living in Sydney. Her new novella, Remedy is forthcoming from PS Publications in 2024. Her collection, Collision was a finalist in the Shirley Jackson Award as well as winning both the Aurealis and Ditmar Awards, and longlisted for both the Locus and Stoker awards. Her novels and stories have won, been nominated, or commended in international awards including  Stoker, Locus Story South, Australian Shadows, Ditmar, Varuna Award, Wonderland Award and James R Tiptree Jnr. Award. Breukelaar’s stories, essays, and poems have appeared in numerous publications including Apex Magazine, The Dark, Black Static, Fantasy, the Shirley Jackson nominated anthology Tiny Nightmares (Catapult), the award-winning Flame Tree anthology series edited by Mark Morris, and elsewhere including several Years Bests. She has a PhD in Creative Writing and Film Studies and teaches writing and literature in Sydney and elsewhere.
people.name: J.S. Breukelaar

people.bio: J.S. Fields is a scientist who has spent too much time around organic solvents. They enjoy roller derby, woodturning, making chainmail by hand, and cultivating fungi in the backs of minivans. They live in the Pacific Northwest with their wife, kid, and Flemish giant rabbit.
people.name: J.S. Fields

people.bio: J.T. Greathouse is the British Fantasy Award nominated author of the PACT & PATTERN trilogy, which began with THE HAND OF THE SUN KING and continues with THE GARDEN OF EMPIRE and THE PATTERN OF THE WORLD. He holds a BA in history and philosophy with a minor in Asian studies as well as a Master's in Teaching from Whitworth University, and spent four months of intensive study in Chinese language and culture at Minzu University in Beijing (中山民族大学, Zhongshan Minzu Daxue). His short fiction has appeared, often as Jeremy A. TeGrotenhuis, in Beneath Ceaseless Skies, Writers of the Future 34, Deep Magic, Orson Scott Card's Intergalactic Medicine Show, and elsewhere. In addition to writing, he has worked as an ESL teacher in Taipei, as a bookseller at Auntie's Bookstore in Spokane, Washington, and as a high school teacher. He was co-chair of the programming committee for the Flights of Foundry conventions in 2020 and 2021. He currently lives in Spokane with his wife Hannah, his cat Ofelia, and several overflowing bookshelves.
people.name: J.T. Greathouse

people.bio: JA Grier (em/em/eir) is a speculative fiction/nonfiction writer, poet, planetary scientist, equity specialist, and astronomy educator, who loves talkative cats, red wine, gothpunk, and hiking.  Dr. Grier’s credits include more than four dozen poems, essays, and stories in venues such as:  Space and Time, Mad Scientist Journal, Mirror Dance, Liquid Imagination, and the Maryland Writer's Association’s "Life In Me Like Grass On Fire,” and two textbooks, "The Inner Planets" (Greenwood Press) and "Airless Bodies in the Inner Solar System" (Elsevier Inc.)  WIPs include a collection of childhood horror poetry and essays pondering the alchemy of science and writing.  http://drjagrier.com
people.name: JA Grier, Ph.D.

people.bio: JJA Harwood is an author, editor and podcaster. She has published two YA fantasy novels: the Sunday Times-bestselling The Shadow in the Glass and The Thorns Remain. You can also find her on the silly and sweary D&D podcast, Lads on Tour.
people.name: JJA Harwood

people.bio: Multi-award-winning international audio fiction producer of titles such as The Springheel Saga, Murder on the Orient Express, Expeditionary Force: Homefront, Circles, Long Night In Egypt, Little Baby Bum, Lellobee City Farm and the acclaimed, 22-time award-winning recreation of London After Midnight, also nominated for multiple international festivals globally.
people.name: Jack Bowman

people.bio: As a professional scientist and science educator, I am passionate about the intersection of science and society. Science Fiction's focus on that intersection has always drawn me to it and my love of Science Fiction has always provided much of the impetus for my own career. I am an Associate Professor Emeritus from the Department of Physics at Southern Illinois University Edwardsville, USA, where I have taught since 2004. Prior to coming to SIUE, I was Director of Laser Development at the Nevada Terawatt Facility in Reno, NV. I have also worked at Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory and the U.S. Air Force Research Laboratory (as well as several other places). I hold a Ph.D. in Optical Sciences (specializing in laser physics and quantum optics) and an MS in Physics both from the University of New Mexico, and a BS in Physics from the University of Arizona. My wife and I live in an earth-shelter house (think "hobbit hole") in rural Illinois with (at the moment) two cats, one dog, and whatever has crept in when we weren't looking.
people.name: Jack Glassman

people.bio: Maltese born Edinburgh emigre. Christened in the upturned bell of a ship. He grew up in the Far East, Britain and Scandinavia. He's written for national newspapers, is a two-time winner of the BSFA Award for Best Novel, and was shortlisted for Le Prix Montesquieu 2015. His work has been translated into numerous languages. He is married to the journalist and novelist Sam Baker. He is currently writing spy thrillers as Jack Grimwood, and researching a PhD in memory and memoir at St Andrews.
people.name: Jack Grimwood, Jonathan Grimwood

people.bio: Jackie Burns is the President, and a Fellow, of the International Association for Astronomical Artists (‘IAAA’), a science communicator, UK and European Lead for S.T.E.A.M (on behalf of the IAAA), and a multi-discipline artist. Her media includes, but is not exclusive to, acrylic on canvas, watercolour, pencil, digital, fibre, glass, metal, clay, and creative writing. I was Artist Guest of Honour at Levitation2024, this year’s EasterCon at Telford, UK.
people.name: Jackie Burns

people.bio: I am an artist and illustrator. My genre illustrations include many for Shoreline of Infinity; my fine art work is inspired by mythology, history and legend.
people.name: Jackie Duckworth

people.bio: I am a PhD Candidate in Literature, Culture, and Translation at the Federal University of Pelotas (UFPEL), Brazil, a recipient of the Capes/DS Scholarship and a Visiting Research Student at the University of Swansea, Wales. My research experience encompasses a range of interdisciplinary topics in the humanities, from pragmatics and speech act theories to feminist epistemologies, gender studies, literary studies, and feminist philosophy of science. My current research interests revolve around the intersections between philosophy and literature, with a particular focus on the study of science fiction as a means to expand ethical-political imaginaries.
people.name: Jade Arbo

people.bio:
Jake Nicholls (they/them) is a developmental editor of science fiction and fantasy, with a focus on queer, trans and otherwise inclusive stories. Jake works directly with authors through their business Future Worlds Editing.

In addition to developmental feedback, Jake provides specialised services such as sensitivity reading for queer, trans and chronically ill characters. They have a particular interest in gender worldbuilding and can help authors make their fiction radically inclusive of all genders.

Jake lives in the UK, but their head is often away in other universes.
people.name: Jake Nicholls

people.bio: Jakob Drud lives in Aarhus, Denmark, with his girlfriend and children. He's published over 40 short stories in English over the years, as well as two books for tweens in Danish.
people.name: Jakob Drud

people.bio: James Bacon (He/Him) is an Irish Train Driver living in London. He enjoys comics, writing about comics, giving papers on comics, running conventions, and editing fanzines. James has won two Hugos, and with Chris Garcia edits Journey Planet. He chaired Dublin 2019 An Irish Worldcon, in Dublin Ireland and is co-chair of the 2025 Belfast Eastercon, the first to be held in Ireland in its 75 year history. A reader of Irish and Railway military history, he admits to enjoying War Comics, Star Wars, Phillip K. Dick stories, pens, trains, post and stamps way too much, and ends up writing about them.
people.name: James Bacon

people.bio: James Bryant A panellist and moderator at the Chengdu, Chicago, Denver, Helsinki, Kansas City, Montreal, & Reno Worldcons (Glasgow & Toronto too, I think - can't remember). An SF book collector (a "Bryant of books" is a standard measure in some SFnal circles - my library contains well over 7000, and a lifelong interest in electronic book technology enables me to carry most of them with me), hypnotist, radio ham (G4CLF), scuba diver, sailor, traveller, FBIS (Fellow of the British Interplanetary Society), raconteur, maker (especially electronic gadgets and 3D printed objects), sculptor's assistant (my wife is Carol Bryant, whose bust of Desmond Tutu is located close to his grave in St George's Cathedral, Cape Town), and cook (sometimes cooking demonstration curries at SF Cons). A member of the Lois Bujold mailing list, I live beside the sea in Southern England.
people.name: James Bryant G4CLF

people.bio: In the words of fanfiction author Musty181, current CSFFA Hall of Fame nominee, five-time Hugo finalist, prolific book reviewer, and perennial Darwin Award nominee James Davis Nicoll “looks like a default mii with glasses.” His work has appeared in Interzone, Publishers Weekly and Romantic Times as well as on his own websites, James Nicoll Reviews (where he is assisted by editor Karen Lofstrom and web person Adrienne L. Travis) and the 2021, 2022, and 2023 Aurora Award finalist Young People Read Old SFF (where he is assisted by web person Adrienne L. Travis).
people.name: James Davis Nicoll

people.bio: James Patrick Kelly has won the Nebula, Hugo and Locus awards. Jim’s most recent books are The First Law of of Thermodynaics Plus (2021), a collection in PM Press’s Outspoken Author series, King Of The Dogs, Queen Of The Cats (2020), a novella from Subterranean Press. He writes a column about the internet for Asimov's Science Fiction Magazine and has a novelette and a novella forthcoming in 2024 in that publication. With John Kessel, he has co-edited five anthologies, including Rewired, the Post-Cyberpunk Anthology and Digital Rapture, the Singularity Anthology.
people.name: James Patrick Kelly

people.bio:
James Webster is an SFF writer, spoken word performer and occasional game master/larpwright.

E writes online as Strange Little Stories & has three collections of flash fiction published with Inspired Quill ('Hopefully Ever After', 'Heroine Chic' & 'Monstrous Ink').

Webster performs slam poetry and interactive storytelling theatre (including at Edinburgh Fringe, Nineworlds Con and Discworld Con).

Eir most widely read story is a retelling of Hansel & Gretel that ends in a bird pun.

Webster's fandoms include tabletop rpgs, superhero fiction/media, wrestling, urban fantasy and plenty more.
people.name: James Webster

people.bio: Dr Jamie Scott entered the University of Glasgow in 1993, and never quite got around to leaving. After several positions involving electron microscopy and material characterisation, he currently supports research computing in the Institute for Gravitational Research.
people.name: Jamie Scott

people.bio:
Jan Kotouč is a Czech author of space operas, military SF and alternative history. His first novel was published in 2009 and since then he has written a number of novels in Czech. Frontiers of the Imperium is the first book in his latest series, the Central Imperium. He is one of the handful Czech writers who has found success on the English-speaking market. Apart from writing, he teaches at a university and is a popular speaker at a number of conventions.

He lives in Prague.
people.name: Jan Kotouc

people.bio:
Jane Flett is a Scottish writer living in Berlin. Her debut novel, Freakslaw—a queer literary horror—was published by Doubleday (Penguin Random House) in June.

Jane's fiction has been commissioned for BBC Radio 4, featured in Electric Literature's Recommended Reading, Highly Commended in the Bridport Prize and performed at the Edinburgh International Book Festival. She's a recipient of the Scottish Book Trust New Writer Award, the New Orleans Writing Residency and the Berlin Senate Stipend for non-German literature.

Jane is also one half of the riot grrrl band Razor Cunts and a founder of Queer Stories Berlin.
people.name: Jane Flett

people.bio: Jane Frank is a writer, collector, and private art dealer (Worlds of Wonder Art, LLC) now living in Santa Fe, NM.  In addition to two books documenting her art collection, written in collaboration with her late husband, Howard Frank: The Frank Collection: A Showcase of the World's Finest Fantastic Art (Paper Tiger 1999) and Great Fantasy Art Themes from the Frank Collection (Paper Tiger, 2003), she has authored two illustrated biographical art books: The Art of Richard Powers (2001, a Hugo Award finalist) and The Art of John Berkey (2003), and many articles on art and collecting – including a weekly blog under the byline “The Artful Collector” for Amazing Stories magazine online (2013-2014) and online articles for NeoText.com (2020-2022) In 2005 she edited two books on William Hope Hodgson: The Wandering Soul – Glimpses of a Life: A Compendium of Rare and Unpublished Works, and The Lost Poetry of William Hope Hodgson (PS Publishing/Tartarus Press). Other publications include: Pixel or Paint?  The Digital Divide in Illustration Art (NonStop, 2007), A Biographical Dictionary of 20th Century Science Fiction and Fantasy Artists (McFarland, 2009) and A Biographical Dictionary of Role-Playing Game and Collector Card Game Artists (McFarland, 2012). She represents several well-known SF/F artists in sales of their art, along with acting as agent for collectors and artists' estates.  Jane was Agent Guest of Honor at Chicon 7, the 70th Worldcon in Chicago, IL, 2012 and has been a featured speaker at IlluxCon since its inception, 2008.
people.name: Jane Frank

people.bio: I'm a retired legal secretary who's finally got the time (and energy) to write.  I read a lot (actual books and audiobooks) and spend a lot of time at London Zoo where I'm a patron.  I've been an SF fan since before even "Doctor Who" aired for the first time. I also support our local hospice when I can.
people.name: Janet Ellicott

people.bio: Janet Forbes is a published fantasy author and RPG developer, best know as lead author of The Dark Crystal RPG, and her work with Kobold Press, Infinite Black etc. In 2017, she and her husband founded World Anvil, the award-winning worldbuilding platform, campaign manager and novel writing software with 3 million users. She is passionate about education, and has given seminars on writing for GenCon, Dragonmeet, Full Sail University, EasterCon24, and others. She also runs Worldbuilding Con (www.WorldbuildingCon.com), a free online convention whose past speakers include R.A. Salvatore, Mary Robinette Kowal and Tracy Hickman, and the World Anvil Worldbuilding Podcast. She's pretty much the friendliest velociraptor you'll ever meet, so come say hi! :)
people.name: Janet Forbes

people.bio:
Jani Ylönen is working on a PhD in literature on science fiction with the topic ethical, class, and gender questions concerning gene technology in contemporary science fiction. 

He does also like to read speculative fiction and has deep seated interest in, for example, depiction of animals and especially dogs in SF.
people.name: Jani Ylönen

people.bio: Janice Gelb has participated in running numerous conventions, published numerous apazines, and spends way too much time posting on social media sites. She has run Program Operations at Worldcon ten times and ran the Hugo ceremony at LAcon III. She was the DUFF (Down Under Fan Fund) representative at the Aussiecon 3 Worldcon and, in a fit of madness, also ran Program Ops there. She liked Australia (and one particular Aussie fan) so much that she migrated there from the US. In Real Life, she works as a technical editor.
people.name: Janice Gelb

people.bio: Janine Wardale's  eclectic style of costuming combines sewing, crocheting, embroidery, bead work, fabric painting and macrame. She loves to reuse, re-purpose, and reinvent vintage finds and to turn them into unique pieces of wearable art and masquerade attire. Her claim to fame is that she spends six hours of embellishing for every one hour of sewing. The results speak for themselves.
people.name: Janine Wardale

people.bio: Jaq Evans is a horror and speculative fiction author based out of Seattle, WA. A graduate of the Stonecoast MFA program, Jaq writes fiction, narrative nonfiction and poetry. What Grows in the Dark is her first novel.
people.name: Jaq Evans

people.bio:
Dr Jasmin Kirkbride is an author and academic. Her short fiction has appeared in places including Reactor, Fictive Dream, and on the cover of Open Pen, and her story ‘Sand’ was featured in Some of the Best from Tor.com 2021.

She has an MA in Creative Writing and PhD in Creative and Critical Writing from the University of East Anglia (UEA), with her thesis exploring radical hope in dystopian climate fiction. Her other research interests include sustainable communities of care, hopepunk in environmentalism, and the ecology of intergenerational trauma.

Her eco-poetry has appeared in places including Frogpond and Presence, and she was the 2022 Researcher-in-Residence for the British Haiku Society, investigating haiku in the climate crisis.

Jasmin is a Lecturer at City, University of London by day, and lives in Norfolk (UK).
people.name: Jasmin Kirkbride

people.bio:
Jasmine Gower, author of Moonshine and other queer fantasy works, hails from Portland, Oregon. Jasmine received a Bachelor of Arts in English and a Master of Arts in Book Publishing from Portland State University.

Inspired to write by a childhood filled with fantasy novels, 90s video games, and the curious experience of growing up in the rural Willamette Valley, Jasmine has a passion for exploring themes of gender, sexuality, and disability through the conventions of speculative fiction, mythology, and fantasy world-building.
people.name: Jasmine Gower

people.bio: I am a queer, non-binary McGill University professor in the Faculty of Medicine and the Director of Research of my university’s simulation centre. My work gives me insight into the latest developments in AI, biometrics, and VR in medicine, training, and most recently, outer space, through consulting with the Canadian Space Agency. My research has been featured in The Guardian and CBC, amongst other media outlets. My comic book, Fake News and Dinosaurs, co-created with my husband and visual artist, Daniel Beaudin, has been featured on Global News TV and the Toronto Star. My fiction is forthcoming from Baffling Magazine and has appeared in Tesseracts, Polar Borealis and elsewhere. I have served on panels for Chicon (WorldCon), World Fantasy, and Can-Con science fiction and fantasy conventions. I live in Montreal, Quebec.
people.name: Jason M. Harley

people.bio: Jason Sanford is an award-winning science fiction and fantasy writer who's also a passionate advocate for fellow authors, creators, and fans, in particular through reporting in his Genre Grapevine column (for which he is a four-time finalist for the Hugo Award for Best Fan Writer). He's also published dozens of stories in magazines such as Apex Magazine, Asimov’s Science Fiction, Interzone, and Beneath Ceaseless Skies along with appearances in a number of "year's best" anthologies and The New Voices of Science Fiction. His first novel Plague Birds was a finalist for both the 2022 Nebula Award and the 2022 Philip K. Dick Award. Born and raised in the American South, Jason's previous experience includes work as an archaeologist and as a Peace Corps Volunteer. His website is www.jasonsanford.com.
people.name: Jason Sanford

people.bio:
Jasper William Cartwright (he/him) is one of the Three Black Halflings alongside Jeremy Cobb (he/him) and Olivia “Liv” Kennedy (she/her): nerdy friends with strong opinions and even stronger Charisma scores. Their weekly podcast is on a continuing quest to explore diversity and roll for melanin in the world of TTRPG, and has been described as “a joyful, creative, and chaotic celebration of gamer culture that puts the Black and BIPOC experience front and centre.”

Three Black Halflings won the Best Podcast Award at the inaugural CRIT (Creator Recognition in TTRPG) Awards in 2023. Liv, Jeremy and Jasper are currently excited to be preparing for their first ever live shows, taking place in Manchester and London in April 2024.
people.name: Jasper William Cartwright

people.bio: Jean Bürlesk is the author of the award-winning collection of fairy tale retellings The Pleasure of Drowning, as well as several plays in English, Luxembourgish, French and German. Hailing from the World’s only remaining Grand-Duchy, he prides himself on his proficiency in five languages, seven or eight of which he’s been known to misuse for literary puposes.
people.name: Jean Bürlesk

people.bio: I'm a Scottish fan, Glasgow-based, long-time Star Trek fan, and I first found out about organised fandom in 1974, and attended my first convention, Terracon '77, a Star Trek convention, in 1977. I've managed attendance in one shape or form at a convention every year since. I was a member of the Saltcoats Space Oddity Society (SOS) and also attended Glasgow's Friends of Kilgore Trout. Moving to London meant that I regularly attended the London Circle (also known as The Tun)  and was also involved in Walthamstow's monthly SF fan gathering.  I ran the Information Desk at Interaction in Glasgow in 2005 and I usually can be found in Ops at most UK conventions and a few Worldcons. I am also one of the admins on the Facebook group for Glasgow SF fandom, Resurgence of Trout. I'm also a member of the Glasgow Doctor Who Society,  the Royal Manticoran Navy, and Glasgow Hash House Harriers.
people.name: Jean Thompson

people.bio: Jeda Pearl is a Scottish Jamaican writer based in Edinburgh, Scotland. In 2022, she was shortlisted for the Sky Arts RSL Award and longlisted for the Women Poets’ Prize. Art installations include Windrush Legacy Creative Reflections, Caledonian Biotech Library 3033 and Acts of Observation. Her poems and short stories are published by New Writing Scotland, Open Book, Not Going Back to Normal, Shoreline of Infinity, Aesthetica, Tapsalteerie, Luna Publishing. Her debut poetry collection, Time Cleaves Itself, was published in July 2024 by Peepal Tree Press. Jeda is also Co-Director of Scottish BPOC Writers Network. @JedaPearl jedapearl.com
people.name: Jeda Pearl

people.bio:
Jeffrey A. Carver is the author of eighteen science fiction novels, including the recently published duo The Reefs of Time and Crucible of Time. With this two-part novel, Carver returns to his signature series, The Chaos Chronicles. Equally popular are his Star Rigger stories, including the Nebula-finalist Eternity’s End—and Battlestar Galactica, a novelization of the critically acclaimed miniseries. His work takes him to the borderland of hard SF and space opera; his greatest love remains character, story, and a healthy sense of wonder. In 2022, he received the Frank Herbert Lifetime Achievement Award for writing science fiction.

Carver has taught writing in many settings, from educational television to Odyssey to MIT to his own workshops. Visit him and his blog at starrigger.net, or his free guide for aspiring authors of all ages at writesf.com.

A native of Huron, Ohio, he lives with his family in the Boston area.
people.name: Jeffrey A. Carver

people.bio:
Jelena Dunato is an art historian, curator, speculative fiction writer and lover of all things ancient. She grew up in Croatia on a steady diet of adventure novels and then wandered the world for a decade, building a career in the arts.

Jelena’s stories have been published in Beneath Ceaseless Skies, The Dark, Future SF and Mermaids Monthly, among others. Her debut novel, Dark Woods, Deep Water, was published in September 2023 by Ghost Orchid Press. She is a member of SFWA and Codex.

Jelena lives on an island in the Adriatic with her husband, daughter and cat.
people.name: Jelena Dunato

people.bio:
I'm an actor, improviser & writer, who teaches and performs internationally. My writing features in Bath Flash Fiction anthologies, Fly on the Wall press, Retreat West, Reflex Fiction and will soon appear in The Map of Lost Places Anthol. (Apex).
In 2018 I wrote my first solo show - Tiptree - about the American science fiction writer, Alice Sheldon. I live in Sussex, I'm a member of Brighton SF & Fantasy writers, I have a dog, a husband and a mostly dead allotment.
people.name: Jen Rowe

people.bio:
Jen Sugden is one of the co-authors of the instant Sunday Times Bestselling novel 'High Vaultage' (Gollancz, 2024): a SFF detective comedy set in a reimagined Victorian past. Along with her co-writer and husband Chris, she is also the co-creator and writer of the critically acclaimed SFF detective comedy podcast 'Victoriocity', and was part of the writing team behind the BBC Sounds weird fiction anthology series 'Murmurs'. She has also written for the award-winning audio dramas 'Wooden Overcoats' and 'The Amelia Project'.

Jen holds a PhD in Victorian Literature. As an academic Jen specialises in the development of Victorian sensation and detective fiction, and the development of characterisation during the ninenteenth century. 

Outside of writing, Jen has also been a recurring player on the popular TTRPG podcast 'Realms of Peril and Glory.'
people.name: Jen Sugden

people.bio: Jenna Hanchey has been called a “badass fairy” and she attempts to live up to the title. A professor of critical/cultural studies at Arizona State University, her research looks at how speculative fiction can imagine decolonization and bring it into being. Her own writing tries to support this project of creating better futures for us all. She is a BSFA award-nominated author with stories appearing in Nature, Daily Science Fiction, Little Blue Marble, and If There's Anyone Left, among other venues. She's cohost of the African SFF podcast "Griots & Galaxies, Poetry Editor at Orion's Belt, and a member of SFWA and the Codex Writers Forum. Follow her adventures at www.jennahanchey.com.
people.name: Jenna Hanchey

people.bio: Jenni Coutts is an illustrator, speculative fiction writer and GP based in Glasgow, Scotland. She is the Art Editor for BFS Horizons and is the art show lead for the World Fantasy Convention in 2024. She won the British Fantasy Award for best artist in 2022 and was nominated for the same in 2023. She was shortlisted for the Scottish New Writers Award in 2019. She has artwork featured in both uk and international publications. In her free time, she enjoys boxing, weight lifting, and chilling with her cat smudge. Find her on instagram @jennicouttsart, twitter @jenni_coutts, or bluesky @jennicoutts.bsky.social.
people.name: Jenni Coutts

people.bio: Jennifer Brozek is an award winning author, editor, and tie-in writer. A Secret Guide to Fighting Elder Gods, Never Let Me Sleep, and The Last Days of Salton Academy were finalists for the Bram Stoker Award. She was awarded the Scribe Award for best tie-in Young Adult novel for BattleTech: The Nellus Academy Incident. Grants Pass won an Australian Shadows Award for best edited publication. A Hugo finalist for Short Form Editor and a finalist for the British Fantasy Award, Jennifer is an active member of SFWA, HWA, and IAMTW. She keeps a tight writing and editing schedule and credits her husband Jeff with being the best sounding board ever. Visit Jennifer’s worlds at jenniferbrozek.com.
people.name: Jennifer Brozek

people.bio:
Jennifer Delaney is a fantasy writer from Liverpool.
She began writing at the age of 8 after seeing Lord of the Rings and fell in love with all things Fantasy.
 She has a BA and an MA in Creative Writing from Liverpool John Moores University.
Jennifer's debut fantasy novel TALES OF A MONSTROUS HEART will be published by Gollancz in August 2024
people.name: Jennifer Delaney

people.bio: Jennifer Rhorer enjoys attending and volunteering at cons. Her Worldcon experience started with volunteering for CONZealand. She assisted with programming for Discon III and Chicon 8 and helped coordinated the virtual side of Chicon 8. She also volunteered for the Hugo nominated FIYAHCon.
people.name: Jennifer Rhorer

people.bio:
Jeremy Cobb (he/him) is one of the Three Black Halflings alongside Olivia “Liv” Kennedy (she/her) and Jasper William Cartwright (he/him): nerdy friends with strong opinions and even stronger Charisma scores. Their weekly podcast is on a continuing quest to explore diversity and roll for melanin in the world of TTRPG, and has been described as “a joyful, creative, and chaotic celebration of gamer culture that puts the Black and BIPOC experience front and centre.”

Three Black Halflings won the Best Podcast Award at the inaugural CRIT (Creator Recognition in TTRPG) Awards in 2023. Liv, Jeremy and Jasper are currently excited to be preparing for their first ever live shows, taking place in Manchester and London in April 2024.
people.name: Jeremy Cobb

people.bio: Jeremy Szal was born in 1995 and was raised by wild dingoes, which should explain a lot. He’s the author of the Common trilogy from Gollancz, which includes STORMBLOOD, BLINDSPACE, and WOLFSKIN, about a drug harvested from alien DNA that makes users permanently addicted to adrenaline and aggression. He’s the author of over fifty science-fiction short stories, translated into eight languages. He carves out a living in Sydney, Australia with his family.  Find him at https://jeremyszal.substack.com/  or @JeremySzal
people.name: Jeremy Szal

people.bio: Jesper is a professor of economics at Luleå University of Technology in Sweden. He usually works on whatever interests him at the moment, and/or whatever has the most urgent deadline; this often entails research on environmental economics, natural resource economics, energy economics, development economics, or several of these at once. He has attended a dozen Worldcons and no longer has any idea how many conventions he has attended in total.
people.name: Jesper Stage

people.bio: Jess is a producer, editor, and writer based in the UK, with over 6 years of experience producing live shows, as well as being the director of getting sh*t done for the TTRPG podcast 3 Black Halflings
people.name: Jess Jewell

people.bio: Jessica Mudd is a weaver of interactive narratives, composer, and a member of Omniverse’s Storytelling Team. She is a host, editor, composer, and sound designer for the "MOTHER, She Wrote" podcast. She served as Associate Producer of The Call of Cthulhu Mystery Program’s acclaimed season, “Night at Howling House”, is a voice actor in Midnight Burger, and is the lead writer and showrunner of the RPG Audio Drama City of Daemons as well as the upcoming historical fantasy audio drama, Étude of the Storm.
people.name: Jessica Mudd

people.bio: Jill Engel-Cox is a senior engineer and scientist with expertise in energy, climate, technology, and the environment. Her first job was climbing smokestacks in Los Angeles, followed by leading industrial programs for small businesses and research laboratories. Her Ph.D. work focused on use of satellite remote sensing for air quality and public policy. Most recently, she has led international planning and technology assessments for renewable energy and environmental sustainability research programs, working extensively in Asia and the Middle East. She also teaches industrial processes and environmental communications courses at Johns Hopkins University and an energy course for University of Colorado Denver.
people.name: Jill Engel-Cox

people.bio:
Two comic strips written by Jim (King’s Crown and Whisky in the Jar) have been adapted for the TV series Metal Hurlant Chronicles. He has written for DC (Batman80-Page Giant, Birds of Prey), Marvel (Spectacular Spider-Man, Uncanny Origins featuring Storm), Dark Horse (Eden, Savant), Judge Dredd Megazine (Calhab Justice, Judge Dredd) and Tokyopop (Star Trek Manga).

He has written three novels, the novel the Light about a pandemic written pre-this-pandemic, and the crime novel GoodCopBadCop and its sequel Good Cop.

His new book is an AI-themed collection of short stories called Rerun to Eden.
people.name: Jim Alexander

people.bio:
Joanne Anderton is an award-winning writer of science fiction, fantasy and horror, children’s books and creative nonfiction. Her most recent collections of speculative fiction short stories are Inanimates: Tales of Everyday Fear and The Art of Broken Things. She's currently undertaking a creative writing PhD at the University of Queensland for which she’s writing a “speculative fiction memoir”: a collection of short stories and essays which interrogates the line between fact and fiction, real and imagined. You can find her at joanneanderton.com.


Kathleen Jennings is an award-winning writer and illustrator of Australian Gothic and fantasy fiction. Her novella Flyaway (2020) won a British Fantasy Award (the Sydney J Bounds Award) and was shortlisted for the World Fantasy Award and the Courier-Mail People's Choice Book of the Year Award, among others. Her most recent book is the short story collection Kindling. She has completed an MPhil in creative writing at the University of Queensland, focusing on Australian Gothic literature, and is currently a PhD candidate there, researching methods of creative observation and writing a novel. You can find her at tanaudel.wordpress.com.
people.name: Jo Anderton

people.bio: Jo Lindsay Walton is a Research Fellow in Arts, Climate and Technology at the University of Sussex, and a SFF author and critic. He is editor-at-large for Vector, the critical journal of the British Science Fiction Association. His edited collection Utopia on the Tabletop, was recently published by Ping Press, and his monograph Postcapitalism and Science Fiction is forthcoming in 2025 from Lever Press. Bluesky: @jolwalton.
people.name: Jo Lindsay Walton

people.bio: Jo Miles is a nonbinary author of optimistic science fiction and fantasy, including the Gifted of Brennex space opera trilogy beginning with Warped State. Their short stories have appeared in magazines including Fantasy & Science Fiction, Strange Horizons, Lightspeed, and more. Fueled by tea and sunshine, they spend their time dreaming up strange new worlds and serving the whims of their two cats. They live in Maryland, USA.
people.name: Jo Miles
