people.bio: Jo Walton is the Hugo, Nebula, and World Fantasy Award winning author of fifteen novels, two essay collections, half a ton of poetry and a short story collection. She lives in Montreal and Florence, and reads a lot.
people.name: Jo Walton

people.bio: Joanna Corrance is a Scottish author of horror and science fiction. Her horror novel 'The Gingerbread Men' was published by Haunt Publishing in 2022 and her science fiction novella 'John's Eyes' was published by Luna Press Publishing in 2021. 'The Gingerbread Men' was recently awarded funding by Publishing Scotland for the production of an audiobook and a radio campaign throughout Scotland. Joanna's work has been reviewed in magazines such as 'Amazing Stories' and others. Joanna has appeared at ACME Scotland Comic Con discussing the publishing process, as well as Cymera and Satellite 7.
people.name: Joanna Corrance

people.bio: Joanne Harris (OBE, FRSL) is the internationally celebrated author of over 20 novels, including CHOCOLAT, (which became a movie in 2001), THE GOSPEL OF LOKI, HONEYCOMB and most recently, THE MOONLIGHT MARKET. She writes in various genres, from folklore to horror, Gothic and literary fiction, and has won numerous UK and international awards. She lives in Yorkshire, performs in the band she first formed when she was 16, and works from a shed in her garden.
people.name: Joanne Harris

people.bio: Joe Abercrombie is the author of The First Law, Shattered Sea, and Age of Madness trilogies, as well as Best Served Cold, the Heroes and Red Country. He is a full time writer and lives in Bath with his wife Lou and three children.
people.name: Joe Abercrombie

people.bio: Joe Haldeman has won five Hugos and five Nebulas and is an SFWA Grandmaster. His best-known book is THE FOREVER WAR. His latest novel is WORK DONE FOR HIRE.  The graphic novels THE FOREVER WAR and FOREVER PEACE are out from Titan. Joe was a combat soldier in Vietnam, which strongly influences his work. He’s retired from M.I.T, where he taught every fall semester for 30 years. When Joe’s not writing or teaching, he paints, bicycles, plays the guitar, and is an amateur astronomer.  He’s been married to Mary Gay Potter Haldeman for 59 years.
people.name: Joe Haldeman

people.bio: Johannes T. Evans is a fantasy, romance, and horror author from the South of Wales, now living in Bradford, Yorkshire. As a gay, disabled trans man, he enjoys romances and character dynamics that go beyond the basic dynamic of boy meets girl and heterosexuality comes next. He writes a wide variety of characters and stories, most exploring themes of trauma, power dynamics, class, and sexuality.
people.name: Johannes T. Evans

people.bio: John Clute Born Toronto 1940, in Chicago and New York before settling in London 1969. Active as sf reviewer and critic from early 1960s for New Worlds, F&SF, Washington Post, Guardian, Strange Horizons. Eight volumes of criticism from Strokes (1988) to Sticking to the End (2022). Plus The Darkening Garden (2006). Co-editor and author of The Encyclopedia of Science Fiction (1979-current). Second novel, Appleseed (2001), is sf. SomeHugos and others, including Pilgrim and Nebula/Solstice. A GoH at Loncon 2014. Latest book: The Book Blinders (2024).
people.name: John Clute

people.bio: John Corcoran is a Senior Writer at Larian Studios, where he has written for titles including Baldur's Gate 3 and Divinity: Original Sin II. He currently resides in Dublin, Ireland.
people.name: John Corcoran

people.bio: John is a scientist by day, focusing mainly on solar system physics: he spends most of his time writing code. By night, he is the co-host of the Octothorpe podcast, a Hugo Award finalist who initially got into fandom through social media (if LiveJournal counts!), and has an interest in how fan activities are moving online. He is a keen tabletop gamer and GMs regularly. In all the other parts of the day, he alternates between feeling guilty he’s not keeping up with his TV shows/playing enough games/reducing his to-read pile.
people.name: John Coxon

people.bio:
⁃	John W has been attending SF CONs since 1993 and leading Braiding and Balloon panels since 1995.  He is a retired computer professional, and was an organizer for E.L.V.I.S. (The Emergency Link to Vital Internet Services) [1994-1999]
	⁃	
	⁃	John has done these 2 panels/workshops (typically solo) for Gathering/Artistic Events; General and/or Children's Programming at several CONs over the years, including over a dozen such panels at NASFiC and World Cons.
people.name: John F. Wardale

people.bio: John G. McDaid is a science fiction writer, folk/filk singer-songwriter, and freelance journalist from Rhode Island. A 1993 Clarion grad, he sold his first short story, the Sturgeon Award-winning "Jigoku no mokushiroku" to Asimov's in 1995. The New York Times called him "A mischievous guitarist and vocalist with a gift for the inimitable phrase." He is a three-time finalist for the writer/composer Pegasus for filk; his debut studio album, Trail of Mars, won the 2021 John Culkin Award from the Media Ecology Association. He's currently working on a WWII alternate history novel. On the web at Web at http://johnmcdaid.com.
people.name: John G. McDaid

people.bio:
Professor John Le Quesne is a cancer biologist and a medical specialist in the pathological diagnosis of cancer. He leads a team of scientists who investigate human tumour biology at the University of Glasgow and the CRUK Scotland Institute in Glasgow.
His group specialise in the application of the latest microscopical imaging methods to reveal the detailed biological strategies deployed by cancer cells, and to identify new opportunities to treat them. They deploy the latest in self-supervised artificial intelligence methods to discover meaning in complex images. They receive grant funding from charities, government and external endowments to pursue this research.
He is an avid life-long fan of science fiction in literature and film.
people.name: John Le Quesne

people.bio: John Pomeranz is a longtime fan from the Washington D.C. area. He is a former president of the Washington SF Association and has worked at a senior level on numerous Worldcons in the Baltimore-Washington area and beyond (and at a more junior level on a hell of a lot more), as well as working on smaller local and regional conventions. With his wife, Kathi Overton, he helped create the long-running television series Fast Forward: Contemporary Science Fiction in 1989. He is inordinately proud of writing a couple of fannish musicals, Smoflahoma and the Pirates of Fenzance, and he notes that if you remember them you are really old.  John is an attorney specializing in the law governing tax-exempt organizations and has advised several Worldcon committees on such issues.
people.name: John Pomeranz

people.bio: John Scalzi is deeply enamored of cheese.
people.name: John Scalzi

people.bio: Swedish, born in Stockholm. Discovered sf at age 6, published first fanzine at age 12. Published some 300 fanzines. Have worked professionally as critic, nonfiction writer (with five books on science fiction so far, including a 2-volume history of the field), translator (into Swedish and from Swedish to English) and publisher. Contributor to the Encyclopedia of SF. As publisher, responsible for around 200 sf and fantasy books in Sweden. Also editor of Nova SF Magazine. Guest of Honor at numerous Swedish conventions, Eurocon 2011, Worldcon 75. See also Wikipedia, SF Encyclopedia and Fancyclopedia III.
people.name: John-Henri Holmberg

people.bio: Jonathan is a retired US Marine colonel and now a full-time hybrid writer living in Colorado Springs in the US. He is a USA Today Bestseller and a two-time Nebula and two-time Dragon Award finalist. He has well over a hundred titles published, eighty being novels, in science fiction, paranormal, YA, historical fiction, and non-fiction. Jonathan is a full member of SFWA where he is currently serving as the CFO and recently served as the Nebula Award Commissioner.
people.name: Jonathan Brazee

people.bio: Jonathan D. Beer is a science fiction writer, whose work in the Warhammer 40,000 universe includes the Crime novel 'The King of the Spoil', and several short stories.
people.name: Jonathan D. Beer

people.bio: Jonathan Strahan is a World Fantasy Award-winning editor, anthologist, and Hugo Award-winning podcaster. He has edited more than 100 books, is reviews editor for Locus, a consulting editor for Tor.com and Tordotcom Publishing, and co-host and producer of the Coode Street Podcast.
people.name: Jonathan Strahan

people.bio: Jonathan Thornton is studying for a PhD in the portrayal of insects in speculative fiction. He is the books reviews editor for Foundation Magazine, and writes reviews for Reactor, The Fantasy Hive and Gingernuts Of Horror, and has had music criticism published in The Quietus.
people.name: Jonathan Thornton

people.bio:
I help run Bulgarian SFF online fanzine ShadowDance which has been going on for close to 25 years already. We do a lot of workshops, competitions, quizes, and also publish thematic editions, most recently a 250 pager on Cyberpunk.

I dabble a lot in politcs, community work, civic activism and tech which is my professional domain. I speak at all sorts of events and usually advocate global revolution. I mean, unity and compassion. SFF is my utter passion but what's interesting for me is weaving it through every aspect of society and arrive at some sort of better us.
people.name: Joro Penchev

people.bio:
Physicist, sailor, reader, organiser, geek.

Jos is a system engineer for a space engineering company, primarily focusing on optical instruments for atmospheric earth observation.
people.name: Jos Dingjan

people.bio: Joe Norman is a Creative and Critical writer based in London, and Lecturer in English & Creative Writing at Brunel University London.
people.name: Joseph S. Norman

people.bio: Josh Winning is the critically acclaimed author of Burn the Negative, which was long-listed for a Bram Stoker Award, Heads Will Roll and The Shadow Glass. He is a senior film writer at Radio Times and has written for Total Film, Gay Times and Den of Geek. During his years as a film journalist, he has been on set with Kermit the Frog (and Miss Piggy), devoured breakfast with zombies on The Walking Dead, and sat on the Iron Throne on the set of Game of Thrones. Josh lives in Suffolk with his cat Penny and dreams of one day convincing Sigourney Weaver to yell “Goddammit!” at him.
people.name: Josh Winning

people.bio: I am a leading literary agent in sf/f, and in publishing for 40 years.  Clients include Brandon Sanderson, Charlaine Harris, Peter Brett, many other bestselling and award-winning authors. Have been on programming at many WorldCons and other conventions.
people.name: Joshua Bilmes

people.bio: Joyce Chng lives in Singapore. They write science fiction and fantasy as well as YA and MG. Their short stories have appeared in The Apex Book of World SF II, The Future Fire and Multispecies Cities. Dragon Dancer (Lantana Publishing) is Joyce’s first picture book, celebrating dragon dancing and Lunar New Year, followed by Oyster Girl (Pepper Dog Press), a tribute to their grandmother and the hawker heritage in Singapore. For YA readers, Fire Heart (Scholastic Asia) is a fantasy book about swords and coming-of-age. You can find Joyce at https://awolfstale.wordpress.com.
people.name: Joyce Chng

people.bio:
Joyce Reynolds-Ward’s work includes themes of high-stakes family and political conflict, digital sentience, personal agency and control, realistic strong women, and (whenever possible) horses, frequently in Pacific Northwest settings.

She is the author of five speculative fiction series: The Netwalk Sequence, Goddess's Honor, The Martiniere Legacy, The People of the Martiniere Legacy, and The Martiniere Multiverse as well as standalones Federation Cowboy, Beating the Apocalypse, Klone's Stronghold and Alien Savvy. Her new trilogy, The Cost of Power, will be released in September, 2024.
people.name: Joyce Reynolds-Ward

people.bio:
Ju Honisch books are mostly fantasy, with some science fiction and a pinch of horror thrown in. You will look in vain for cute fairies and sweet little elves in her novels, though. Her books are not meant for children. 
For her debut novel "Das Obsidianherz" (English version =“Obsidian Secrets”), she was awarded the German Fantasy Award “Deutscher Phantastik Preis”. In 2014, she was awarded the SERAPH for Best Fantasy Book at Leipzig Book Fair for "Schwingen aus Stein" (=“Wings of Stone”). She was shortlisted for these awards three more times.
Ju Honisch writes both in German and in English.
people.name: Ju Honisch

people.bio: Just an ordinary guy born into a Colombian family. Into SF since I could see Trek. In my early teens got heavily into literary SF.  I have worked conventions, written for fanzines, and been on podcasts.
people.name: Juan Sanmiguel

people.bio: Julia Rios (they/them) is a queer, Latinx writer, editor, podcaster, and narrator whose fiction, non-fiction, and poetry have appeared in Latin American Literature Today, Lightspeed, and Goblin Fruit, among other places. Their editing work has won multiple awards including the Hugo Award. Julia is a co-host of This is Why We’re Like This, a podcast about the movies we watch in childhood that shape our lives, for better or for worse. They’ve narrated stories for Escape Pod, Podcastle, Pseudopod, and Cast of Wonders.
people.name: Julia Rios

people.bio: Julia is a trial lawyer in Silicon Valley. She attended U.C Berkeley and majored in Asian Studies. She often writes with co-author Ken Bebelle. Their novel Ebony Gate, an Asian-inspired urban fantasy, was published by TOR in July 2023. Blood Jade releases in July of 2024.  Ebony Gate was a 2023 Golden Poppy Finalist for the Octavia E. Butler award.
people.name: Julia Vee

people.bio: Julie Nováková is a scientist, educator and award-winning Czech author, editor and translator of science fiction, fantasy and detective stories. Her work in English appeared in Clarkesworld, Asimov’s, Analog, and elsewhere. Her works have been translated into ten languages so far, and she translates Czech stories into English (in Tor.com, Strange Horizons, F&SF, Clarkesworld, and Welkin Magazine). She edited or co-edited four anthologies, most recently Life Beyond Us (Laksa Media, 2023). Julie’s own newest book is a story collection titled The Ship Whisperer (Arbiter Press, 2020). She is a recipient of the European fandom’s Encouragement Award and multiple Czech genre awards. She’s active in science outreach, education and nonfiction writing, and co-leads the outreach group of the European Astrobiology Institute. She’s a member of the XPRIZE Sci-fi Advisory Council.
people.name: Julie Novakova

people.bio: Juliet E McKenna is a British fantasy author. Her debut epic fantasy, The Thief's Gamble, appeared in 1999. In 2023 her 25th novel, The Green Man’s Quarry continues her popular contemporary fantasy series. She also returned to swords and sorcery with a female-centered Arthurian retelling, The Cleaving. She writes diverse shorter fiction, showcased in a 2024 collection for the Newcon Press Polestars series.  She reviews for genre magazines, teaches creative writing, comments on book trade issues, and has served as a judge for major genre awards. As J M Alvey, she has written historical murder mysteries set in ancient Greece.
people.name: Juliet E McKenna

people.bio:
Juliet Kemp (they/them) is a queer, non-binary, writer. They live in London by the river, with their partners, kid, and dog. The first book of their fantasy series, The Deep And Shining Dark was on the Locus 2018 Recommended Reads list; the fourth and final book, The City Revealed came out in 2023. Their short fiction has appeared in venues including Uncanny, Analog, and Cast of Wonders. They were short-listed for the WSFA Small Press Award in 2020 and 2023, and had a story in the 2021 Lambda Awards shortlisted anthology Trans-Galactic Bike Ride.

When not writing or child-wrangling, Juliet knits, indulges their fountain pen habit, and tries to fit an ever-increasing number of plants into a microscopic back garden. They can be found on Twitter as @julietk, on Mastodon as @juliet@zirk.us, and on Bluesky as @julietk.bsky.social.
people.name: Juliet Kemp

people.bio: Sunday Times bestselling author and creator of Doctor Who: Redacted.
people.name: Juno Dawson

people.bio: Justin C. Key is a speculative fiction writer and psychiatrist whose short stories have appeared in The Magazine of Fantasy & Science Fiction, Strange Horizons, Tor.com, Escape Pod, and Lightspeed. A graduate of Clarion West, his debut short story collection, The World Wasn't Ready For You, is out now from HarperCollins. When Justin isn’t writing, working with patients, or exploring Los Angeles with his wife, he’s chasing after his three young (and energetic!) children. You can follow his journey at www.justinckey.com
people.name: Justin C. Key

people.bio:
Justin spent 15 years as a professional writer and editor before his debut novel, Carpet Diem, was published in 2015. It became a best-seller and won a 2018 Audie award. His second book, The Lost War, won the 2020/21 SPFBO award and was picked up by Orbit as the first of the four-book Eidyn Saga.

Justin lives with his family in East Lothian, just outside his hometown of Edinburgh.
people.name: Justin Lee Anderson

people.bio: I am an SF and Fantasy writer, published since 1999, with books that span hard SF to frivolous entertainment. I mostly write about AI, cybernetics, found family, relationships and romance. My stories are often based in philosophical ponderings about life and the universe.
people.name: Justina Robson

people.bio: Master in English Literature by the Federal University of MInas Gerais in Brazil. Currently studying Creative Writing and researching the intersection between Fantasy, Mythology and Ecocriticism, through "The Chronicles of Narnia".
people.name: Júlia Cadar Cunha

people.bio: K. A. Laity is an award-winning author, scholar, filmmaker, critic, editor, and arcane artist. Current research includes medieval Scots, crime fiction/films, medievalism and gothic in the writings of Leonora Carrington.
people.name: K. A. Laity

people.bio:
As a kid, K.C. spent a great deal of time at a tool and die shop operating a forty-ton punch press and cutting metal with an electrical discharge machine. He spent most summers in Mexico, fishing with his dad or blowing things up with cheap m-80 firecrackers.

In high school, he organized book clubs on both the football and wrestling teams. They read Stephen King and Isaac Asimov on the long bus rides to and from competitions. In hindsight, K.C. realizes this could be why they lost so many games. Too much focus on robots and clowns.

He always knew he wanted to be a writer. And some have reported that he bleeds printer’s ink — but it’s probably just Oreos and caffeine.

After high school, he married his high school sweetheart (strangely enough, they first met in the infant care center where they were both born). He and his wife worked their way through college, had three amazing little humans of their own, and did their very best to act like responsible adults despite going slowly insane.

K.C. found that his dawning insanity was most helpful in writing stories. He cleared some space in the garage and raided yard sales for a suitable desk. Much of his writing took place in between feedings and diaper changes in the middle of the night. In time, he began having some success. Remember the Sunflowers and Progeny of the Storm were his first published short stories (both available on his website), and his first completed novel was a prize-winning finalist in Del Sol Press’ Best First Novel Competition. Her Gilded Voice will be his first published novel.

Currently, K.C. teaches Language Arts in Los Angeles County. When he isn’t teaching or spending time with his family, he is often lost in thought… the fragments of his next story clanking together like bits of metal from his childhood punch press.
people.name: K.C. Aegis

people.bio: Kai Ray is a writer and artist based in London, currently completing a MSc in Creative Writing at the University of Edinburgh. Much of her work explores the intersection of folklore, survival, and liminality. This takes many forms, dipping into cozy fantasy and speculative gothic horror as well as fantasy futurism. Her novels in progress address issues such as climate change, alienation, and generational trauma through the lens of whimsy and the eerie. Her first set of poems can be found in From Arthur’s Seat Volume 9. When she’s not writing, you can usually find her in the studio casting silver, painting, and sculpting Venetian papier mâché.
people.name: Kai Ray

people.bio: Dr Kanta Dihal (she/her) is a Lecturer at Imperial College London, where she runs the Master’s in Science Communication, and Associate Fellow of the Leverhulme Centre for the Future of Intelligence, University of Cambridge. Her research focuses on the portrayals and perceptions of AI across cultures, and how they help us think about ethics and bias in new technologies. She led the research project ‘Global AI Narratives’ from 2018–2022. She is co-editor of the books AI Narratives (2020) and Imagining AI (2023). She has a PhD from the University of Oxford on the communication of quantum physics.
people.name: Kanta Dihal

people.bio: Dean Graduate Education Tufts University School of Eng
people.name: Karen panetta

people.bio: Kari Sperring is a fantasy novelist and mediaeval historian from the UK. She is owned by cats and often wishes she was a musketeer.
people.name: Kari Sperring

people.bio: Karina Steffens lives in Dublin and co-owns a boutique web design agency. Born in Ukraine, she emigrated twice and settled down in Ireland at the turn of the millennium. A lifelong bookwyrm, she devoured science fiction, fantasy, and Slavic folklore and amassed a small hoard of books, which is yet to achieve L-Space or open a portal to another world. To help it along, she turned her hand to writing. Her studies include BAs in Communication and Journalism and International Relations. Her work has appeared in The Fairy Tale Magazine, Empyreome, Gathering Storm, and the anthology Runs Like Clockwork from Wyldblood Press.
people.name: Karina Steffens

people.bio: Swedish fan and filker. Interfilk guest at Consonance 2022, and has hosted the Eurofilk online filk circle every second week since 2020.
people.name: Karl-Johan Norén

people.bio: Karolina Fedyk writes speculative fiction and poetry about lost histories, found families, and futures born out of resistance and resilience. You can find their work in Lackington's, Fireside, Strange Horizons, and other venues.
people.name: Karolina Fedyk

people.bio: Freelance book editor specialising in sex, sleuths, swords and spaceships. I work with both self-publishing authors and traditional publishers. Fan of SFF, crime and historical fiction. Now my children are grown and living their amazing lives, I live in my wee Scottish cottage with my dog and two cats. Late-diagnosed AuDHD.
people.name: Kat @ Athena Copy

people.bio:
Kat Clay is an award-winning tabletop game writer, reviewer, and the GUFF delegate to Worldcon for 2024.

She is the author of two bestselling Call of Cthulhu games, The Hammersmith Haunting and The Well of All Fear. The latter won the silver ENNIE for Best Community Content at the 2024 Awards, and was also nominated for Best Adventure - Short Form. 

Her short stories have been published in Interzone, Cosmic Horror Monthly, and Aurealis. Her non-fiction and criticism has been published in The Guardian, Interzone, and Weird Fiction Review, and she was a contributor to the Locus winning and Hugo nominated Dangerous Visions and New Worlds: Radical Science Fiction, 1950 to 1985.

She has twice recieved the Ditmar Award for Best Fan Writer, acknowledging her contributions to Australian fandom through her blog and YouTube channel, where discusses writing for fiction and games.
people.name: Kat Clay

people.bio: Kat Kourbeti is a speculative fiction writer, culture critic, and podcaster based in London, UK. She is a Hugo-nominated and British Fantasy Award-winning podcast editor at Strange Horizons magazine. She writes a column on speculative theatre for the BSFA's Vector journal, and organises Spectrum, the largest critique group for SFF writers in the UK. Her day job is in theatre. You can find her on all social media as @darthjuno.
people.name: Kat Kourbeti

people.bio:
Katalina was Longlisted for Penguin Write Now 2020 and received a 2021 Ladies of Horror Fiction Writers Grant. They are published in various magazines and anthologies including Haunted Voices, Unspeakable, To Root Somewhere Beautiful, and Haunted Hallways and have appeared at Edinburgh International Book Festival, Cymera, and FIYAHCON. Katalina is represented by Robbie Guillory at Underline Literary.

Katalina is Literature Officer at Creative Scotland and previously worked in Audio and Digital for Canongate and Hachette and as founding Audio Director for khōréō (Winner 2022 Ignyte Award for Best Fiction Podcast; Shortlisted 2022 Ignyte Best Community Award; Nominated 2023 Hugo Award for Best Semiprozine). Katalina was the 2021 Next Level Awardee for Literature Alliance Scotland’s career development programme. They have worked in event programming for independent bookshops and studied English Literature at the University of Glasgow and Publishing at Edinburgh Napier University.

Katalina has appeared at numerous literary events for Edinburgh International Book Festival, Granite Noir, and FIYAHCON. They have led writing workshops for Cymera Festival, Scottish BPOC Writers Network, and SQIFF. She is a member of Codex and Society of Authors.

Katalina has mentored for the Society of Young Publishers Scotland and judged Scottish Book Trust’s 2023 New Writers Awards and 2024 Ignite Fellowship.
people.name: Katalina Watt

people.bio:
Kate Baker is the Podcast Director and Non-fiction Editor for Clarkesworld Magazine. She has been very privileged to narrate over 1000 short stories/poems by some of the biggest names in Science Fiction and Fantasy and related genres. 

She has been nominated for a Parsec Award, and a World Fantasy Award. Kate won the Hugo Award for Best Semiprozine in 2011 and 2013, the British Fantasy Award for Best Magazine in 2014 and the World Fantasy Award for Special Award: Non Professional in 2014 alongside the wonderfully talented editorial staff of Clarkesworld Magazine.

Kate has narrated a few audiobooks and has read for a variety of other venues including The Dark Magazine, Cast of Wonders, Beneath Ceaseless Skies, Podcastle, Mythic Delirium, StarShipSofa, Escape Pod, Nightmare Magazine, Mash Stories, and The Drabblecast.

Kate is also a professional SFF genre writer. You can find her short stories at various venues.
people.name: Kate Baker

people.bio: Kate is a video editor by day, science fiction and fantasy author by night. Her love for creating new worlds is fuelled by a steady diet of coffee, books, and Marvel movies, and when she's not telling stories, you can find her haunting London cafes like an over-caffeinated ghost. She currently has two science fiction novels out: Mindwalker and Mindbreaker, and her fantasy debut, Until We Shatter, will be following in October 2024
people.name: Kate Dylan

people.bio: Kate Elliott has been publishing science fiction and fantasy for over thirty years with a particular focus in immersive world building and epic stories of adventure & transformative cultural change. She’s written epic fantasy, space opera, science fiction, Young Adult fantasy, and the Afro-Celtic post-Roman alternate-history fantasy with lawyer dinosaurs, Cold Magic, as well as two novellas set in the Magic: The Gathering multiverse. Her work has been nominated for the Nebula, World Fantasy, Norton, and Locus Awards. Her novel Black Wolves won the RT Reviewers’ Choice Award for Best Epic Fantasy 2015. She lives in Hawaii, paddles outrigger canoes, and spoils her schnauzer.
people.name: Kate Elliott

people.bio: Dr Kate Forsyth is an award-winning Australian author best known for The Witches of Eileanan, a heroic fantasy named Best First Novel by Locus and Bitter Greens, a reimagining of ‘Rapunzel’ which won the American Library Award for Best Historical Fiction. Her most recent novels are Psykhe, a reimagining of the ancient Greek myth of ‘Eros and Psykhe’ and  The Crimson Thread, a retelling of the myth of the minotaur set in Crete during World War II which The Washington Review called ‘a riveting tale of courage, love, and betrayal’. She runs creative writing & literary retreats in Australia, Greece, the Cotswolds and Scotland.
people.name: Kate Forsyth

people.bio:
Kate is a general purpose nerd with interests in literature, fanfic and crafting. She co-leads fantasybookclub.org. In her spare time she is Director of Finance for a London university.

Kate paints mostly in watercolour, with excursions into other media.  She is exhibiting in the Art Show:
https://glasgow2024.org/artists/kate-towner/

Kate made the Glasgow2024 Tartan Armadillo, and regularly makes clothes without bothering with a pattern.
https://glasgow2024.org/blog/2023/10/how-to-make-a-tartan-armadillo-or-any-soft-toy-without-a-pattern/
people.name: Kate Towner

people.bio: Kate Watson is a PhD student in creative writing at the University of Exeter, with bylines including VICE Media. Her background is in the intersection between the STEM subjects and humanities – she is a practicing veterinary surgeon, holds degrees in computer science, veterinary medicine, and creative writing, and is a former Cambridge University Science Fiction Society Chairbeing. Kate is currently writing a biography of atomic pioneer Muriel Howorth. Her other academic interests include science communication, environmental futures in speculative fiction, and the nature of human authorship. She blogs about these and other issues at loreandordure.com
people.name: Kate Watson

people.bio: Kate has been a sci-fi fan since reading her way through the school library in alphabetical order (age 12). Since then, she has been an active participant in sci-fi and romance fandom.
people.name: Kate Wood

people.bio: Katherine Inskip is the Editor of Cast of Wonders, the YA speculative short fiction magazine/podcast, and an astrophysicist by trade. She is autistic, a mother to two autistic teens, and enjoys chaos, tree-climbing, and thwarting plans for world domination.  Katherine is addicted to chocolate, logic puzzles, and the social deduction game Blood on the Clocktower, and narrates for a variety of podcasts.
people.name: Katherine Inskip

people.bio: Kathleen Jennings is an illustrator and writer based in Brisbane, Australia. As an illustrator, she has won one World Fantasy Award (and been a finalist three other times), and has been shortlisted once for the Hugos, and once for the Locus Awards, as well as winning a number of Ditmars. As a writer, she has won a British Fantasy Award (the Sydney J Bounds Award) and two Ditmars and been shortlisted for World Fantasy Awards, the Courier-Mail People’s Choice Book of the Year Award, the Crawford Award, the Australian Shadows Award, the Eugie Foster Memorial Award, and several Aurealis Awards.
people.name: Kathleen Jennings

people.bio: Kathleen Kramer is the 2024 President Elect of IEEE, the world’s largest technical organization that is dedicated to advancing technology for humanity. She is also a Professor of Electrical Engineering at the University of San Diego, San Diego, CA, USA. Her technical interests are in multisensor data fusion and applications of neural and fuzzy systems to navigation and data security. She is a Distinguished Lecturer for IEEE Aerospace & Electronics Systems Society (AESS).  She was named a fellow of ABET for advances to the engineering criteria, including mechatronics and cyber security.
people.name: Kathleen Kramer

people.bio: Kathryn Sullivan writes stories where girls are the explorers, the wizards and the ones who solve problems and rescue people.
people.name: Kathryn Sullivan

people.bio:
Katrina Archer writes science fiction, fantasy, and romance. She has worked in aerospace, video games, and film, and is the editor of speculative climate fiction magazine Little Blue Marble.
Katrina’s work was a 2016 Library Journal Indie Ebook Awards Honorable Mention. She is an alumna of the Viable Paradise and Paradise Lost writing workshops, and a member of SFWA and Codex Writers.
She can operate almost any vehicle that can’t fly, doesn’t believe in life without books or chocolate, and with her spouse puts up with the antics of a sweet potato and a chaos goblin masquerading as cats.
people.name: Katrina Archer

people.bio: Chairman ConFiction 1990 worldcon, translator, worked on a number of worldcons as advisor and have been the adverisement sales man for the Souvenir Book for the last six or seven years. Worked on 2014 and 20109 cons; started in 1965 and attend Heicon 1970 in person.
people.name: Kees van Toorn

people.bio: Keith Williams is reader in English at the University of Dundee and convened its Science Fiction MLitt. He has published widely on late nineteenth and early twentieth century SF, including H.G. Wells, Modernity and the Movies (2007). He has been leading a major project to research and republish the work of a Scottish SF pioneer, contemporary to Stevenson and Conan Doyle. The first critical edition of a selection of his work, co-edited with Ari Brin, is forthcoming with Bloomsbury in February 2025: The Essential Robert Duncan Milne: Stories by the Lost Pioneer of Science Fiction.
people.name: Keith Williams

links.othersocialmedia: I have no personal social media footprint.

people.bio: Kelli Fitzpatrick is a sci-fi author, editor, and game writer. She won the 2016 Star Trek Strange New Worlds contest from Simon and Schuster and has written for the Star Trek Adventures tabletop roleplaying game. Her fiction has been published by Flash Fiction Online, Crazy 8 Press, and others, and she has written for the NASA Hubble Space Telescope Outreach team and Arizona State University’s Interplanetary Initiative. A former high school teacher, she is an advocate for public education, the arts, and gender rights and representation. Find her at KelliFitzpatrick.com and on Bluesky @KelliFitzWrites.
people.name: Kelli Fitzpatrick

people.bio: Kelly Kanayama is a pop culture and comics critic, editor and educator with a PhD in comics research. Born and raised in Hawaii but now living in Scotland, she has written for The Independent, the official 2000 AD website, Shelfdust, the Eisner-Award-nominated Critical Chips, Bitch Media, the Eisner-winning site Women Write About Comics, and Nerdist, among others. She is the Events and Editorial Manager for the Scottish BPOC Writers Network, is full of ridiculous facts about the pre-Disney Star Wars Expanded Universe, and is currently writing a book about the comics of Garth Ennis.
people.name: Kelly Kanayama

people.bio: Kelly Lonesome is a Hugo Award-nominated editor of novels and novellas. She joined Tor Publishing Group in 2019, and hasn't had a good night's sleep since then from all the nightmare fuel she gets to read at Nightfire! She has the privilege of working with terrifyingly talented authors like Catriona Ward, Gretchen Felker-Martin, Chuck Tingle, Lucy A. Snyder, Cassandra Khaw, and CJ Leede (among many others!).
people.name: Kelly Lonesome

people.bio: Kelly Sue DeConnick writes for comics, film, television, and stage. Notable comics include transforming Carol Danvers into CAPTAIN MARVEL at Marvel and creating WONDER WOMAN HISTORIA: THE AMAZONS at DC, the latter earning two Eisner Awards and marking DeConnick’s second occasion as a Hugo finalist. Her independent comics, BITCH PLANET and PRETTY DEADLY, have also garnered acclaim. Outside comics, DeConnick develops television, wrote stage show AWAKENING for the Wynn Resort Las Vegas, and founded the #VisibleWomen Project, promoting gender diversity in comics hiring. Her newest comic, the surrealist FML, is set to release from Dark Horse Comics later this year.
people.name: Kelly Sue DeConnick

people.bio: Ken MacLeod (he/him) is a celebrated SF writer who, over the course of his career, has written 18 novels, and has won multiple BSFA and Prometheus Awards, in addition to being shortlisted by the Hugos, Nebulas, Locus Awards, and more. Ken writes everything from dystopian SF to space opera, and is known for work that’s as engaged with politics as it is with science.
people.name: Ken MacLeod

people.bio: Keren Landsman is an Israeli, Luxembourg-based author, epidemiologist, and public health expert whose writing interests are primarily in creating dark speculative fiction, urban fantasy, and science fiction. Her first book, Broken Skies (2015), won the Geffen Award for Best Original Science Fiction or Fantasy Novel for 2015, and her second book, The Heart of The Circle (published by Angry Robot in 2019) won the Geffen Award for Best Original Science Fiction or Fantasy Novel for 2019. Her short stories have been winning awards since 2011 with “Schrödinger’s Gorgon”, published in More Zion’s Fiction short stories collection, and most recently in 2022 for a short titled “Dust”.
people.name: Keren Landsman

people.bio: Dr Kerry McInerney (she/her, chair) is a Senior Research Fellow at the Leverhulme Centre for the Future of Intelligence, where she co-chairs the Global Politics of AI research stream on how AI is impacting international relations. She is also an AHRC/BBC Radio 3 New Generation Thinker and a Research Fellow at the AI Now Institute. Her research focuses on the intersections of race, gender, AI and political violence, and she also teaches on the Leverhulme Centre’s AI Ethics Masters and MPhil programmes. She is the co-editor of Feminist AI and The Good Robot: Why Technology Needs Feminism.
people.name: Kerry McInerney

people.bio: Kerstin Hall is the author of Asunder, Star Eater, and the Mkalis Cycle. She lives in Cape Town, South Africa.
people.name: Kerstin Hall

people.bio:
I am a Librarian with Glasgow Libraries and have worked both within the Mitchell Library and Community Libraries.

I am currently Librarian for Hillhead Library and have a city wide responsibility for the purchase of fiction. This includes Sci Fi, Fantasy, Horror and Graphic Novels . I have a genuine interest in all of these categories with a specioal interst in speculative fiction. My favourite writers include Christopher Priest and Walter M Miller. 

I have experience of chairing author events and am on the steering Committe for the Byres Road Book Festival as well as working with local publishers to cteate a programme of free events for Library users.
people.name: Kevan Smith

people.bio: Kevin is a public defender in Atlanta, Georgia, USA who edits, produces, and creates music for the Hugo, Girl! podcast
people.name: Kevin Anderson

people.bio:
Kevin Roche is a research engineer at IBM Research Almaden, specializing in magnetoelectronics, spintronics, and related technologies, and an IBM Quantum Ambassador, leveraging his ability to explain weird science to almost anyone. 

Kevin is also a lifelong science fiction fan and costumer – he’s been making costumes since he was 8, and chaired Worldcon 76 in San Jose in 2018,  Costume-Con 26 in San Jose in 2008, and Westercon 66 in Sacramento in 2013 with his husband Andy --after their Olive Country hoax/party went viral in site selection. Kevin is currently president of both the International Costumers’ Guild and San Francisco Science Fiction Conventions, Inc (SFSFC)

His creation, Thinbot, is the 4x gold-medalist in robotic bartending at Robogames, and his San Jose Galactic LIght Tower, a 32’ replica of the historic San Jose Electric Light Tower. won gold for Static Art Bots at the 2018 Robogames. . He’s also the editor of Yipe! The Costume Fanzine of Record (www.yipezine.com),
people.name: Kevin Roche

people.bio: Senior Writer at Larian Studios - Divinity: Original Sin 2 and Baldur's Gate 3. Proud father of Beast, Lae'zel of K'liir, and Wyll Ravengard.
people.name: Kevin VanOrd

people.bio: Khan has a past as a poet, cellist, arts funder and internationally known hula hooper. His debut novel, The Circus Infinite, was published by Angry Robot Books in 2022. It was longlisted for the BSFA Best Novel category, and was a finalist for the Lambda Literary Award. His next novel, Down in the Sea of Angels, will be published by Angry Robot in 2025.
people.name: Khan Wong

people.bio: Kieron Gillen is a writer best known as co-creator of comics such as The Wicked + the Divine, DIE and Once & Future, as well as his many works for Marvel comics. He is based in London.
people.name: Kieron Gillen

people.bio: Kim Whysall-Hammond is a Londoner who now lives deep in the English countryside. She has worked in Climate Research and in Telecommunications. Her poem, As slow as Starlight, tied for third place in the 2023 Dwarf Star award. Other poems have appeared in Andromeda Spaceways, Dreams and Nightmares, Eternal Haunted Summer, Frozen Wavelets, Kaleidotrope, On Spec, Silver Blade, Star*line and The Dread Machine. Her chapbook, Messages from the Road, will be published by Palewell Press in Autumn 2024.
people.name: Kim Whysall-Hammond

people.bio: Associate Professor of Philosophy, Faculty of Humanities, Chiba University, Japan.
people.name: Koji Tachibana

people.bio: Kola is a writer and researcher based in Palo Alto, California, where he is pursuing a PhD in Stanford University's Modern Thought and Literature program. His fiction is about people and their entanglements with climate, art, virtuality, and magic. You can find his stories in Strange Horizons, Logic(s), Reckoning, and other places.
people.name: Kola Heyward-Rotimi

people.bio:
I have a background in software engineering (MSc) and interaction design research. I currently work as a senior researcher at RISE Research Institutes of Sweden, where I have focused on AI, decision support and digital ethics since four years. In addition to applied research, I hold talks and workshops on the practice and ethics of generative AI. 

Hobbies include reading (a lot, preferably science fiction but also fantasy, mainstream, mysteries), painting (mostly digital but also water colour and urban sketching), board gaming, rpgs, larps, hiking, cooking.
people.name: Kristina Knaving

people.bio:
Kristina Pérez is the Managing Director of Pérez Literary & Entertainment, a full-service agency based in the heart of London. She has a decade of experience in publishing as both an author and an agent. She was born and raised in the Big Apple by an Argentine dad and a Norwegian mom, speaking three languages at home. 

Kristina's first great literary love was Arthurian legend which led her to reading Anglo-Saxon, Norse and Celtic studies for her BA and completing a PhD in Medieval Literature at the University of Cambridge. Her monograph, The Myth of Morgan la Fey was published by Palgrave Macmillan, using feminist psychoanalysis to recenter the famed sorceress at the heart of the Arthurian tradition.

Kristina has also written several novels for young adults. The Sweet Black Waves trilogy (Macmillan) draws on Kristina’s expertise in medieval literature to retell the legend of Tristan and Isolde, while The Tesla Legacy (Tor Teen) reimagines the classic superhero origin story with a precocious female scientist at its helm. Kristina’s first novel for adults, The Many Lies of Veronica Hawkins  is a thriller set in Hong Kong (Little,Brown/Pegasus).

Being both an agent and an author allows Kristina to fully guide her clients through every step of the publishing process. She loves launching debut authors’ careers as well as working with mid-career authors looking for new challenges. Kristina sees each client relationship as a true partnership in which they develop the right strategy for a client’s career together.
people.name: Kristina Perez

people.bio: Krys Keller, admin and co-chair,  The Expanse Geeks on Facebook (17,000 international members) is an original Screaming Firehawk. She taught creative writing at NYU and is currently living and writing in New York City. She has spoken on SRO panels in Denver, LA, New Orleans, Silicon Valley Con with Adam Savage, Dragon Con San Diego Comic Con, and other venues, and co-chaired Oslo and New York City Expanse fan meetups.
people.name: Krys Keller

people.bio: L.R. Lam was first Californian and now Scottish. Lam is the Sunday Times Bestselling and award-winning author of Dragonfall (the Dragon Scales trilogy), the Seven Devils duology (co-written with Elizabeth May), Goldilocks, the Pacifica novels False Hearts and Shattered Minds, and the Micah Grey trilogy, which begins with Pantomime. They are also a writing coach at The Novelry.
people.name: L.R. Lam

people.bio:
LIZA GROEN TROMBI is the four-time Hugo Award winning Publisher and Editor-in-Chief of Locus Magazine. A life-long reader of science fiction, fantasy, and horror, she studied literature, history, and translation at university, and worked in several fields before joining the magazine in early 2003. She has been Editor-in-Chief and Publisher since 2009. Trombi also participates in convention panels and awards juries, runs the Locus Awards Weekend and writing workshops, publishes books with Locus Press, and serves as board president of the Locus Science Fiction Foundation.

She lives in California with her two daughters and a little dog, too.
people.name: LIZA GROEN TROMBI

people.bio: LaShawn M. Wanak writes short fiction, essays, and poetry. She served as the lead writer for Meow Wolf's "The Real Unreal" immersive art exhibit permanently open in Grapevine, Tx, and she is the editor-in-chief of the online speculative magazine GigaNotoSaurus.
people.name: LaShawn M. Wanak

people.bio:
After doing time at several NY publishers, Laura Anne went freelance, a decision she sometimes second-guesses, but never regrets.

Her books have been hailed as “a true American myth” by NPR, and praised for “deft plotting and first-class characters” by Publishers Weekly. Her work includes the Devil’s West trilogy, the Cosa Nostradamus  series, the Huntsmen novels, and several story collections.  Her Patreon also spawned the non-fiction collections, I have Strong Opinions and I Have (More) Strong Opinions.

Laura Anne lives in Seattle with a cat, a dog, and many deadlines.
people.name: Laura Anne Gilman

people.bio: Laura Antoniou has been writing erotica for over thirty years. Best known for her Marketplace series, she has also edited and appeared in many anthologies. The Killer Wore Leather, is her award-winning comedy murder mystery set at leather/BDSM convention. She also collaborated with Cecilia Tan and Midori on a 3-novella erotic, time-shifting, alt-Japan fantasy tale titled Silk Threads. Find her at patreon/kvetch or facebook.com/NYCKvetch.
people.name: Laura Antoniou

people.bio: Laura Pearlman’s short fiction has appeared in Nature, Shimmer, Flash Fiction Online, and a handful of other places. Her LOLcat captions have appeared in McSweeney’s. She edits the feline speculative fiction podcast CatsCast. She has a tragically neglected blog called Unlikely Explanations and can be found on Bluesky at @laurasbadideas.bsky.social.
people.name: Laura Pearlman

people.bio: Dr. Laura Woodney is a planetary scientist, physics professor,  and longtime science fiction fan.  She specializes in studying small icy bodies in the solar system (comets, Centaurs, anything too small to be a spheroid that has ice). She's worked on mission concept design for NASA, loves teaching physics and also knitting and cats.
people.name: Laura Woodney

people.bio: Lauren Beukes is the award-winning South African author of six novels, a short story collection and NYT-best-selling graphic novels, including Zoo City which won the Arthur C Clarke Award and the Kitschies Red Tentacle, The Shining Girls, now a major AppleTV show with Elisabeth Moss, and, most recently, the reality-bending mother-daughter-dreamworm novel, Bridge. Her work has been translated into 25 languages and she's also worked in kids animation, TV scriptwriting and directed an award-winning documentary.
people.name: Lauren Beukes

people.bio:
Laurence Raphael Brothers is a writer and a technologist with five patents and a background in AI and Internet R&D.

His noir urban fantasy novella series consisting of The Demons of Wall Street, The Demons of the Square Mile, and The Demons of Chiyoda has recently added a new volume, The Demons of Montmartre. while his latest standalone novel is a psychedelic transapocalyptic fantasy, “The World's Shattered Shell”.

He has published over 50 short stories in such magazines as Nature, PodCastle, and Galaxy's Edge. His story “Houseproud” won an “Intelligence in Fiction” award from the Berkeley Machine Intelligence Research Institute.

Laurence is a member of SFWA and Codex. He attended the Viable Paradise workshop.

Pronouns: he/him.
people.name: Laurence Raphael Brothers

people.bio: Lawrence Schick is a game designer and writer mainly known for role-playing games. At TSR in the late 1970s he was a game designer and head of the editorial staff. In the early 1980s he moved to video and computer games and has done most of his work in digital media since then. At AOL in the late 1990s, he was influential in the birth of online gaming. He was “Loremaster” for The Elder Scrolls Online and Principal Narrative Designer for Baldur’s Gate 3. He writes, edits, and translates historical fiction under the name Lawrence Ellsworth.
people.name: Lawrence Schick

people.bio: Leadie Jo Flowers received a BA from Stetson University in English and Russian studies. Also, she holds a Master of Fine Arts Writing Popular Fiction from Seton Hill University. She teaches English to private and business students and has taught at Moscow State University and The Russian Academy of Public Relations. Currently she is working on a global website for authors, educators and fans to grow the use of science fiction in the classroom, increasing students critical thinking skills and imagination as well as interest in STEM classes and careers. Her short stories have been published in three anthologies.
people.name: Leadie Jo Flowers

people.bio: Lettie Prell’s science fiction stories often explore people merging with their technology, touching on topics of transhumanism and artificial intelligence. She has also explored justice-related themes, which stem from her long-standing career as a researcher in that field. Her work has appeared in Analog, Apex, Clarkesworld, Tordotcom, Wired, and elsewhere. Various works have been reprinted in anthologies, including The Best American Science Fiction and Fantasy, “best of” publications curated by Neil Clarke and Rich Horton, and The New Voices of Science Fiction (Tachyon). Several of her stories have been translated into Chinese, Japanese, and other languages. She lives in the Midwestern region of the United States.
people.name: Lettie Prell

people.bio: Lev Grossman is the author of the New York Times bestselling Magicians trilogy. His new book, The Bright Sword, is a reimagining of the legend of King Arthur.
people.name: Lev Grossman

people.bio: Lezli Robyn is a mostly-blind Australian author, as well as executive editor and associate publisher of Arc Manor and its three imprints, who lives in Myrtle Beach, South Carolina, with her blue-eyed chiweenie, Bindi (which means “little girl” in several indigenous Australian dialects). Lezli's known for writing bittersweet fiction, her public speaking on editorial process, as well as being a lover of chocolate and gardening who is forever drawn by the call of the ocean.
people.name: Lezli Robyn

people.bio: Liat Shahar Kashtan is the chairperson of The Israeli Society for Science Fiction and Fantasy and head of the anti-harassment team in the Israeli cons for many years. She is also an agronomist, and divides her time between nurturing plants and sci-fi and fantasy communities.
people.name: Liat Shahar Kashtan

people.bio: Dr. Lilith Acadia is a visiting professor at Heidelberg University, an assistant professor at National Taiwan University, Taiwan Literature Base 2024–2025 Writer-in-Residence, and PI of a lit lab funded by the Taiwan National Science and Technology Council researching AI in SciFi. Lilith received a PhD from Berkeley, fellowships including Fulbright and Marie Curie, and publishes academic and speculative fiction work. Connect on Twitter and Instagram: @acadialogue
people.name: Lilith Acadia

people.bio: Linda’s first Worldcon was Noreascon I (1971), where she attended her first WSFS Business Meeting and was secretary of those annual meetings from 2008-2022 (with one break). Linda also served as WSFS Division Head for Sasquan in 2015 and DisCon III in 2021. Linda was thrilled to be awarded the Big Heart Award in 2021.
people.name: Linda Deneroff

people.bio: Lindsey is a historian and author. Her debut novel will be released in 2025. Specializing in speculative fiction, Lindsey's work primarily focuses on tightly character driven narratives that challenge social dogmas.
people.name: Lindsey Byrd

people.bio: Lisa Padol is a second generation SF fan, a filker, a gamer, playtester and editor of games, and a player and writer of LARPS. She sings adequately and consistently fails to identify harp tunes when her husband, Joshua Kronengold, is noodling around on the harp.
people.name: Lisa Padol

people.bio: Scottish-American writer of SF, fantasy and horror since the 1970s. Recent books include The Curious Affair of the Missing Mummies (Jo Fletcher Books), My Death (NYRB) and Riding the Nightmare (Valancourt). Writes a monthly roundup review column for The Guardian.
people.name: Lisa Tuttle

people.bio: Liz is one-third of the Hugo-nominated podcast Octothorpe, where she pontificates about fandom, conrunning, awards, and other items of fannish interest. When not keeping up with fannish news, she is a scientist specialising in genomics and molecular microbiology of infectious disease, and currently works on tropical infectious disease research in southeast Asia.
people.name: Liz Batty

people.bio: Liz Bourke holds a Ph.D in Classics from Trinity College, Dublin. She's written about SFF for Locus Magazine and Reactor Magazine (formerly Tor.com), among other places. Her first book, Sleeping With Monsters, a collection of reviews and criticism, was published in 2017 by Aqueduct Press. She lives in Ireland with her wife, an insomniac small child, and their two very put-upon cats.
people.name: Liz Bourke

people.bio: Ljiljana Trajkovic received the Dipl. Ing. degree from University of Pristina, Yugoslavia, the M.Sc. degrees in electrical engineering and computer engineering from Syracuse University, Syracuse, NY, and the Ph.D. degree in electrical engineering from University of California at Los Angeles. She is currently a professor in the School of Engineering Science, Simon Fraser University, Burnaby, British Columbia, Canada. Her research interests include communication networks and dynamical systems. She served as IEEE Division X Delegate/Director (2019–2020), President of the IEEE Systems, Man, and Cybernetics Society (2014–2015), and President of the IEEE Circuits and Systems Society (2007). Dr. Trajkovic serves as Editor-in-Chief of the IEEE Transactions on Human-Machine Systems and Associate Editor-in-Chief of the IEEE Open Journal of Systems Engineering. She served as a Distinguished Lecturer of the IEEE Circuits and System Society (2021–2022, 2010–2011, 2002–2003) and a Distinguished Lecturer of the IEEE Systems, Man, and Cybernetics Society (2020–2021). She is a Fellow of the IEEE.
people.name: Ljiljana Trajkovic

people.bio: Dr Lois Wilson-McFarland is a Lecturer in Religion and Literature at the School of Divinity, University of Edinburgh. She is part of the steering committee for the Scottish Network for Religion and Literature and the New College Festival of Books and Belief. Her areas of research include speculative fiction, religion, feminist/womanist/queer theory, affect and ecology.
people.name: Lois Wilson-McFarland

people.bio:
Lola Johnson is the Dyer and Designer behind Third Vault Yarns. They take inspiration from Science Fiction and Fantasy and incorporate it into their fibre art.

They also publish TTRPGs under the umbrella Johnson Ofair. They like to write games that explore challenging themes, help people envision kinder worlds, radicalise people to push for change and make a difference by challenging norms. You can find them Dyeing, Knitting, Writing or Playing TTRPGs for stream.
people.name: Lola

people.bio: Co-host of the Hugo, Girl! podcast
people.name: Lori Anderson
Lorraine Wilson

people.bio: Lucy A. McLaren is a fantasy author and professional counsellor, passionate about writing stories that include a realistic representation and exploration of mental health issues. She is a lifelong fan of fantasy stories, and enjoys reading, writing, watching and playing them. McLaren’s debut novel, Awakening: The Commune’s Curse Book 1, released from Santa Fe Writers Project in May 2022. She also has a fantasy short story featured in the Reign of Fire anthology which released from Dragon Soul Press in January 2023.
people.name: Lucy A. McLaren

people.bio: Lucy Holland is the author of The Times bestselling Sistersong, which was a finalist for the Goldsboro Books Glass Bell Award and the British Fantasy Award for Best Novel in 2022. Her second historical fantasy novel, Song of the Huntress, is published by Pan Macmillan in 2024. As Lucy Hounsom, she wrote the Worldmaker Trilogy. She worked twelve years in corporate account sales for Waterstones Booksellers before becoming a full-time author. Lucy co-hosts the intersectional feminist podcast ‘Breaking the Glass Slipper’, which won Best Audio in the 2019 British Fantasy Awards. She lives in Devon.
people.name: Lucy Holland

people.bio: Luise is a third year PhD candidate at the University of Glasgow. Her research is interdisciplinary, combining literary criticism and in particular fantasy studies with biblical reception history. In her thesis, she is looking at SFF from around the 1990s that engages with Genesis and the Book of Revelation.
people.name: Luise Roessel

people.bio: Luke Elliott is a writer whose speculative fiction has appeared in Reckoning, Metaphorosis, and the Buckman Journal, among other magazines and podcasts. He is also the co-host of the “Ink to Film” podcast where he discusses books and their film adaptations from a craft perspective with a filmmaker co-host and industry guests. He has an MFA in Writing Popular Fiction from Seton Hill University and is a graduate of the Viable Paradise writer’s workshop. Originally from Central Florida, Luke now lives with his wife and the dogs he spoils like children in Portland, Oregon, USA.
people.name: Luke Elliott

people.bio:
Lyda Morehouse came out as a lesbian when Ronald Reagan was president, Act Up was staging Kiss-Ins at the Mall, and the AIDS crisis was in full swing. Though it took almost two decades until its publication, it was in this political environoment that the seeds of her first novel, the Shamus Award winning and Locus Award nominated novel Arcangel Protocol were germinated. She followed that book up with the rest of the five book trilogy: Fallen Host, Messiah Node, Apocalypse Array (Philip K Dick Special Citation of Excellence winner), and Resurrection Code. 

Lyda has since faded in and out of obscurity, remade herself as best-selling paranormal author Tate Hallway (the Garnet Lacey Series, the Vampire Princess of St. Paul series, and the Alex Conner series) and has written over a million words of anime fanfic pseudonymously.  She is still publishing and will have a new science fiction book, Welcome to Boy.net, out in 2024 from Wizard’s Tower Press (UK).

Like her writing career, Lyda’s sense of her own queerness is ever expanding. She lives in St. Paul, Minnesota (USA), with her wife of over thirty years, and their grown son.
people.name: Lyda Morehouse

people.bio: Lynda Clark is a writer, maker of interactive things and alleged academic. Her novel Beyond Kidding (Fairlight Books, 2019) is currently being developed as a feature film by writer/director William Stefan Smith (Top Boy; Avenue 5; The Vince Staples Show). Her short story collection Dreaming in Quantum (Fairlight Books, 2021) includes the highly acclaimed 'Ghillie's Mum', which was shortlisted for the BBC Short Story Award and Tom Gallon Prize and won the Commonwealth Prize for Europe and Canada. She is Lecturer in Creative Writing for Interdisciplinary Futures at the University of Edinburgh and is particularly interested in strange and non-human voices.
people.name: Lynda Clark

people.bio: Lyndsey is a Scottish author of strange and speculative fiction based in Edinburgh. She writes stories inspired by Scottish folklore, nature and the environment, and often the dark side of technology. Her work has been published or forthcoming in several magazines and anthologies, including with Flash Fiction Online, Analog, Apex, and PseudoPod. She's a Scottish Book Trust New Writers Awardee, British Fantasy Award Finalist, former Hawthornden Fellow, and a Ladies of Horror Fiction Writers Grant Recipient. Her debut novelette Have You Decided on Your Question was published in 2023 with Shortwave Publishing, and she has a number of longer projects in the works. Find out more about her and her work http://www.lyndseycroal.co.uk
people.name: Lyndsey Croal

people.bio: Lyndsey Luther is fantasy author and costumer. She has been a writer for Reactor (fka TOR.com) for almost ten years and works the Renaissance Faire circuit as a stage combatant in New England, USA.
people.name: Lyndsey Luther

people.bio:
M E Rodman writes LGBTQ+ fantasy with elements of horror and crime, and themes of family, personhood and the Other. Their short fiction has appeared in anthologies; Airship Shape and Bristol Fashion, Fire, Goddesses of the Sea and online at Expanded Horizons and Zetetic, a Record of Unusual Inquiry.

Their short story ‘The Selkie; A Tale of Love, Obsession and the Sea,’ was adapted and performed as a live radio play for the Sanctum Project in 2015. And their novella, Clockwork Sister, was longlisted for the BFSA Awards, 2021.

Currently living near Glasgow, with their partner, child and small dog, they have a deep love of liminal spaces, abandoned places and, most especially, bogs.
people.name: M E Rodman

people.bio: M. H. Ayinde was born in London’s East End. She is a runner, a lapsed martial artist, and a screen time enthusiast. Her debut novel A SONG OF LEGENDS LOST, the first in an epic fantasy trilogy, will be published by Orbit UK in April 2025. Her short fiction has appeared in FIYAH Literary Magazine, F&SF, Fantasy Magazine, and elsewhere, and she was the 2021 winner of the Future Worlds Prize. She lives in London with three generations of her family and their Studio Ghibli obsession.
people.name: M H Ayinde

people.bio: M V Melcer is the author of science fiction novel Refractions. Her critically acclaimed short fiction has appeared in Clarkesworld, GigaNotoSurus, Daily Science Fiction, Nature, and others. Born in Poland, M V has lived in the USA, the Netherlands and Belgium before settling in the United Kingdom. When not writing, she is pursuing a degree in astronomy.
people.name: M V Melcer

people.bio:
M. Darusha Wehm is the Nebula Award-nominated and Sir Julius Vogel Award-winning author of the interactive fiction game The Martian Job, as well as over a dozen novels including the Andersson Dexter cyberpunk detective series and the humorous coming-of-age novel The Home for Wayward Parrots. 
Darusha is a member of the Many Worlds writing collective and their short fiction and poetry have appeared in many venues, including Strange Horizons, Terraform and Nature. Their poetry has been a finalist for the Rhysling Award.
Originally from Canada, Darusha lives in Te Whanganui-a-Tara Wellington, Aotearoa New Zealand after several years sailing the Pacific.
people.name: M. Darusha Wehm

people.bio: Maya Evan MacGregor (Maighea Eòghainn MacGriogair) is a bilingual Nebula-nominated author of fantasy for adults and young adults and an award-winning Gaelic singer-songwriter who has represented Scotland internationally both chorally and solo. Maya is a fluent Gaelic speaker and writes in both English and Gaelic.
people.name: ME MacGriogair / Maya MacGregor

people.bio: Maciej Matuszewski is a conrunner fan and mathematical physicist, currently working at the University of Durham. Having started researching String Theory, Maciej now focuses on the pedagogy of mathematics in Higher Education, with a particular focus on automated e-assessment.
people.name: Maciej Matuszewski

people.bio: Con-runner, gamer.
people.name: Mad Elf

people.bio:
Japanese SF fan
Head of the secretariat of SF seminar
people.name: Madamrobot

people.bio: Maddy Belton is a Literary Agent at Madeleine Milburn Literary Agency, specialising in SFF and working across the children's and adult markets.
people.name: Maddy Belton

people.bio:
Australian author Madeline Te Whiu.
Genre; New Adult Fantasy, Dark Fantasy, Romantasy.

Work(s):
The Assassin Thief
The Soul Thief

Shortlisted for the West Australian Premier Award's Prize for Emerging Writers (2023) with her debut novel.
Guest author at Supanova Comicon Supanova Gaming 2023 (Adelaide and Brisbane events) + upcoming Melbourne, Gold Coast, Sydney, and Perth Supanova (2024)
Guest author at Perth Festival Writers Weekend (panel appearance)
people.name: Madeline Te Whiu

people.bio: I am a VFX artist and speculative fiction fan. I have worked on Star Trek Beyond, Cloud Atlas, Jupiter Ascending, Matrix Resurrections, Avengers Infinity Wars, Black Panther, Flash and Meg 2. I specialise in creating large scale environments and have been working at DNEG for the last 8 years. DNEG is the principle VFX studio for the Dune movies, Blade Runner 2049 and all of Christopher Nolans films.
people.name: Mak Knighton

people.bio: Malka Older is a writer, aid worker, and sociologist. Her science-fiction political thriller Infomocracy was named among the best books of 2016 by Kirkus; with sequels, it was finalist for a Hugo award. The Mimicking of Known Successes, a murder mystery set on Jupiter, was published in 2023 to rave reviews. The sequel, The Imposition of Unnecessary Obstacles, came out in February 2024. She is a Faculty Associate at Arizona State University, where she teaches on predictive fictions. Her opinions can be found in The New York Times, The Nation, and Foreign Policy, among other places.
people.name: Malka Older

people.bio: Maquel A. Jacob is an author of gender shifter social science fiction with a bit of romance and a touch of gore. She originally hails from Chicago Il and currently resides in the Pacific Northwest. She has three different series. You can find her short stories in various anthologies and magazines. She holds degrees in Accounting, Business Administration, and Digital Film and Video. Maquel was Head of Programming for Orycon41 and 42, and an instructor at the 2022 Cascade Writers Critique Workshop. She is a member of SFWA, PNWA, NIWA, and ALLi.
people.name: Maquel A. Jacob

people.bio: As a fine art professional, Mar has wielded katanas and handled Lady Gaga's shoes. As a veterinary assistant, she has cared for hairless cats, hedgehogs, and, one time, a coyote. As a writer (under Marissa James or Mar Vincent), her short fiction can be found in Escape Pod, Fusion Fragment, Apex's Robotic Ambitions anthology, and many other publications. She is a Pushcart Prize and Coyotl Award nominee,  a reader for Interstellar Flight Press, and a graduate of the Wayward Wormhole. She resides in the Pacific Northwest or can be found on various social media @MaroftheBooks.
people.name: Mar Vincent

people.bio: A fan and conrunner from Poland. He loves travelling to conventions and blogs about them and fandom at www.FandomRover.com. In 2018 he was a GUFF delegate. During this trip he attended Continuum 14 in Melbourne. So far he visited over 250 cons and doesn’t plan to stop at that. Currently Marcin administers European Fan Fund and chairs local SFF club in Kraków.
people.name: Marcin 'Alqua' Klak

people.bio:
Marcus Gipps was an influential sales manager with Blackwells flagship store – the British Book Awards winning Charing Cross branch – where he masterminded bookselling for Latitude Festival and the Jewish Book Week, among others, and was a print-on-demand pioneer. He joined Gollancz as an editor in 2011, commissioned his first two authors within three months, snapped up Saladin Ahmed’s award-winning debut novel, and embarked on some innovative publishing and a personal project, republishing Quentin Blake’s much-loved and then out of print Uncle stories.

Marcus was identified as a 2012 Bookseller Rising star, and began to divide his time between working on classic SFF – including the complete update and republication of Michael Moorcock’s body of work – and publishing original novels. He stepped up to become Editorial Director of the SFF Gateway, the worlds largest digital SFF collection, in 2017, and again to become Publishing Director of Gollancz in 2020. He counts Andrzej Sapkowski (whose work is the basis of Netflix’s The Witcher series), Joe Hill, Ursula K. le Guin, Lucy Kissick, Karen Lord, Stephen Baxter, Stephen Donaldson and M. John Harrison among his authors.
people.name: Marcus Gipps (Gollancz)

people.bio: I'm a retired educational laboratory technician best known as a role playing game designer, most notable for the Forgotten Futures and Diana: Warrior Princess RPGs. I also write fanfic, with an emphasis on weird crossovers, and have published more than 200 stories.
people.name: Marcus Rowland

people.bio:
Marguerite Kenner (she/her) is a California transplant living in the UK. She is the President and CEO of  Escape Artists Foundation, a US 501(c)(3) nonprofit bringing free and accessible speculative fiction to a global audience.

A practicing technology lawyer, Marguerite loves doing voice work for podcasts and playing video games, often where people can watch. She is a multiple Hugo finalist, the former editor of Cast of Wonders, and teaches business skills to indie creatives.
people.name: Marguerite Kenner

people.bio: Stories and poems by Mari Ness have appeared in Tor.com, Clarkesworld, Uncanny, Lightspeed, Nightmare, Apex, Beneath Ceaseless Skies, Reckoning, Nature Futures, Baffling, Diabolical Plots, Strange Horizons, and many more zines and anthologies. She lives in central Florida.
people.name: Mari Ness

people.bio: Maria Haskins is a Swedish-Canadian writer and reviewer of speculative fiction. She is a fiction editor at House of Gamut, and a staff writer at psychopomp.com. Currently, she’s located just outside Vancouver with two kids, a husband, a snake, several noisy birds, and a very large black dog. Her work is available in the short story collection Wolves & Girls and in the short story collection Six Dreams About the Train. Maria’s work has appeared in several publications and anthologies, including Best Horror of the Year, Nightmare, Lightspeed, The Deadlands, Beneath Ceaseless Skies, The Deadlands, and elsewhere.
people.name: Maria Haskins

people.bio:
A true bibliophile, Maria has been an avid reader since the age of 5 and an active writer since the age of 12.
She's the author of the comedic fantasy novel Saving Hell, a supernatural joint through a surprisingly pleasant Hell. 
Maria has a bachelor’s degree in Popular Fiction from the South Gate Creative Writing School, as well as a master’s degree in Creative Writing from the University of Dundee.
people.name: Maria Sjöstrand

people.bio: Mariana Rios Maldonado holds a PhD in Comparative Literature from the University of Glasgow. Her research focuses on philosophy and Otherness in Tolkien’s literary production as well as Germanophonic fantastic literature between the 19th and 20th centuries. Her most recent chapter was published in the edited collection The Romantic Spirit in the Works of J.R.R. Tolkien (2024). Mariana is the Officer for Equality and Diversity at Glasgow University’s Centre for Fantasy and the Fantastic and part of the editorial team for Mallorn, the Tolkien Society’s academic journal. She is the Research Impact Adviser for Glasgow’s Research and Innovation Services.
people.name: Mariana Rios Maldonado

people.bio:
Marianna “Kisu” Leikomaa has managed to do a lot during her years in fandom. She discovered fandom through Finnish Tolkien Society and quickly found out there was no way back.

Kisu has, for example: written for fanzines,  reviewed books and short stories, translated novels, short stories and articles, been in award juries, founded a smial, written filks, and of course been involved in various roles in organising various events of various shapes and sizes.

Her main fandom interests are Discworld, Tolkien, and she is especially obsessed with The Sandman. She sings loudly off-key.
people.name: Marianna "Kisu" Leikomaa

people.bio: Nebula nominated author Marie Vibbert's short fiction has appeared in top magazines like Nature, Analog, and Clarkesworld, and been translated into Czech, Chinese and Vietnamese. Her debut novel, Galactic Hellcats, was long listed by the British Science Fiction Award and her work has been called "everything science fiction should be" by the Oxford Culture Review. She also writes poetry, comics, and computer games. By day she is a computer programmer in Cleveland, Ohio.
people.name: Marie Vibbert

people.bio: Marina Berlin is a writer and media critic who grew up speaking three languages. She holds degrees in sociology and film, and is the creator and host of Pop Culture Sociologist - a podcast that analyzes media from a social perspective. Her words have appeared in Strange Horizons, IGN, Vice, Tor and many other outlets. She's currently working on her first novel, which was included on the honor list for the Otherwise Fellowship, dedicated to encouraging the exploration and expansion of gender in SF/F. You can chat with her on twitter at @berlin_marina, or read more of her work on her website.
people.name: Marina Berlin

people.bio: Marita Arvaniti is a Greek PhD student in the University of Glasgow, investigating the representations of theatre in contemporary Fairy Fantasy literature. She is a member of the Centre for Fantasy and the Fantastic. Marita recently directed a production of Nicholas Stuart Gray's 1963 fantasy play The Seventh Swan with her amateur dramatics group Puck's Players and always has something to say about puppets, theatre, fairies, folk horror or anything else you could possibly think to ask her about.
people.name: Marita

people.bio: Mark Gerrits is a civil service software developer by day and a board game designer by night. His published games include SteamRollers, Mini Rails, Mini Express, and most recently Lacuna, a cosy game of mystical geography. He lives in Leuven, Belgium, across from the Tree of Great Sorrow.
people.name: Mark Gerrits

people.bio: Physicist, chemical engineer, teacher, science writer, public engager, unrecognised literary genius.
people.name: Mark Haw

people.bio: Mark Plummer has been enjoying science fiction since he was a child and publishing fanzines and running conventions since he was in his early twenties, all of which started in a previous century; this might be why he's interested in fan history. He has been a judge for the Arthur C Clarke Award and involved with the running of the BSFA and the Friends of the SF Foundation, and has won a plethora of awards too, mostly for fanzines. He has been researching the minutiae of British fandom in the 1930s and 1940s for Fancyclopedia 3 and is unable to function without Claire Brialey.
people.name: Mark Plummer

people.bio: Mark Sabalauskas is the Indie-Groundbreaker nominated designer of Return to the Stars, an optimistic SciFi tabletop RPG that mashes up sci-fi exploration with fan culture. In 2023 Return to the Stars was covered in Polygon's article The Future of Tabletop Roleplay is Hope. Mark is a member of SFWA and they publish The Stellar Beacon zine, which features fiction, adventures and essays by noted SFF writers and game designers.
people.name: Mark Sabalauskas

people.bio: Mark Tompkins’ debut novel, The Last Days of Magic (published by Penguin Random House), was hailed by The Washington Post as “a beautifully detailed book and an entertaining read” and named one of the best new books by People Magazine. His new novel, How to End the World,  is a neo-noir detective story set in a semi-dystopian near future and spanning parallel worlds, mundane Earth and magical Areth. Apple TV hired Mark as executive producer and screenwriter for a show based on his novel. Mark founded the Aspen Writers’ Network and served on the board of Aspen Words.
people.name: Mark Tompkins

people.bio: Marshall Ryan Maresca is a fantasy and science-fiction writer, author of the Maradaine Saga: Four braided series set amid the bustling streets and crime-ridden districts of the exotic city called Maradaine, which includes The Thorn of Dentonhill, A Murder of Mages, The Holver Alley Crew and The Way of the Shield, as well as the dieselpunk fantasy, The Velocity of Revolution. He is also the co-host of the Hugo-nominated, Stabby-winning podcast Worldbuilding for Masochists, and has been a playwright, an actor, a delivery driver and an amateur chef. He lives in Austin, Texas with his family.
people.name: Marshall Ryan Maresca

people.bio: Martha Wells has been a science fiction and fantasy author since her first fantasy novel was published in 1993. Her New York Times Bestselling series The Murderbot Diaries has won Nebula Awards, Hugo Awards, Locus Awards, and an American Library Association/YALSA Alex Award. Her work also includes The Books of the Raksura series, the Ile-Rien series, and other fantasy novels, most recently Witch King (Tordotcom, 2023), as well as short fiction, non-fiction, and media tie-ins for Star Wars, Stargate: Atlantis, and Magic: The Gathering. She is a member of the Texas Literary Hall of Fame, and her work has also appeared on the Philip K. Dick Award ballot, the British Science Fiction Association Award ballot, the USA Today Bestseller List, the Sunday Times Bestseller List, and has been translated into thirty languages.
people.name: Martha Wells

people.bio: Martin is a Junior Writer at Larian Studios. After spending time in games journalism, Baldur's Gate 3 was his first time writing for a game and not about one - and he's still a little overwhelmed by it all to be honest.
people.name: Martin Docherty

people.bio: Martin Hendry is Professor of Gravitational Astrophysics and Cosmology at the University of Glasgow, where he is also Clerk of Senate and Vice Principal of the University.  He is a senior member of the LIGO Scientific Collaboration: the global team of more than 1500 scientists who, with their colleagues in the Virgo Collaboration, made the first ever detection of gravitational waves - a discovery awarded the 2017 Nobel Prize for Physics. Martin is a Fellow of the Institute of Physics and is also a Fellow (and currently Vice-President) of the Royal Society of Edinburgh – Scotland’s National Academy. During 2024 he has been leading the University of Glasgow's celebration of the bicentenary of Lord Kelvin's birth, on June 26 1824..
people.name: Martin Hendry
