people.bio: Marvellous Michael Anson has been writing for over a decade and has self-published a thriller, His Dark Reflection, to critical acclaim. She was shortlisted for the Future Worlds Prize in 2023, winning mentorship from a top UK editor. Her debut fantasy novel, FIRSTBORN OF THE SUN was shortlisted for the 2022 Jericho Writers Friday Night Live Competition and the 2022 Kit De Waal Bursary, was longlisted for the 2023 REVPIT competition, and won the 2023 Jericho Writers’ Self Edit Course Bursary. In addition, Marve is a filmmaker who wrote and produced an award-winning short film in 2016 and is a recipient of the 2017 AFRIFF Film School Scholarship Program. She works as a technology consultant during the day and a storyteller at night. She is a member of the Society of Authors, Alliance of Independent Authors and the British Fantasy Society. She is represented by Kesia Lupo, Bindery Agency.
people.name: Marve Michael Anson

people.bio: Mary G. Thompson is the author of The Word, Flicker and Mist, and other novels for children and young adults, as well as the forthcoming sci-fi novella A Small Universe. Her contemporary thriller Amy Chelsea Stacie Dee was a winner of the 2017 Westchester Fiction Award and a finalist for the 2018-2019 Missouri Gateway award. Her short fiction has appeared in Apex Magazine, Dark Matter Magazine, and others. She holds an MFA in Writing for Children from The New School and completed the UCLA School of Theater, Film & Television's Professional Program in Screenwriting. She lives in Washington, DC.
people.name: Mary G. Thompson

people.bio: Now a retired computer programmer, occasionaI artist and maker in the American Midwest. I’ve attended Worldcon (& art show) in the US and internationally, including Glasgow (2005) and London(2014). I’ve been doing maker workshops at the Teslacon steampunk convention, and hosted my first worldcon workshop at Chicago(2022).  I’m looking forward to bring some papercrafting magic to Glasgow.
people.name: Mary Prince

people.bio: Mary Robinette Kowal is the author of The Spare Man, Ghost Talkers, The Glamourist Histories series, and the Lady Astronaut Universe. She is part of the award-winning podcast Writing Excuses and a four-time Hugo Award winner. Her short fiction appears in Uncanny, Tor.com, and Asimov’s. Mary Robinette, a professional puppeteer, lives in Tennessee. Visit at maryrobinettekowal.com.
people.name: Mary Robinette Kowal

people.bio: Mason Porter is a Professor in the Department of Mathematics at UCLA. He is also a Professor in the Department of Sociology (0%) at UCLA and is an External Professor at Sante Fe Institute. Mason does research in networks, complex systems, nonlinear systems, and their applications.
people.name: Mason Porter

people.bio: Matt Hill grew up in Tameside, Greater Manchester. He is the author of five novels including Philip K. Dick Award nominee Graft (Angry Robot, 2016) and The Breach (Titan Books, 2020). His most recent novel Lamb (Dead Ink Books) was a Times best SF novel of 2023. Instagram: @matthillwriter
people.name: Matt Hill

people.bio: Matthew Sangster is Professor of Romantic Studies, Fantasy and Cultural History at the University of Glasgow, where he co-directs the Centre for Fantasy and the Fantastic.  He is the author of An Introduction to Fantasy (2023); external curator of the British Library exhibition Fantasy: Realms of Imagination (2023-24); and co-editor (with Tanya Kirk) of Realms of Imagination: Essays from the Wide Worlds of Fantasy (2023).
people.name: Matthew Sangster

people.bio:
MAURIZIO MANZIERI
2021 and 2022 HUGO AWARD NOMINEE
Best Professional Artist

is an Italian illustrator based in Turin, appointed European Grand Master by the European Science Fiction Society for his international contribution in the field of Imaginative Realism. During his decades-long career he has earned numerous awards including two Italia Awards, one Chesley Award and four Asimov’s Readers’ Awards. His artwork has been showcased in exhibits all around the world and included in many annuals, such as Spectrum, The Best in Contemporary Fantastic Art and Infected by Art.

Over the years he has graced the covers of many books and illustrated limited editions for authors such as Ursula K. Le Guin, Aliette de Bodard, Terry Brooks, Clive Cussler, Elizabeth Bear, Peter S. Beagle, Robert Silverberg, Robert J. Sawyer, Kelley Armstrong, Peter S. Beagle and many others (Clients: Mondadori Libri SpA, Subterranean Press, MacMillan, Putnam/Berkley, Penny Publications – Asimov’s SF, Analog – The Magazine of F&SF).

Guest of Honor at numerous festivals in Italy and Switzerland, Manzieri has been often hired by the organizers as a Visual Artist, creating mascots and official posters for prestigious events such as: Lucca Comics & Games (2014), Sassari Comics & Games (2016), Fantasy Basel, the Swiss Comic Con (2016), Zurich Game Show (2018, 2019), Cartoons on the Bay, the International Cross-Media and Children Television Festival (2019), EuroCon (2021) and StarCon Italia (2023).
people.name: Maurizio Manzieri

people.bio: Meg Hyland is a PhD candidate in Celtic and Scottish Studies at the University of Edinburgh. She also holds an MA in Mediaeval History from the University of St Andrews. Her current research focuses on the role of music in the lives of Scottish herring gutters and packers in the 19th and 20th century fishing industries. She also runs a public history art and writing project online called Women of 1000 AD. Her work experience is in public engagement, music, and tourism. She is committed to researching and sharing stories of women's history with a wide variety of audiences.
people.name: Meg Hyland

people.bio:
Dr. Meg MacDonald (she/her) is co- Division Head for Promotions for Glasgow 2024 and was startled to find that conrunning involves filking, punning, and applying glitter to friends and strangers alike: along with emails, spreadsheets, and timelines. She has a PhD in English Literature, her thesis, “Gods Wall to Wall: Gods in Fantasy 1989-2020”, considers concepts of agency, belief and transforming grand narratives in genre fantasy. She works at the University of Glasgow as Research Support Manager for the College of Science and Engineering. She loves board games, cosplay, books of all styles, baking, knitting, and all sorts of nerdery.

Thesis https://aru.figshare.com/articles/thesis/Gods_wall_to_wall_gods_in_fantasy_1989-2020/25746666/1?file=46073745
people.name: Meg MacDonald

people.bio:
Dr Meganne Christian FRAeS (she/her) is Reserve Astronaut / Exploration Commercialisation Lead at the UK Space Agency, developing strategy on human and robotic spaceflight in the post-ISS landscape.

In November 2022, she became a member of the ESA astronaut reserve, one of only 17 candidates selected from a pool of more than 22,500 applicants across Europe. Dr Christian holds a Bachelor of Engineering and a PhD in Industrial Chemistry from the University of New South Wales. From 2014 to 2023, she was a materials science researcher at the National Research Council of Italy and took two parabolic flight campaigns to test graphene coatings for thermal management in satellites.

Dr Christian has also undertaken two missions, including as a winter-over scientist, to the Concordia station in Antarctica, where she was a research scientist in charge of atmospheric physics and meteorology.
people.name: Meganne Christian

people.bio: Melissa A Watkins is a speculative fiction writer, nerdy reader, and educator. Her work can be found in The Magazine of Fantasy and Science Fiction, Fantasy Magazine, and khoreo. When she's not writing, she does audio description for the visually impaired at live theatre productions. She's also had stints as an AI content trainer, a content writer, and one-third of a world music band whose only common language was no-one's native one.
people.name: Melissa A Watkins

people.bio: Melissa A. Hosek is a scholar of Chinese science fiction. She has a PhD in Chinese from Stanford University.
people.name: Melissa A. Hosek

people.bio: Melissa Caruso is the author of two complete fantasy trilogies from Orbit Books: Swords & Fire (THE TETHERED MAGE, THE DEFIANT HEIR, THE UNBOUND EMPIRE) and Rooks & Ruin (THE OBSIDIAN TOWER, THE QUICKSILVER COURT, THE IVORY TOMB). Her seventh fantasy novel, THE LAST HOUR BETWEEN WORLDS, is forthcoming in November 2024 from Orbit Books. Her debut novel was shortlisted for the Gemmell Morningstar Award in 2017, and her books have received starred reviews, been selected as Amazon Editor's Picks,  and made countless Best Of lists. Melissa is a tea drinker, larper, and mom, and lives in Massachusetts with her video game designer husband, two superlative daughters, and assorted pets.
people.name: Melissa Caruso

people.bio: Melissa Kocias is a professional cat-herder, part-time writer, dancer, sewist, fencer, defender of the serial comma, and time traveler extraordinaire. (Ask her about that time she got a job in 1848!)  Aficionado of foliage both large and small, she is often found messing around in the dirt, turning her kitchen into an alchemy lab, and wandering, feral, in the forest.
people.name: Melissa Kocias

people.bio:
Merav Hoffman (she/they) wears a lot of hats, including singer, songwriter, archivist for Love Song Productions, director of the Harold M. Stein Memorial Filk Archive, Vice President of Interfilk and co-director of the Interfilk mini-grants committee. She's also a founding member of the bands Lady Mondegreen, The Funny Things, and Goldberry and moonlights with Via Bella and The Goat Rodeo.

Merav lives in New Jersey with her family and an awful lot of houseplants. In 2021 Merav was inducted into the Filk Hall of Fame. She has published short fiction and poetry under her own name. You can stay up to date with her work at https://www.ladymondegreen.com/merav
people.name: Merav Hoffman

people.bio: Mercury Natis (they/them) is a student with Signum University and is about to begin their PhD with the University of Glasgow, with a focus on J.R.R. Tolkien and the Queer Fantastic. They hold a previous MA in Museum Education and a BA in Art History. Their primary focus is queer resonances and reception in works of the fantastic produced in the early 20th century, alongside contemporary critical reception and adaptation. Mercury is a long-time Sci-fi lover, thriving at the intersection of Star Trek Utopianism and Dystopian Existential Horror where hopeful idealism meets critical dread.
people.name: Mercury Natis

people.bio:
Mia Tsai is a Taiwanese American author and editor of speculative fiction. Her debut novel is
a xianxia-inspired contemporary fantasy titled Bitter Medicine. She is also an associate editor for GigaNotoSaurus.
people.name: Mia Tsai

people.bio:
Micaela Alcaino is a book cover designer and illustrator who relocated from her home in Sydney, Australia to London, UK in 2013. Her career has been marked by significant achievements, including being named one of The Bookseller's Rising Stars in 2021 and winning the prestigious Designer of the Year title at the British Book Awards in 2022, with a subsequent nomination in 2024.

Acknowledged for her influence in the industry, Micaela was featured in The Bookseller 150 in 2022 and shortlisted for Future Leader of the Year at the FutureBook Conference in 2023, highlighting her commitment to fostering positive change and inclusivity within publishing.

She is currently a finalist for the Hugo Award in the category of Best Professional Artist, with the winner to be announced at the 2024 World Science Fiction Conventions (Worldcon) in Glasgow.

With over a decade of experience, Micaela has worked with major publishing houses globally, showcasing a distinct blend of creativity and artistry influenced by her travels, cultural heritage, and passion for the fine arts. Her portfolio can be viewed on her website, www.micaelaalcaino.com.
people.name: Micaela Alcaino

people.bio: Micaiah Johnson is the Compton Crook Award-winning author of The Space Between Worlds and Those Beyond the Wall. Her debut novel was an Editor's Choice at The New York Times and was named one of best books of 2020 and one of the best science fiction books of the last decade by NPR. She was raised in California's Mojave Desert surrounded by trees named Joshua and women who told stories. She received her bachelor of arts in creative writing from the University of California, Riverside, and her master of fine arts in fiction from Rutgers-Camden. She studies at Vanderbilt University, where she focuses on critical race theory and automatons.
people.name: Micaiah Johnson

people.bio: Senior Writer for Friends of Comic Con, Moderator of Expanse Panels at Fan Expo Denver, Los Angeles Comic Con, and Denver Pop Culture Con.
people.name: Michael

people.bio:
Dr Michael Davidson CChem CSci FRSC was, until his recent retirement in April 2024, head of the Radioanalytical Group at the United Kingdom Health Service Agency, with the responsibility for leading the analytical response to nuclear emergencies in the UK. He is a UK representative to the International Standards Organisation in the area of radiochemical analysis, and is Chair of the UK national mirror committee run by British Standards Institute.

In 2007 he co-founded Satellite Conventions, Scotland's (roughly) biennial fan-run SF convention, the by-line of which is Science Fiction, Science Fact, Science Fun. Michael has chaired seven of the conventions, including Satellite 4 (Eastercon 2014). He is currently co-Area Head for the Science & Technology Programme track at Glasgow 2024.
people.name: Michael Davidson

people.bio: Michael Everson, based in Dundee in Scotland, is an expert in the writing systems of the world. He has been active in supporting minority-language communities, especially with character standardization for Unicode. He is a linguist, typesetter, and font designer. As Evertype, he has published Alice’s Adventures in Wonderland in more than 90 languages, and The Hobbit in six, with more forthcoming. Most recently he has been working on the whole textual history of Ursula K. Le Guin’s Ekumen and Earthsea cycles, studying Ursula as a language creator, especially with regard to Kesh, the language of Always Coming Home.
people.name: Michael Everson

people.bio: Michael Green is a data scientist, writer, and founder of Lynit, a tool to wrangle your ideas into a well-structured novel. He loves reading and writing speculative fiction, singing, and learning something new every day. He grew up in Washington, DC; has lived in NYC, Paris, and Melbourne; and currently lives in Mexico City.
people.name: Michael Green Jr

people.bio: Michelle has held numerous positions in convention leadership, including her home convention Norwescon (Member Services Director, Secretary) and Seattle Worldcon in 2025 (Division Head - Exhibits). Her special passion project is the Norwescon Little Free Library book exchange, where thousands of books get rehomed each year. She reviews contracts by day, prowls the Seattle goth scene by night, looks for any excuse to wear elf ears, and lives by the creed, “I read, therefore, I am.”
people.name: Michelle Morrell

people.bio: Miguel O. Mitchell, PhD (he/him) is a Black speculative poet, SFF author, visual artist, and retired chemist. His poems have appeared in Amazing Stories, Dreams & Nightmares, Eye to the Telescope, Scarlet Dragonfly Journal, Scifaikuest, Star*Line, and Year’s Best African Speculative Fiction (2022). He also published a poetry collection, Periodic Table of Alien Species (Elements 1-86) (Barnes & Noble Press, 2021). His poetry chapbook Surrealia (Gnashing Teeth Publishing) will launch in August 2024. He has also published fantasy short stories in Scarlet Leaf Review (https://www.scarletleafreview.com/short-stories23/miguel-o-mitchell-the-revenant-saga) and Fantasy (https://www.fantasy-magazine.com/fm/fiction/trading-with-monsters/). He has been an online panelist at Chicon 8 and Balticon 57.
people.name: Miguel O. Mitchell

people.bio: I'm a part-time maths tutor with the OU and have been involved in the UK Filk community for around 30 years. I'm an amateur level harper, and have been following the space program for a number of years.
people.name: Mike Richards

people.bio: Mikko Rauhala is a bilingual Finnish SF author. Informed by their master's degree in intelligent systems, they're most at home in hard science fiction settings, though they're not exclusive and like to cross genres. Whether the subject is steam powered gnomes or universal quantum suicide, Rauhala enjoys taking an eccentric premise and bringing it to its logical conclusion. As befits a Finn, their plot-driven narrative is often seasoned with a touch of dark, dry humor.
people.name: Mikko Rauhala

people.bio: I am polish fan and conrunner active in fandom since 2015, master student of Environmental Economics at University of Copenhagen. I am member of Warsaw based Avangarda Society promoting SF, RPG etc. Since 2022 I am also board member of ESFS as an Award Administrator.
people.name: Mikolaj Kowalewski

people.bio: I’m a full time writer of fantasy, science fiction and historical fiction. I enjoy research above all things, and also enjoy martial arts, wilderness camping, gaming (especially rpgs) and cats. And dogs! I’m the suthor of Artifact Space, tge Red Knight and most recently, Deep Black as well as 47 other titles.
people.name: Miles Cameron

people.bio: Minerva Cerridwen (xe or she) is a neurodiverse genderqueer aromantic asexual author from Belgium. Xe enjoys baking, drawing, and learning languages. Xyr queer fairy tale novella THE DRAGON OF YNYS came out with Atthis Arts in 2020. Find more information about Minerva's writing on xyr website: https://minervacerridwen.wordpress.com/
people.name: Minerva Cerridwen

people.bio:
Miranda is a theatre producer, events manager and disability advocate with a keen interest in representations of disability and chronic illness. A passionate sci-fi and fantasy reader, she founded and runs the London Sci-Fi and Fantasy Book Club, and plays in TTRPG livestreams on Heroes without Limits, a channel dedicated to tabletop players with disabilities, and Hoard of Tales, a channel prioritising diversity and representation.
Embedded in her all work, projects and dreams, is a deep-rooted desire for everyone to experience comfort and care.
people.name: Miranda Debenham

people.bio:
Mitchell Burnside Clapp is an Australian-American aerospace engineer, former test pilot, and musician. He received Bachelor of Science degrees in Physics, Aeronautics and Astronautics, and Russian, as well as a Master of Science degree in Aeronautics and Astronautics, from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology. In the late 1980s and 1990s, he attended the U.S. Air Force Test Pilot School and worked on the YA-7F and DC-X projects. Burnside Clapp founded Pioneer Rocketplane in 1996, and served as a program manager at DARPA from 2011 to 2016.

As a musician, he has won several awards for filk music including two Pegasus awards.
people.name: Mitchell Burnside Clapp

people.bio: I lead the London office of the Bent Agency, where I represent authors including Stephanie Burgis, Frances Hardinge, Peadar O Guilin, Louie Stowell, and Angie Thomas.
people.name: Molly Ker Hawn

people.bio: Molly Tanzer is the author of five novels and two collections. Her work has been nominated for the Locus Award, the British Fantasy Award, the Wonderland Book Award. Her novel Creatures of Charm and Hunger won the Colorado Book Award in 2021, and her work adapting manga for English-speaking audiences has been nominated for the American Manga Awards. Her critically acclaimed short fiction can be found in The Big Book of Cyberpunk, The Magazine of Fantasy & Science Fiction, and The Year's Best Dark Fantasy and Horror. Follow her on Instagram @molly_tanzer.
people.name: Molly Tanzer

people.bio: Monique Poirier is an enrolled member of the Seaconke Wampanoag Tribe and a  lineal descendant of Ousamequin Massasoit. She is an author, costumer, convention-goer, and activist currently living in Pawtucket, RI. Her novel, To Shape a Dragon's Breath, is a finalist for the Lodestar Award for Best YA Book.
people.name: Moniquill Blackgoose

people.bio: Morag is one half of the writing duo MK Hardy. Together they write sapphic speculative fiction. Their debut gothic horror novel THE NEEDFIRE (Solaris) releases in July 2025.
people.name: Morag Hannah (MK Hardy)

people.bio: Morag Lewis is a research scientist, an indie author and a comic artist. She studies the genetics of progressive hearing loss by day, and tells stories by night, mostly fantasy stories with occasional forays into science fiction and mystery. She is part of Sweatdrop Studios, a UK-based comic collaborative and independent publisher which has been producing comics for more than 15 years. She loves telling stories with and without pictures, and finds worldbuilding enormous fun as well as very distracting.
people.name: Morag Lewis

people.bio: Morgan L. Ventura (They/She) is a writer, poet, and former archaeologist whose work appears in The Magazine of Fantasy and Science Fiction, Augur, Lackington's, and Shoreline of Infinity, among others.
people.name: Morgan L. Ventura

people.bio:
My name is Muaiyd Abu Ali , 
35 years old
i'm from Saudi Arabia Makkah 
I'm a writer and physical therapy
My novel name ( Legend Of The Octagram )
people.name: Muaiyd

people.bio: Mur Lafferty is a podcaster, writer, and editor. Her work has been recognized with the Hugo, Nebula, and Philip K Dick nominations, and in 2015 she was inducted into the Podcast Academy Hall of Fame. She lives in Durham, NC, USA with her family.
people.name: Mur Lafferty

people.bio: N.L. Bates is a Canadian author of science fiction, fantasy, and slipstream stories, and is the moderator of the long-running critique group Reading Excuses. When not writing stories, she enjoys biking, dancing, and tabletop RPGs. She also writes and performs music as her alter ego, Natalie Lynn, and filks occasionally, usually by accident.
people.name: N.L. Bates

people.bio: Nadia El-Fassi is the pen name of Nadia Saward, who is a Commissioning Editor at Orbit. Before working in publishing, they completed an MA in Creative Writing at Royal Holloway, receiving a distinction and worked as a Waterstones bookseller. She lives in London with her husband and perfectly round cat and can be found impulse-buying new dice sets for D&D or watching horror movies.
people.name: Nadia El-Fassi

people.bio:
42 Years Old (yes, I know the answer now). Digital marketing manager by day, Sci Fi and Fantasy fan daily, combining the two from day to day. SMoF of the Israeli fandom, used to be global GoHs commity chair. BA in Communications and Media Studies, MFA in TV Studies.
Mother of two geeky girls.
people.name: Naomi Karmi

people.bio: Naomi Kritzer is a science fiction and fantasy writer from St. Paul, Minnesota. Her fiction has won the Hugo Award, the Edgar Award, and the Minnesota Book Award. She has a spouse, two grown kids and three cats (the number of cats is subject to change without notice). You can find Naomi online at naomikritzer.com or on Bluesky as @naomikritzer.bsky.social. Her latest book, Liberty’s Daughter, came out in November 2023.
people.name: Naomi Kritzer

people.bio: Naseem Jamnia (they/them) is a Persian-Chicagoan, former neuroscientist, and the Astounding Award-nominated and Judith A. Markowitz Award-winning author of The Bruising of Qilwa (Tachyon Publications, 2022), which was shortlisted for IAFA's Crawford Award, the Locus Award, and the World Fantasy Award. Naseem is the managing editor at Sword & Kettle Press, a tiny publishing house of feminist speculative writing. Their middle grade horror debut, Sleepaway, comes out in 2025 (Aladdin). Find out more and join their newsletter at www.naseemwrites.com or on Instagram @jamsternazzy.
people.name: Naseem Jamnia

people.bio:
Natania Barron is an award-winning fantasy author long preoccupied with mythology, monsters, and magic. Her often historically-inspired novels are filled with lush description and vibrant characters. 

In 2020, Barron's Queen of None was hailed as "a captivating look at the intriguing figures in King Arthur’s golden realm" by Kirkus, and won the Manly Wade Wellman award the following year. The rest of the Queens of Fate series will be published by Solaris Books in 2024 and 2025. Additionally, her Regency romantasy series, Love in Netherford, will also be published by Solaris starting in August 2024.

Her shorter works have appeared in Weird Tales, EscapePod, and various anthologies, RPG, and game settings. In addition, she's also known for her ThreadTalks, which dive deep into the unseen, and often forgotten, world of fashion history. 

Barron lives in North Carolina, USA, with her family and two dogs. When she's not writing, you can find her wandering the woods, tending her garden, and collecting rocks.
people.name: Natania Barron

people.bio: Artist, author, game developer. Author of Machina Fantasia, released just this year.
people.name: Nathan Philpott

people.bio: Navah Wolfe is a two-time Hugo Award-winning Executive Editor of science fiction, fantasy, horror at DAW Books. She is the co-editor, with Dominik Parisien, of three anthologies: The Mythic Dream, Robots vs Fairies, and The Starlit Wood, which won the Shirley Jackson Award, and were finalists for the World Fantasy, British Fantasy and Locus Awards. The books she's edited have won the Hugo, Nebula, Locus and BSFA AWards, and been finalists for the World Fantasy, Stoker, and Tiptree Awards. She lives in Connecticut with her husband, four small humans, and one cat, where she dabbles in tea, boxing, Eurovision and dad jokes. Find her on Twitter @navahw.
people.name: Navah Wolfe

people.bio: Recovering academic. Currently doing bits and bobs around community development, evnvironment, sustainability, etc. Live/work in Glasgow, Scotland.
people.name: Nayab Khalid

people.bio: Neil Clarke (neil-clarke.com) is the multi-award-winning editor of Clarkesworld Magazine and over a dozen anthologies, including the Best Science Fiction of the Year series. An twelve-time finalist and the 2022/2023 winner of the Hugo Award for Best Editor Short Form, he is also the four-time winner of the Chesley Award for Best Art Director. In 2019, Clarke received the SFWA Kate Wilhelm Solstice Award for distinguished contributions to the science fiction and fantasy community. He currently lives in New Jersey with his wife and two sons.
people.name: Neil Clarke

people.bio:
Neil Williamson lives in Glasgow, Scotland. His books include The Moon King, Queen of Clouds, The Memoirist and Charlie Says, and some of his seventy-odd short stories can be found in the collections, The Ephemera and Secret Language. He also co-edited Nova Scotia: New Scottish Speculative Fiction the last time Worldcon came to Glasgow. His work has been nominated for British Fantasy, British Science Fiction Association and World Fantasy awards.

For Worldcon 2024 Neil is working on Nova Scotia 2, a new celebration of Scottish genre fiction, and Gallus, an anthology of stories by the legendary Glasgow SF Writers' Circle.
people.name: Neil Williamson

people.bio: Neon Yang is the author of the Tensorate series of novellas from Tor.Com Publishing (The Red Threads of Fortune, The Black Tides of Heaven, The Descent of Monsters and The Ascent to Godhood) and the novel The Genesis of Misery. Their work has been shortlisted for the Hugo, Nebula, World Fantasy, Lambda Literary and Locus awards, while the Tensorate novellas were an Otherwise Award honoree in 2018. They have over two dozen works of short fiction published in venues including Tor.com, Uncanny Magazine, Lightspeed, and Strange Horizons.
people.name: Neon Yang

people.bio:
Ng Yi-Sheng (he/him) is a Singaporean writer, researcher and translator with a keen interest in Southeast Asian history and myth.

He is the author of the speculative fiction collection Lion City (winner of the Singapore Book Award for Best Literary Work 2019 and the Singapore Literature Prize 2020). His creative works have been published in Clarkesworld, Strange Horizons and Best of World SF Vol 1. His essays include “A Spicepunk Manifesto: Towards a Critical Movement of Southeast Asian-Inspired SFF”, "A History of Singapore Horror" and "A Not-So-Swiftly Tilting Planet: Global Inequities in SFF Publishing."

Additionally, he served as editor of A Mosque in the Jungle: Classic Ghost Stories by Othman Wok and Wok and EXHALE: an Anthology of Queer Singapore Voices. He has spoken at numerous festivals, including the Singapore Writers Festival, the Ubud Writers and Readers Festival, Wordstorm Darwn and Flights of Foundry.
people.name: Ng Yi-Sheng

people.bio: Niall Harrison is a reader, critic, and fan, based in Newcastle Upon Tyne. He is a former editor of Vector and of Strange Horizons, and his own writing has also appeared in Locus, The Los Angeles Review of Books, Foundation and other venues. He has served as a judge for the Arthur C. Clarke Award and for the William L. Crawford Award.
people.name: Niall Harrison

people.bio:
Nicholas Binge is a bestselling author of speculative thrillers, literary science-fiction, and horror. His work has been featured in The New York Times, The Sunday Times, The Wall Street Journal, The FT, Entertainment Weekly, The Washington Post, and more.

His first novel, Professor Everywhere, was selected as a prize-winner by The Proverse Prize for Literature in Hong Kong. His most recent novel, Ascension, a New York Times Editor’s Choice Pick, has been hailed as a must-read “5-star horror novel” by Stephen King, with Publisher’s Weekly calling it both “incredible” and “pitch-perfect” in their starred review. It has since been critically praised across almost every major media outlet and nominated for the Goodreads Choice Award, as well as being translated into nine languages and being optioned for film.

Binge has lived in Singapore, Switzerland, and Hong Kong, and is currently based in Edinburgh, UK. Outside of fiction, he has written for The Guardian, Literary Hub, and CrimeReads, amongst others. When he’s not writing himself, he also lectures in creative writing at Edinburgh Napier University. He is an active member of ESFF (Edinburgh Science-Fiction & Fantasy) and can often be found at book festivals and events around Scotland and the rest of the UK.
people.name: Nicholas Binge

people.bio: Nicholas Eames is the author of The Band series, which currently includes Kings of the Wyld and Bloody Rose. His work has garnered numerous awards (most of which are also weapons) and has been translated into more than a dozen languages.
people.name: Nicholas Eames

people.bio: I'm a mathematics lecturer (Assistant Professor) at the University of Warwick, UK.
people.name: Nicholas Jackson

people.bio: Former programmer, ex-soldier, retired winemaker, and now computing academic, Nick Falkner works in data ethics, distributed ledger tech, and big ideas for sustainable living. A systems guy who loves people, he's always trying to make things work better, reducing bureaucracy, and driving change for the common good. He grew up inspired by the possibilities he saw in science fiction and loves to share that wonder. He lives in Australia but works closely with colleagues in Germany, Sweden, Finland and Estonia on a range of interesting projects. He writes SF around people and technology, and fantasy around really weird things.
people.name: Nick Falkner

people.bio: I am a nonbinary SF critic and reviewer, who lives in Aberystwyth, Cymru. I've published well over 100 reviews and articles about SFF in publications such as Strange Horizons, Los Angeles Review of Books, Tribune, Jacobin, Foundation, Vector, BSFA Review, ParSec, and various academic journals and book collections.
people.name: Nick Hubble

people.bio: Film hack, Classicist, exiled Glaswegian, Friend of Kilgore Trout from 1976, Interzone columnist since 1985.
people.name: Nick Lowe

people.bio: Nick Mamatas is an author, editor, and anthologist. His novels include The Second Shooter, I Am Providence, and Move Under Ground. Nick's short fiction has appeared in McSweeney's, Tor.com, Best American Mystery Stories, Asimov's Science Fiction, Weird Tales, and many other magazines and anthologies. Nick is also an anthologist: his books include the Bram Stoker Award winner Haunted Legends (with Ellen Datlow), the Locus Award nominee The Future is Japanese (with Masumi Washington), and Wonder and Glory Forever: Awe-Inspiring Lovecraftian Fiction. Nick's fiction and editoral work has variously been nominated for the Hugo, World Fantasy, and Shirley Jackson awards.
people.name: Nick Mamatas

people.bio: Nicolai is a lifelong SFF fan by inclination and sysadmin and technology manager by profession. Formerly one of the many people who built the modern Internet, he now works for a large online travel company. He has wide-ranging interests in hard science and SF, and deep knowledge of the aviation industry, yet the thing that interests him more is how people live with and use technologies.
people.name: Nicolal Plum

people.bio: Dr. Nicolle Lamerichs is senior lecturer and team lead at Creative Business, HU University of Applied Sciences, Utrecht. She holds a PhD in media studies from Maastricht University (2014). She has published books, peer-reviewed articles and chapters on fandom, media culture, cosplay and game practices. Her current research focuses on participatory culture on new media platforms, specifically in relation to identity, sustainability and play.
people.name: Nicolle Lamerichs

people.bio: Nige is a societal and organisational resilience subject matter expert having spent the last 25+ years working in scientific and technological sectors specilising in resilience. He has a MSc in Risk Crisis and Disaster Management & he is a Fellow of the Institute for Strategic Risk Management and a Chartered Security Professional. Nige has been a life long fan of science fiction with his first convention being Worldcon in 1988. He has worked at conventions in the UK and US as a volunteer as well as being a committee member on various Eastercons and on the Worldcon, Loncon 3 in 2014.
people.name: Nige F

people.bio: Nikita Andester is a multidisciplinary artist and an NYC Midnight judge. Raised in the deep south, Nikita’s writing draws on their past lives as a waitress, ESL teacher, and (terrible) organic farmer to uncover the magic lurking in the everyday lives of working-class characters. Always experimenting with something new, Nikita runs Snail Mail Sweethearts a postcard club and historical fiction newsletter, where she mails original art and prose to folks' homes each month. Their work has recently appeared in "The New Orleans Review," "Bourbon Penn," and "Typehouse Literary Magazine."
people.name: Nikita Andester

people.bio: Nina Allan is a novelist and critic, a previous winner of the British Science Fiction Award, the Kitschies Red Tentacle, and the Grand Prix de L'imaginaire. Her novelette 'The Art of Space Travel' was shortlisted for a Hugo Award in 2017. Her essays and reviews have appeared in the Guardian, the TLS, the Los Angeles Review of Books and Strange Horizons. Her most recent novel is Conquest (Riverrun Books 2023).
people.name: Nina Allan

people.bio: Nnedi Okorafor (she/her) is an internationally award-winning author who explores her Nigerian heritage through her Africanfuturist and Africanjujuist novels and short works. She is also a comics writer who has written a number of popular series for Marvel’s Black Panther, along with her own Hugo and Eisner-Award-winning graphic novel, LaGuardia
people.name: Nnedi Okorafor

people.bio: Co-founder and Editor-in-Chief of Shoreline of Infinity, and founder and Editor of SF Caledonia
people.name: Noel Chidwick

people.bio: Grew up in Edinburgh, retired from Middlesex University (London) 2002, now back in Edinburgh for many years. Has had publications on early modern British political and social history, including a witch hunt in the village where she grew up.
people.name: Norah Carlin
Nova Scotia Vol 2: New Speculative Fiction from Scotland

people.bio:
Award-winning former journalist and photographer whose work has appeared in the Guardian, Strange Horizons, the Wizards of the Coast website, and the Encyclopedia of the Marvel Comic Book Universe. Hugo finalist for fanzine in 2021 and 2022.

On the Judging Panel for the Sidewise Award for Alternate History.
people.name: Olav Rokne

people.bio: Oliver K. Langmead writes speculative fiction. His new verse-novel, Calypso, will be published by Titan Books in 2024. Glitterati was shortlisted for a British Fantasy Award and named one of New Scientist’s best Science Fiction books of 2022, and the French edition of Birds of Paradise, Les Oiseaux du Paradis, was published summer 2023. He is a Lecturer in Creative Writing at the University of Lancaster, and in late 2018 he was the writer in residence at the European Space Agency’s Astronaut Centre in Cologne.
people.name: Oliver K. Langmead

people.bio: I'm a writer and editor who concentrates on scientific knowledge, technological change and their effects, currently working as a senior editor at tThe Economist. I have written four books on the history, understanding and imagining of planetary processes: Mapping Mars: Science, Imagination and the Birth of a World (2002); Eating the Sun: How Plants Power the Planet (2007); The Planet Remade: How Geoengineering Could Change the World (2015); and The Moon: A History for the Future (2019). I'm chair of the trustees of The Degrees Initiative, a charity which funds research on geoengineering in the Global South, and the namesake of Asteroid 10716 Olivermorton.
people.name: Oliver Morton

people.bio:
Olivia “Liv” Kennedy (she/her) is one of the Three Black Halflings alongside Jeremy Cobb (he/him) and Jasper William Cartwright (he/him): nerdy friends with strong opinions and even stronger Charisma scores. Their weekly podcast is on a continuing quest to explore diversity and roll for melanin in the world of TTRPG, and has been described as “a joyful, creative, and chaotic celebration of gamer culture that puts the Black and BIPOC experience front and centre.”

Three Black Halflings won the Best Podcast Award at the inaugural CRIT (Creator Recognition in TTRPG) Awards in 2023. Liv, Jeremy and Jasper are currently excited to be preparing for their first ever live shows, taking place in Manchester and London in April 2024.
people.name: Olivia “Liv” Kennedy

people.bio:
Ken Gordon is the ESA Space Solutions Business Ambassador for Scotland, Northern Ireland. For the last 15 years he has been helping organisations understand and apply for UK and EU funding to do innovative things. His previous experience includes managing design teams focussed on the aerospace, explosives, automotive and consumer sectors, managing EU innovation programmes and as a bid writing consultant. 

In his spare time, he paints, makes podcasts, performs improvised comedy and is learning mandarin. Not in that order.
people.name: One Small Step for Mankind, one giant leap for business!

people.bio: Oriana Leckert is the Head of Publishing at Kickstarter, where she helps creators bring a marvelous array of literary projects to life. She's written and edited for Vice, MTV News, Slate, Hyperallergic, Gothamist, Atlas Obscura, and many more. Her first book, Brooklyn Spaces: 50 Hubs of Culture and Creativity (Monacelli, 2015), grew out of a multi-year project chronicling the rise and fall of under-the-radar creative places across New York City. Follow her at @orianabklyn on most social platforms.
people.name: Oriana Leckert

people.bio: A retired teacher I have enjoyed reading and writing SF and F since I was a boy. In my retirement I have published ten novels of which five are fantasy published by Elsewhen Press. I am non-binary, live in South Wales and enjoy participating in writing groups, playing tennis and navigating the British canal system.
people.name: P R Ellis
PS Livingstone

people.bio: Paolo Bacigalupi is the internationally bestselling author of THE WINDUP GIRL, SHIP BREAKER, and THE WATER KNIFE, among others. He has won the Hugo, Nebula, World Fantasy, and Michael L. Printz Awards, and was a National Book Award Finalist. His latest book is NAVOLA, an epic fantasy set in an Italian Renaissance-inspired world.
people.name: Paolo Bacigalupi

people.bio: Patrick Nielsen Hayden is Editor-at-Large at the Tor Publishing Group, where he's worked for over thirty-five years. He is responsible for launching or helping to launch the careers of several notable SF and fantasy novelists, including Maureen F. McHugh, Susan Palwick, Cory Doctorow, Jo Walton, John Scalzi, Ada Palmer, and Charlie Jane Anders. For his original anthology Starlight 1 (Tor, 1996), he won a World Fantasy Award; he's also won three Hugo Awards for his editorial work. With his wife, Teresa Nielsen Hayden, he's among the regular instructors at the Viable Paradise writers' workshop.
people.name: Patrick Nielsen Hayden

people.bio: Patrick S. Tomlinson is a sci-fi author and television contributor living in Milwaukee with his wife, two cats, an array of houseplants in varying levels of health, and a Ford Mustang. He has been published by Angry Robot Books and Tor Books.
people.name: Patrick S. Tomlinson

people.bio:
Paul Carroll is a writer and comic creator from Dublin. He is best known as the editor of Turning Roads, Down Below and Fractured Realms, and the creator of the Dark House.

He is a founding member of Limit Break Comics, Cupan Fae, and IrishComics.ie. 

In 2023, Paul was selected to join the Evolution Programme with the Irish Writers Centre, and to teach in the University of Galway.

His obsessions include tea, foxes and spreadsheets, and his collection of enamel pins.
people.name: Paul Carroll

people.bio: Paul Cornell has written episodes of Elementary, Doctor Who and many other TV series.  His creator-owned comics include I Walk With Monsters, The Modern Frankenstein, Saucer Country and This Damned Band.  He’s the writer of the Lychford novellas and the Shadow Police novels.  He’s won a BSFA Award, Eagle Award and Hugo Award and shares in a Writer’s Guild Award, the Grand Prix Nova and a Scribe award.  He’s co-host of Hammer House of Podcast.  His latest book is the SF novella Rosebud and his latest comic series is Con and On from Ahoy.
people.name: Paul Cornell

people.bio: Paul Kincaid is the author of books on Iain Banks, Christopher Priest, Brian Aldiss and Robert Holdstock. He has twice won the BSFA Non-Fiction Award and has also won the SFRA Clareson Award.
people.name: Paul Kincaid

people.bio: Paul Weimer is not really a Prince of Amber. He is a photographer, SFF reviewer, writer, critic, and podcaster. He lives in a city between St. Paul and Minneapolis in Minnesota and continually dreams of his next photographic adventure. He can best be found on the internet under the name @princejvstin.
people.name: Paul Princejvstin Weimer

people.bio:
Penelope Hill has been fascinated with storytelling for as long as she can remember.  Inspired by her ancient Greek namesake when young, she learned how to weave with words as well as with thread.   A writer, a gamer, and a lover of world-building, she crafts fantastic settings and mythic histories -  but can also be found with a needle (or two) in her hands, practising her stitch-craft.  
Publications include Working Weekend and The Vanished Mage from Elsewhen Press.  She lives with four cats, a huge library of books, a treasure hoard of fabric and thread, and far too many dice.
people.name: Penny Hill

people.bio: Pepper likes science, cats, and conventions.
people.name: Pepper

people.bio: Perrianne Lurie is a retired infectious disease epidemiologist and public health physician. She is a board gamer, con runner and an avid reader and consumer of tv and films.
people.name: Perrianne Lurie

people.bio: Peter F. Hamilton has been published since 1993, and is mainly known for Space Opera series.  His latest novel, The Archimedes Engine, is due out September 2024, and is set in the Exodus game universe.
people.name: Peter F. Hamilton

people.bio: Peter S. Beagle was born in 1939 and raised in the Bronx near Woodlawn Cemetery, which inspired his first novel, A Fine and Private Place. Today, thanks to classic works such as The Last Unicorn, Tamsin, and The Innkeeper’s Song, he is America’s greatest living fantasy author; his dazzling abilities with language, characters, and storytelling have earned millions of fans worldwide. Peter has also written numerous teleplays and screenplays, including the animated versions of The Lord of the Rings and The Last Unicorn, plus the “Sarek” episode of Star Trek: The Next Generation. He is a gifted poet and singer/songwriter.
people.name: Peter S. Beagle

people.bio: A lifelong fan of sf in all its forms. Has been an Endeavour Award reader, a fan critic of anime. Currently publishes SMOF News on Substack every Wednesday and runs Pathfinder Society games at her friendly local gaming store.
people.name: Petrea Mitchell

people.bio: Phil has been working in aerospace and defence since the late 1980s.  In that time he's seen an awful lot of bad ideas and wishes to share them.
people.name: Phil

people.bio: I used to study wars but I don't any more. Leftie. Conrunner. Cats. 90s guitar music. Harnessed in slums and wants to be free. Fuck off if you're a TERF.
people.name: Phil Dyson

people.bio: Phoebe Wagner is an author, editor, and academic writing at the intersection of speculative fiction and climate change. Their debut novel A Shot of Gin explores Nevada’s high desert through vampires and American gods, and Publishers Weekly called their novella When We Hold Each Other Up a “fresh take on climate fiction.” She is the editor of three solarpunk anthologies, including Sunvault: Stories of Solarpunk & Eco-Speculation. They blog at the Hugo- and Ignyte-winning Nerds of a Feather, Flock Together. Wagner holds a PhD in literature, and she is an Assistant Professor at Lycoming College. Follow them at phoebe-wagner.com.
people.name: Phoebe Wagner

people.bio: Phoenix Alexander (pronouns: he/him) is the Jay Kay and Doris Klein Librarian for Science Fiction and Fantasy at the University of California, Riverside, where he curates one of the world’s largest collections of catalogued science fiction.
people.name: Phoenix Alexander

people.bio:
Active member of Polish fandom for more than 40 years. Con organizer, fanzin publisher.

Translator by profession (among others Pratchett, Zelazny, Card, Gibson)

Mathematician by education
people.name: Piotr W. Cholewa

people.bio: Pippa Goldschmidt is an author living in Edinburgh and Berlin, she has a PhD in astronomy and is an Honorary Fellow at the Science, Technology and Innovation Studies unit at the University of Edinburgh. Her most recent book is Night Vision (Broken Sleep Books), an essay about our social and cultural relationship with the night sky. Her short story collection about women in science; Schrödinger’s Wife (and other possibilities), is due in autumn 2024 from Goldsmiths Press/Gold SF.
people.name: Pippa Goldschmidt

people.bio: Premee Mohamed is a Nebula, World Fantasy, and Aurora award-winning Indo-Caribbean scientist and speculative fiction author based in Edmonton, Alberta. She has also been a finalist for the Hugo, Ignyte, British Fantasy, and Crawford awards. She is an Assistant Editor at the short fiction audio venue Escape Pod and the author of the 'Beneath the Rising' series of novels as well as several novellas. Her short fiction has appeared in many venues and she can be found on her website at www.premeemohamed.com.
people.name: Premee Mohamed

people.bio: Bio: A 2016 MBA graduate and published author, Priya Sridhar has been writing fantasy and science fiction for fifteen years, and counting. Capstone published the Powered series. Priya lives in Miami, Florida with her family.
people.name: Priya Sridhar

people.bio:
My current position is Professor in Drug Delivery within the Strathclyde Institute of Pharmacy and Biomedical Sciences, University of Strathclyde, Glasgow, Scotland. In 1998 I gained my PhD from the University of London investigating the role of liposomes for DNA vaccines and drug delivery. I then worked within a newly established Drug Delivery Company (Lipoxen Technologies Ltd) for two years, developing their liposome drug delivery platform technology before moving into Academia to set up my own research group. I joined Aston University in 2000 and was appointed Professor in Drug Delivery in 2007. In 2016, I moved to the University of Strathclyde as Professor in Drug Delivery as part of the Global Talent Appointment Programme where I continue to develop and advance my research strategies.

My research is multi-disciplinary and focuses on developing drug delivery systems to facilitate the delivery of drugs and vaccines, thus providing practical solutions for current healthcare problems. I am an internationally recognised expert in the field of liposomes and particulate drug delivery research. My laboratory is fully equipped to manufacture and analyze a wide range of nanoparticles, including a suite of microfluidic systems that will provide the underpinning support for this project. I maintain a steady funding stream to support my research team through various sources, including Government Research Councils, European Framework Funding, Industrial Partners, and Charities.

My research and academic leadership has been recognised via a range of fellowships and awards including the Royal Pharmaceutical Society Harrison Memorial Medal (2019),  50th Anniversary Chair in Drug Delivery (2016), membership of the Controlled Release Society College of Fellows (2015), Fellow of the Royal Pharmaceutical Society (2014), Fellow of the Royal Society of Biology (2012), Eminent Fellow of the Academy of Pharmaceutical Sciences (2012), the Royal Pharmaceutical Society Pharmaceutical Scientist of the Year (2012), the British Science Festival Collaboration in Formulation Award (2011) and the Royal Pharmaceutical Society Science Conference Medal (2007).
people.name: Prof Yvonne Perrie

people.bio: Neil is Professor of Philosophy and XR Technology at the University of Glasgow. With over 17 years of XR industry experience, Neil has worked on a variety of subjects ranging from the Metaphysics of Causation, philosophical issues in Safety and Engineering and has carried out a host of philosophical investigations and projects concerning Virtual, Augmented and Mixed Reality Technology. Neil is Chair of the ARC XR Operations board within UofG’s Advanced Research Centre as well as Principal Investigator of the Scoping Extended Educational Realities (SEER) Research Group.
people.name: Professor Neil McDonnell

people.bio:
R.S.A. is a writer of speculative fiction and a Sturgeon, Nebula, Locus and Ignyte Award finalist.

Her Amazon Bestselling science fiction mystery, Lex Talionis, received a starred review from Publishers Weekly and the Silver Medal for Best Scifi/Fantasy/Horror Ebook from the Independent Publishers Awards (2015).

She has published short fiction in venues such as Clarkesworld Magazine, Escape Pod, Strange Horizons and Internazionale Magazine. Her stories have been long-listed for the British Science Fiction Awards, translated into several languages, and included in a number of anthologies, including the critically acclaimed The Best of World SF, The Best Science Fiction of the Year, and The Apex Book of World SF. Her scifantasy duology, beginning with The Nightward, is forthcoming from Harper Voyager in Fall 2024.

She lives in Trinidad and Tobago with an extended family and too many cats. Learn more at rsagarcia.com.
people.name: R.S.A. Garcia

people.bio: R.W.W. Greene is a traditionally published speculative-fiction writer who lives in New Hampshire, USA. His novels include The First Planets duology (Mercury Rising and Earth Retrograde) with Angry Robot Books.
people.name: R.W.W. Greene

people.bio: RJ Taylor is a queer speculative fiction writer from the Boston area. She studied at Emerson College and Grub Street's Novel Incubator program, is a SFWA member, active in the Codex Writer’s Group, and part of the Viable Paradise class of 2022. Her short fiction has appeared in Clarkesworld, Apex, and The Magazine of Fantasy & Science Fiction.
people.name: RJ Taylor

people.bio:
Rachael K. Jones grew up in various cities across Europe and North America, picked up (and mostly forgot) six languages, and acquired several degrees in the arts and sciences. Now she writes speculative fiction in Portland, Oregon.

Rachael is a Hugo, Nebula, Stoker, World Fantasy, and Locus Award finalist, and her fiction has appeared in multiple Year's Best anthologies and dozens of venues worldwide. Her stories can be found in Uncanny, Lightspeed, Beneath Ceaseless Skies, Strange Horizons, and all four Escape Artists podcasts.
people.name: Rachael K. Jones

people.bio: Rachel Gutin is a writer and special education teacher. Her short fiction has been published in venues such as Escape Pod and khōréō. She lives in Brooklyn, NY, and is a member of the organizing team for Brooklyn Speculative Fiction Writers.
people.name: Rachel Gutin

people.bio: Rachel Lara van der Merwe is an assistant professor in the Centre for Media and Journalism Studies at the University of Groningen. Her research explores the intersection of media, national identity, and coloniality within South Africa. Her upcoming book, We are not South African: Mediating National Identity in a Post-Apartheid State, is a decolonial critique of national identity as a broken form of mediation by which communities and individuals make sense of their belonging in the world. Rachel also studies the role video games play in facilitating national and cultural identities and the emerging video game industry in South Africa.
people.name: Rachel Lara van der Merwe

people.bio: Rachel Rener is an award-winning, #1 bestselling contemporary fantasy author who loves blurring the line between science and magic.
people.name: Rachel Rener

people.bio: Rachel Swirsky is a science fiction and fantasy short story writer with more than 100 publications since 2006. Her work has twice won the Nebula Award, and been nominated for the Hugo, Locus, and World Fantasy Awards. Her recent novella "January Fifteenth" came out from Tor.com in 2023.
people.name: Rachel Swirsky

people.bio: RAJAN KHANNA is a writer, game designer, and musician who lives in Philadelphia. His Ben Gold novels, starting with Falling Sky, take place in a post-apocalyptic world of airships and floating cities. His short fiction has appeared in Analog, Asimov’s, Beneath Ceaseless Skies, Clarkesworld, Fantasy, Lightspeed, and multiple anthologies. His articles, reviews, and commentary have appeared on Tor.com, LitReactor, and The Geek’s Guide to the Galaxy. His game design work for the Dungeons and Dragons and Tales of the Valiant TTRPGs can be found on DMsGuild.com and in multiple Kobold Press products. His website is www.rajankhanna.com.
people.name: Rajan Khanna

people.bio: Randee Dawn is the author of the Amazon bestselling funny, fantastical pop culture novel "Tune in Tomorrow," which was a finalist in the 2023 Next Generation Indie Awards. Her latest story, "The Fifth Horseman," appears in the new antholgy "The Four ???? of the Apocalypse." An entertainment journalist who writes for The Los Angeles Times, Variety, Today.com and many other publications, Randee lives in Brooklyn, New York with her spouse and a fluffy, sleepy Westie.
people.name: Randee Dawn

people.bio: Rebecca grew up reading in the Rockies and has lived in many places, including Tokyo, Japan & Stuttgart, Germany. Rebecca's short fiction has been published by or is forthcoming from Flame Tree, Apparition Lit, Galaxy's Edge, Air & Nothingness Press, and others. She is the managing editor at Apex Magazine and Apex Book Company. Rebecca reads, edits, and writes when she's not playing Stardew Valley or raising her children. She is fueled by cheese-covered starch and corgi fur. Find her on the internet: https://linktr.ee/rebeccaetreasure
people.name: Rebecca E. Treasure

people.bio: Rebecca Gault is an early-career academic from Glasgow, Scotland. She has a MA in English Literature and an MLitt in Fantasy Literature from the University of Glasgow. Their research interests include monstrosity, LGBTQ+ studies, and modes of fantasy. With previous research on the sexual politics of monstrosity, she is an up-and-coming researcher and writer in fields of the fantastic. She is the co-host of Out To Get You, a queer horror podcast (@OutToGetYouPod on Instagram) featuring guests such as Gretchen Felker-Martin. She is also a performer in TTRPG Actual Play spaces. Rebecca can be found on BlueSky at @phoenixforce.
people.name: Rebecca Gault

people.bio: Rebecca is a short story writer, podcaster and gamer.
people.name: Rebecca Rajendra

people.bio: Rebecca Zahabi is a mixed-heritage SFF writer. Her début adult novel, The Collarbound, came out with Gollancz in May 2022 and made it to the top 10 Sunday Times bestseller list. The final volume of the trilogy is due for May 2024. Her short stories have appeared in The Magazine of Fantasy & Science-Fiction, Shoreline of Infinity and PodCastle, and are due to appear in Infinite Worlds and Cast of Wonders. Aside from writing traditional fiction, she also writes for videogames.
people.name: Rebecca Zahabi

people.bio:
Red The Wizard is a linguist and conlanger, creator of the Celenian language for L. R. Lam's bestselling novel Dragonfall. 


Tha An Draoidh Dearg nan cànanaiche 's cànanadair, chruthaich iad an cànan Celenian airson sàr-ùirsgeil Dragonfall le L. R. Lam.
people.name: Red The Wizard

people.bio: Regina Kanyu Wang is a writer, researcher, and editor, currently a doctoral research fellow under the CoFUTURES project at the University of Oslo. She writes science fiction, nonfiction and academic essays in both Chinese and English. She is co-editor of the Chinese SF special issue of Vector, The Way Spring Arrives and Other Stories: A Collection of Chinese Science Fiction and Fantasy in Translation from a Visionary Team of Female and Nonbinary Creators, New Voices in Chinese Science Fiction, and the English version of The Making of The Wandering Earth: A Film Production Handbook. She has won multiple Chinese Nebula Awards, and been a finalist of Hugo Awards and Locus Awards, for her stories, reviews, editorial works, and more.
people.name: Regina Kanyu Wang

people.bio:
Regina M Hansen is the author of the young adult supernatural novel The Coming Storm set in her birthplace of Prince Edward Island, Canada, and incorporating Scottish and Scottish diaspora folklore and music. The book is out now in paperback from Atheneum Books for Young Readers, and was a nominee for the 2022 Red Maple and Mythopoeic Awards.

​Her nonfiction essays have appeared in The Boston Globe, Enchanted Living, The Wall Street Journal Review, and The Conversation. 

​Regina has written and edited scholarly essays and books on many topics, including monsters, Halloween, horror movies, elves, angels, demons and Christmas stories.  Most recently, she is the co-editor (with Jeffrey Weinstock) of Giving the Devil His Due: Satan and Cinema (Fordham University Press), nominated for the Bram Stoker Award.  She teaches at Boston University.
people.name: Regina M Hansen

people.bio: Professor of Geography, McGill University. Conduct research on smart cities, open data, and climate modeling. Most recently, research AI ethics and public participation in AI.
people.name: Renée Sieber

people.bio: Ric Bretschneider obsessively collects geek activities. If you Google him, you'd swear you're looking at five different guys. A professional software developer for decades, your computer likely has at least one application he's worked on. Founder of the San Jose branch of the Pecha Kucha presentation event, he loves the city and jumps at any chance to promote or contribute to its arts community. He consults with individuals and groups on how to effectively present and engage an audience, and he serves on the executive board of The Presentation Guild. Producer, sound engineer and contributor to the weekly Fanboy Planet Podcast, he’s excited to have produced over 600 episodes of fan-interest news and commentary. Lately he’s been into pro and fan applications of e-communities and podcasting. When he has a moment, Ric reads books and comics, and plays analog board and card games. He's here to help people, it's what he does. You can learn more about his creative, rebellious, and social sides by visiting his web site at ricbret.com
people.name: Ric Bretschneider

people.bio: Richard Gilliam is a veteran writer/editor of short-stories and non-fiction.
people.name: Richard Gilliam

people.bio: 4+ decades of professional writing (TV and radio scripts, plays, libretti, lyrics, books).  Comedy credits include the Schoolmaster sketch for Rowan Atkinson (Secret Policeman’s Ball), Not The Nine O’clock News and much UK TV before moving to LA when hired by Columbia Picture TV.  Author of fantasy adventure (with plenty of comedy) New Rock New Role, published December 2023 by US imprint CAEZIK SF&F, the first of four so far written in the New Rock series.  First sequel, New Rock New Realm, is to be published in November.
people.name: Richard Sparks

people.bio:
Richard Swan is a critically acclaimed British genre writer. His debut fantasy novel, The Justice of Kings, was an instant Sunday Times bestseller and has been translated into seven languages. His other work includes the Art of War and Great Silence trilogies, as well as short fiction for Black Library and Grimdark Magazine.

Richard is a qualified lawyer, and before writing full time spent ten years litigating multimillion pound commercial disputes in London. He currently lives in Sydney with his wife and three young sons.
people.name: Richard Swan

people.bio:
Rick Danforth is an author from Yorkshire, England, where he works as a Systems Architect to fund his writing habit.

His short fiction can be found in Hexagon, Translunar Traveller’s Lounge, and many other places. Two of his stories have been shortlisted for BSFA awards.

He one day hopes to introduce himself as an author without feeling awkward about it.
people.name: Rick Danforth

people.bio: Rivers Solomon is an author of literary and speculative fiction. They write about life in the margins, where they are much at home. Their books, An Unkindness of Ghosts, The Deep, and Sorrowland have received critical acclaim. Model Home, a novel about what it's like to in the aftermath of growing up in a house that savored the taste of your collapse, comes out 1 October, 2024.
people.name: Rivers Solomon

people.bio: Riziki Millanzi (she/her) is a final-year PhD student at the University of Sussex, England. She has just submitted her thesis "Empowerment, Protest and Celebration: The representation of ‘Black Girl Magic’ in Speculative Fiction and Contemporary Culture". Riziki was the recipient of the 22/23 Thomas W. Wilkins Fellowship from the Huntington Library in San Marino, California, where she accessed the papers of the late Science Fiction author Octavia E. Butler. Riziki's research interests include the representation of Black women and Black feminist thought in Speculative literature, film, and comics.
people.name: Riziki Millanzi

people.bio: Rob Cameron is a teacher, linguist, and writer. Among other publications, he has poetry, stories, and essays in Star*Line, The Magazine of Fantasy & Science Fiction, Tor.com, Foreign Policy Magazine, Solarpunk Magazine as well as curricula material for the Carterhaugh School of Folklore. His debut middle grade novel Daydreamer  from Labyrinth Road, Random House Kids, was released August 6th '24.  http://www.rob-cameron.com/daydreamer.html His debut novelette Ice Like Honey, comes out in Lightspeed Magazine, Fall 2024.
people.name: Rob Cameron / Cameron Roberson

people.bio: Rob J. Hayes has been a student, a banker, a marine research assistant, a chef, and a keyboard monkey more times than he cares to count. But eventually his love of fantasy and reading drew him to the life of a writer. He’s the author of multiple award winning series including The First Earth Saga, The Mortal Techniques, The War Eternal, and the upcoming God Eater Saga.
people.name: Rob J. Hayes

people.bio: Robbie Guillory runs Underline Literary Agency, Glasgow's only literary agency, which specialises in science fiction, fantasy and horror.
people.name: Robbie Guillory

people.bio: Long-time SF fan and convention goer, geek and techie type.
people.name: Robert (nojay) Sneddon

people.bio:
Robert Berg is a freelance copy editor, proofreader, and writer. For many years, he ran the successful entertainment reviews blog, Rob Will Review..., as well as HensonBlog, which was specifically dedicated to the works and career of Jim Henson. Some of his online critical writing has been published in physical form, including in Jurassic London's Hugo-nominated Speculative Fiction 2012: The Best Online Reviews, Essays and Commentary, as well as its 2013 follow-up. He is the co-founder of the new queer SFF indie press, Bona Books, whose first anthology, I Want That Twink OBLITERATED!, is coming out later this year. He lives in London on a narrowboat with his partner, Trip Galey.

Pronouns: he/him
people.name: Robert Berg

people.bio: Rob's day job makes him accountable for the security of a major research university. A life long love of SF and Fantasy was a great preparation for the stories he hears every day.
people.name: Robert Maughan

people.bio:
Robert Ramsay was born in 1964 and is still wondering about that. Wizard, lyricist, and some sort of musician, he has been a member of 'Men Are Dead', 'Tinyfish', and 'Tits Out For Captain Power', and is now a solo artist, Consulting Lyricist to the Gentry, and, if you have need of such a thing, a voiceover for your recording project.

He's been in a triumphant live concert video, played festivals in Britain, Poland and the U.S., and once saved the Swedish Stock Exchange.

His album 'Confound and Disturb' is available on Bad Elephant Music, and does what it says on the tin.

In parallel to this, he has spent thirty years researching relativity, quantum physics, entropy and chaos theory to try and make some sense of parapsychology, and the nature of reality. He has published his findings as the paperback and ebook, 'The Engineering of Coincidence', searching for a truly scientific explanation of magic, with none of that 'aetheric vibrations' nonsense, nor indeed any mention of the gypsies originating from Atlantis.

He says about his book: "Since I'm dealing with remodelling the Universe, the ideas in the book can be difficult. That's why I resolved to make the writing as clear as possible."
people.name: Robert Ramsay

people.bio: Profesional writer since 1955.  Hundreds of novels and short stories published.  Winner of Hugos and Nebulas, former Worldcon guest of honor, SFWA Grand Master.
people.name: Robert Silverberg

people.bio: Robin Duncan is a Scot born and living in Glasgow. A Civil Engineer by profession, he has written since 1980, but seriously only for the last 12 years. Robin’s debut novel The Mandroid Murders published in 2022; its sequel The Carborundum Conundrum in 2023. The Rigel Redemption is due 2024. His stories feature in Space Wizard’s Distant Gardens, Farther Reefs, Lofty Mountains and World of Juno anthologies. Robin’s story “The NEU Oblivion” was long-listed for the 2019 James White Award. Robin belongs to the Glasgow SF Writers’ Circle, Reading Excuses, the British Fantasy Society, and the British Science Fiction Association.
people.name: Robin CM Duncan

people.bio: Rochele Rosa is a creative consultant, strategic communications specialist, screenwriter and novelist. Her business Arxegos, aims to be a production house for building and consulting with multimedia franchises. She has a science ficiton novel, Vicious Circle, released October 27, 2023 that she has adapted into a short film.
people.name: Rochele Rosa

people.bio: Born in London, Rogba was raised across both London and Lagos, Nigeria. He is a descendant of John Augustus Otunba-Payne; the noted lawyer, writer and murdered prince of the Ijebu-Ode royal family. His debut, 'The Dance of Shadows', is an epic fantasy inspired by West African spirituality and the passed-down stories of his youth. A seasoned people watcher, Rogba is most alive when writing speculative fiction which examines the deep-rooted beliefs, myths and stories that underpin culture and the beautiful lies that inspire them.
people.name: Rogba Payne

people.bio: Rosalie M. Lin is a Chinese-American writer from the San Francisco Bay Area. She has, at various points in the past decade, graduated with a degree in Comparative Literature, pole-danced in two Beijing nightclubs, and dropped out of a biomedical PhD program before seriously pursuing her original dream of becoming an author. Daughter of Calamity is her debut novel.
people.name: Rosalie M. Lin

people.bio: Rachel Kareem (better known by her pen name Rosario Blue) is a British-Nigerian, autistic writer, and freelance journalist who has written for various online and print publications, like the Bookseller, STV, Techradar, and The Peckham Peculiar. She writes Afrofuturism and fantasy as colourful as she often presents and is influenced by Nigerian history, particularly Yoruba spirituality.
people.name: Rosario Blue

people.bio: ROSE DREW is a public speaker, book publisher, events manager, physical and forensic anthropologist, and performance poet. Rose and Alan Gillott operate small press Stairwell Books, and truly love creating small indie press festivals! Rose presented a TEDx talk on performance poetry in 2015. Rose is most pleased with creating poetry series “Poetry For All”, the first large poetry event in the UK to include BSL interpretation, and to feature disabled and non-disabled performers, famous and local. The first headliner was Raymond Antrobus, who has since won the Ted Hughes prize.
people.name: Rose Drew

people.bio:
Roseanna Pendlebury is a member of 2024 Hugo finalist nerds of a feather, flock together.

She's a London-based reviewer mainly interested in scifi and fantasy, but occasionally prone to dabble in historical and mythological fiction. She is currently an editor and contributor at Ignyte winning fanzine the Nerds of a Feather, and has her own blog at readerofelse.wordpress.com. When not reading, she can be found playing rugby, collecting too many crafting hobbies or attempting to learn how to fight with a longsword.
people.name: Roseanna Pendlebury

people.bio:
Rotem Baruchin is a published author, playwright, director, and screenwriter. Her novel, "The City Guardian" (2022, https://www.kinbooks.co.il/about-us" -Zmora Bitan Publishing, Israel) won the Geffen Award (https://geffen.sf-f.org.il/geffen_2022/the-geffen-award) (the Israeli Hugos). She also won the Geffen Award for several of her short stories, novelettes, and novellas. She studied screenwriting at Tel Aviv University. She wrote screenplays for television, indie movies, radio drama, and web series.
Her plays and musicals have been featured in Israel at the Tzavta Theater, the LGBT Center, and various festivals and conventions. Some of her plays included interactive audience participation. She also wrote a two-year serialized story for the Israeli YA magazine Rosh 1. Some of her stories have been translated into English.
Rotem Baruchin works in the tech industry and is a regular participant in Israeli SF/F conventions, in which she runs writing workshops and other events, and is also a member of a volunteer group dedicated to the prevention of sexual harassment at conventions.
https://www.imdb.com/name/nm5959287/
people.name: Rotem Baruchin

people.bio: Russell is a historian, fiction author and games writer, when he remembers half of these things. At other times, he can be found gaming, whether via a table or a computer. Loves a bunch of fandoms and will talk about just about anything. It will surprise nobody who knows him that he likes planes too.
people.name: Russell A Smith

people.bio: Ruth EJ Booth is a multiple award-winning writer and academic based in Glasgow, Scotland. Her poetry and fiction can be found in Black Static, Pseudopod and The Dark magazine, amongst others. She is a winner of the BSFA Award for Best Short Fiction and the British Fantasy Award for Best Non-Fiction for her regular column in Shoreline of Infinity. Ruth co-edited the Fantasy and Gaming special issue of the British Fantasy Society Journal (due 2024). She is currently working on a creative PhD exploring experimental forms and the impact of (anti-)feminist metanarratives in video-game fandom.
people.name: Ruth EJ Booth

people.bio:
Ruth Frances Long writes romance and fantasy from the heart which often strays into weird and wonderful liminal places. She works in a specialized library of rare & occasionally crazy books.
She writes fantasy of all kinds, often featuring scary fairies. In 2015 she won the European Science Fiction Society Spirit of Dedication Award for Best Author of Children’s Science Fiction and Fantasy for A Crack in Everything.
As Jessica Thorne she writes adult fantasy women’s fiction, which wanders from Space Opera to time travel to epic fantasy.
people.name: Ruth Frances Long / Jessica Thorne

people.bio: I am an enthusiastic fan. I have attended 21 Eastercons since my first in 2001, and 4 Worldcons.  I have been BSFA judge on the Arthur C Clarke Award twice (2009 and 2013). I am also a very experienced primary school teacher (21 years and counting!)  In that role, I have recently rebuilt my primary school library.  I always enjoy a debate in programme items - whether I am moderating, on the panel, or in the audience.
people.name: Ruth O'Reilly

people.bio: Ruthann writes dark speculative, gothic horror, and fantasy fiction from her home on a rural cattle ranch in Texas, USA. Many successful anthologies feature her solo work. She now writes collaboratively with Natasha Sinclair of North Lanarkshire, Scotland. The pair have a unique partnership, working closely six thousand miles apart, and the popularity of their imprint “Brazen Folk Horror” continues to grow through readers and events. Their current work, a three-book series titled “The Delevan Trilogy,” is a “contemporary Gothic classic” rooted in Scottish folklore and mythology.
people.name: Ruthann Jagge/ Brazen Folk Horror

people.bio:
Ryan Cahill is the award-winning author of the bestselling epic fantasy series, The Bound and The Broken.

Born and raised in Ireland, Ryan now resides amongst the rolling hills and hobbit holes of Middle-Earth, New Zealand. He does not own enough swords, would sell his left kidney for a dragon egg, and despises mushrooms in all their eldritch forms.

There are three things Ryan has always told himself about writing. Write the books you want to read. Write the books that your younger self would be proud of you for reading. Make sure they have dragons.
people.name: Ryan Cahill

people.bio:
After escaping his hometown in Central Florida, Ryan made his way to the University of Southern California, studying to become a chemical engineer. He was sure he would one day be an asteroid miner.

A year later, he was an English major working in concert production and writing a fantasy novel. These days, Ryan lives in Boston with his partner and their dog, which is *not* a demon. He still works in production and writes about ridiculous things, like a world where people eat kaiju to gain superpowers. 

His debut novel, *Seven Recipes for Revolution*, is expected Summer 2025.
people.name: Ryan Rose

people.bio: Ryann Fletcher is a science-fiction and fantasy author with too many hobbies and opinions about pasta.
people.name: Ryann Fletcher

people.bio: I am a local science-fiction and fantasy fan from Krakow, Poland. Professionally, I am engaged in project management, but after hours, for over a decade, I have been organizing SFF conventions. I first encountered fantasy during primary school, delving into the works of J.R.R. Tolkien and Philip Pullman. I am a fan of all things pop culture, film, and TV shows . I am an avid gamer of board and card games. During the conventions I attend, I often share stories about space exploration and the cosmos itself.
people.name: Rynvord

people.bio: S.B. Divya is a lover of science, math, fiction, and the Oxford comma. She is the Hugo and Nebula nominated author of Meru and Machinehood. Her short stories have appeared in numerous magazines and anthologies, and she is a former editor of Escape Pod, the weekly science fiction podcast. Divya holds degrees in Computational Neuroscience and Signal Processing. She worked for twenty years as an electrical engineer before becoming an author. Born in Pondicherry, India, Divya now resides in Southern California with her spouse, child, and two fur babies. She enjoys subverting expectations and breaking stereotypes whenever she can.
people.name: S.B. Divya

people.bio: S.L. Dove Cooper (she/they) is a queer author and editor. She spends much of her time exploring asexuality and aromanticism in literature, finally having found a good use for her MA in English literature and creative writing. She currently resides on an island off the Euroepan continent and her idiom and spelling are, despite her best efforts, geographically confused, poor things. She has been chasing stories in some way or another since she was old enough to follow a narrative.
people.name: S.L. Dove Cooper

people.bio: Simon R Green is a professional author, with eighty novels, two short story collections and one film. That includes the Deathstalker books, and the Nightside and Ishmael Jones series. He has also worked as a journalist, actor and bicyle repair mechanic.
people.name: SIMON R GREEN

people.bio: SJ Groenewegen wrote the novels The Disinformation War (GoldSF, 2023), Lethbridge-Stewart: A Most Haunted Man (Candy Jar, 2022), and Lethbridge-Stewart: Daughters of Earth (Candy Jar, 2017). SJ also wrote the Black Archive on Doctor Who's Face the Raven, as well as numerous essays on Doctor Who, SFF, gaming, and being queer. SJ's short fiction has won awards (Scarlet Stiletto in 2002), appeared in Big Finish’s Doctor Who Short Trips range, the Lethbridge-Stewart Havoc Files collections and UNIT anthologies. In 2016, SJ was awarded a British Empire Medal (BEM) for services to law enforcement and LGBTQIA diversity. SJ is a committee member of the Society of Authors in Scotland.
people.name: SJ Groenewegen

people.bio:
I am an artist and have exhibited at numerous conventions and will do so again in Glasgow. I knit and take photos.
I am also a masquerader. I am frequently on programme items relating to media, art and my day job of crisis management.
I have volunteered for numerous con committees and was the Head of Programme for Paragon Eastercon 2001
people.name: Sabine Furlong

people.bio: Sabine Sharp is a writer whose work explores the intersections of trans theory, feminist history, and science fiction. They were awarded a PhD by the University of Manchester in 2021; their thesis traced the emergence of the category “trans” and explored the insights feminist science fiction works might offer current debates on trans issues.
