They are currently developing new scholarly writing on trans-authored science fiction. Together with Douglas A. Vakoch, they are co-editor of The Routledge Handbook of Trans Literature, published April 2024, and The Handbook of Transgender Science Fiction (forthcoming). Their writing has been published in Contemporary Women’s Writing and Corridor8.
people.name: Sabine Sharp

people.bio: Consultant Obstetrician and long time science fiction and fantasy afficionado
people.name: Sacha Haworth

people.bio: Sam Beckbessinger is the author of the bestselling Manage Your Money Like a Fucking Grownup and the horror novel Girls of Little Hope (co-authored with Dale Halvorsen). Her interactive story about climate change, Survive the Century, was featured in New Scientist and Gizmodo. She teaches creative writing at Bath Spa University, writes kids' TV and picture books, once wrote for Marvel, and is weirdly obsessed with spreadsheets. She grew up on a farm near Durban with a pet donkey named Mr Magoo, but now lives in London.
people.name: Sam Beckbessinger

people.bio: Sam Bradbury is Publishing Director for Del Rey at Penguin Random House UK, and publishes science fiction, fantasy and horror. She previously worked for Hodderscape, and Jo Fletcher Books. She also holds a master’s degree in Publishing and a Bachelor of Science in Psychology. In her spare time, she is a nerd of many flavours, aspiring monster slayer, and proud owner of a dinosaur terrarium.
people.name: Sam Bradbury

people.bio:
Sam Scheiner is a long-time fan and scientist. He grew up in the Pittsburgh area and got involved in fandom during college. At the University of Chicago, he reincarnated the science fiction club. He met his wife at Windycon in Chicago, and his daughter attended her first con at the age of 4 weeks, sleeping underneath a huckster table. Currently he is involved in the Washington Science Fiction Association and is a past chair of the local convention – Capclave.  

 

His scientific areas of expertise are ecology and evolution, and he has published 11 books, including The Ecology of Plants and The Theory of Ecology, and over 120 scientific papers. He has also co-authored a book with SF author Phyllis Eisenstein on arthritis. For the past 25 years he has worked at the U.S. National Science Foundation giving away money.
people.name: Sam Scheiner

people.bio: Sam Tegtmeyer is a 1st year PhD researcher at the University of Glasgow. His project ‘Opening a Canon of Maggots: Tradition, Innovation, and the Ideologies of Fantasy’ explores the pernicious persistence of problematic ideologies in the Fantasy genre and the ways authors conscious of that persistence have actively challenged it. His research interests include queer theory, gender theory, and postcritique as well as anti-colonial pedagogies to explore the different ways we can inhabit the fantasy genre and challenge received ideologies.
people.name: Sam Tegtmeyer

people.bio:
Sam Wilson is a writer and director living in Cape Town, South Africa. He is the author of Zodiac (Penguin) and The First Murder On Mars (Orion).

He is the current director and head writer of the  animated series Jungle Beat, with 11 million subscribers and 5.5 billion views on YouTube, and wrote and directed the feature film Jungle Beat 2 The Past.
people.name: Sam Wilson

people.bio:
Samantha is a classically trained actor, best known as Karlach in "Baldur's Gate 3". This role won them the GANG Award for Best Voice Performance, alongside nominations for the BAFTA and DICE Awards.
 
Other sci-fi and fantasy parts include Random in "The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy" on Radio 4 and national theatre tours, Calliope in Neil Gaiman's "The Sandman" for Audible and Orr in "Torchwood" for Big Finish Productions.

They are the creator and host of “It Takes A Village”, a streaming chat show with people who work in the games industry on themes of collaboration, friendship and community.
people.name: Samantha Béart

people.bio: Samantha Shannon is the New York Times and Sunday Times bestselling author of the Bone Season and Roots of Chaos series. Her work has been translated into twenty-six languages. The Priory of The Orange Tree, her first book outside the Bone Season series, was an international bestseller and has sold over a million copies worldwide. Her latest novel, A Day of Fallen Night, was an instant #1 Sunday Times bestseller, as well as a New York Times bestseller. She lives in London.
people.name: Samantha Shannon

people.bio:
Samuel Poots is the Writer-in-Residence at Ulster University and a PhD researcher in Creative Writing, examining revolution within High Fantasy. His stories have been published by Neon Hemlock, Cast of Wonders, and Dark Matter, and he is a regular contributor to games such as Warhammer Fantasy Roleplay, Imperium Maledictum, and Jim Henson's Labyrinth: The Adventure Game. He communicates primarily through Pratchett quotes and can often be seen wandering the Antrim coast. If found, please give him a cup of tea and send him home via the nearest post office.
Follow Sam across social media as @pootsidoodle
people.name: Samuel Poots

people.bio: Sandra Bond is a novelist ("The Psychopath Club", "The Devil's Finger"), poet and the current European TAFF administrator. She is queer, trans, neurodivergent, feminist, determined, and often downright stroppy. She has been involved in SF and fandom for more than half her life, and has yet to learn better. Her newest novel, "Three Men In Orbit", launches at this Worldcon.
people.name: Sandra Bond

people.bio: Sandy Manning is a semi-retired math/science teacher who spent her time teaching in the Bush of Alaska. Currently, she teaches one semester a year and travels the rest of the year.  She has been involved in costuming since the age of 15 and has been involved with Masquarade both onstage and behind stage since the 1980's at least.  She also loves playing with uses of technology for the math classroom. In additions, she loves learning things.
people.name: Sandy Manning

people.bio: Santiago is a mental health therapist working with Latinx immigrants in New York City. Originally from Mexico, he’s passionate about weaving culture, mental health, queerness, and social justice into all his stories; as well as Spanish, his native language. He’s been published in Litro Magazine USA, Occulum Journal, and Latin@Literatures, and won second place in Flash Fiction Magazine’s 2023 contest. He’s been rejected by many other magazines, but sometimes nicely. He is a graduate of Taos Toolbox 2023, where he won George R. R. Martin’s 2023 Terran Prize.
people.name: Santiago Márquez Ramos

people.bio: Sara Felix is a Hugo award winning mixed media artist working in inks and resin. She also creates a weekly tiara for Tiara Tuesday and has been working on them since the beginning of the pandemic.  She is president of ASFA and the head of publications for Glasgow 2024 and created the logo for the convention and other art for the con.
people.name: Sara Felix

people.bio: Dr. Sara L. Uckelman is an associate professor of logic and philosophy of language at Durham University.  Her short stories and poems are published or forthcoming in Manawaker Studio Flash Fiction Podcast, the Martian Wave, Pendemic.ie, Pilcrow & Dagger, Speculatief, Story Seed Vault, and With Painted Words, and anthologies published by BCubed Press, Black Hare Press, Exterus, Flame Tree Publishing, Grace & Victory, Hic Dragones, Jayhenge Publications, QueerSciFi, and WolfSinger Publications.  She is also the co-founder of the reviews site SFFReviews.com, and founder of the small press Ellipsis Imprints (EllipsisImprints.com).
people.name: Sara L. Uckelman

people.bio: Sarah Beth Durst is the New York Times bestselling author of over twenty-five books for adults, teens, and kids, including cozy fantasy The Spellshop. She's been awarded an American Library Association Alex Award, as well as a Mythopoeic Fantasy Award. Several of her books have been optioned for film/television, including Drink Slay Love, which was made into a TV movie and was a question on Jeopardy! She lives in Stony Brook, New York, with her husband, her children, and her ill-mannered cat. Visit her at sarahbethdurst.com.
people.name: Sarah Beth Durst

people.bio:
I work in a variety of roles including Game Designer, Writer, and Creative Technologist.

Under the banner of Patchwork Fez I create TTRPGs, boardgames, and video games. My upcoming book of horror TTRPG scenarios set in the modern British countryside is called Darkened Hill & Dale. 

Other projects most often associated with me include the British Council’s 1940s cultural propaganda film collection and my own annual games-y event, Trick or Retreat. 

Sometimes I also write traditional SFF and horror fiction.
people.name: Sarah Cole

people.bio: Sarah Gulde is the Editor-In-Chief of Star Trek Quarterly, a three-time Hugo Award Finalist for Best Fanzine, and the 2024 TAFF delegate. She has appeared on Star Trek panels at cons across the US and abroad, and you can catch her in the Star Trek: Deep Space Nine documentary "What We Left Behind". Sarah lives in a former arboretum in Portland, OR.
people.name: Sarah Gulde

people.bio: Sarah J. Daley is a fantasy writer and former chef based outside of Chicago, Illinois. Her first novel Obsidian was a finalist for the Compton Crook Award for Best Fantasy Debut and picked as the American Library Journal’s Debut of the Month, January 2022. Her sophomore book is expected in July 2025, a tale of angels, machine guns and righteous fury.
people.name: Sarah J Daley

people.bio: Sarah Jackson writes speculative fiction and poetry and her work has appeared in Strange Horizons, Translunar Travelers Lounge, and Electric Spec. She is editor of Inner Worlds magazine and offers friendly and supportive writing workshops. Her website is https://sarah-i-jackson.ghost.io and you can find her on Mastodon as sarahijackson@wandering.shop
people.name: Sarah Jackson

people.bio: Sarah Langan's an award-winning novelist and screenwriter. Her most recent novel, A Better World, is out now. She's also the author of Good Neighbors, The Keeper, The Missing, and Audrey's Door. She has an MS in Environmental Toxicology from NYU, and lives in Los Angeles with her husband, daughters, and maniac rabbits.
people.name: Sarah Langan

people.bio: Creative Writing PhD student at the University of Derby, researching the influence of consuming science fiction on people's decision to study STEM subjects.
people.name: Sarah Margree

people.bio: Sarah Pinborough is a NYT and sunday times bestselling cross-genre author and screenwriter. She's written nearly thirty books and recently adapted her novel INSOMNIA for Paramount+.
people.name: Sarah Pinborough

people.bio: Sarah Pinsker is the Hugo, Nebula, and Philip K Dick Award winning author of A Song For A New Day, We Are Satellites, Sooner or Later Everything Falls Into the Sea, Lost Places, and over sixty works of short fiction. Her stories have appeared in Asimov's, Strange Horizons, Fantasy & Science Fiction, and Uncanny, and in numerous anthologies and year's bests; her novella Haunt Sweet Home will be published by Tordotcom in autumn 2024. She is also a singer/songwriter with four albums on various independent labels. She lives in Baltimore, Maryland, USA with her wife and two weird dogs. Find her online at sarahpinsker.com.
people.name: Sarah Pinsker

people.bio: Sarah Rees Brennan was born in Ireland by the sea, and is the New York Times bestselling, Carnegie nominated, Lodestar shortlisted writer of many novels. After living in New York, London and Melbourne she came home with late-stage cancer and after beating cancer, settled by a centuries-old library. A lifelong fan of villains because they have the best lines, her villainous fantasy Long Live Evil, out August 1, is her first adult work.
people.name: Sarah Rees Brennan

people.bio: Sarah Guan (she/her) is the publisher of Erewhon Books and a Hugo Award-nominated editor who came to Erewhon after a varied career at Ace, DAW, and Orbit. She has worked with acclaimed authors such as C. L. Polk, E. Lily Yu, Fran Wilde, Cassandra Khaw, Victor Manibo, Fonda Lee, Tasha Suri, Tade Thompson, Kacen Callender, and many more.
people.name: Sarah T. Guan

people.bio: I'm an autistic nonbinary creative based in North Lanarkshire. I was a 2022 All Stories mentee for my MG novel, I have a Masters in Writing for TV, and I wrote a play on commission for Birds of Paradise theatre company, which had a rehearsed reading at Rose Theatre Kingston. My first short story was published in Schoolbooks & Sorcery. My debut short film, Dead Susan, based on the song by Talis Kimberley screened at two BAFTA qualifying festivals, Oska Bright and LSFF. My next film, Quiet Hands, starring Louise Jameson, was funded by a Creative Youth grant.
people.name: Scar Ward

people.bio: Scott Edelman has published 120+ stories in such magazines and anthologies as Lightspeed, Analog, Apex, and MetaHorror. His collection of zombie fiction, What Will Come After, was a finalist for the Shirley Jackson Memorial Award, and his science fiction short stories have been collected in What We Still Talk About. His most recent collection is Things That Never Happened, about which Publishers Weekly wrote, "his talent is undeniable." He is an eight-time Stoker Award finalist and a four-time Hugo Award finalist in the category of Best Editor, Short Form. He is also host of the Eating the Fantastic podcast.
people.name: Scott Edelman

people.bio: Scott Lefton is an engineer and artist working in a variety of media including metal, glass, wood, leather, plastics, electronics, and Photoshop. He created the 2004 Hugo trophies and the 2015 mini-Hugo rocket that was displayed aboard the ISS. He is occasionally serious about photography. His hobbies include travel, creating unusual flavors of ice cream, learning new art and craft skills, and powerlifting. He lives in Melrose, Massachusetts with his wife Rachel.
people.name: Scott Lefton

people.bio: Scott Lynch was born in St.Paul, Minnesota in 1978. He sold his first novel, The Lies of Locke Lamora, in 2004. The latest novel in that series, The Thorn of Emberlain, is forthcoming. In addition to his writing, he also has a background in game design and firefighting. Scott currently lives in Massachusetts with his wife, award-winning SF/F novelist Elizabeth Bear.
people.name: Scott Lynch

people.bio: Sean is opening a new sf/f publisher in 2025.  A lifelong fan, he has worked in ten countries as a branding consultant, valuation expert, attorney, and strategist.  Interested in the interplay of history, cultures, law and technology, he finds sf/f a great landscape in which to explore these ideas.   Sean synthesizes these interests in his writings and panel discussions.
people.name: Sean Mead

people.bio: Seanan McGuire writes things.  It is difficult to make her stop.  She lives with several very large cats and a lot of My Little Ponies in the Pacific Northwest of the United States, and is very excited to return to Glasgow, where some of her favorite owls are located.
people.name: Seanan McGuire

people.bio: I am from Silesia, Poland, currently chasing polar bears in Finland. Translator turned IT, with a knack for solving problems and a tendency to go overboard with books, boardgames and theatre.
people.name: Serathe

people.bio: Seth Haddon is a queer Australian writer of fantasy. He is the author of REFORGED, REBORN, the upcoming RECLAIMED, and has sold two SF novellas to Tordotcom. VOLATILE MEMORY, the first of these trans sapphic novellas, is releasing 2025. He is a video game designer and producer, has a degree in Ancient History, and previously worked with cats. He lives in Sydney with his geriatric cat. Some of his previous adventures include exploring Pompeii with a famous archaeologist and being chased through a train station by a nun.
people.name: Seth Haddon

people.bio: Lifelong science fiction fan originally from Alaska, but living in Oregon since the late 90s, host of the Hugos There (since 2017) and Take Me To Your Reader (since 2014) podcasts, the former focused on reading award-winning SFF books, the latter focused on science fiction in adaptation.
people.name: Seth Heasley

people.bio:
Sgioba Luaidh Inbhirchluaidh is a group of between 7 and 9 women who perform Scottish Gaelic waulking songs in Jacobite (Outlander) costume and also other periods.

We have been waulking tweed for nearly 20 years and have  waulked 13 real tweeds in that time, but for performances and workshops we use a dry tweed. We have sung and demonstrated waulking at  many venues from small church halls to castles, small  groups to Clan Gatherings,and have been as far afield as Poland. We can be found on the last saturday of each month throughout the summer at the preserved township of Auchindrain, near Inverary.

Details about us and our songs can be found on our website www.waulk.org.
people.name: Sgioba Luaidh Inbhirchluaidh (Inverclyde Waulking Song Group)

people.bio: Shana Worthen is a historian of medieval technology and sff tie-in cookbooks. Originally from the US, she currently lives in Sweden where she takes photos of bridges and organises science fiction conventions.
people.name: Shana Worthen

people.bio: Shannon Chakraborty is the critically acclaimed, New York Times bestselling author of The Daevabad Trilogy and The Adventures of Amina al-Sirafi. Her work has been translated into over a dozen languages and nominated for the Hugo, Locus, World Fantasy, Crawford, and Astounding awards. You can find her online at www.sachakraborty.com or on Instagram at @SAChakrabooks.
people.name: Shannon Chakraborty

people.bio: A speculative fiction writer from Trinidad and Tobago, Shari Paul has been published in FIYAH, The Dark, Clarkesworld and Escape Pod, with reprints in Podcastle and Il Buio. Shari has a BA in Literatures in English from the University of the West Indies, and is currently under examination for an MFA in Creative Writing. Shari can usually be found on X, formerly known as Twitter.
people.name: Shari Paul

people.bio: Sharon Diane King (Ph.D., UCLA, Comparative Literature) is an Associate at UCLA's Center for Medieval and Renaissance Studies and director of the medieval / Renaissance theatre troupe Les Enfans Sans Abri. Recent academic publications include essays in the critical anthologies Of Bread, Blood and The Hunger Games; Supernatural, Humanity, and the Soul; and The Last Midnight: Critical Essays on Apocalyptic Narratives in Millennial Media. Her fiction has appeared in Dark Recesses Press Magazine, Galaxy's Edge Magazine, Kaleidotrope, On the Premises, All Due Respect, Creepy Podcast, and several anthologies by both Dragon's Roost Press and Third Flatiron Press.
people.name: Sharon Diane King

people.bio: Sharon Emmerichs is an author and a university professor. She received her Ph.D. in early modern and medieval literature and she teaches Shakespeare, poetry, drama, and prose from Beowulf to Milton. In 2021, she graduated with her MFA in Creative Writing--Fiction. Her debut novel, Shield Maiden, was an instant top ten Sunday Times bestseller, and she's never fully recovered from the shock of that happening.
people.name: Sharon Emmerichs

people.bio: Sharon Sheffield has been a fan of genre fiction since she could read. She has degrees in Linguistics & Anthropology and Divinity. An Episcopal priest, she moonlights as a writer, historical reenactor, and musician. She loves reading, singing, crafting, and perpetrating bad puns on friends.
people.name: Sharon Sheffield

people.bio: Shauna Lawless is an avid reader of Irish mythology and folklore. As an Irish woman, she loves that Irish mythology has inspired so many stories over the years, however, she wanted to explore the history and mythology of Ireland in a more authentic way. She lives in Northern Ireland with her family. Follow Shauna on twitter @shaunaLwrites, or on her blog at www.shaunalawless.com
people.name: Shauna Lawless

people.bio:
Sheenjini Ghosh has completed her Bachelor’s degree in English from St. Xavier’s College, Kolkata and
Masters in the same from Presidency University, Kolkata. She has worked as an English teacher in Delhi Public
School, Newtown, Kolkata and thereafter at Newtown School, Kolkata. She was associated as a Guest Lecturer
at the School of Languages, Jadavpur University in March,2018 and continued till February 2020. Currently,
she is associated as an SACT (Category I) at the English department of Gokhale Memorial Girls’ College. She
has a degree in Communicative French from Ram Krishna Mission, Golpark and has been an active volunteer
with C.R.Y since 2016. She has also conducted different projects and has been an integral part of different
teaching projects conducted by MacMillan and British Council in association with the Directorate of Education,
India. Her fields of interest include Partition studies, Film and media studies , Adaptation studies, Indian
Writing in English, Ecocriticism, Popular Literature, 19th -20th C literature, Detective Fiction, Women studies,
Feminism, Gender Studies, Queer Studies. Besides this, she takes avid interest in music. She maintains a blog
of her own which predominantly holds pieces of flash fiction, Writing short stories and poems in English and
vernaculars like Bengali and Hindi is also a favourite pastime of hers.
people.name: Sheenjini Ghosh

people.bio: Sherwood Smith has published over fifty books, one of which was an Anne Lindbergh Honor Book; she’s twice been a finalist for the Mythopoeic Fantasy Award and once a Nebula finalist. She teaches writing at Viable Paradise Writing Workshop on Martha’s Vineyard. Website at sherwoodsmith.net, and she has a Patreon, where she posts a chapter a day.
people.name: Sherwood Smith

people.bio:
Scottish fantasy author Shona Kinsella is the author of The Heart of Winter, The Vessel of KalaDene series, dark Scottish fantasy novella Petra MacDonald and the Queen of the Fae, British Fantasy Award shortlisted industrial novella The Flame and the Flood, and non-fiction Outlander and the Real Jacobites: Scotland’s Fight for the Stuarts. Her short fiction can be found in various magazines and anthologies. She served as editor of the British Fantasy Society’s fiction publication, BFS Horizons for four years and is now the Chair of the British Fantasy Society.

Shona lives near the picturesque banks of Loch Lomond with her husband and three children. She enjoys reading, nature walks, and spending time with her family. When she is not writing, doing laundry, or wrangling children, she can usually be found with her nose in a book.
people.name: Shona Kinsella

people.bio:
I'm a climate scientists working at Trinity College Dublin. I am interested in what the natural world will look like as we continue to change the planet.

I also play, GM and occasionally design tabletop RPGs. I am a founding member of Indie RPGs Dublin, an open and inclusive community for story focused, rules light TTRPGs.
people.name: Silvia Caldararu

people.bio: I'm a commissioning editor at Angry Robot Books. I've worked in publishing for nearly 35 years, including twenty years as an editorial director at Gollancz. I read, acquire and love SF, Fantasy and Horror - the weirder the better.
people.name: Simon Spanton

people.bio:
Simone Caroti is a Course Director in the Creative Writing BFA at Full Sail University in Winter Park, Orlando, Florida. He teaches the "Literary Genre 3: Science Fiction and Fantasy" class.

He has published two books so far - a history of the generation starship concept in science fiction and an overview of Iain M. Banks' Culture series. Both books were published by McFarland.

Simone is currently working on his third book, a reappraisal of the cyberpunk movement of the 1980s, for which he is under contract with McFarland.
people.name: Simone Caroti

people.bio: Sofia Rhei (Madrid, 1978) is an experimental and speculative author, with more than 50 published books. Her fantasy books for kids include the series El joven Moriarty (solds right to 3 languages) as well as many individual titles such Andersens Snow Queen sequel La calle Andersen (La Galera), cowritten with Marian Womack. As a poet, she was shortlisted for the Rhysling awards ad won the Dwarf Stars. Her genre novels for adults are Rondola (Minotauro), Celsius award winning humorous fantasy fairytale retelling, Esperame en la ultima pgina (Plaza y Janes), a ghost story about books (rights sold to 5 languages) and Newropia, Kelvin award-winning multi-utopian satire. Sofiarhei.com
people.name: Sofía Rhei

people.bio: Sonia Focke is an author and Egyptologist. Her many accomplishments include learning the velocipede at the tender age of 40, having a titanium rod for a backbone (literally) and knowing an insane number of songs by heart. Her work has appeared in several anthologies, Wyngraf and Fantasy & Science Fiction magazine (pending as of writing).
people.name: Sonia Focke

people.bio: Sonia Sulaiman writes short speculative fiction inspired by Palestinian folklore. Her work has appeared in Arab Lit Quarterly, Beladi, FANTASY, FIYAH Magazine, Xenocultivars: Stories of Queer Growth, Seize the Press, Lackington’s Magazine, and Ask the Night for a Dream. Her stories have been nominated for a Pushcart, Lammy, and Best New Weird awards. In her spare time, she curates the Read Palestinian Spec Fic Reading list.
people.name: Sonia Sulaiman

people.bio: Soph is a fan of science fiction and fantasy. They studied Physics a while ago, but have since got a job doing Automated Software Testing. They have a few creative hobbies like art, music. and TTRPGs, and most of their recent fandom experience comes from Eastercon. They are originally from North Wales, but they now live in England. They feel awkward writing a bio about themself in third person.
people.name: Soph Williams

people.bio: Stark Holborn is the author of the British Science Fiction Award-nominated Factus Sequence, the British Fantasy Award-nominated Triggernometry series and the groundbreaking digital serial, Nunslinger. Stark has worked as a games writer on BAFTA and TIGA-award winning projects and is currently lead writer on SF detective game Shadows of Doubt and a contributing writer on cyberpunk slice of life sim, Nivalis. Stark is a judge for the Arthur C. Clarke Award.
people.name: Stark Holborn

people.bio: Steen Comer is a writer redefining accepted ideas of what constitutes the fantastic. He is a graduate of Viable Paradise, and has previously been published in _Escape Pod_, the _Odd Salon Irregular_, and the _Sockdolager_ anthology, among others.
people.name: Steen Comer

people.bio: Stefan has narrated, produced, directed, and/or published over 5,000 audiobooks for Skyboat Media, Audible, Blackstone, MacMillan, Harper and PRH Audio, among them multiple titles by Gregory Benford, Fredric Brown, John Brunner, Orson Scott Card (Ender’s Game, etc.), Samuel R. Delany, Harlan Ellison, Jonathan L. Howard, Shirley Jackson, Henry Kuttner & CL Moore, Joe R. Lansdale, Ursula K. LeGuin, Anne McCaffrey, Robert Silverberg and Jack Vance. Skyboat’s audio publishing line now exceeds 350 titles, 2/3 of them SF. In addition to being named a “Golden Voice” by AudioFile Magazine, Stefan has received two GRAMMYs, a Bram Stoker Award, a Ray Bradbury Award, a Fringe First at The Edinburgh Fringe (Salford Road), two Hugos (Lightspeed Magazine), and over a dozen Audie Awards. Stefan has taught at college level and chaired Departments of Theatre, Film and Dance.
people.name: Stefan Rudnicki

people.bio: Stephen Aryan is an award winning fantasy author. He has written two trilogies, the Age of Darkness, and the Age of Dread, plus a prequel novella, set in the magic-infused world of Mordana. He has also written the Quest for Heroes duology, The Coward and The Warrior, published by Angry Robot Books. His latest novel, The Blood Dimmed Tide, is the second instalment in a Persian-inspired historical fantasy trilogy, The Nightingale and the Falcon.
people.name: Stephen Aryan

people.bio: Stephen Cave is Co-Director of the Institute for Technology and Humanity, and Academic Director of the Leverhulme Centre for the Future of Intelligence, both at the University of Cambridge. His research is mostly in the philosophy and ethics of technology, with two strands. First, he writes about the ethics of AI and robotics. His publications on this include the co-edited volumes AI Narratives (Oxford University Press, 2020), Imagining AI (Oxford University Press, 2023), and Feminist AI (Oxford University Press, 2023). Second, he writes about the ethics of life-extension and the philosophy of (im)mortality. His publications on this topic include Immortality (Crown, Penguin Random House, 2012), a New Scientist book of the year, and Should You Choose To Live Forever? (with John Martin Fischer, Routledge, 2023). His work has been covered in many hundreds of media outlets around the world, and he regularly appears on television and radio.
people.name: Stephen Cave

people.bio:
Writer, role-playing game designer, academic, reviewer, recovering bookseller. Author of dark fantasy novels THE ART OF ARROW CUTTING and SHADOWS BITE and three SHADOWRUN tie-in novels. 120 short stories published in assorted magazines and anthologies (including a Big Finish Doctor Who story), reprinted in three collections.
Nominated for Bram Stoker Award, BSFA Award, Seiun Award, Sidewise Award and Gaylactic Spectrum Award; won Aurealis and Ditmar Awards.
Have written for GURPS, Car Wars, V&V and other TTRPGs.
Former co-owner and manager of science fiction specialist bookshop. 13 years teaching creative writing at University of Western Australia, including SF/Fantasy writing. PhD thesis published as MAY THE ARMED FORCES BE WITH YOU: THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN SCIENCE FICTION AND THE UNITED STATES MILITARY
people.name: Stephen Dedman

people.bio: Stephen Granade is an interactive narrative designer, writer, and co-editor of Small Wonders, a speculative fiction magazine for flash fiction and poetry. Their latest game, "Professor of Magical Studies," is available from Choice of Games, and their short fiction has appeared in Strange Horizons, Escape Pod, Baffling Magazine, and elsewhere.
people.name: Stephen Granade
Stephen Oram

people.bio:
This is my 10th WorldCon, the first also being in Glasgow back in 1995. I was one of the founders and organisers of the Redemption series of convention in the UK. And I have been involved in running Eastercons and was part of the committee for two of them. 

My SF likes cover books, TV, films, theatre and even radio shows - I used to listen to Hitchhiker's Guide on a transistor radio at university. I was very involved in Blake's 7 fandom, and even tried my hand at some fan fiction at the time.

And I may see some of you on Thursday evening, as I am one of the organisers of the Worldcon Pub Crawl, where we will explore some of Glasgow's interesting venues.
people.name: Steve Rogerson

people.bio:
Steve Toase was born in North Yorkshire, England, and now lives in the Frankenwald, Germany. His fiction has appeared in Analog, Nightmare Magazine, Shadows & Tall Trees 8, Three Lobed Burning Eye, and Shimmer amongst others. His stories have been selected for Ellen Datlow’s Best Horror of the Year series, and Paula Guran’s Year’s Best Dark Fantasy and Horror. He also likes bonsai forests, old motorbikes. and vintage cocktails. His debut short story collection ‘To Drown in Dark Water’ is published by Undertow Publications You can find him at stevetoase.co.uk

From 2014 he was lead writer and associate producer, with Becky Cherriman and Imove Arts on Haunt, the Saboteur Award shortlisted project inspired by his own teenage experiences of being homeless and vulnerably housed, about Harrogate’s haunting presence in the lives of people experiencing homelessness in the town. (https://www.tessagordz.co.uk/haunt-harrogate/)
people.name: Steve Toase

people.bio: Steve Willis is an engineer and innovator with decades of experience providing solutions to environmental problems for large-scale industries. The start of the covid lockdowns gave him pause to think carefully about climate solutions, what was needed and what it would take to get there. This led to a collaboration with the GreenStories team to produce the No More Fairy Tales anthology for COP27. 5 stories from this anthology have been developed into a complete novel – Fairhaven, a novel of climate optimism. Steve continues to work on large-scale climate solutions, currently developing a CO2 sequestration mineralisation process which can be deployed at the million-tonne scale.
people.name: Steve Willis   Fairhaven - A Novel of Climate Optimism

people.bio: Stewart Hotston lives in Reading, UK. With a Celtic-Indian mother and a father of North African/Roma descent, Stewart is a somewhat confused second-generation immigrant living in the UK. His writing concerns those whose voices are more than capable but too frequently marginalised and how they build hope, connection and live in the worlds in which they find themselves. His loves big ideas, weird worlds and people who refuse to give up. His novels include the BFS and Subjective Chaos finalist, Entropy of Loss as well as the tech thriller, Tangle’s Game and the science fiction novels based in the Watch Dogs universe - Daybreak Legacy and Stars & Stripes.
people.name: Stew Hotston (he/him)

people.bio: Gautam Bhatia is an Indian SF writer, reviewer, and co-ordinating editor of the Strange Horizons magazine. He is the author of the SF duology, The Wall (2020) and The Horizon (2021). He has been long-listed for the Astounding Award, and a finalist for the BSFA Award (non-fiction). His third novel, The Sentence, is due out in September 2024.
people.name: Strange Horizons

people.bio: I'm a former convention organiser, amateur comics historian and one of the writers for Marvel's official Handbooks and related titles.
people.name: Stuart Vandal

people.bio: Su J  Sokol is a social rights activist and a writer of speculative and interstitial fiction. A former legal services lawyer from New York City, xe now makes Montréal xyr home. Sokol is the author of three novels: Cycling to Asylum, which was long-listed for the Sunburst Award and later published in French under the title Les lignes invisibles, Run J Run, and Zee, a finalist for the Janet Savage Blachford Prize for Children’s and Young Adult Literature. Five Points on an Invisible Line, the sequel to Cycling to Asylum, is scheduled to be published in the spring of 2025. When Su is not writing, battling slumlords, bringing evil bureaucracies to their knees, and smashing borders, xe curates and participates in readings and literary events in Canada and abroad.
people.name: Su J Sokol

people.bio:
Writer's Bio:
Of Indian origin, Sultana Raza is an independent scholar. She’s presented papers on Romanticism (Keats) and Fantasy (Tolkien) in international conferences e.g. Oxonmoot (2019-2023), PCA/ACA 2018, IMC Leeds (2019 & 2021), Mythcon 2022, WorldCon 2019, CoNZealand 2020, and at Chicon8.

Her CNF was published in Literary Ladies Guide, Literary Yard, Litro, impspired, Dream Pop Journal etc. Her fiction received an Honorable Mention in Glimmer Train Review. Her poems/fiction/CNF have appeared in 200+ journals. SFF work in: Abyss & Apex, Entropy, Columbia Journal, Star*line, Bewildering Stories, Focus & Vector (BSFA), Unlikely Stories Mark V, Galaxy series, Blaze Vox, Musing on Muses Anthology (Birgid Gate’s Press), Nephilim Anthology (Iron Faerie) Antipodean SF, File770, and Penumbric (in future).

Artist’s Bio
An awarded artist, Sultana Raza received the Leonardo Award at the Cianciano Biennale (2013), and Honorbale Mentions in the 22nd & 23rd Julia Cameron Awards (Digital category Feb. & May ’24), and in the 21st Pollux Awards (May ’24).
She has exhibited in group exhibitions in Europe (ECA in Luxembourg, Italy, Monaco, Finland), and the USA. Her artworks were published in various art publications, including New Collector’s Book in 2013, Contemporary Masters, Royal Monaco. Also, in literary journals including Bewildering Stories (Issues 954 & 1022), Utopia Science Fiction (in Dec. ’23), Amon Hen (Feb 2022, Tolkien Society), Vingilot (Winter 2023, Tolkien Society), and Alchemy Spoon (Dec.2023). Also, in 3Elements Review (2016, 2022, & Cover Art in Aug. ’23 & Feb.’24), and as Cover Art of Focus (BSFA: 2022, 2023 & 2024), and Rigorous (July ’23 & Jan ’24).
https://www.facebook.com/sultana.raza.7
people.name: Sultana Raza

people.bio: SunnyJim is a bespoke shoemaker and artist working primarily in textiles. An avid collector of skills and a deep fan of Lord of the Rings, she was once described as the love child of Martha Stewart and MacGuyver. Her owners, a pair of incorrigible housecats, diligently supervise all of her work.
people.name: SunnyJim Morgan

people.bio: Sunyi Dean was born in Texas, grew up in Hong Kong, and now resides in North England. She writes speculative fiction with a weird slant, and has both too many books and too many children. Her poetry and short fiction has been published in places like Tor Dot Com, Aurealis, Prole, FFO, and other magazines. Her debut novel, THE BOOK EATERS, launched Aug 2022 and was an instant #2 Sunday Times Bestseller. She is also the founder and co-host of the Publishing Rodeo Podcast, an industry talkshow devoted to starting big conversations about transparency in publishing.
people.name: Sunyi

people.bio: Susan Weiner is a Biology professor, larp writer, songwriter, and general trouble maker. They also make ridiculously complicated meals and tweet about the Talmud.
people.name: Susan Weiner

people.bio: Susan has been active in fandom for more than forty years as a costumer, masquerade emcee, and all-around fan.  She has worked as a book reviewer for Publisher's Weekly and the Amazon Breakthrough Novel Contest and ran the Hugo Awards Ceremony in 2012.  Professionally, she is a social dance historian who conducts balls, teaches dance workshops, and DJs for blues and waltz events.
people.name: Susan de Guardiola

people.bio: Susie Williamson (she/her) is a double award-winning author, artist and poet. Her fantasy series, Blood Gift Chronicles, published by Stairwell Books, begins with Return of the Mantra and The Warder. Inspired by authors such as Ursula Le Guin and Nnedi Okorafor, Susie loves inventive worlds, diverse characters and thought-provoking, contemporary themes. She is currently working on the third novel in her series, continuing with the themes of wildlife and the environment, social justice and marginalisation, magic, animism and dragons.
people.name: Susie Williamson

people.bio: Suzan Palumbo is a Trinidadian Canadian writer and editor who has been nominated for the Nebula and World Fantasy awards. Her debut short story collection Skin Thief: Stories was published by Neon Hemlock in 2023. Her novella, Countess, will be published by ECW Press in 2024.
people.name: Suzan Palumbo
Sven von Vittorelli

people.bio: Swen is the founder of Larian studios and game director on Baldur's Gate 3. He's been making games since 1997 and is best known for his work as programmer, designer and director on the Divinity series which includes Divinity:Original Sin 1 & 2.
people.name: Swen Vincke

people.bio: T. C. Weber is the author of the War for Reality near-future cyberpunk trilogy (Sleep State Interrupt, The Wrath of Leviathan, and Zero-Day Rising); as well as Born in Salt, a character-oriented alternate history novel; The Survivors, a post-apocalyptic cli-fi horror novella; and The Council, a satire of local government. More works are on the way. Mr. Weber is a member of Poets & Writers, the Science Fiction & Fantasy Writers Association, and the Horror Writers Association. By day, Mr. Weber works as an ecologist, and lives in the USA with his wife Karen.
people.name: T. C. Weber

people.bio: T. Kingfisher is the author of multiple award-winning books for children and adults, including Digger, Nettle & Bone, and What Moves The Dead. She likes interesting animal facts.
people.name: T. Kingfisher

people.bio:
T. R. Napper is a multi-award-winning science fiction author, including the Aurealis three times. His short fiction has appeared in Asimov’s, Interzone, the Magazine of Fantasy & Science Fiction, and numerous others. He received a creative writing doctorate for his thesis: 'The Dark Century: 1946 - 2046 - Noir, Cyberpunk, and Asian Modernity.'  

Before turning to writing, T. R. Napper was an aid worker, delivering humanitarian programs in Southeast Asia for a decade. During this period he was a resident of the Old Quarter in Hanoi for several years, the setting for his debut novel, 36 Streets
people.name: T. R. Napper

people.bio: T.H. Dray is a British Fantasy Award nominated writer who lives in Glasgow in a house where humans are outnumbered by dogs.
people.name: T.H. Dray

people.bio: T.L. Huchu’s work has appeared in 'Lightspeed', 'Interzone', 'Analog Science Fiction & Fact', 'The Year’s Best Science Fiction and Fantasy 2021’, 'Ellery Queen Mystery Magazine', 'Mystery Weekly', 'The Year’s Best Crime and Mystery Stories 2016', and elsewhere. He is the winner of a Hurston/Wright Legacy Award (2023), Alex Award (2022), the Children’s Africana Book Award (2021), a Nommo Award for African SFF (2022, 2017), and has been shortlisted for the Caine Prize (2014) and the Grand prix de l'Imaginaire (2019). The Edinburgh Nights series is now on its third instalment. Find him @TendaiHuchu
people.name: T.L. Huchu

people.bio: TJ Berg is a writer and scientist. She has only caused one lab fire.
people.name: TJ Berg

people.bio: TJ Burnside Clapp has been active in science fiction fandom for over 40 years. An O.G. cosplayer (whose 1977 X-wing pilot costume has gone viral on the Internet), TJ has served on concoms and run masquerades at multiple conventions, and has appeared as Fan GoH and musical guest at dozens more. A founding member of the 1980s filk trio Technical Difficulties, TJ is best known these days as a singer/songwriter who wrote the filk anthem "Lullaby for a Weary World,” and often performs with husband and fellow filker Mitchell Burnside Clapp. TJ & Mitchell currently reside in Arlington, Virginia.
people.name: TJ Burnside Clapp

people.bio: Taeyeon Song (she/her) is a Korean novelist, playwright, and performer based in Glasgow. She holds an MLitt Theatre Studies and MLitt Creative Writing from University of Glasgow. She has also just completed her second year of a DFA Creative Writing also at University of Glasgow. Taeyeon’s work explores the themes of colonialism, cultural identity, contemporary politics, intergenerational trauma, and the Korean diaspora. She was recently awarded Highly Commended Honours at the 2023 Kavya New Writers' Award and her work has been featured at the 2023 'Korean Youth: Spaces, Places, and Technolgies conference' and the 2023 'Before, Behind, Beyond the Wave: Korean Popular Culture in Perspective Symposium.'
people.name: Taeyeon Song

people.bio: Tammy Coxen is a long-time conrunner, including chairing Detcon1, the 2014 NASFiC in Detroit and being a Division Head for several Worldcons, including Dublin 2019 and Glasgow 2024. When not chairing conventions she is the Chief Tasting Officer of Tammy's Tastings, where she has been teaching cocktail classes since 2011, including online classes since 2020. In 2023 she launched My Tiny Bottles, a YouTube/Podcast/Website devoted to exploring a collection of miniature vintage liquor bottles she inherited from her Grandmother.
people.name: Tammy Coxen

people.bio: Tania Chen is a Chinese-Mexican queer writer of living nightmares. Their work was selected for Brave New Weird Anthology by Tenebrous Press, and has also appeared in Unfettered Hexes by Neon Hemlock, Apparition Lit, Strange Horizons, Pleiades Magazine, Baffling Magazine, Longleaf Review, The Dread Machine among others. They are a graduate of the Clarion West Novella Bootcamp Workshop of 2021, Clarion West Workshop 2023, and a recipient of the HWA’s Dark Poetry Scholarship. Currently, they are assistant editor at Uncanny Magazine and can be found on twitter@archistratego or https://bsky.app/profile/archistratego.bsky.social
people.name: Tania Chen

people.bio: Active in SF fandom since 1992; former Clarke Award judge and BSFA Committee Member; reads, writes, reviews.
people.name: Tanya Brown

people.bio:
Tanya DePass (she/her) is a Hugo Nominated Editor (for Fireside Magazine), award-winning games content creator and developer, and creator of the Into the Mother Lands RPG.

Tanya is a lifelong Chicagoan who loves everything about gaming and wants to make the industry better and more inclusive for everyone. She is the founder and Director of I Need Diverse Games, a not-for-profit organization dedicated to better diversification of all aspects of gaming. She was part of the Rivals of Waterdeep actual play stream from its inception, and is the creator and Creative Director of Into the Mother Lands, a new sci fi afro-futurist RPG developed with a team of all POC and Black creators. Tanya often writes and speaks on issues of diversity, feminism, race, intersectionality & other topics online, at conventions and as a public speaker.
people.name: Tanya DePass

people.bio:
Tao Wong is a full-time author in the scifi and fantasy genres with wide and varied work within the space. A multiple times international Amazon bestseller, he is best known for the System Apocalypse and A Thousand Li universes, with over 40 full-length novels and numerous shorter works published. Tao was a finalist for the Kindle Storyteller UK Award in 2021.
As a reader, he's an avid fan of science fiction and fantasy, having cut his teeth decades ago on Dragonlance, Terry Brooks and Asimov before graduating to Jordan, Gaiman, Bujold and more.

When he's not writing and working, he's practicing martial arts, reading and picking up random hobbies. 

Tao became a full-time author in 2019 and is a member of the Science Fiction and Fantasy Writers of America (SFWA) and NINC.

More details about Tao's latest books can be found on his website: http://www.mylifemytao.com
people.name: Tao Wong

people.bio: Tara Campbell is a writer, teacher, Kimbilio Fellow, fiction co-editor at Barrelhouse, and graduate of American University's MFA. Publication credits include Masters Review, Wigleaf, Electric Literature, CRAFT Literary, Uncharted Magazine, Daily Science Fiction, Strange Horizons, and Escape Pod. She's the author of the eco sci-fi novel TreeVolution, two hybrid collections of poetry and prose, and two short story collections from feminist sci-fi publisher Aqueduct Press. Her sixth book, City of Dancing Gargoyles, is forthcoming from Santa Fe Writers Project (SFWP) in fall 2024. She teaches writing at venues such as Johns Hopkins University, Clarion West, The Writer's Center, and Hugo House.
people.name: Tara Campbell

people.bio: Tasha Suri is the World Fantasy Award winning author of the Burning Kingdoms trilogy, the Books of Ambha duology, What Souls Are Made Of and Doctor Who: The Cradle. She is a writing tutor, an occasional librarian and cat owner. She lives with her family in a mildly haunted house in London.
people.name: Tasha Suri

people.bio: Teika Marija Smits is a UK-based freelance editor and the author of the short story collections Umbilical (NewCon Press) and Waterlore (Black Shuck Books), as well as the poetry pamphlet Russian Doll (Indigo Dreams Publishing). A fan of all things fae, she is delighted by the fact that Teika means fairy tale in Latvian.
people.name: Teika Marija Smits

people.bio:
Tej Turner is an SFF author and travel-blogger. His debut novel The Janus Cycle was published by Elsewhen Press in 2015 and its sequel Dinnusos Rises was released in 2017. Both are hard to classify within typical genres but were contemporary and semi-biographical with elements of surrealism. He has since branched off into writing epic fantasy and has an ongoing series called the Avatars of Ruin. The first instalment – Bloodsworn – was released in 2021, and its sequel Blood Legacy in 2022. The third – Blood War – was released in 2024.

He has also spent four years travelling around Asia and Latin America during which he kept a blog about his adventures.
people.name: Tej Turner

people.bio: Teresa Nielsen Hayden has edited books by, among others, Poul Anderson, Avram Davidson, John M. Ford, Jane Lindskold, James White, Robert Charles Wilson, Jo Walton, and Charles Stross. At various points in her career she has also edited comic books, literary criticism, and utopian literature. Her essay collection Making Book (NESFA Press, 1994) was a finalist for the Hugo Award; for other writing and publishing, she has been a Hugo finalist four more times. In 2016 she and Patrick were guests of honor at the Worldcon. A second collection, Making Conversation, was published by NESFA Press in connection with that.
people.name: Teresa Nielsen Hayden

people.bio: Terese Mason Pierre (she/her) is an award-winning writer and editor whose work has appeared in multiple literary and speculative journals, online and in print. She is an editor at Augur Magazine, the current Chief Programming Officer of Augur Society, and the co-director of AugurCon. She is the author of two chapbooks, and her debut poetry collection is forthcoming in Spring 2025 from House of Anansi. Terese is an MFA candidate at the University of Guelph and lives in Toronto, Canada.
people.name: Terese Mason Pierre

people.bio: Terilee is a long time larper and gamer, full time nerd, and professor of anthropology and archaeology. Her most popular course is ANTH 314: Anthropology of Zombies at George Mason University. Her academic publications and presentations focus on fan cultures, popular culture, digital ethnography, and gender. In academic and fannish settings she has presented work on MLP:FIM (My Little Pony: Friendship is Magic) fandom, female hockey fans and other nerdy topics. Theatre, History, and the Space Program are also important aspects her nerdom. Terilee started attending science fiction conventions as a teenager and they positively changed her life.
people.name: Terilee Edwards-Hewitt

people.bio: Terri Ash is the manager, artist wrangler, and professional killjoy of Geek Calligraphy. She has been part of organized fandom for approximately 14 years, and disorganized fandom for much longer. If left unchecked she will talk your ear off on such various subjects as Jewish influences in comics, feminism in SF/F, and why all artists need wranglers.
people.name: Terri Ash

people.bio: Terri Windling (she/her) is a beloved writer, editor, artist, and folklorist, who has written over 40 books, and received 10 World Fantasy Awards, the Mythopoeic Award, the Bram Stoker Award, and the SFWA Solstice Award, in addition to numerous prestigious shortlists. Her work ranges from the fictional to the academic, but all revolving around the magical and the fantastic.
people.name: Terri Windling

people.bio:
Terry Jackman, variously teacher, tutor, trainer, Clark's shoe fitter, award-winning picture framer, article-writer and/or commitee chair [for the UK's Fine Art Trade Guild], joined the first of the Brish Science iction's online Orbit [writers' group] in 2005 and developed it into fourteen groups over the next sixteen years - scary thought - until she foolishly interrupted covid's arrival with a brain tumour. so she gave the day jobs, but finally shared some stories.
[Yes she still hates being 'wordy'and is still known for making every word count!]
people.name: Terry Jackman

people.bio: Dr. Theresa Jean Tanenbaum (“Tess”) is a scholar, songwriter, game designer, activist, and practicing witch. Tess’s work is playful, provocative, and interdisciplinary, frequently straddling the line between art, design, research, and activism. She is an internationally recognized expert on interactive storytelling, identity, and play. She founded the Name Change Policy Working Group, creating trans-inclusive policies that have been adopted by every major academic publisher. She is the co-creator of the upcoming historical fantasy audio drama Étude of the Storm, and her autobiographical podcast musical about gender transition and marriage during the COVID pandemic is currently under production at Omniverse Media.
people.name: Tess Tanenbaum

people.bio: Author of ten published novels, nine of the supernatural horror genre, one of the historical genre. All on Amazon. Another one in the pipeline! Greatest interests: Tudor history and anything associated with the Ancient Romans. Mother, grandmother, mother-in-law, living in retired Royal Navy accommodation in Southsea, Portsmouth.
people.name: The Fossil

people.bio:
Mark Painter was born in Reading, Pennsylvania and studied at the University of Pennsylvania. He has worked as an electrical engineer and practiced law in the field of disability rights. He served in elected office for seventeen years, including a term in the Pennsylvania House of Representatives.
After his retirement, he took up writing fantasy and science fiction, as well as producing and hosting the popular History of the Twentieth Century podcast.
His wife is a retired United Methodist pastor. They have four children and two grandchildren.
people.name: The History of the Twentieth Century

people.bio: Theodora Goss is the World Fantasy, Locus, and Mythopoeic Award-winning author of the short story and poetry collections In the Forest of Forgetting, Songs for Ophelia, and Snow White Learns Witchcraft, as well as novella The Thorn and the Blossom and novels The Strange Case of the Alchemist's Daughter, European Travel for the Monstrous Gentlewoman, and The Sinister Mystery of the Mesmerizing Girl. She has been a finalist for the Nebula, Crawford, and Shirley Jackson Awards, as well as on the Tiptree Award Honor List. Her work has been translated into fifteen languages. She teaches literature and writing at Boston University.
people.name: Theodora Goss

people.bio: Therese Norén, known as Thette in most online spaces, is a Swedish physician specialised in radiology.
people.name: Therese Noren

people.bio: A member of the open-source space community Nexus Aurora. Entrepreneur designing and operating large-scale close-loop food production systems.
people.name: Thomas Bjelkeman

people.bio: Thoraiya Dyer is an Aurealis- and Ditmar-Award winning Australian writer and veterinarian. Her short science fiction and fantasy stories have appeared in Clarkesworld, Analog, Fantasy Magazine, Apex, Podcastle, Cosmos, Nature, anthology “Bridging Infinity” and boutique collection “Asymmetry.” Thoraiya’s big fat fantasy novels in the Titan’s Forest Trilogy are published by Tor books. A member of SFWA, represented by the Ethan Ellenberg agency, she is an avid hiker and arbalist inspired by wild spaces and the unknown universe. Find her online at thoraiyadyer.com or at https://mastodon.social/@ThoraiyaDyer .
people.name: Thoraiya Dyer

people.bio: Tiffani Angus (PhD) is a BSFA- and BFS-award finalist for her debut novel Threading the Labyrinth. She's also co-author with academic and author Val Nolan on the BSFA-finalist Spec Fic for Newbies: A Beginner's Guide to Writing Subgenres of Science Fiction, Fantasy, and Horror Vol 1. Spec Fic Vol 2 will launch at Glasgow Worldcon. She lives in Bury St Edmunds and is currently at work on a novel, a novella, a short story collection, and another scandalous new project.
people.name: Tiffani Angus

people.bio: Son of Brian Aldiss and working in conjunction with The Aldiss Literary Estate
people.name: Tim Aldiss

people.bio: Tom Coughlin, President, Coughlin Associates is a digital storage analyst and business/ technology consultant. He has over 40 years in the data storage industry with engineering and senior management positions. Coughlin Associates consults, publishes books and market and technology reports and puts on digital storage and memory-oriented events. He is a regular contributor for forbes.com and M&E organization websites. He is an IEEE Fellow, 2024 IEEE President, Past-President IEEE-USA, Past Director IEEE Region 6 and Past Chair Santa Clara Valley IEEE Section, and is also active with SNIA and SMPTE. For more information on Tom Coughlin go to https://www.tomcoughlin.com/
people.name: Tom Coughlin

people.bio:
Tom Doyle is the author of the American Craftsmen trilogy from Tor Books, in which two modern magician-soldiers fight their way through the legacies of Poe and Hawthorne as they attempt to destroy an undying evil.
Tom's latest work for Graphic Audio is the Agent of Exiles series of supernatural spy adventures in the 6th century BCE. His recent SF novel, Border Crosser, follows the far-future journeys of Eris, a psychologically extreme secret agent whose shifting loyalties cause chaos wherever she goes.
A description of Tom’s apocalyptic scholarship is here: https://www.tomdoyleauthor.com/2024/04/26/tom-doyles-millennial-scholarship/ He has survived Harvard, Stanford, and cancer, and he writes in a spooky turret in Washington, DC.
people.name: Tom Doyle

people.bio: Tom Toner is the author of the Amaranthine Spectrum, a space opera series published by Gollancz.
people.name: Tom Toner

people.bio: Fan, event organizer, editor of fiction, producer of independent theatre
people.name: Tomasz Kozlowski

people.bio:
Tommy Ferguson is a Belfast fan who got into fandom in the early 1980s via the now defunct Irish Science Fiction Association - and never looked back.

He attended his first EasterCon a few years later - Albacon 3 in Glasgow - and had so much fun decided run his own convention in Belfast in 1986. Four further NICons followed, culminating in the National Universities’ convention in 1989. In the 1990s these morphed into a series of ten conventions called Mecons run by the Queen's University of Belfast Science Fiction and Fantasy society; which he co-founded in 1985.

Since then, he has been actively involved in the Belfast SF group, attending conventions in Ireland, the UK and all over the world, unsuccessfully running for TAFF, was a Corflu 50 representative and generally been present in fandom. A brief sojourn to Toronto in 1997 saw him found the First Thursday meeting, modelled after the London Tun meetings, when he discovered there was no social hub for Toronto fandom. The meeting is still going strong to this day.

As fanzine fan he has published many issues of his perzine TommyWorld, a number of genzines and contributed to fanzines all over the world. As chair of Corflu Craic in 2023 he finally brought the fanzine fans' convention to his home city - and as Co-Chair of Reconnect - the 2025 EasterCon in Belfast - has realised a long-held ambition to close the circle from Albacon in 1986 - bringing Eastercon to the 'home' of British fandom.

I’ll be on the fan tables flogging memberships, taking part in panels or in the bar; say hello!
people.name: Tommy Ferguson

people.bio: Tonya R. Moore writes and edits speculative fiction. She is a Poetry Acquiring Editor at the 2024 Hugo Award-nominated FIYAH Literary Magazine, Poetry Editor at Solarpunk Magazine, and an Associate Writer at Galactic Journey.
people.name: Tonya R. Moore

people.bio: Tori Bovalino is the author of three published YA horror novels and the editor of the bestselling anthology, The Gathering Dark: An Anthology of Folk Horror. Tori holds a PhD in Creative Writing and splits her time writing, working in publishing, and teaching students at Goldsmiths, University of London. Her next book is her adult fantasy debut, coming in September 2025.
people.name: Tori Bovalino

people.bio: Trip is a writer, a doctor of the academic persuasion, and a researcher of all things pursuant to bargains, exchanges, and compacts of a faery nature. It is inadvisable to attempt to make a deal with him. He is 1/3 of the queer small press Bona Books, 1/2 of multiple writing partnerships, and 100% geek. Frequently writes as a ghost. Mostly harmless.
people.name: Trip Galey

people.bio: An award-winning longtime journalist and current freelance editor, Trish E. Matson has loved science fiction and fantasy since childhood, helping to organize a Doctor Who convention as a teenager. She reviews books and media with the Skiffy and Fanty team and on her own blog, and participates in several podcasts via discussions and audio editing. She has also enthusiastically returned to role-playing games in the last few years, including on some Twitch streams. Other interests include wordplay, poetry, libraries, audio dramas, music, dancing, and martial arts.
people.name: TrishEM

people.bio:
Tristan Gray is an Edinburgh-based dark fantasy author working on tales inspired by dark-age Scotland and Gaelic mythology.

Outside writing he works as a software engineer, practices acrobatics, is a tabletop RPG games master, and is an LGBT+ rights activist.
people.name: Tristan Gray

people.bio:
Trudie Skies is a non-binary author based in North East England, though they have been living inside fantasy worlds ever since they discovered books and refuse to return to reality. Within Trudie’s daydreams you’ll find SPFBO and BBNYA finalist The Thirteenth Hour, a gaslamp fantasy described as obnoxiously British and best read with a cup of tea.

When not conjuring new worlds, Trudie spends their free time exploring the realms of indie books and video games, staring at clouds, and chasing after their fluffy companions.
 
Visit Trudie’s worlds at www.trudieskies.com
people.name: Trudie Skies

people.bio: Ursula Whitcher is a mathematician, writer, editor and poet.
people.name: Ursula Whitcher

people.bio: Dr V Anne Smith is on the Biology faculty at St Andrews University in Scotland, where she researches computational biology, applying machine learning and artificial intelligence to understand complex biological systems. She studies biological systems as diverse as genes, brains, and ecosystems. When not researching, she enjoys writing speculative fiction: she has published a few short stories and her first novel, A Code For Carolyn: A Genomic Thriller, forms part of Springer's Science and Fiction series. As science fiction written by a scientist, the novel includes an essay where she explains the science behind the story.
people.name: V Anne Smith

people.bio:
V.Castro is a two time Bram Stoker Award nominated Mexican American writer from San Antonio, Texas now residing in the UK. She writes horror, erotic horror, and science fiction. Her books include The Haunting of Alejandra, Alien: Vasquez, Mestiza Blood, The Queen of the Cicadas, Out of Aztlan, Las Posadas, Rebel Moon (official Netflix film novelization) and Goddess of Filth.
Her forthcoming novel is Immortal Pleasures from Del Rey.
Connect with Violet via Instagram and Twitter @vlatinalondon or www.vcastrostories.com. She can also be found on Blue Sky, Goodreads and Amazon. TikTok@vcastrobooks
people.name: V. Castro

people.bio: I am an amateur science fiction writer and professional astronomer form Bulgaria, working in Chile and Germany. My interest in the genre dates from high school years. Specific topics of my interest are: the interplay between science and science fiction, alternative history, space opera and particularly - speculative fiction outside the English speaking world. Recently I have been one of the organizers of the Bulgarian national convention Bulgacon.
people.name: Valentin D. Ivanov

people.bio: Valerie Estelle Frankel is the author of over 90 books on pop culture, including Hunting for Meaning in The Mandalorian; The Villain’s Journey; and Star Wars Meets the Eras of Feminism. Many of her books focus on gender in fiction, from her heroine's journey guides From Girl to Goddess and Superheroines and the Epic Journey to The Trans Hero’s Journey. Her Chelm for the Holidays (2019) was a PJ Library book, and now she’s the editor of Jewish Science Fiction and Fantasy, publishing an academic series for Lexington Press (submissions welcome!). vefrankel.com
people.name: Valerie Estelle Frankel

people.bio: Went to my first SF con in 1981, I am best known in fandom as a filker, although I have been involved in other fannish activities over the years, including Pernfandom, writers' workshops, conrunning, and running a fannish choir. I have been GoH at various filkcons, most recently at Consonance in California in 2023, and I will be the Emerita GoH at Contabile 35 in February 2025. I was producer/director and one of the composers of the performance of "Before the Dawn" at Loncon 3 in 2014. My hobbies include choral singing, playing guitar and banjo, song writing, and fiction writing.
people.name: Valerie Housden

people.bio: Vanessa MacLaren-Wray (she/her) writes science fiction and fantasy about people—human and otherwise—connecting in this complex universe. She’s the author of the Patchwork Universe series: All That Was Asked, Shadows of Insurrection, and Flames of Attrition. She writes for the Truck Stop at the Center of the Galaxy consortium and guest-hosts for the podcast Small Publishing in a Big Universe. Vanessa is an active member of the Science Fiction and Fantasy Writers Association and Strong Women-Strange Worlds. When not arguing with her cats, she works on new stories, her email journal Messages from the Oort Cloud, and her website, Cometary Tales.
people.name: Vanessa MacLaren-Wray

people.bio: Vera Brook is a neuroscientist turned science fiction, fantasy, and romance writer. Her short fiction has appeared in Analog, Escape Pod, Cast of Wonders, Factor Four Magazine, and Utopia Science Fiction, among other places. She also writes novels (which usually turn into a series, because she gets too attached to her characters). Visit verabrook.com to learn more about Vera's writing.
people.name: Vera Brook

people.bio: Verity is a SFF fan who is very interested in mustelids. They are helping SKAO build the world's largest radio telescope. Their research interests include women in science and computing, history, and high performance computing for radio astronomy.
people.name: Verity Allan

people.bio: Veronica G. Henry is the author of Bacchanal, The Quarter Storm, The Foreign Exchange (Mambo Reina) and The Canopy Keepers. Her work has debuted at #1 on multiple Amazon bestseller charts, was chosen as an editors’ pick for Best Fantasy, and shortlisted for the Manly Wade Wellman Award. She is a Viable Paradise alum and a member of SFWA. Her stories have appeared in The Magazine of Fantasy & Science Fiction, Many Worlds, and FIYAH Literary Magazine.
people.name: Veronica G. Henry

people.bio:
I joined Bloomsbury after six years at HarperVoyager – where I left as Editorial Director, having won ‘Imprint of the Year’ and launched YA Crossover imprint, Magpie Books. I’m setting up Bloomsbury’s first dedicated SFF imprint – aiming to recruit new readers to genre and provide something really special for existing fans. 

I publish writing that broadens SFF, honouring, challenging and expanding the traditions of speculative writing, from high fantasy and space opera to folklore, romance and horror. I want to uplift new voices and new ideas and believe every tale could be improved with magic.
people.name: Vicky

people.bio: Victor Manibo is a Filipino novelist living in New York. As a queer immigrant and a person of color, he writes about people who live these identities as they navigate imaginary worlds. A 2022 Lambda Literary Emerging Voices Fellow, he is the author of the science fiction novels THE SLEEPLESS and ESCAPE VELOCITY from Erewhon Books. Aside from fiction, he also spins fantastical tales in his career as a lawyer. He lives in Queens with his husband, their dog, and their two cats. Find him online at victormanibo.com and on most social media platforms @victormanibo.
people.name: Victor Manibo

people.bio: Vida Cruz-Borja is a Filipina fantasy and science fiction writer, editor, and conrunner. Her short fiction and essays have been published in F&SF, Fantasy, Strange Horizons, PodCastle, Expanded Horizons, and various anthologies. She won the 2022 IGNYTE Award for Best Creative Nonfiction for “We are the Mountain: A Look at the Inactive Protagonist,” which was reprinted in "Letters to a Writer of Color" (2023). She is the author of the National Book Award-winning "Song of the Mango and Other New Myths" (2022). Currently, she’s a freelance book editor with Tessera Editorial and The Darling Axe.
people.name: Vida Cruz-Borja

people.bio:
Vincent Docherty is a fan and con-runner, who co-chaired the Glasgow Worldcons in 1995 & 2005.

His home town is Glasgow, Scotland, where he studied and researched in Chemistry. His career in the energy industry has taken him to London, Muscat (Oman) and The Hague, where he currently lives.

He had an early interest in SF&F, Space and Science, and at 16, he attended the first SF convention in Glasgow, quickly becoming involved in organizing SF societies and conventions, including British National Eastercons and Worldcons. He has been Fan Guest of Honour at the UK Eastercon and other cons and was presented with the Big Heart Award in 2014.

He remains an active con-runner and programme participant, including chairing the 2011 & 2021 SMOFcons, Hugo Award Administration, the symphonic concert lead for the 2014, 2019 & 2024 Worldcons and Chair's advisor and Division Head for the Dublin 2019 and Glasgow 2024 Worldcons.
people.name: Vincent Docherty

people.bio: Virginia has been a fan of science fiction and fantasy since childhood. She teaches a module on the political economy of science fiction as part of her day job, and reads all sorts of science fiction and fantasy. In lockdown she started learning pottery and making things with tentacles, as you do.
people.name: Virginia Preston

people.bio: Vivian (Xiao Wen) Li is a queer and neurodivergent Chinese-Canadian writer, musician, and interdisciplinary artist. Her creative works are forthcoming or published in Uncanny, F&SF, Strange Horizons, Heartlines Spec, The Fiddlehead, The Massachusetts Review, and The New Quarterly, among others. Most recently, she was Longlisted for the CBC Short Story Prize, Shortlisted for the Peter Hinchcliffe Short Fiction Award and a Finalist for The Kenyon Review Short Nonfiction Contest Contest. She is the author of Someday I Promise, I'll Love You (845 Press), as well as the writer and director of three short films that have premiered across Canada as well as internationally in festivals such as Reel Asian Film Festival, Bali International Short Film Festival, and Whistler Film Festival. She is also a 2024 ScreenCraft TV Pilot Script Competition Semifinalist. Her slipstream and fantasy writing often engages with mental health, climate change, and experiences of time. She loves exploring non-traditional plot structures as well as the musicality and emotional texture of words. An editor for Augur, she can be reached @vivianlicreates.
people.name: Vivian (Xiao Wen) Li

people.bio: Vivian Abraham (any pronouns) is a gamer, a community organizer, and an attorney.  They are a life-long member of fandom, an avid reader, a game designer, and the current president of the Arisia Eboard.  Bios are the worst, come and say hi instead!
people.name: Vivian Abraham

people.bio: W. Jade Young is an author, editor, writing advisor, and game designer from Indiana, USA. She holds a Master's in Fine Arts in Creative Writing and English from Southern New Hampshire University and has been published in literary magazines and anthologies. She is the founder of Bad Habit Publishing, LLC, an independent publishing outfit, and is the author of The Rainbow Quill Writing Tool and Tarot Deck for Storytellers.
people.name: W. Jade Young

people.bio: Mathematician, filker and fan.
people.name: Watson Ladd

people.bio: Wendy Van Camp, Anaheim's Poet Laureate Emerita, is a dynamic voice in speculative poetry, blending cutting-edge technology, astronomy, and daydreams. Her talent has earned her nominations for the Elgin Award, Pushcart Prize, and Dwarf Stars Award. Wendy's poems, stories, and articles grace journals worldwide such as "Star*Line," "Scifaikuest," and “San Diego Poetry Annual.” She regularly contributes to “Indy Author Magazine.” Find her books at most online booksellers. Her debut poetry collection, "The Planets," was nominated for the Elgin Award twice.  An active podcaster, you can see Wendy as a panelist on the "Con-Tinual" stable of podcasts "Fandom" and "The Panel Room". You can hear her as a rotating host of "Poets Cafe" on KPFK 90.7 FM Los Angeles or on her own audio podcast "No Wasted Ink Ramblecast." As a member of SFWA, SFPA, and IBPA, Wendy is a passionate advocate for the speculative community.
people.name: Wendy Van Camp

people.bio: Wendy Wheeler is a Texas writer and instructor in writing craft whose work has appeared in The Year's Best Fantasy & Horror. Her fiction ranges from adult fairytale anthologies (Silver Birch, Blood Moon; Snow White, Blood Red - edited by Datlow/Windling), magical alternate history anthologies (The Crafters, both Volumes I and II), Analog, Aboriginal SF, Daily SF, horror magazines (Gorezone) and many others. She's also won awards for her screenplays and does freelance story development for Hollywood. She's at work on her 5th try at writing a novel and has started a fantasy musical. More at www.wendy-wheeler.com.
people.name: Wendy Wheeler

people.bio: Will "scifantasy" Frank is an intellectual property attorney and specialist in trademark law. Fannishly, he is a filker, former Hugo Administrator, and general Guy People Might Know.
people.name: Will "scifantasy" Frank

people.bio: I am a biochemist/chemist/molecular biologist with experience in drug discovery, astrobiology and anti-aging medicine (the real sort). Fan since ~1965. Written 5 fact books, no fiction, ~160 papers, some pop sci articles etc.. Current interests are technosignatures, ‘The Fermi Paradox’ and the evolution of intelligence, evidence for life on Venus (appeared on Sky at Night about that), and developing genuinely effective anti-aging drugs, which my current start-up company is working on. Books of potential interest: “The Cosmic Zoo” (https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-3-319-62045-9). Basically, a life science tech-head.
people.name: William Bains

links.website: www.williambains.co.uk (this not updated for some years!)

people.bio:
William C. Tracy writes and publishes queer science fiction and fantasy through his indie press Space Wizard Science Fantasy (spacewizardsciencefantasy.com).

His largest work is the Dissolutionverse: a space opera with music-based magic, including ten books and an RPG. He also has a standalone epic fantasy with seasonal fruit-based magic through a LGBTQ+ small press.

William is a North Carolina native and a lifelong fan of science fiction and fantasy. He has a master’s in mechanical engineering and has both designed and operated heavy construction machinery. He has also trained in Wado-Ryu karate since 2003 and runs his own dojo in Raleigh NC. He is an avid video and board gamer, a beekeeper, a reader, and of course, a writer.

You can get a free Dissolutionverse novelette by signing up for William’s mailing list at http://williamctracy.com

Follow him on Twitter at https://twitter.com/wctracy or on Mastodon at https://wandering.shop/@wctracy for writing updates, cat and bee pictures, and thoughts on martial arts.
people.name: William C. Tracy

people.bio: William Ledbetter is a Nebula Award winning author with three novels and more than seventy speculative fiction short stories and non-fiction articles published in five languages, in publications such as Asimov's, Fantasy & Science Fiction, Analog, Escape Pod and the SFWA blog. He's been a space and technology geek since childhood and spent most of his non-writing career in the aerospace industry. He is a member of SFWA, the National Space Society, and a Launch Pad Astronomy workshop graduate. He lives near Dallas with his wife, a needy dog and three spoiled cats.
people.name: William Ledbetter

people.bio: WOLE TALABI is an engineer, writer, and editor from Nigeria. He is the author of the nebula-moninated novel SHIGIDI AND THE BRASS HEAD OF OBALUFON (DAW books/Gollancz, 2023). His short fiction has appeared in places like Asimov’s Science Fiction, Lightspeed Magazine, Tor.com and is collected in the books CONVERGENCE PROBLEMS (DAW books, 2024) and INCOMPLETE SOLUTIONS (Luna Press, 2019). He has been a finalist for the Hugo, Nebula, and Locus awards, as well as the Caine Prize for African Writing and he has won the Nommo award for African speculative fiction and the Sidewise award for Alternate History. He has edited five anthologies including the acclaimed AFRICANFUTURISM: AN ANTHOLOGY (Brittlepaper, 2020) and MOTHERSOUND: THE SAUÚTIVERSE ANTHOLOGY (Android Press, 2023). He likes scuba diving, elegant equations, and oddly shaped things. He currently lives and works in Australia. Find him at wtalabi.wordpress.com and at @wtalabi on Twitter, Instagram, Bluesky and Tiktok.
people.name: Wole Talabi

people.bio:
Climber, tattoo collector, and peanut-butter connoisseur, Xan van Rooyen is an autistic, non-binary storyteller from South Africa, currently living in Finland where the heavy metal is soothing and the cold, dark forests inspiring.

Xan has a Master’s degree in music, and–when not teaching–enjoys conjuring strange worlds and creating quirky characters. You can find Xan’s stories in the likes of Three-Lobed Burning Eye, Daily Science Fiction, and Galaxy’s Edge among others. They have also written several novels including YA fantasy My Name is Magic (Tiny Ghost Press), and adult arcanopunk novel Silver Helix (Android Press). 

Xan is also part of the Sauutiverse, an African writer’s collective with their first anthology Mothersound having been published by Android Press November 2023.
people.name: Xan van Rooyen

people.bio: Xiuqi Huang is a PhD student in comparative literature at the University of Edinburgh. Her work focuses on transhumanism, non-human sentience and extraterrestrial life in Chinese and Anglophone science fiction. She is keen on exploring the boundary between the human and the inhuman, and the intersection of Chinese science fiction and Anglophone science fiction.
people.name: Xiuqi Huang

people.bio: Xueting C. Ni is Chinese culture writer, speaker, consultant and translator based in London. She is the author of From Kuan Yin to Chairman Mao: An Essential Guide to Chinese Deities, Chinese Myths, and award-winning Sinopticon: A Celebration of Chinese Science Fiction. She has collaborated with a diverse range of festivals, institutes, and companies, including Tor, the BBC and the Confucius Institute. Her new anthology Sinophagia: A Celebration of Chinese Horror, will be published in September 2024.  She is currently working on a book on wuxia culture and various other projects.
people.name: Xueting C. Ni

people.bio: Dr. Xuying Yu is an Associate Professor in the School of Arts and Social Sciences at Hong Kong Metropolitan University. Her research interests include Chinese science fiction, modern Chinese intellectual history, and Taiwanese literature. Dr. Yu has published several papers in leading Chinese journals and contributed book chapters to volumes published by Palgrave and Routledge. She has successfully secured research grants from various sources. These projects encompass studies on Chinese ecological science fiction, critical reflections on Anthropocene in Chinese science fiction, the May Fourth Movement and Chinese Enlightenment, as well as dystopia and anti-utopia in Chinese science fiction.
people.name: Xuying Yu
