people.bio:
Yaroslav Barsukov is a writer of fantasy, science fiction, and everything in between. He’s best known for his science fantasy noir novella Tower of Mud and Straw, which became an Amazon bestseller, was shortlisted for the prestigious Nebula Award as well as the SCKA Award, and received a Kirkus Star, eventually landing on Kirkus Reviews’ “Best Books of 2021” list.

He’s a full member of Science Fiction & Fantasy Writers Association (SFWA) and combines his writing duties with volunteer work, serving as chair of SFWA’s Information Systems Committee.
people.name: Yaroslav Barsukov

people.bio: Yasir AlYasiri is an acclaimed director, producer, and writer in the Arab entertainment industry. Initially a successful music video director, Yasir gained recognition with his film debut "Murk Light" (2012), the first Emirati film showcased at the Tribeca Film Festival. His films, including "Shabab Sheyab" (2018) and "122" (2019), the first Egyptian film in 4DX, have earned international acclaim. Recently, he was the showrunner for "Kaboos" (2023), the first Starzplay original series, and is currently working on "HWJN" (2024), set to be a landmark film in the region. His work continues to innovate and captivate audiences.
people.name: Yasir Alyasiri

people.bio:
Co-Founder of Yatakhayaloon a company dedecated to develop and grow the SciFi culture accross Arabia. Author of Yaqteenya the first Arabian ulternate history, and co-author of HWJN the best selling Saudi novel adapted to a movie.
Computer Engineer, futurest, serian entreprenuir.
people.name: Yasser Bahjatt

people.bio: Yidan HU is a PhD candidate in English Literature at the University of Edinburgh. She has studied at University College London, Utrecht University, the London School of Economics & Political Science, and Nanjing University of Science & Technology. She is a member of the British Science Fiction Association, British Society for Literature and Science, and British Association of Film, Television and Screen. She has published her scholarship in the field of literary and film studies, and she has been invited to present her work at conferences in the UK, Ireland, and Japan. Her current research focuses on sci-fi and Economic Humanities.
people.name: Yidan HU

people.bio: Yilin Wang (she/they) is a writer, poet, editor, and Chinese-English literary translator. Her work has appeared in Clarkesworld, Fantasy Magazine, Words Without Borders, Guernica, The Mahalat Review, Samovar, and anthologies like The Way Spring Arrives (TorDotCom) and Asian Ghost Short Stories (Flame Tree Press). She is the editor and translator of a book of poetry translations and original essays on translation entitled The Lantern and the Night Moths (Invisible Publishing 2024). Her work has been a finalist for the Aurora Award, been nominated for the Rhysling Award, and received an Honorable Mention in the poetry category of Canada's National Magazine Awards. She is an editor for Augur Magazine and was a guest editor for Strange Horizons' Wuxia and Xianxia special issue. She has an MFA in Creative Writing UBC and is a graduate of the Clarion West Writers Workshop.
people.name: Yilin Wang

people.bio: Yume Kitasei (www.yumekitasei.com) is the author of THE DEEP SKY and THE STARDUST GRAIL (Flatiron Books). She is half Japanese and half American and grew up in a space between two cultures—the same space where her stories reside. She lives in Brooklyn with two cats, Boondoggle and Filibuster. Her stories have appeared in publications including New England Review, Catapult, SmokeLong Quarterly, and Baltimore Review. She chirps occasionally @Yumewrites at Instagram, TikTok, and Blue Sky.
people.name: Yume Kitasei

people.bio: Yves Meynard is an award-winning, bilingual Canadian author of over 20 books and 60 short stories. He was fiction editor for the québécois magazine Solaris from 1994 to 2001 and has co-edited some anthologies. Born in Québec City, he now makes his home in Ottawa.
people.name: Yves Meynard

people.bio:
Yvette Keller is the planet earth authority on Douglas Adams literary tourism, a Towel Day Ambassador and the author of the Douglas Adams’ London guide from Herb Lester Associates. 

Her short fiction leans toward SF/Fantasy at an extravagantly relaxed angle. You can find her work in literary magazines such as Enheduanna, Imitation Fruit Literary Magazine, and The Santa Barbara Literary Journal.

For fun, Yvette time travels in self-made historical costumes, reads constantly, and performs in short-form improv and live storytelling shows. She lives in the world of the television phenomenon, Psych, finding contract work as a business consultant, an industrial voiceover professional, and a holistic detective.
people.name: Yvette Keller

people.bio: Yvette Lisa Ndlovu is a Zimbabwean sarungano. Her debut short story collection Drinking from Graveyard Wells (University Press of Kentucky) won the Cornell University 2023 Philip Freund Prize for Creative Writing, shortlisted for the Ursula Le Guin Prize for Fiction and nominated for the British Science Fiction Association Award for Best Collection. Her novel manuscript-in-progress was selected by George R.R. Martin for the Worldbuilder Scholarship. She earned her BA at Cornell University and her MFA at UMass Amherst. Her work has been supported by fellowships from the Tin House Workshop, Bread Loaf Writers Workshop, and the New York State Summer Writers Institute. She is the Newhouse Visiting Assistant Professor of Creative Writing at Wellesley College and has taught at UMass Amherst, Clarion West online, and the Juniper Institute for Young Writers. She is the co-founder of the Voodoonauts Summer Fellowship for Black SFF writers. Her work has been anthologized in the World Fantasy Award-winning anthology Year’s Best African Speculative Fiction 2021 and the NAACP-award nominated Africa Risen (Tor). Her work has appeared or is forthcoming in the Columbia Journal, F&SF, Tor.com, Lightspeed, FANTASY Magazine, and Fiyah Literary Magazine for Black Speculative Fiction. She is currently at work on a novel.
people.name: Yvette Lisa Ndlovu

people.bio: Z. K. Abraham is a writer and psychiatrist. She has been published in Clarkesworld, Fantasy Magazine, Podcastle, Apparition Lit, Necessary Fiction, The Rumpus, and more. She is represented by Carleen Geisler at ArtHouse Literary.
people.name: Z. K. Abraham

people.bio: Zach Weinersmith is the creator of the webcomic Saturday Morning Breakfast Cereal, and too many books, including Soonish, Open Borders, Bea Wolf, and A City on Mars.
people.name: Zach Weinersmith

people.bio: Producer for Zombies, Run! and Marvel Move. Writer, plays too much Destiny. Active in creative fandom for longer than I care to remember.
people.name: Zalia Chimera

people.bio: Zhui Ning Chang is a Malaysian editor, writer, librettist and theatre maker based in London, UK. They serve as editor-in-chief at award-winning khōréō magazine, assistant editor for SFWA’s Publishing Taught Me series with Nisi Shawl, and co-edited the anthology Best of Malaysian Short Fiction in English 2010-2020 (Malaysian Writers Society). Their writing for performance includes queer romcom Seashore Yuanfen and time travel project Asian Pirate Musical; their reviews and essays have appeared in Strange Horizons, The BSFA Review, Library Journal, Fantasy/Animation, and more. Currently, Zhui Ning is a PhD researcher in Southeast Asian speculative fiction at Birkbeck, University of London.
people.name: Zhui Ning Chang

people.bio: My name is Zoe Burgess-Foreman. I hold 2 Masters in Contemporary Film and Japanese Culture. I am an author and artist of queer cosmic horror. I also research Anime/Manga and Podcast.
people.name: Zoe Burgess-foreman

people.bio: Brought up on Japanese animation in Italy in the 80s, now an anime and manga enthusiast who prefers good stories and characters to "endless battles and characters that just grow ever more powerful!" dakkar works as a software developer in London
people.name: dakkar

people.bio:
YouTuber and writer.

Science Fiction/Fantasy Romance, and Fanfiction writer and fan.
Preferred genre: M/M Science fiction/Fantasy Romance.

Published in Dutch and English.
Linguistic knowledge of 8 languages.
people.name: ilana

people.bio: I've been attending conventions since 2014 (still relatively recent) often promoting another conventions. I've always loved reading books (mostly fantasy and space-opera, but also alternative history). I like watching Dr Who, but also Outlander (I bought the first book in the series in the nineties). I admire creative people, but am not one of them. I am an introverted reader who just likes going to fan based conventions and enjoys meeting friends there. I have been on 1-2 panels about music and sci-fi and about the Eurocon
people.name: klara lammers

people.bio: Ádám Gerencsér is co-editor of Sci Phi Journal, a Hugo, Locus and Utopia-nominated quarterly publication dedicated to the intersection of philosophy and speculative fiction, and winner of the 2022 European Award for Best SF Magazine. His essays on the history of SF literature have appeared in Hungarian and English, incl. in the Science Fiction Research Association Review. A fan of both rancorous tabletop gaming and relaxed fireside banter, he lives with his family in Brussels, Belgium, and works for the European Union and its utopian ideals on the frontlines of multilateral diplomacy.
people.name: Ádám Gerencsér

people.bio:
In 2013, I started writing microfiction on Twitter, as X was called until recently. Since then I have written over four thousand microstories, and branched out to other social media platforms.

Hugo Award finalist for Best Fan Writer in 2024 (and 2023).

20+ years of doing historical re-enactment - both combat and living history displays - for institutions like English Heritage and British Museum.
people.name: Örjan Westin (MicroSFF)
